title: jcl-bridge rejects DCB=dsname / DCB=(dsname,...): whole job lost (>=25% of production jobs)

title: MOVE operand serialisation drops subscripts, qualifiers and LENGTH OF
description: The ASG cache is written as json.dumps(asg.to_dict()) (cobble/cobble/parsing/parse_corpus.py:99), so every operand field the to_dict side omits is lost before any later stage reads it. MoveStatement._operand_dict (cobol_asg/cobol_statements.py:165) emits only name, ref_mod_start and ref_mod_length, while RefModOperand (cobol_asg/ref_mod.py:145) also carries subscripts, qualifiers, length_of and rounded, and from_dict reads all of them. ComputeTarget.to_dict serialises subscripts, so MOVE is inconsistent with its neighbour. Effect: a cache built with the current jar still has zero subscripted MOVE operands, and MOVE is the highest-volume verb in the corpus. A LENGTH OF source is worse than lossy -- it round-trips to an operand with an empty name. Refines 8y0, which correctly cleared the bridge and stopped one layer too early: the serialiser between bridge and cache is the culprit, and the stale cache masked it.
design: Serialise the full RefModOperand from _operand_dict, following ComputeTarget.to_dict's shape (emit each optional field only when set, so unsubscripted operands keep their current compact form and existing fixtures stay valid). Round-trip test: a subscripted operand and a LENGTH OF operand must survive to_dict then from_dict unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: to_dict/from_dict round-trip preserves subscripts, qualifiers, length_of and rounded on MOVE operands; unsubscripted operands serialise byte-identically to before; red-dragon suite green.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in red-dragon d07c3581 (MOVE operands keep their subscripts through to_dict), merged into forge via the submodule bump on main. Confirmed by the re-parse: the rebuilt cache carries 102,922 subscripted MOVE operands where the old one carried 0, with total and ref_modified byte-identical.

title: [bug] Bridge drops subscripts on MOVE operands: the interpreter silently reads and writes row 1 of every table
description:
MOVE is the only statement whose operands lose their subscripts. The source

    MOVE WS-MSG-LINE (WS-IDX) TO MSG-OUT

arrives as

    {"type": "MOVE", "operands": [{"name": "WS-MSG-LINE"}, {"name": "MSG-OUT"}]}

with (WS-IDX) silently gone. RefModOperand.from_dict already reads a "subscripts"
key and expr_from_dict already parses the nodes, so the Python side is ready; the
Java bridge simply does not emit them for MOVE. It does emit them elsewhere --
counted over 60 cached ASGs, subscripts appear under IF 958 times, PERFORM 50,
SEARCH 41, ADD 20, WHEN 5, and under MOVE exactly 0.

MEASURED COST, 300 programs, from the dataflow spike:
  114,448 references resolve to a table item with no subscript to place it
   91,602 MOVEs (19% of 492,405) therefore degrade to a weak update, unioning
          provenance into every row of the table instead of writing one

Weak updates are correct but they are the coarsest answer available, and they are
being forced by missing data rather than by genuine uncertainty. The distinction
matters most exactly where the corpus uses it: WS-MSG-LINE(WS-IDX) is a variable
subscript and has to widen, but SCR-CODE(3) and WS-FLAGS(1) are literal and must
not -- and cobble/dataflow/layout.py already materialises every occurrence with an
`index` tuple precisely so a literal subscript lands on one cell. None of that
precision is reachable until the bridge emits the operand.

Fix is Java-side in proleap-bridge: emit "subscripts" on MOVE operands the way the
condition and arithmetic paths already do. Then re-run the spike and the weak-update
count should drop to the genuinely-variable subscripts only.

Repro: grep any ONLINE program for a subscripted MOVE (PROG-B5:215, PROG-B1:1530,
PROG-B6:1306) and compare against the MOVE node in its ASG.
notes: Redacted 2026-09-07: corpus program, file, field and paragraph names replaced with stable pseudonyms (PROG-*, FILE-*, MST-*, SCR-*, BUF-*, LAY-*, MSG-*). Measured numbers and source line references are unchanged. The mapping and the pre-redaction text are in .knowledge_graph_scratch/ (untracked, per-machine).
close_reason:
NOT A BUG -- retracted. My evidence was a stale ASG cache, not the current bridge.

serializeMoveOperand (StatementSerializer.java:2183) is a one-line delegate to
serializeRef, the unified structured-reference serializer that emits "subscripts"
whenever non-empty. Commit 1a99c445 "feat(bridge): emit structured subscripts (bare
name + all subscripts), retire flattening (red-dragon-6ddr)" landed exactly this, and
57cf80e9 then retired _SUBSCRIPT_RE / parse_subscript_notation on the Python side
because subscripts had become fully structural. The lowering consumes them at
lower_arithmetic.py:419,436.

My cached ASGs were generated before 6ddr, so every MOVE in them has bare operands.
The "interpreter reads row 1 of every table" claim does not hold and the P0 was wrong.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DATAFLOW SPIKE: its subscript numbers are worthless and must be
rediscovered against a rebuilt cache. Specifically these were cache artifacts, not
corpus properties:
  114,448 references to table items with no subscript
   91,602 MOVEs degraded to weak updates (19%)
Rebuild the cache with the current jar and re-run before quoting any of them.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text:
SEVERITY ESCALATION -- this is not an analysis limitation, it is a silent
wrong-answer bug in the interpreter.

The IR lowering already asks for MOVE subscripts and already knows what to do with
them. interpreter/cobol/lower_arithmetic.py, lower_move at 351:

    419:                    subscripts=target.subscripts,
    436:            subscripts=stmt.source.subscripts,

and emit_context.py resolve_field_ref handles them properly -- 1-D via
"(idx-1)*stride + base", multi-D by accumulating per-dimension OCCURS strides
(red-dragon-1wy3), with an explicit error when the subscript count exceeds the
declared dimensions.

But emit_context.py:263 reads:

    if not subscripts:

and falls through to the base FieldLayout. The bridge hands MOVE an empty subscript
tuple, so that branch is always taken. Consequence:

    MOVE WS-MSG-LINE (WS-IDX) TO MSG-OUT

lowers to a LoadRegion at WS-MSG-LINE's base offset with no index arithmetic emitted
at all. The interpreter reads row 1. Every subscripted MOVE in every program reads
and writes row 1 of the table, silently -- no error, no warning, no diagnostic.
the corpus uses subscripted MOVE constantly (PROG-B5:215, PROG-B1:1530/1575/2269/2370-75),
so any the corpus online transaction that indexes a table is executing against the wrong row.

Other verbs are unaffected because the bridge does emit their subscripts: counted over
the cached ASGs, IF 958, PERFORM 50, SEARCH 41, ADD 20, WHEN 5, MOVE 0.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: tests/unit/cobol/test_ref_mod_operand_subscripts.py and
test_resolve_field_ref_subscripts.py both hand-construct the dicts they feed to
RefModOperand.from_dict. They prove the Python half parses subscripts and the lowering
half consumes them. Neither crosses the Java seam, so the one thing that is broken --
the bridge not emitting them for MOVE -- is exactly the thing untested.

Regression test to add alongside the fix: parse a source containing a subscripted MOVE
through the real bridge and assert the operand's subscripts are non-empty. An
end-to-end execution test that MOVEs into row 3 and reads row 3 back would also fail
today.

title: Extract the system catalog into its own component shared by jackal and cicada
description:
On z/OS the catalog and the datasets it labels belong to the system: batch jobs and CICS regions read the same catalog and the same VSAM clusters (CardDemo's CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL jobs close a file in CICS, update it in batch, reopen it). In the forge they are split: jackal owns `SystemCatalog` (labels incl. `KsdsLabel`, dataset bytes under one directory), while cicada's VSAM engine (`cics/vsam/`) reads its own `data_dir` with record lengths and keys hand-written in the region config. A record written by a job never reaches a region, and cicada takes unlabelled datasets.

Extract the catalog (labels, dataset store) into its own component that jackal and cicada both depend on, with cicada's file control reading through it. Design via brainstorming before any code. Blocks red-dragon-forge-jr5 (the runner), whose CICS datasets come from this catalog via the CSD.
close_reason: Commits 318d03b 0a2c1a4 4bfaba7 7e98bba e8f9ab9 0e687bc and the docs commit

title: JCL parser resolves an omitted DISP before existence is known: MOD on a new dataset should default to DELETE, not KEEP
description:
The JCL parser resolves an omitted DISP normal (and abnormal) disposition at parse time (jackal/jcl/wire.py disp_from_words: KEEP for OLD/SHR/MOD, DELETE for NEW), so the model cannot tell `DISP=MOD` from `DISP=(MOD,KEEP)`.

IBM's rule (MVS JCL Reference, DISP "Defaults"): "If you omit the normal termination disposition subparameter, the default is DELETE for a NEW data set or KEEP for an existing data set." "New" means the data set does not exist when the step allocates it — Figure 12-1 lists "MOD treated as new" with the NEW rows — not that NEW was coded. "If you omit the abnormal termination disposition subparameter, the default is the disposition specified or implied by the second subparameter. However, if the second subparameter specified PASS, the default abnormal termination disposition is DELETE for a NEW data set or KEEP for an existing data set."

So `//OUT DD DSN=J.LOG,DISP=MOD` on a dataset that does not exist creates it and, with no normal disposition coded, deletes it at step end; jackal keeps it.

Wanted: the model records an omitted normal or abnormal disposition as not coded; the default is applied where existence is known — at allocation, when the catalog knows whether it found or created the dataset — and the resolved disposition travels with the allocation to disposal.

Corrected 2026-10-11 from primary sources: the first version of this issue claimed an omitted normal disposition on a received passed dataset defaults to PASS. Figure 12-1 shows such a dataset is kept, and with SMS "the system replaces PASS with KEEP for permanent VSAM and non-VSAM data sets", so that claim was wrong.
notes: Decisions and IBM sources (z/OS 3.1 JCL Reference, DISP Defaults p.153, MOD-as-new p.149, Table 17): docs/records/design/2026-10-11-jackal-dataset-decisions.md, D11-D12.
close_reason: Omitted DISP subparameters are recorded as Omitted and defaulted at allocation by whether the dataset existed (IBM JCL Reference 3.1 DISP Defaults); MOD treated as new now defaults to DELETE and counts as created for PASS. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-11-jackal-dataset-decisions.md.

title: jcl-bridge: compound JOB COND is a grammar error; EVEN/ONLY between EXEC COND tests crashes the serializer
description:
Two COND defects, found by the object-model acceptance review (2026-10-10).

1. JOB card COND with more than one test is a grammar error: //J JOB (A),'D',CLASS=A,COND=((8,LE),(12,EQ)) -> line 1:48 mismatched input ','. The JCL Reference allows up to eight tests on JOB COND.
2. EXEC COND with EVEN or ONLY between return-code tests crashes the Java serializer: COND=((4,LT),EVEN,(8,EQ,S1)) -> NumberFormatException: "EVEN". The JCL Reference lets EVEN/ONLY sit before, between or after the tests.

Pinned by jackal/tests/acceptance/test_cond.py::test_cond_parses. Fix in jackal/jcl-bridge with Java tests beside JclSerializerTest.
notes: Part 1 (compound JOB COND grammar) fixed in unit 2 task 1; part 2 (EVEN/ONLY between tests) lands with the new contract.
close_reason: Bridge half fixed by the unit 2 contract (ContractTest). The model half lands in units 3-4 (2cy.9, 2cy.10), pinned by the acceptance suite.

title: cicada: a CICS spec built without a program cache makes every LINK fail silently
description:
`build_cics_spec` takes `program_cache: dict | None = None`, and `CicsLoweringStrategy` substitutes a fresh `{}` for anything that is not a `MutableMapping`. A caller that forgets the cache gets programs whose `EXEC CICS LINK` resolves against a private empty dict, so every LINK fails as an unknown program, silently.

Commit 3ce3c25 fixed one caller (`cics/tn3270/region.py`) by passing a cache in. `cics/bootstrap.py` still builds its spec without one and fills a separate cache afterwards, so a LINK between programs of a bootstrapped region is expected to fail the same way.

Fix the cause: the cache is required, so no caller can forget it. Add a regression test for LINK in both a TN3270-served region and a bootstrapped one.
notes: a0ea45b fixed run_carddemo_region, with a regression test (LINK reaches the callee: DONE, INIT without the fix). Remaining: program_cache is still optional on build_cics_spec and the strategy still substitutes an empty cache, so a future caller can repeat the bug; about 55 build_cics_spec calls and 35 direct strategy constructions, nearly all tests, omit it. The TN3270 region has no regression test.
close_reason: build_cics_spec and CicsLoweringStrategy require program_cache (keyword-only) and the empty-cache fallback is gone; forgetting it is a TypeError naming the argument. Both regions pass the cache they fill (a0ea45b). The TN3270 region has no LINK test of its own; the requirement covers it structurally.

title: Fixpoint ~7x slower on CardDemo after the partial-overwrite split (COACTUPC)
description:
The byte-precise partial-overwrite split (commit e106b1e) made `cobble-dataflow-fixpoint --all` on CardDemo about 7x slower: 10.45s before, 72.6s after.

Almost all of the extra time is in COACTUPC:
- worklist dequeues went from about 20k to 86k;
- time went from 8.4s to 70.6s.

The likely cause is that splitting creates fragmented state keys. Two paths fragment the same record differently, joins union both key sets, and states take more rounds to stabilise and cost more to hash. This is a hypothesis, not yet profiled.

Candidate fix: put the state into a canonical form. Coalesce adjacent pieces that carry identical sources and sliced values back into one entry, so equal states compare equal regardless of how they were fragmented. Profile first.

Acceptance: the CardDemo fixpoint returns to within 10% of the pre-split runtime, with byte-identical output to the split version.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in red-dragon a9d6c005: RegionId and Precision now hash by identity, and FieldExtent computes its hash once (rebuilt on unpickle, so worker processes stay correct). CardDemo --all fixpoint: 10.9s and 11.0s, against 10.7s before the split and the 11.8s target; every table byte-identical. Forge picks it up through the vendor/red-dragon submodule bump.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: CardDemo --all fixpoint, wall time, same machine: pre-split (e106b1e^) 10.7s; after split (e106b1e..4b99ea4) 73.1s; d5b16f1 canonical join 31.0s; same-name canonical form 14.8s. Every table byte-identical to the pre-change run. Acceptance (10.45s + 10%) still unmet. Remaining hotspot: COACTUPC needs 28,923 dequeues against 21,480 pre-split, because the value map stays split (exact_values needs exact keys); the rest is FieldExtent hashing (Python Enum.__hash__) in _joined_sources/_arrived lookups and the {**proxy} copies, which rehash every key. Copying via MappingProxyType.copy() measured 13.3s but needs State's field types changed.

title: VSAM partial-key access: FCT key length overrides KEYLENGTH (GENERIC READ/STARTBR/DELETE suspected broken)
description:
Suspected: partial-key access ignores KEYLENGTH. VsamEngine._klen returns `geom.key_length or key_length`, so a file's configured key length always wins over the KEYLENGTH option. READ/DELETE build the search key as `key[:klen]`. A READ GENERIC KEYLENGTH(4) on an 8-byte-key file would then search for the full 8-byte RIDFLD, bytes after the generic prefix included, instead of the 4-byte prefix. (Read, not reproduced: STARTBR passes key_length to the driver and browse.py says "a short KEYLENGTH already narrows the driver's key comparison", so browse may differ from point operations.)

Reach (census): KEYLENGTH on 46.7% of READs (1,143 programs), ~44% of STARTBRs, ~13% of READNEXTs. GENERIC on 41 READs, ~10% of STARTBRs, 54 DELETEs (27 programs). STARTBR GTEQ 81.7%. Partial-key positioning is a real pattern, not an edge case.

First task: failing tests on a KSDS with an 8-byte key, for READ GENERIC KEYLENGTH(4) EQUAL and GTEQ, STARTBR GENERIC KEYLENGTH(4) GTEQ then READNEXT, and DELETE GENERIC KEYLENGTH(4). Real CICS DELETE GENERIC removes every record with the prefix and returns NUMREC; the current delete removes at most one. If the tests pass, close this as verified with the tests kept.

Note: when KEYLENGTH equals the full key length, which is likely common, behaviour is the same either way, so programs that do not use GENERIC are mostly unaffected.

title: Measure cobble + cicada on the target CICS estate; census command-form grammar regression test
description:
Measure the real gap on the target estate before changing anything.

1. Run the cobble build (and its diagnosis commands for unparseable COBOL and unresolved COPYs) over the estate. The CICS grammar is not the risk; the probe parsed every census command form. The risks are ProLeap's COBOL parse rate on 2,000+ production members and copybook resolution. Keep outputs in an untracked experiment directory (data-security.md).
2. Record: COBOL parse rate, programs with at least one unparsed EXEC CICS, CSD availability (or whether synth_csd must reconstruct transactions), dynamic LINK targets the dataflow pass could not resolve.
3. Turn the census's command forms into a cicada grammar regression test with made-up names: the 42 forms already probed on 2026-10-05 (READ/STARTBR/DELETE with DATASET, KEYLENGTH, GENERIC, GTEQ, UPDATE, TOKEN; RESETBR; LINK/XCTL/START TERMID FROM/RETRIEVE/RETURN TRANSID; HANDLE/IGNORE CONDITION; HANDLE AID; FORMATTIME with YYMMDD/DATESEP/TIMESEP; ASSIGN USERID; BIF DEEDIT; SEND MAP/TEXT/PAGE, ROUTE, bare SEND/RECEIVE; WRITEQ/READQ/DELETEQ TS; SPOOLOPEN/WRITE/CLOSE; DELAY; SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK; GETMAIN; ENQ/DEQ; INQUIRE/SET TERMINAL; ENTER TRACEID; QUERY SECURITY; ALLOCATE/CONNECT PROCESS/FREE; ASKTIME), each asserting the exact verb and option set.

title: CICS production-estate readiness (census-driven 80/20): cobble static + cicada runtime
description:
Get cicada and cobble ready for a production-scale CICS estate that is not CardDemo, ordered by how many programs each gap touches. Evidence: a feature-usage census of an external production CICS estate (2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; static scan, 2026-10-05), plus a probe of cicada's CICS grammar and a read of its lowering, VSAM engine and dispatcher.

Where the estate's calls go: VSAM file control 43%, program/transaction control 28%, ASKTIME/FORMATTIME 11%, condition handling 7%, BMS 5%, everything else ~6%. House error-handling style: NOHANDLE plus checking EIBRESP/DFHRESP inline (92% of programs), so the values the runtime writes (EIBRESP, EIBRESP2) matter more than condition dispatch.

Parsing is not a blocker: the CICS grammar parses all 42 command forms the census found (probe, 2026-10-05).

Static (cobble) is close: LINK/XCTL, RETURN TRANSID, START TRANSID, SEND/RECEIVE MAP and file verbs (with the DATASET alias) are already in the graph. Gaps: TS queues, START TERMID routing, spool -> JES.

Execution (cicada) gaps by reach: FORMATTIME ignores ABSTIME (1,641 programs), possibly partial-key access (up to 1,143), DUPKEY/alternate-index paths (1,044), START to another terminal (1,017), EIBRESP2 (708), conditions that never fire, TS queues (66), unit of work over VSAM, and the low-volume verb tail.

Three of these are structural: one terminal per region, no unit of work over recoverable files, no alternate-index paths. Living roadmap: cicada/docs/cics-production-roadmap.md.

Unused in the census, deprioritize: channels/containers, WEB/DOCUMENT/SOAPFAULT, SIGNON/SIGNOFF/VERIFY PASSWORD, interval scheduling (START INTERVAL/AT/AFTER, CANCEL), WAIT/POST/CONVERSE, explicit ABEND/DUMP, TD queues.

title: cobble JCL graph: &&temp datasets as job-scoped nodes (data flow within a job)
description:
cobble's jcl_graph drops every DD without a dataset identity outside the job (`_has_dataset_identity`, jcl_graph.py:153), and that includes `&&temp` datasets. That is right for linking jobs to each other, but it hides the main way data moves inside a job: step A writes &&EXTR with DISP=(NEW,PASS), step B reads it with DISP=(OLD,PASS). Today the graph shows A and B with no connection.

Reach: the census calls temp chaining with `DISP=(,PASS)` the dominant step-to-step data-passing idiom. Backward `*.step.dd` DSN references, the alternative, were never used (0 occurrences). So for that corpus, temps are the only data flow within a job.

Work: represent each temp dataset as a node scoped to its job, so it never merges with another job's &&EXTR. STEP -> temp edges use the same DISP-derived READS/WRITES kinds as other datasets. The one-ampersand spelling that temp_if_unresolved already reads as a temp is included.

Design choice to settle at brainstorm, not here: a job-scoped dataset node (keeps one rule, DD -> dataset edge, and shows the temp's name), or a direct STEP -> STEP flow edge (smaller graph, but a new edge kind and no node for the data). The first fits the existing graph better.

Interacts with S3 only by sharing the DSN match sites; independent otherwise.

title: GDG relative generations as a typed DSN; cobble graph keys the GDG base (lineage across jobs)
description:
A GDG relative reference (`DSN=P.HIST(+1)`, `(0)`, `(-1)`) reaches the model as a DirectDSN whose literal includes the suffix. So cobble makes `P.HIST(+1)` and `P.HIST(0)` separate dataset nodes, and the lineage that GDGs exist for disappears: job A writes (+1), job B reads (0), and the graph shows them touching different datasets.

Reach: >=25% of census jobs (212+ files, lower bound) use relative generations, usually as `(+1)` with `DISP=(NEW,CATLG)`, often created by an IEFBR14 step with `UNIT=(,,DEFER)`.

Work:
1. A GDG-relative DSN type in jackal/dsn.py (base name + signed relative generation), produced where the DSN is parsed (bridge serializer or deserializer), not by regex downstream (design-principles: no information in string representations). Absolute generations (`.G0001V00`) stay DirectDSN unless the corpus shows they matter.
2. cobble jcl_graph: the node is the GDG base. The edge carries the relative generation as an attr, so "writes the next generation" and "reads the current one" stay distinguishable without splitting the node. READS/WRITES still come from DISP as today.
3. dsn_key and every match on DSN variants must handle the new type (refactoring.md: map the blast radius with ast-grep first).

jackal-1o2.4 (GDG execution) reuses this type, which is why it depends on this issue.
close_reason: Bridge emits a typed relative generation (JCL Reference DD DSNAME p.166 rule); jackal model GenerationDSN(base, relative); cobble keys the GDG base node with the generation on the edge. Execution still uses the old rendered name until jackal-1o2.4.

title: JclSerializer drops concatenated DDs after the first, silently
description:
Concatenated DD statements (a named DD followed by unnamed `//  DD` continuations) parse, but JclSerializer emits only the first dataset. The rest are silently dropped from the Job JSON, so cobble has no READS edge for them and jackal never sees them.

Reach: the census lists concatenation as common, mainly multi-source merges into SORTIN-style inputs. No exact count, because the pattern search could not isolate unnamed continuation cards. In the census corpus JOBLIB also appears on almost every job, and load-library chains are often concatenated.

Reproduce:
  //S1 EXEC PGM=SORT
  //SORTIN DD DSN=P.A,DISP=SHR
  //       DD DSN=P.B,DISP=SHR
-> one DD, SORTIN -> P.A; P.B is missing.

The grammar already models it: `ddStatementAmalgamation -> ddStatement ddStatementConcatenation*` (JclSerializer.java header). The serializer just never walks `ddStatementConcatenation`.

Work:
1. Serializer: emit each concatenated dataset, with its own DSN and DISP, in order.
2. Model (jackal/model.py): a DD carries an ordered tuple of datasets, or a concatenation type. This is a model decision to settle at brainstorm; jackal-1o2.5 already sketches `DD.datasets: tuple[...]`. The deserializer, proc_expand overrides (an override can target a concatenation member) and jcl_graph all follow.
3. cobble jcl_graph: one edge per concatenated dataset, sharing the ddname, with the concatenation position as an edge attr.
4. jackal runner: until jackal-1o2.5 implements concatenated reads, reject a concatenated DD with an explicit error naming the step and ddname. Never silently use only the first dataset.

Execution semantics stay in jackal-1o2.5, which depends on this.
close_reason: Bridge half fixed by the unit 2 contract (ContractTest). The model half lands in units 3-4 (2cy.9, 2cy.10), pinned by the acceptance suite.

title: Measure the real JCL parse gap on the target corpus + census-construct bridge regression fixture
description:
Before changing anything, measure the real gap on the target corpus instead of relying on the census estimate.

1. Run `diagnose-jcl --config <corpus>.toml` over the target corpus (cobble/README.md, "Diagnose unparseable JCL and COBOL before building"). Record the parse-failure count and group failures by first error token; keep the output in an untracked experiment directory (data-security.md: no corpus identifiers in tracked files).
2. Turn the census constructs into a bridge regression fixture under jackal's tests, with made-up names only: one tiny job per construct (TYPRUN/NOTIFY job card, JOBLIB, OUTPUT + OUTPUT=(*.x) back-reference, AMP=, DD concatenation, DCB=*.dd, DCB=(model,...), DCB=model, GDG (+1)/(0) with UNIT=(,,DEFER), (MOD,DELETE)+SPACE=(TRK,0), compound COND=((4,LT),(8,LT,S1)), EXEC <proc> without PGM=, IKJEFT01 with DSN/RUN PROGRAM/END, $DJDE$ lines in DD *, IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF, PARM='X (Y' and PARM='A=(,255)', JCLLIB). Each asserts the exact deserialized Job, so S1, S2, S6 flip expected values as they land; mark the currently broken cases xfail with this issue's id until their fix.

The 2026-10-05 probe already established: every construct parses except DCB=(dsn,...) and DCB=dsn (whole job fails, S1); concatenation loses DDs after the first (S2); IF/THEN loses the condition (S6).

Acceptance: a recorded parse rate for the target corpus, and the fixture suite committed.

title: JCL static analysis ready for a production-scale corpus (census-driven 80/20)
description:
Get cobble's JCL extraction to a trustworthy job -> step -> program -> dataset graph on a production-scale JCL corpus that is not CardDemo, before any execution work.

Evidence: a feature-usage census of an external production batch corpus (~860 jobs; counts are lower bounds from pattern search), plus a construct-by-construct probe of the jcl-bridge with synthetic jobs (2026-10-05). CardDemo parses 38/38, but CardDemo does not use the constructs that dominate production JCL, so "parsing is solved" does not carry over.

Census constructs and where they stand today:
- DCB=(model-dsn,...) paired with GDG (+1) on >=25% of jobs: the bridge rejects the whole job (child S1).
- &&temp chaining with DISP=(,PASS): the dominant step-to-step idiom; parses, but cobble drops temp DDs, so there is no data flow within a job (S4).
- GDG relative generations on >=25% of jobs: parsed as a literal, so each relative ref becomes its own dataset node and lineage across jobs breaks (S3).
- DD concatenation, common for multi-source merges: the serializer silently drops every DD after the first (S2).
- COND= on the large majority of EXEC statements: parsed, not shown on the graph (S5).
- IF/THEN/ELSE on ~1% of jobs: flattened, so both branches look unconditional (S6).
- Already correct, no work: IKJEFT01 -> DB2 RUN PROGRAM (26%, TSO_RUNS_PROGRAM), cataloged procs absent from the corpus (read as program nodes), OUTPUT statements, $DJDE$ print payload in DD *, AMP=, TYPRUN=, JOBLIB, PARM with unbalanced parens inside quotes, DD DUMMY (correctly no node).
- Not used by the census corpus: SET/&var symbolics (0), backward *.step.dd DSN refs (0), in-deck PROC/PEND (~0), RESTART= (0), JCLLIB (2 jobs).

Order: S0 (measure) and S1 first; S1 is the keystone because nothing else applies to a job that does not parse. Then S3 and S4 (the two largest data-flow gaps), S2, S5, S6.

Execution follow-on lives under jackal-1o2; see jackal/docs/jcl-execution-roadmap.md.

title: cobble srccfg: lower ON EXCEPTION / ON OVERFLOW branches
description: The bridge now carries CALL ON EXCEPTION / NOT ON EXCEPTION and STRING/UNSTRING ON OVERFLOW / NOT ON OVERFLOW (red-dragon-jqw2, closed; in the ASG since the 4fcd1436 bump), but desugar never reads on_exception/on_overflow, so the statements in those branches are absent from the CFG and every analysis on it. Lower each as a two-armed decision after the statement.
close_reason: CALL ON EXCEPTION and STRING/UNSTRING ON OVERFLOW lower as arms after their statement; the statement index reads the same ARM_CLAUSES

title: cobble srccfg: lower NEXT SENTENCE
description: Once the bridge serialises NEXT SENTENCE and sentence boundaries (red-dragon-dp1w), desugar must lower it as a jump to the statement after the next separator period. Today it reads as CONTINUE, so the statements between it and the period look reachable on that arm.
close_reason: NEXT SENTENCE lowers to a GOTO edge to a landing node after its sentence's last statement

title: cobble srccfg: lower EXIT PARAGRAPH
description: Once the bridge carries EXIT PARAGRAPH (red-dragon-khp6), desugar must lower it as a jump to the current paragraph's #end. Until then a program using it gets no ASG and is lost to every cobble stage.
close_reason: EXIT PARAGRAPH / EXIT SECTION lower to a GOTO edge to the paragraph's or section's #end

title: cobble: bind CALL USING arguments to the callee's parameters across programs
description: aliases.py refuses every CALL site (call-using-unsupported: 18 dead ends on CardDemo), so the fixpoint, cobble-fields-trace and the query's --across-calls never connect a CALL USING argument to the callee parameter it binds. Bind each argument positionally to the callee's PROCEDURE DIVISION USING entry: BY REFERENCE as shared storage (a write-back, as LINK's commarea), BY CONTENT/VALUE as a copy in only. Needs the ASG to carry the USING list: red-dragon-y2ce.
close_reason: CALL USING arguments bind by position to the callee's PROCEDURE DIVISION USING in aliases.jsonl; BY REFERENCE returns, BY CONTENT/VALUE inbound only; the query crosses them. The trace follow-up is coo.

title: cobble fixpoint: a value on one path joined with a miss on the other reads back as certain
description: state._joined_values takes an extent held on one side only as-is, treating the other side's missing entry as 'no path yet'. But a missing entry also means 'never written' and 'written with content the walk cannot name' (NOT_A_LITERAL/UNINITIALISED are deliberately not stored, _UNINFORMATIVE). So IF c MOVE 'PROGA' TO X ELSE COMPUTE X = ... END-IF joins to X = {PROGA} with no reasons, and a dynamic call through X becomes a proven edge rather than a candidate. Reproduced on the state functions: join(write(EMPTY, x, s, of_value(b'PROGA')), EMPTY) reads {PROGA}, reasons {}. Fix: an explicit unreached state for the fixpoint's starting point, and a one-sided extent picking up the other side's miss reason. Shares its root with red-dragon-forge-111 (the miss reason itself).
close_reason: a one-sided join entry takes the other side's view; first arrival no longer joins with EMPTY

title: cobble fixpoint: PERFORM ... VARYING's init and step writes are never applied
description: PERFORM P VARYING WS-I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL ... lowers to synthetic #init and #step SET nodes with no statement behind them, so the walk applies no write. A read of WS-I inside P reports its VALUE clause (e.g. '0   ') with no reasons -- a wrong value asserted as certain -- and no definer for the counter. Expected: #init writes the FROM value, #step writes the counter from itself (not a literal), both as definers.
close_reason: Fixed in 16e480d: #init/#step indexed as MOVE/ADD statements.

title: cobble srccfg: sections have no CFG node, so PERFORM / GO TO / WHENEVER to a section connect to nothing
description: The CFG gives every paragraph a label node but no section one. Jump targets resolve against paragraph labels, so PERFORM WORK-SECTION, GO TO ERR-SECTION and EXEC SQL WHENEVER SQLERROR GO TO ERR-SECTION produce their nodes and no edge. Code in a performed or jumped-to section is unreachable to the fixpoint, the trace and the src-cfg drawings. Fix: a SECTION#label node flowing to the section's first paragraph; PERFORM section returns after its last paragraph; the program entry is the first section label when the division opens with one.
close_reason: Fixed in 5e813e8: sections get #label and #end nodes; PERFORM/GO TO/WHENEVER to a section resolve.

title: copybook_dirs entry that is not a directory: ProLeap NPEs, and both JVM stages cache it per member
description:
## What is wrong

A `copybook_dirs` entry that is not an existing directory makes every member of
the corpus die inside ProLeap, and both JVM stages record each death as if the
member itself were at fault. The cache is then permanently poisoned and the next
run reports success.

Reproduced against the bridge directly, three cases:

- directory absent -> `java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read the array
  length because "<local4>" is null` at
  `CobolWordCopyBookFinderImpl.findCopyBookInDirectory:45`. `File.listFiles()`
  returns null for a path that is not an existing directory, and the finder
  reads `.length` off it unguarded.
- a FILE given where a directory is expected -> the same NPE.
- directory present but the copybook absent -> the GOOD path, a
  `CobolPreprocessorException` naming the copybook, which
  `ProLeapCobolParser._enrich_copybook_error` then annotates with the searched
  directories. Nothing to fix here.

So the trigger is exactly `not Path.is_dir()`, and one predicate covers both bad
cases.

## Why it is worse than a bad error message

Reproduced end to end with `cobble-expand-corpus` on CardDemo, with `sym/` not
yet generated (`sym` is a `copybook_dirs` entry that `cobble-sym` creates):

1. First run: 27 of 29 members "fail", each writing a `<member>.fail` holding a
   Java stack trace. 2 members that reference no copybook succeed.
2. `cobble-sym` is then run, so `sym/` exists and the corpus is now correct.
3. Second run against the same directory reports
   `29 expanded, 0 to expand` and exits 0.

The output directory holds 2 real expansions and 27 stack traces, and the tool
says it is finished. The resumability that makes these stages cheap is what
makes the damage permanent: a `.fail` means "this member will never expand, do
not pay the JVM again", which is true for a missing copybook and false for a
missing copybook DIRECTORY.

`cobble-parse-corpus` has the identical exposure. Its `parse_one` catches bare
`Exception`, so a run-wide configuration fault is written per member into
`asg_dir` exactly the same way.

## Decided fix

**Pre-flight `copybook_dirs` in the entry points of the two stages that start a
JVM, before any work is submitted.**

A new leaf, `cobble/parsing/copybook_dirs.py`, exposing one function that takes
the configured directories and raises `SystemExit` naming every entry failing
`Path.is_dir()`. Called from `expand_corpus.main` and `parse_corpus.main` after
the config loads and before `ProcessPoolExecutor` is entered.

Why there and not elsewhere:

- It is the only place that can fail ONCE. Any check further in runs per member
  or per worker process, and in `parse_corpus` it would be swallowed by the
  bare `except Exception` and cached, which is the actual defect.
- Nothing is written before it fires, so there is no cache to clean up
  afterwards. That matters more than the error text.
- The stage entry points already own the other whole-run precondition, the
  bridge JAR (`bridge_jar` raises `SystemExit` naming `bridge-env.sh`). This is
  the same kind of check with the same failure mode, so it reads as a sibling
  rather than a new convention.

`Path.is_dir()` is the predicate: false for both a missing path and a file,
which is exactly the set of inputs that NPEs.

## Rejected, and why

- **Validate in `corpus_config.py`.** One place, every stage. Rejected: that
  module deliberately does no filesystem I/O and deliberately does not resolve
  relative paths, so a config valid on one machine would stop LOADING on
  another. It would also fire for stages that never look at a copybook.
- **Validate in `ProLeapCobolParser.__init__` (red-dragon).** The natural
  construction-site check, and it would cover cicada and jackal too. Rejected as
  the primary fix because the parser is built inside the worker process, so in
  `parse_corpus` the failure still lands in the bare `except Exception` and
  still gets cached per member. Worth doing as the next ring; see below.
- **Narrow `parse_one`'s `except Exception` to `CobolParseError`.** Does not
  separate the cases: ProLeap reports the NPE and a genuine unparseable member
  through the same non-zero exit, so both arrive as `CobolParseError`. Telling
  them apart would mean matching on the message text, which
  `design-principles.md` rules out.
- **Guard inside the Java bridge.** Fixes every caller, but per JVM, so the
  complaint arrives 3779 times and cobble still caches it.

## Known cost

`parse_corpus.py` carries ten standing python-fp-lint violations, so wiring the
call into its `main` adopts all ten and they must be fixed in the same commit
(no suppressions without approval). They are mechanical and of the same shape
already fixed in `cobol_asg/cobol_parser.py` under red-dragon-fhj7: a `+=` loop
in `_build_command`, a `list.append` and two reassignments in the progress
tally, a bare `except Exception`, an `is None`, and `main` exceeding the
complexity and statement ceilings. Budget for that, or the commit will not pass
the gate.

## Next ring, not this issue

- `ProLeapCobolParser.__init__` validating its `copybook_dirs` would cover
  cicada, jackal and red-dragon's own callers, which have the same exposure and
  no pre-flight of their own. Belongs upstream in red-dragon.
- `cobble/diagnosis/copybooks.py` states it mirrors
  `CobolWordCopyBookFinderImpl` EXACTLY, and at this one point it does not: it
  warns and returns an empty tuple for a missing directory, on the stated
  ground that a corpus can be onboarded before its copybook library is staged.
  That stance is right for a read-only report, but it means the diagnostic whose
  whole purpose is predicting parse failures without paying for the parse will
  report ordinary missing copybooks for a config on which every parse instead
  dies wholesale. Either the divergence gets documented where the EXACTLY claim
  is made, or the diagnostic grows a distinct louder finding for it.
notes:
## Where the defect actually lives, and why we still do not fix it there

The root cause is an UPSTREAM ProLeap defect, not something our fork introduced.
`CobolWordCopyBookFinderImpl.findCopyBookInDirectory` iterates
`copyBooksDirectory.listFiles()` with no null check, and `File.listFiles()`
returns null for any path that is not an existing directory. Its own caller
guards `params.getCopyBookDirectories() != null` three lines earlier, so this is
an oversight in that method rather than a deliberate contract.

Verified it is untouched by us: the fork's local commits are all grammar and
preprocessor fixes, and the last changes to that file are upstream's own
(dependency removals, "version 3.0.0"). `origin/red-dragon-copybook-fix` holds
nothing `origin/main` does not, so it is not prior art for this.

**We are deliberately NOT patching the vendored fork.** Reasons, in order:

- It would not fix the defect that actually costs us. The harm is not the
  exception, it is that cobble caches a run-wide configuration fault as a
  per-member `.fail` and then reports the corpus done. A guarded `listFiles()`
  returns "copybook not found" for every member instead of an NPE for every
  member, and cobble caches that just as permanently. The output directory is
  equally wrong; only the text inside the `.fail` files changes.
- Every local patch to the fork is permanent merge debt against upstream. The
  fork carries six such patches already, each earning its keep by fixing
  something no amount of calling-code care could work around. This is not one of
  those: the caller can check `Path.is_dir()` itself, once, for free.
- It fires per JVM, so on a 3779-member corpus the complaint arrives 3779 times
  and no run-level decision is ever made.

The pre-flight check decided above sits in front of all of this and makes the
question moot: no directory that fails `Path.is_dir()` ever reaches ProLeap, so
the unguarded `listFiles()` is never called with a null-yielding argument.

Recording it here so a later reader does not "helpfully" patch the fork and
inherit the merge debt without gaining anything.

Reporting it to upstream (uwol/proleap-cobol-parser) is a separate, optional
step. It costs us nothing and needs no local change; it has not been done.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] The EVALUATE ALSO lowering loop has no TRUE/FALSE guard, so a condition in ALSO position compares against a field named TRUE
description:
The primary-subject path in lower_evaluate guards against the EVALUATE TRUE form -- `stmt.subject.upper() != "TRUE"` at lower_arithmetic.py:1815 and :1854 -- so a WHEN under EVALUATE TRUE lowers its branch as a condition rather than as a comparison. The ALSO loop at :1895 has no such guard.

For `EVALUATE TRUE ALSO TRUE / WHEN cond-a ALSO cond-b`, a plain-string also_cond such as a level-88 name falls through to the else at :1984-1991 and lowers as `ref "TRUE" == value`, comparing against a field literally named TRUE. Cobble gets this right: conditions.py:335-340 routes TRUE/FALSE subjects to condition-reading.

No test exists for TRUE ALSO TRUE in either repo, which is why this survived.

Acceptance: EVALUATE TRUE ALSO TRUE lowers each ALSO branch as a condition, matching the primary-subject path and cobble's reading, with an e2e test covering it.
close_reason: Fixed in red-dragon 4c53bd12: an ALSO subject of TRUE now takes the same condition path the first subject does, instead of comparing against a field named TRUE. Tests cover TRUE ALSO TRUE matching and a false ALSO condition not taking the branch.

title: [bug] EVALUATE ALSO subjects are serialized as bare leaf names, losing qualifiers and ref-mod
description:
Commit a928ec5d fixed the primary EVALUATE subject to travel as a structured ref rather than a name, adding EvaluateStatement.subject_ref and structuredSubjectRef() in the bridge. The ALSO subjects were left on the old path: StatementSerializer.java:914 takes only qualifiedSubjectLeaf() for each entry of getAlsoSelects(), while structuredSubjectRef() is called at :901 for the primary subject alone. There is no also_subject_refs key anywhere in the ASG.

So `EVALUATE X ALSO FA OF GA(1:2)` ships the ALSO subject as the bare leaf `FA`. lower_arithmetic.py:1972,1986 then rebuild `{"kind":"ref","name": also_subj}` from that flat string, and the qualifier and reference modification are gone -- exactly the defect a928ec5d fixed, still present one subject position over.

A secondary mismatch sits alongside it: lower_arithmetic.py:1895 zips also_subjects against also_conditions non-strictly, so a length mismatch silently truncates, whereas cobble's desugar.py:544-551 pads with empty subjects under strict=True and treats an unmatched ALSO value as a condition in its own right. The two layers disagree on the same malformed input.

Cobble never reads subject_ref at all (no hits in cobble/ or its tests), so even the fixed primary subject is still the flat leaf name in cobble's CFG.

Acceptance: an ALSO subject carrying a qualifier or ref-mod round-trips with its structure intact and lowers through the same reference path as the primary subject; the zip disagreement between lower_arithmetic and cobble is resolved one way or the other.
close_reason: Fixed in red-dragon 4c53bd12: also_subject_refs rides alongside also_subjects, positional with an empty slot for a subject that is only a name, and the lowering reads it through _also_subject_ref instead of rebuilding a bare ref from the leaf name. Tests cover the bridge shape, the slice being compared, and the qualifier resolving.

title: cobble has no blocking pyright gate: 436 errors behind a vestigial '|| true' hook
description:
Observed 2026-09-23 while committing on fix/cics-program-subscript: two `git commit`
runs printed "(no files to check) Skipped" for file-scoped hooks -- pyright among them --
even though staged files matched those hooks' patterns. Pyright errors went in. They were
caught only by running the gates by hand afterwards and fixed in a follow-up commit
(668a19bb).

The consequence is the whole point: **a commit can pass with its gates silently
skipped**, and the output looks exactly like the legitimate case. "(no files to check)"
is also printed correctly and often -- a submodule-pointer bump really does touch no
Python -- so there is no way to tell a real skip from a missed one by reading the log.

Not reproduced deliberately yet; the two occurrences were noticed in passing. First job
is a reproduction: stage a file that matches a file-scoped hook, commit, and see whether
the hook runs. Suspects worth eliminating in order: pre-commit's own file filtering
against `--from-ref`/`--to-ref`, staged-vs-worktree divergence when an earlier hook
(Black) rewrites a file mid-run, and anything in .pre-commit-config.yaml's `files`/
`exclude` patterns that interacts with paths under a package subdirectory.

Worth an audit of today's commits once reproduced -- several carried "(no files to
check)" lines that were read as correct at the time, including on commits that did touch
Python. If the skip is real rather than an artefact of how the hook reports, some of
today's commits were not gated.

Note the repo's standing rule is that `--no-verify` is never used, precisely so the gates
are trustworthy. A hook that silently does not run defeats that rule without anyone
bypassing it.
notes:
2026-09-23: the original premise is WRONG and would send someone hunting a pre-commit bug
that does not exist. Corrected here rather than rewritten, so the misreading is visible.

The hooks behaved correctly. The forge's pyright hook is

    files: ^(cicada/cics|cicada/bms_copybook_gen|squall/squall|jackal/jackal|red_dragon_forge)/

and its comment says it "mirrors pyrightconfig.json `include`" -- which it does, exactly:

    "include": ["cicada/cics", "cicada/bms_copybook_gen", "squall/squall",
                "jackal/jackal", "red_dragon_forge"]

**cobble is in neither.** So staging cobble files and seeing "(no files to check)" is the
honest answer: those files were never in pyright's scope. Nothing was skipped that should
have run. Same for cicada/tests, squall/tests, jackal/tests, tools and root tests/, all of
which ARE covered by Black and fp-lint but not by pyright.

The real defect is the absence of a blocking type gate over cobble:

  * `cobble/pyrightconfig.json` exists and includes cobble + tests
  * `cobble/.pre-commit-config.yaml` -- vestigial, from when cobble was a standalone repo --
    runs `uv run pyright || true`, which can never fail
  * measured 2026-09-23: **436 errors**

So cobble Python is type-checked by nothing that blocks. fp-lint and Black DO cover it
(`^(...|cobble/cobble|cobble/tests|...)/`), so the gap is pyright alone, not "ungated
commits" generally. My earlier claim that commits could pass ungated was too broad.

Fix direction, and the forge's own pyright hook already states the policy that makes it
viable: "Blocking on staged files: touching a file obliges fixing its errors, while
untouched files' backlog does not block unrelated commits." Add cobble to the hook's
`files:` pattern on that basis -- the 436 become a backlog that blocks only the files
someone actually touches. Decide separately whether cobble's vestigial
.pre-commit-config.yaml should be deleted; it is dead in a monorepo and its `|| true` is
what let the backlog grow.
close_reason:
cobble is now inside the blocking pyright gate. Added cobble/cobble and cobble/tests to pyrightconfig.json's include and to the pre-commit pyright hook's files: pattern, so the staged-files policy the hook already documents applies to cobble too -- touching a file obliges fixing its errors, the 436-error backlog blocks nothing else. Deleted cobble/.pre-commit-config.yaml, vestigial from cobble's standalone days and dead in a monorepo (no .git under cobble; pre-commit only reads the repo-root config), whose 'uv run pyright || true' could never fail and is what let the backlog grow.

Verified falsifiable rather than assumed: pre-commit run pyright --files on a clean cobble file Passes, and on cobble/tests/test_build_graph.py FAILS with its two pre-existing _CollectingWriter/GraphWriter errors. Before the change both reported 'no files to check'.

The original premise was wrong and is corrected in the note above: the hooks behaved correctly all along, the pattern mirrored pyrightconfig.json exactly, and cobble was in neither. Nothing was being skipped that should have run; cobble simply had no type gate. fp-lint and Black always covered it, so the gap was pyright alone.

title: cobble reads a CICS PROGRAM() operand's text and drops its subscript
description:
cobble resolves an EXEC CICS LINK/XCTL callee from CicsOperand.text, which is the bare
operand name, and ignores CicsOperand.subscripts, which carries each index as a
structured ExprNode. So a subscripted target loses its index.

NOT a dialect-parser defect. cicada's parser separates the two deliberately --
cics/cics_visitor.py's CicsOperand docstring: "text preserved verbatim ... subscripts
carries each index as a structured ExprNode". cicada's runtime reads `subscripts`, which
is why CardDemo's menu dispatch works today. Only cobble's analysis reads the wrong field.

Site: cobble/dataflow/srccfg/desugar.py:1037, `_option_text(statement, PROGRAM_OPTION)`.

Repro, CardDemo's main-menu dispatch (COMEN01C.cbl:157, :185):

    EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION))
                   COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)
    END-EXEC

cobble sees the operand as 'CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME'. The site then resolves at arity 0,
finds no cell for a field that is declared OCCURS 12, and reports "no declared extent".

Severity is in the diagnosis as much as the miss. "No declared extent" reads like a
layout gap -- a field the data-division walker failed to map -- and it is not one. The
field is mapped; the analysis asked for the wrong thing. Anyone chasing it would tune
layout mapping to fix a field-selection bug. Three of CardDemo's 30 dynamic transfer
sites currently misreport their reason this way (constprop spike, 2026-09-22).

Consequence for the graph: COMEN01C has no resolved call edge to ANY menu program, so
the main menu -- the hub of the online application -- is a hole in the call graph. With
the subscript read it becomes a candidate set over the OCCURS 12 table.

No runtime consequence. cicada executes these correctly; this is analysis only.

Fix direction: read the operand structurally rather than by text. Note the table entry is
selected by WS-OPTION, a runtime value, so the honest resolved answer is a candidate set
of the table's occurrences, not a single program -- see the sibling beads for the
constant-propagation tiers.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged to main. Landed in three commits: 26f3aa48 read the operand structurally at the consuming sites; 3c74aa28 moved the real fix upstream into cicada, where the loss actually was -- ExecCicsStatement.to_dict kept only text/is_literal, so subscripts were gone before any reader ran; 555ab5f4 reduced it to one conversion. cicada's operand form now round-trips subscripts and ref-mod bounds, borrowing RefModOperand's codec rather than copying it (a CICS operand is a COBOL operand reference under another name). cobble's parallel type and asg_dialect_scope registration were deleted: cobble is permitted cicada's static surface and already imported CicsOperand in three places. Net cobble -183, cicada +163.

Five operand-reading sites found; three needed changing (desugar.py's PROGRAM option, depgraph/cics_cache.py's _operand, fields/transfer.py's _cics_targets -- COMMAREA and INTO/SET receivers had the identical arity-0 defect). flows.py's operand_name left deliberate (selector rule). A fourth misread operand surfaced: COMEN01C's EXEC CICS INQUIRE PROGRAM, not a transfer.

Measured before/after on CardDemo: no-extent:unknown-name 3 -> 0, extent:CLAMPED 0 -> 3, 26 EXACT and 2 literal unchanged. COMEN01C's dispatch node went from no extent to WORKING_STORAGE start=354 len=514 CLAMPED across all 12 occurrences, so the site is addressable storage and reaching-definitions at it is a well-formed query for the first time -- it answers 'no definers', which is forge-1o4's territory.

No new paths unlocked, and that is the honest result: closure from COSGN00C is 3 members / 7 calls / 2 aliases both ways, cobble-build set-identical at 449 nodes / 803 edges, no callee invented, no new errors (29/29 parse, exit 0). 27 of 29 ASGs byte-identical; the two that differ are the only members with a subscripted operand.

Surfaced forge-af6 (since fixed): the downstream-only version would have crashed on any reference-modified CICS operand, passing only because CardDemo has none. cicada 582 passed, cobble 1342 passed.

title: COTRTLIC F10 update writes row 01's description into the selected row
description:
Surfaced by bumping vendor/red-dragon to 10d2e1f8, which fixed INSPECT TALLYING
operand resolution (forge-twn) and so made COTRTLIC's F10 branch reachable for the
first time. The branch was previously dead, hidden behind WS-UPDATES-REQUESTED
always being 0, so this defect has never been observable before now.

Repro: tests/integration/test_carddemo_db2_headless.py::test_admin_five_updates_the_highlighted_row
(admin option 5, live Db2).

  terminal.press(TRTSEL5="U", TRTYPD5="REFUND PROCESSED")   # select row 5, overtype
  -> screen correctly shows "Update HIGHLIGHTED row. Press F10 to save"
  -> row 05 still ("REFUND", 6) on a third connection.      # correct, no DML this turn
  terminal.press(PF10)
  -> row 05 becomes ("PURCHASE", 50)                        # WRONG
     expected ("REFUND PROCESSED", 50)

'PURCHASE' is the seeded description of row **01**, not row 05 and not the overtyped
text. The UPDATE itself fires and commits correctly -- the length is 50, which is the
padded DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN, so the write path and the SYNCPOINT are working. What
is wrong is the VALUE: the selected row's key (05) is paired with row 01's
description.

That pairing points at the map read-back rather than the SQL: 9200-UPDATE-RECORD
(COTRTLIC:1846-1850) keys off the protected TRTTYP5 field read back out of the map,
so either the symbolic-map read is returning the first occurrence of a repeated field
group rather than the selected one, or the overtyped TRTYPD5 never reaches the
program and the description defaults to the first row's.

Two candidate causes, not yet distinguished:
  (a) cicada's BMS symbolic-map handling of repeated field groups (TRTSELn/TRTYPDn) --
      returning index 1 regardless of which row was selected;
  (b) MDT/field-preservation on the pseudo-conversational turn, so the overtyped value
      is dropped and stale map content is written back.

Whether this is our defect or CardDemo's own is the first thing to establish.
Distinguishing (a) from (b): if the overtyped text is absent from the program's
working storage on the F10 turn it is (b); if present but the wrong index is read it
is (a).

The test is pinned xfail(strict=True) against this bead in the meantime, so it turns
red the moment the cause is fixed.
close_reason: Verified fixed upstream in red-dragon: commit d76d0380 'fix(cobol): keep the subscript on an intrinsic FUNCTION argument' (bridge serializer + lower_arithmetic.py). Forge submodule bumped in commit ce78bf3a 'feat(forge): bump red-dragon to d76d0380, admin 5 green on its own terms'. test_admin_five_updates_the_highlighted_row now passes with NO xfail -- confirmed by this session's own full-suite run (12/12 passing in tests/integration/test_carddemo_db2_headless.py).

title: RedDragon: INSPECT ... TALLYING ... FOR ALL <operand> treats the operand as a literal string
description:

Consequences: 'INSPECT x TALLYING c FOR ALL SPACES' counts occurrences of the 6-character text 'SPACES' (always 0), and 'FOR ALL LIT-UPDATE-FLAG' counts occurrences of the identifier's NAME rather than its value. Confirmed in isolation on a PIC X(7) field of spaces: FOR ALL SPACES tallies 0, FOR ALL ' ' tallies 7.

title: VARCHAR host variables bind wrongly for real DCLGEN copybooks: field_meta only comes from squall's own JSON sidecars
description:
squall's level-49 VARCHAR codec exists and is correct, but is unreachable for real IBM DCLGEN copybooks. binding.py gates the 49-group path on field_meta[name]['category'] == 'VARCHAR', and field_meta is populated ONLY from a <NAME>.json sidecar (preprocess.py), which only squall's own dclgen generator writes. CardDemo's hand-written .dcl files have no sidecar.

Result: :DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION binds as a 52-byte alphanumeric whose first two bytes are the binary length. SELECT ... INTO clobbers the -LEN field; UPDATE ... SET sends a binary-prefixed blob to Db2. TR_DESCRIPTION is the ONLY editable field on both CardDemo Db2 screens, so this corrupts the one thing those screens exist to change.

Silent: no error, wrong data.

The missing piece is a READER, not a generator: something that derives field metadata from the copybook's own 49-level group (or from the DECLARE TABLE text that DCLGEN ships alongside it), rather than requiring a sidecar. Note dclgen.py's NotImplementedError on VARCHAR does NOT leak here — that is generation-side only.
close_reason: Verified fixed: squall/squall/dclgen_meta.py (new module) derives VARCHAR host-var metadata directly from the raw ProLeap bridge JSON's data_fields tree (level-49 group shape: S9(4) COMP length + X(n) text), with no dependence on a squall-generated sidecar. Landed in commit 7c3bbf44 'feat(squall): derive DCLGEN VARCHAR metadata from the level-49 group'. Closes the gap that corrupted DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION for hand-written IBM DCLGEN copybooks.

title: DECLARE CURSOR in WORKING-STORAGE never reaches squall: the bridge drops EXEC_SQL data entries
description:
proleap-bridge's DataFieldSerializer serialises only DataDescriptionEntryGroup and ...Rename; an EXEC_SQL data-description entry falls off the end of the if-chain with no error and no JSON node. A DECLARE CURSOR written in WORKING-STORAGE (rather than PROCEDURE DIVISION) therefore never reaches squall at all, _h_declare_cursor never runs, and the later OPEN returns SQLCODE -1.

CardDemo's COTRTLIC declares BOTH its cursors in WORKING-STORAGE, so admin menu option 5 cannot work regardless of anything else.

Silent: it compiles and runs, and fails only at OPEN.

Owning layer is the bridge serialiser (vendor/red-dragon/proleap-bridge), so the fix likely belongs in red-dragon; raised here because it blocks a forge-visible feature (forge-9kx). Verify against COTRTLIC.cbl before fixing.
notes: Found by the layer-gap survey after the CardDemo Db2 attempt stopped. Survey: .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-18-carddemo-db2-tn3270/layer-gap-survey.md (gitignored; re-derive if needed).
close_reason: Verified fixed: vendor/red-dragon's DataFieldSerializer.java now has an explicit DataDescriptionEntryExecSql branch (deliberately separate from the unhandled-type else, which now logs loudly) plus serializeExecSqlEntries collecting every EXEC SQL data-description entry (including WORKING-STORAGE DECLARE CURSOR) tagged by DATA DIVISION section. Landed in red-dragon commits d9e5afd4 and 889a15d1, picked up via commit 18dbbecf 'feat(squall): recover DECLARE CURSOR from WORKING-STORAGE via the bridge'. COTRTLIC's two WORKING-STORAGE-declared cursors now reach squall.

title: squall's EXEC SQL scan misses the trailing 8-digit sequence field, so 3-line INCLUDE blocks are never rewritten
description:
squall/squall/exec_sql_scan.py's _SEQ_NUM_LINE strips only LEADING 6-digit sequence numbers (cols 1-6). Fixed-format COBOL also carries a TRAILING 8-digit sequence field in cols 73-80, and CardDemo's app-transaction-type-db2 sources use both.

When an EXEC SQL block spans lines and the trailing field lands mid-block, the captured parse_text retains those digits. COTRTUPC.cbl's three-line form

  EXEC SQL
  INCLUDE SQLCA
  END-EXEC

is therefore never rewritten to COPY SQLCA. -- parse_exec_sql classifies it Kind.GENERIC and it survives as raw EXEC SQL into ProLeap.

Found while diagnosing the COTRTUPC compile gate; independent of that gate's blocker (fixing this alone does not make COTRTUPC compile). Fix: strip the trailing cols-73-80 sequence field as well as the leading one when building parse_text, and cover the 3-line INCLUDE form in tests.
notes:
SCOPE BADLY UNDERSTATED when filed. Measured on the real file by executing find_exec_sql_spans + parse_exec_sql over COTRTUPC.cbl: 5 of its 7 EXEC SQL spans degrade to Kind.GENERIC because of the unstripped cols-73-80 identification area — not just the 3-line INCLUDE. Pre-stripping to 72 columns turns them back into INCLUDE / SELECT_INTO / UPDATE / INSERT / DELETE.

Why that is severe: GENERIC falls through _HANDLERS.get(kind, _h_query) in builtins/exec_sql.py, so the mangled text — with sequence digits like '14750000' embedded mid-statement — ships verbatim to Db2 with no out_vars bound. All four CRUD statements of the program are affected. Silent: no error, wrong SQL.

COTRTLIC has no identification area and parses 16/16 clean, which is precisely why this was invisible until a second real program was tried.

Raising to P1.
close_reason: Verified fixed: squall/squall/exec_sql_scan.py's own comment (line 63) confirms sequence numbers are now stripped 'never from columns 1-7 or 73-80'; exec_sql_scan.py handles the trailing 8-digit sequence field alongside the leading one, closing the gap that degraded 5/7 COTRTUPC EXEC SQL spans to Kind.GENERIC. Landed alongside task 7's DECLARE CURSOR recovery work (commit 18dbbecf and neighbors).

title: XCTL to an unknown program crashes the driver instead of abending cleanly
description:
Reproduced headlessly via CardDemo admin option 5 (COADM01C XCTLs to COTRTLIC, which is not in the region). _route_xctl (cics/dispatcher.py:132) correctly returns DispatchResult(ABEND, 'PGMI') and the region terminates -- but the result handed back to PseudoConversationalDriver still has kind=XCTL, so driver._settle (cics/screen/driver.py:90) calls region.step() again and gets RuntimeError('step() called on a region that has terminated').

Over the wire this raises inside the session thread rather than painting the abend, so selecting admin 5 or 6 should be expected to drop the 3270 connection instead of showing a diagnostic -- NOT yet confirmed on the wire, only headlessly. Any XCTL to an uncompiled program hits this; admin 5/6 is just the reachable route in the shipped config.
