A COBOL step that CALLs a program by data-name (CALL WS-PGM) does not reach it.

Found in red-dragon-forge-355. red-dragon links only callees discovered from CALL 'LITERAL' edges (cobol_asg/cobol_imports.py scans literals; a data-name CALL is noise), and lower_call dispatches a data-name CALL at run time against the linked modules only. So the target is never linked and the CALL takes the unresolved-call path.

On z/OS a dynamic CALL loads the target from the step's program library at run time (STEPLIB/JOBLIB, then the link list).

Options (a decision for the user):
1. jackal links every program in its source directories into each step (faithful to "the library is everything callable"; one parse per member per step).
2. Upstream: red-dragon resolves an unlinked dynamic target at run time through an injected program loader that compiles and links it on first CALL.
3. Link targets named by a data-name's VALUE literal (a static guess; misses names built at run time).

Related upstream: red-dragon-dxij (ON EXCEPTION for an unresolved callee), red-dragon-t3kl.
Test: jackal/tests/integration/test_called_programs.py::test_a_dynamically_called_program_writes_to_its_own_dd (strict xfail).
close_reason: A CALL by data-name reaches programs on the runner's link list (JobRunner linked_programs, CLI --link). Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-dynamic-call-link-list.md. Follow-ups: xzw (target outside the run unit), btr (list derived from cobble).

title: jackal: a JclFeature enum for @covers, retag tests by the JCL feature they exercise, and a feature-coverage audit
description:
Every jackal test (730 at filing) is tagged @covers(NotLanguageFeature.INFRASTRUCTURE), because jackal/tests/covers.py is a minimal stub of red-dragon's with no feature enum. The marker therefore carries no information, and tests that do exercise JCL language features (DISP=PASS and the other dispositions, &&temps, COND= and COND=EVEN/ONLY, referbacks, PARM=, SET, PROC expansion and overrides, in-stream DDs, DUMMY) are mislabelled as infrastructure.

In red-dragon, @covers(CobolFeature.X) links a test to a language-feature enum and scripts/feature_coverage_audit.py reports which features have tests; NotLanguageFeature.INFRASTRUCTURE is ignored by the audit and exists only to satisfy the covers-guard hook.

Decided 2026-10-11 (user): give jackal the same. A JclFeature enum covering the JCL statements and parameters jackal parses or runs; retag every test that exercises one (keep INFRASTRUCTURE for tests that do not, e.g. catalog internals, CLI plumbing); wire the coverage audit for jackal so it reports JCL features with and without tests, including FeatureStatus.UNSUPPORTED/PARTIAL for known gaps. Check where the covers-guard hook is configured and whether it applies to jackal.

title: Steps after a failed allocation are Flushed(AfterAllocationFailure)
description:
On z/OS, once a step fails allocation, every later step in the job is flushed, whatever its COND says (JCL Reference: a step that terminates abnormally during scheduling, such as a JCL error or an inability to allocate space, makes the system bypass the remaining steps, no matter what the COND parameter requests).

Blueprint §6/§8: those steps get `Flushed(AfterAllocationFailure(step))`; gate rule 2 applies it before any COND test, and ahead of EVEN/ONLY.

Needs allocation failures as outcomes first (the allocation-failure issue).
close_reason: Steps after a failed allocation are Flushed(AfterAllocationFailure); unexpanded calls and unresolved referbacks are gated first

title: A DD that cannot be allocated is an AllocationFailed outcome, not an exception
close_reason: AllocationFailed outcomes with StrictAllocation/LenientAllocation strategies; referbacks copy the name and allocate

title: JCL grammar: a DD parameter with no value (UNIT=, VOL=, DISP=, DSN=) fails to parse
description: Nullifying a DD parameter in an override, e.g. //P1.IN DD DSN=X,UNIT=,VOL= (JCL Reference p.29), failed the whole member with 'no viable alternative': every ddParm rule required a value after EQUAL. The lexer already accepts it; only the parser rules needed the value made optional. Prerequisite for red-dragon-forge-5my, whose merge must tell a nullified parameter from one not coded.
close_reason: Every ddParm KEYWORD EQUAL value rule takes an optional value; pinned by ParseFixesTest.aDdParameterWithNoValueParses

title: jackal: support JCL SET statements (job-level symbols)
description: The bridge ignores // SET NAME=value, so expand_procs starts with no job-level symbols. A PROC symbol the job defines only by SET stays unbound, and when it is a lone DSN symbol the temp rule then reads a catalogued library as a temporary: CardDemo samples/jcl/CICDBCMP.jcl sets DCLLIB=&HLQ..DCL, and its PROC's DSN=&DCLLIB,DISP=SHR expands to &&DCLLIB (the old proc_expand did the same). Needs: a SET statement in the wire contract (in statement order, since SET applies to what follows), and expand_procs seeding symbols from it. Found by the object-model units 2-4 review (2026-10-10).
close_reason: SET statements serialized in order (jobs and PROCs, inside IF too), modelled as SetStatement, folded through expansion: later SET wins, EXEC > PROC default > SET, job-level steps substituted. CardDemo DCLLIB now AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DCL.

title: JCL object model unit 5: census run on the production-scale corpus
description: Unit 5 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-jackal-jcl-object-model-build-design.md (section 4.3). Run parse_jcl + expand_procs over the census corpus and record: share of members that parse, share that expand, failures grouped by JclError variant and by bridge error. Output stays in an untracked experiment directory; no names from that corpus enter the repo (guidelines/data-security.md). Each failure class becomes a construct fixture with made-up names plus a fix, or an issue. The corpus is not on the development machine where units 1-4 were built (2026-10-10); run this where it is.
notes: Runbook for the agent on the corpus machine: docs/how-to/census-jcl-object-model.md (script, data to gather, confidentiality rules, what to return).

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: First census run: 5 of 860 members failed expansion, all on references into PROCs missing from the library. The coordinate model now expands them, with the unresolved PROC, step or DD recorded as an unresolved coordinate and a warning. Re-run the updated runbook to confirm.

title: jcl-bridge kept the period that ends a symbol: &HLQ..X read as HLQ + ..X
description: A period directly after a symbolic parameter ends the symbol and is dropped (JCL Reference, symbolic parameters). The bridge kept it, so &HLQ..X with HLQ=T resolved to T..X. Fixed in object-model unit 2 (the new contract drops it in ValueParts); pinned by ContractTest and the CardDemo snapshot's expected changes.
close_reason: Fixed by the unit 2 contract (ValueParts drops the period after a symbol).

title: jcl-bridge: DD DATA loses its card images
description: //D DD DATA followed by card images emits no in-stream lines (in_stream: []), so the model gets no data and DD DATA reads as an empty DD. DD * keeps its cards. Found while planning the object-model acceptance suite (2026-10-10); pinned by jackal/tests/acceptance/test_dsn.py::test_dsn_kinds_parse. Fix in jackal/jcl-bridge with a Java test.
close_reason: Bridge half fixed by the unit 2 contract (ContractTest). The model half lands in units 3-4 (2cy.9, 2cy.10), pinned by the acceptance suite.

title: jcl-bridge: PARM.procstep= with an empty value is a grammar error
description: //S6 EXEC TWO,PARM.P1='' (and PARM.P1= with nothing after it) is a grammar error, so the whole job is lost. The JCL Reference uses an empty value to nullify a parameter on a PROC step (blueprint 4.6). Found by the object-model acceptance review (2026-10-10); pinned by jackal/tests/acceptance/test_overrides.py. Fix in jackal/jcl-bridge with a Java test.
close_reason: Fixed in the jcl-bridge lexer/grammar (object-model unit 2, task 1); pinned by ParseFixesTest.

title: jcl-bridge rejects a JOB card whose only positional is a quoted string followed by a continuation
close_reason: Fixed in the jcl-bridge lexer/grammar (object-model unit 2, task 1); pinned by ParseFixesTest.

title: cicada: a CICS spec built without the region's transaction map rejects every START
description:
`build_cics_spec` and `CicsLoweringStrategy` default `transid_to_program` to an empty mapping. Every compiled program's `EXEC CICS START` builtin resolves transactions against the mapping it got at compile time, so a caller that forgets it gets a region whose every START is rejected with UNKNOWN_TRANSID, whatever its configuration says. The TN3270 region did exactly that until fb3826b passed `config.transactions`.

This is the same trap `program_cache` was (red-dragon-forge-q6d): an optional argument whose default silently disables a verb. The TN3270 fix has no test; the region needs BMS maps and an HLASM export to build, so the cheaper guard is to require the mapping, as `program_cache` now is.
close_reason: build_cics_spec and CicsLoweringStrategy require transid_to_program (named, never positional) and the empty default is gone; forgetting it is a TypeError naming it, pinned with program_cache by one test. The TN3270 region passes config.transactions (fb3826b).

title: docs: cicada roadmap links an analysis record that is not in the repository
description: Commit 3ce3c25 adds four rows to `docs/roadmaps/cicada.md` that link `records/analysis/2026-10-09-tn3270-link-cache-runtime-gaps.md`, and two say "repro in the same doc". The file is not in the repository, so the links are dead and the repros are lost. The rows need to stand without it; the repros need recording again if they still matter.
notes: The roadmap rows no longer link the missing record (a0ea45b). Still open: the two repros (OCCURS sibling-group names, a non-UTF-8 byte in source) were never recorded and need writing down again.

title: diagnose-cobol does not refuse an absent copybook_dirs entry; every member reports a NullPointerException
description: cobble-parse-corpus and cobble-expand-corpus refuse to start when a copybook_dirs entry is not an existing directory (cobble/parsing/copybook_dir.py). diagnose-cobol has no such guard. Reproduced on CardDemo: running it before cobble-sym (sym dir absent) reports nearly every member under one signature, java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read the array length because ? is null, instead of naming the missing directory. Fix: call the same unscannable() check before submitting jobs.

title: cobble: bridge subprocesses run without a timeout, so a hanging member stalls a corpus run silently
description: cobble-parse-corpus, cobble-expand-corpus, diagnose-cobol, diagnose-jcl and cobble-build start the ProLeap and JCL bridges as subprocesses with no timeout (cobol_asg.subprocess_runner, the JCL bridge runner). A member the bridge never returns from makes the run look stuck with no diagnostic. A timeout must be a reported skip (recorded like a .fail), not a silent one. Carried over from the retired cobble onboarding tracker.

title: Restore the partial-overwrite split without unbounded keys
description:
The partial-overwrite split (090794d), and the canonical join built on it, are reverted. Splitting an entry into arbitrary remainder spans let the set of keys grow with the square of the write boundaries. Joins kept every path's different cuts, so on large programs the fixpoint stopped settling and memory grew until the run ran out.

Without the split, an exact write into part of an exact entry keeps the whole entry's old writers. A sub-field overwritten after a whole-record copy still reports the copy as a writer, and the cross-program combine reports more spurious candidates. `test_a_sub_field_overwritten_after_a_record_copy_forgets_the_copy` in `cobble/tests/dataflow/fixpoint/test_jumps_synthetic.py` is marked xfail for this.

Tried and rejected: cutting remainders at fixed atoms, which were the start and end offsets of every write target. That settled, but each remainder became many keys. On the 6,931-line fixture (SYNPERFC) it peaked at 4.4 GB, against 2.6 GB with the split and 2.1 GB reverted. The patch is not kept in the repo.

Next attempt: a coalesced canonical form. After each write and join, merge adjacent same-name pieces with identical writer sets, so every path gets the same keys without the atoms' fan-out. It must beat the recorded rows in `cobble/tests/dataflow/fixpoint/test_fixpoint_cost_synthetic.py` (steps, settling, keys, peak RSS) and make the xfail test pass.
close_reason: Restored with a coalesced canonical join: one field's exact pieces are cut at every boundary and adjacent pieces with equal sources merged. Settles all three cost fixtures; on SYNPERFC peaks at 2.63 GB (split 2.62, reverted 2.09) in 125 s (split 285 s). The extra memory is real per-byte writer differences, accepted for the precision.

title: Cicada: a BMS DRK field (Update User password) is shown in clear on a 3270
description:
On CardDemo's Update User screen (COUSR02C, map COUSR2A), served over TN3270 to c3270, the password field shows its value in clear. The BMS map declares that field `ATTRB=(…,DRK)`: dark, not displayed.

Seen in the recorded c3270 session (`docs/presentation/artifacts/cics/carddemo-3270.mp4`, around 1:48-2:00). It was not root-caused.

Expected: a field with DRK (non-display) intensity is sent with the non-display attribute in its field attribute byte, so the terminal does not show it, whatever its contents.

Check that the BMS attribute → 3270 field-attribute mapping (cicada BMS / tn3270 encoder) covers DRK, and that a program's attribute override does not clear it.

title: Cobble: CICS RIDFLD operands are not recorded as reads (fixpoint and fields-access)
description:
The RIDFLD key of an `EXEC CICS READ` (and presumably of READNEXT, READPREV, STARTBR, REWRITE and DELETE, which take a RIDFLD too) is not recorded as a read of that field. This applies to the dataflow fixpoint and to `cobble-fields-access`.

Found while building the deck's byte-level query slide. In CardDemo COACTVWC, line 778 reads the account file with `RIDFLD (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X)`. Neither `cobble-dataflow-fixpoint-query readers` nor `cobble-access-query` lists that statement as a reader of those bytes. The record's key is exactly the value a reader of this program wants traced.

Expected: the RIDFLD operand of every CICS file command is a read of its extent, at that node.

Check that `fields/transfer.py`'s CICS handling covers RIDFLD for every file verb, and that `cobble-fields-access` collects it.

title: Fixpoint lets a PERFORMed paragraph fall through into the next, so pre-PERFORM writes do not dominate
description:
The dataflow fixpoint does not track PERFORM context, so the end of a paragraph that is only ever PERFORMed falls through into the next paragraph in its model. At runtime such a paragraph returns to its performer and never falls through.

Effect: a write that every real path makes before `PERFORM X` does not dominate X in the fixpoint, because the fall-through path from the preceding paragraph reaches X without it. The fact at a jump inside X keeps the earlier writer and its reason (typically `inbound-linkage`).

Observed on CardDemo after the cross-program combine landed. Seven return-to-previous-screen sites gain their own program name as an XCTL candidate: COADM01C, COMEN01C, COTRN00C, COTRN01C, COUSR00C, COUSR02C, COUSR03C.

Example, COTRN00C:
- Every PERFORM of RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN is preceded by a MOVE to CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM (lines 108 and 123).
- RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN (line 510) sits directly after INITIALIZE-TRAN-DATA, which is only PERFORMed.
- The fact at the XCTL lists the whole-commarea copy (line 111) as a writer, together with `inbound-linkage`.
- The combine's value-restricted edges then pin the inbound CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM to the name each caller used to reach the program, which is the program itself.

These seven self-XCTL_CANDIDATE edges are in reference/graph.jsonl (448/843) and are documented in cobble/README.md.

Fix direction: respect PERFORM return context at paragraph ends in the fixpoint walk, as srccfg's reaching_conditions already does with its frame stack. Measure fixpoint runtime, since the walk is per program.

The diagnosis is from reading the source and the fact's writers. The fall-through edge in the fixpoint CFG has not been confirmed directly; confirm it first.
notes: Correction to the close reason: inbound-linkage is gone at all 11 changed XCTL sites, not 10.
close_reason: Fixpoint prunes FALLTHRU edges only a returning PERFORM reaches (cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/fallthrough.py). CardDemo: 392 of 541 fall-throughs pruned; 11 XCTL sites lose doubt reasons (inbound-linkage gone at 10), candidates unchanged; 7 self-XCTL_CANDIDATE edges gone, reference graph 448/843 -> 448/836; fixpoint 10.7s -> 9.5s.

title: aliases.jsonl omits jumps to targets the single-program fixpoint already resolved
description:
aliases.jsonl lines up a caller's passed bytes with the callee's only for jumps whose target is written literally. fields/aliases.py refuses every site whose PROGRAM operand is a field (reason "dynamic-target"), even when the single-program fixpoint resolved that field completely in the same run.

Measured on CardDemo (demo pipeline, 2026-10-05): all 24 dynamic XCTL sites are dynamic-target rows; 20 of them are fully resolved in targets.jsonl, e.g. COMEN01C's menu XCTL to 11 programs and COADM01C's to 6. So cobble-dataflow-fixpoint-query --across-calls, the table's one downstream reader, cannot follow those jumps, though nothing about them needs cross-program analysis.

Fix: in the fixpoint run, after a member's targets are resolved, emit an aliases row per (site, candidate) for every resolved dynamic site, lined up exactly as a literal jump is (same window and rebase rules; returns as for the transfer). Keep a site's dynamic-target dead-end row only when it has no candidates; mark incomplete sites so a consumer can tell "these candidates and maybe more" (the targets row's reasons) from a literal edge.

Independent of the cross-program combine design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-cross-program-dataflow-combine-design.md, red-dragon-forge-hab): this makes the no-combine pipeline cover everything knowable without looking across programs.

title: Fixpoint does not carry caller-supplied COMMAREA values into dynamic XCTL targets (return-to-caller sites miss targets)
description:
The dataflow fixpoint resolves a dynamic XCTL/LINK/CALL target only from values the calling program itself assigns. A value that arrives in the COMMAREA from the program that transferred in is not followed (targets.jsonl flags such sites with reasons "inbound-linkage" / "unmodelled"), so "return to whoever called me" sites miss real targets.

Verified on CardDemo (demo pipeline, 2026-10-05): 24 dynamic sites, all EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM(<var>); no dynamic CALL or LINK. The knowledge graph mirrors targets.jsonl exactly (48 candidate pairs + 2 literal XCTLs), and the menu-table sites (COMEN02Y, 11 programs; COADM02Y, 6) are exact. 20/24 sites are complete; 4 each miss one real target:

| Site | Candidates | Missing | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| COCRDSLC:331 | COMEN01C | COCRDLIC | COCRDLIC stamps LIT-THISPGM into CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM (521) then XCTLs to COCRDSLC (538); COCRDSLC PF3 does MOVE CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM TO CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM (320) |
| COCRDUPC:473 | COMEN01C | COCRDLIC | same, COCRDLIC 549 -> 566; COCRDUPC 453 |
| COUSR02C:258 | COADM01C, COSGN00C | COUSR00C | COUSR00C stamps WS-PGMNAME ('COUSR00C') at 194 then XCTLs at 196; COUSR02C PF3 113-117 |
| COUSR03C:205 | COADM01C, COSGN00C | COUSR00C | same, COUSR00C 204 -> 206 |

COACTUPC/COACTVWC are complete only by coincidence (their sole caller is the menu, which their LIT-MENUPGM default covers); COTRN01C only because it also holds a literal 'COTRN00C'. The checked-in reference/graph.jsonl has the same gap (the demo graph matched it, 448/832), so cobble-compare cannot catch it.

Constraint for the fix: do not analyse a whole-program supergraph. The value has to cross programs as a per-program summary (a transfer function over the COMMAREA) composed along transfer edges, so each program is still analysed once. Design to be brainstormed before implementation.
close_reason: Fixed by cobble-dataflow-combine (cross-program linking over per-program fixpoint results). On CardDemo all four missing targets are found: COCRDSLC and COCRDUPC gain COCRDLIC, COUSR02C and COUSR03C gain COUSR00C. reference/graph.jsonl regenerated to 448/843. Seven self-XCTL candidates remain from fixpoint PERFORM fall-through, filed as red-dragon-forge-x5m.

title: EIBRESP2 is always 0: set documented RESP2 values per command and condition
description:
EIBRESP2 is always 0: builtins/system.py writes EIBRESP2 as a packed zero, and no verb sets it.

Reach (census): EIBRESP2 referenced 9,543 times in 708 programs, mostly to tell VSAM sub-conditions apart (e.g. which kind of INVREQ, NOTFND or LENGERR). The RESP2 option itself is almost unused (17 programs), so programs read the EIB field directly.

Work: set EIBRESP2 alongside EIBRESP for every condition the runtime produces, using IBM's documented RESP2 values per command (file control first: READ, READNEXT/READPREV, STARTBR, WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE, then RETRIEVE, LINK, START, TS). Reset it to 0 on NORMAL. One table, next to the EIBRESP mapping; not a second table (see forge-rkh).

The values must come from the CICS Application Programming Reference, per command and condition, not be guessed. Research before implementing.

title: Region models one terminal: START TERMID to any other terminal is rejected (structural)
description:
A cicada region models exactly one terminal. builtins/interval.py rejects any START whose TERMID is not the region's own (RejectReason.NO_SUCH_TERMINAL), and the dispatcher runs started tasks only for that terminal.

Reach (census): START in 1,017 programs, 99.8% with TERMID, used as an immediate hop that starts a transaction on a named terminal (another display or a printer), with the payload read back by RETRIEVE (922 programs). Unless TERMID is the issuing terminal, every such START is refused today.

Why structural: the terminal is folded into the region instead of being a resource the region owns. A real region owns many terminals; each has a queue of pending STARTs and an attached task at a time; printers take output, not input. SEND TEXT ... PRINT (85% of SEND TEXT), ROUTE LIST, SEND PAGE, and INQUIRE/SET TERMINAL UCTRANST all address terminals other than the current one, and TS queue names commonly embed EIBTRMID.

Target (to settle at brainstorm): a terminal table in the region (termid -> kind (display | printer), screen/output channel, pending START queue); START queues on the named terminal; the dispatcher drives tasks per terminal; output to a printer terminal is captured, not displayed. Related: forge-95b (dispatcher and CicsRegion disagree about which terminal a next-transid task gets).

title: Alternate-index paths: no DUPKEY, read-only linear scan (structural, shared model with jackal-1o2.22)
description:
cicada has no real alternate-index path. VsamEngine routes a file with a non-zero key offset to `open_alternate_key_driver`: a linear scan, read-only. It never reports DUPKEY, and REWRITE/DELETE through a path cannot work.

Reach (census): DFHRESP(DUPKEY) compared 3,017 times in 1,044 programs; IGNORE CONDITION DUPKEY 163 mentions (103 programs); HANDLE CONDITION DUPKEY 14 programs. DUPKEY is only raised by reading a non-unique alternate key, so this volume implies files read through AIX paths are common in the estate. CardDemo has one (CXACAIX, see forge-1zu.10).

CICS semantics needed: READ via a path returns the first record with that alternate key plus DUPKEY if more exist; READNEXT through duplicates returns DUPKEY on every record except the last of the group; the base cluster is the store and the path is a view; upgrade-set AIXs are maintained when the base is written. EIBRESP2 distinguishes some of these cases (see the EIBRESP2 issue).

Shared model: jackal-1o2.22 (VSAM AIX in batch: DEFINE AIX, BLDINDEX, PATH) needs the same base + AIX + path structure. Design both against one model in red-dragon's access-method layer or a shared forge component; cicada must not import jackal (.importlinter), and vendor/red-dragon changes go upstream.

title: cobble CICS graph: TS queues as nodes with program read/write/delete edges
description:
cobble's CICS flow graph has no TS queues, so data shared between programs through temporary storage is invisible.

Reach: WRITEQ TS 88, READQ TS 97, DELETEQ TS 136 statements across ~66 programs in the census. ITEM/NUMITEMS on most reads (indexed item access); MAIN storage on 64% of writes. TS queues carry pseudo-conversational scratch state between transactions of one terminal and between cooperating programs. No TD queues anywhere in the census.

Work: a TS_QUEUE node kind; PROGRAM -WRITES/READS/DELETES-> TS_QUEUE edges from cobble/cics/verb_source_asg.py, alongside the file verbs. Queue names are often built at run time (a prefix plus EIBTRMID is a common idiom), so a non-literal QUEUE operand is carried unresolved for the dataflow pass, as PROGRAM operands of LINK/XCTL already are (`program_operand`); never invent a node from a data-name.

title: COBOL step compiles like cicada: compile_program with injected CoprocessorSpecs + source_search_dirs (CALL closure, EXEC SQL, LE stubs)
description:
A COBOL step runs one compilation unit. A batch program that CALLs another program (date routines, shared validation modules, common in production batch) cannot resolve the callee, a program with EXEC SQL cannot compile, and LE callable services have no stubs.

Today: jackal/cobol_step.py runs either run(source, ...) or compile_cobol(source, parser=..., copybook_dirs=...). Neither passes source_search_dirs, and neither sees a CoprocessorSpec. So the step is not what z/OS runs: a load module, i.e. the main program plus everything it statically or dynamically CALLs, with its coprocessors.

Do what cicada does (cicada/cics/tn3270/region.py, _compile_one): compile every COBOL step through red-dragon's interpreter.project.coprocessor_compile.compile_program(source, parser, specs, source_search_dirs=<source dirs>). compile_program folds each spec's own source_search_dirs in (cicada's spec contributes its LE stubs dir) and links the CALL closure via compile_cobol.

- One compile path for every COBOL step; today the with-PARM and without-PARM paths differ. PARM stays an initial-VM concern (run_linked with the PARM frame).
- The specs are injected into JobRunner at construction, never imported by jackal. Standalone jackal passes none; red_dragon_forge composes squall's spec (and any LE stubs it needs) and passes them in. jackal must not import squall or cicada (.importlinter).
- The source directories passed as source_search_dirs are the runner's COBOL source dirs.
- Do not pass ast_cache_dir alongside source_search_dirs: vendor/red-dragon/interpreter/project/cobol_compile.py:137 documents that the combination silently drops disk-resolved callees.

Tests first:
1. A two-program fixture where the main program CALLs a subprogram that writes to a DD; assert the DD's exact records.
2. Static (CALL 'LIT') and dynamic (CALL identifier) forms. Not yet checked how red-dragon resolves a dynamic target from the search dirs.
3. An injected spec reaches compile_program: a forge-level test that a batch step with EXEC SQL compiles and runs with squall's spec composed in.

Component [10] in docs/records/design/2026-10-05-jcl-to-be-architecture.md.
close_reason: Every COBOL step compiles through compile_program with injected CoprocessorSpecs (JobRunner coprocessors=) and the runner's source dir as search path; callees' FILE-CONTROL resolved to DDs. Static CALL works; dynamic CALL is red-dragon-forge-ua7. Forge test runs an EXEC SQL batch step with squall's spec.

title: Datasets own their record attributes (RECFM/LRECL/DSORG) + a record codec that can frame variable records
description:
A dataset has no record format of its own; whoever opens it decides the record boundaries.

Today:
- red-dragon's SequentialDriver stores a flat file as concatenated fixed-length records, with record_length passed by the opener. COBOL takes it from the program's FD.
- catalog.Dataset carries org/key/record_size, but only IDCAMS DEFINE CLUSTER sets them; a PS dataset allocated from a DD has record_size=0.
- The jackal-ifq workaround (`record_size` override on catalog.open_dataset, used by IDCAMS REPRO to borrow the output KSDS length) is this defect already visible.

Breaks:
- RECFM=V/VB cannot be represented: with no RDW or other framing on disk, record boundaries are lost.
- SORT, IEBGENER and REPRO have no program FD; they must read LRECL/RECFM from the dataset (jackal-1o2.3).
- DCB=*.ddname and DCB=(model-dsn,...) inheritance (>=25% of jobs in a production census) has nothing to inherit from (jackal-1o2.12).
- The z/OS DCB merge (program DCB, then DD DCB, then dataset label; the first non-zero wins) has no dataset label to merge with.

Target (to settle at brainstorm): a Dataset owns its attributes (DSORG, RECFM, LRECL, BLKSIZE; key extent for KSDS), set once at creation from the merged DD DCB, the IDCAMS DEFINE, a model dataset, or the first OPEN OUTPUT's FD; seeded datasets declare theirs. A record codec between drivers and storage frames records per RECFM: fixed = raw concatenation, as today; variable = RDW-prefixed. Open decision: whether the codec lives in jackal (wrapping drivers) or upstream in red-dragon's drivers; the latter needs an upstream change, since vendor/red-dragon is never modified here.

Reframes jackal-1o2.12 from "honor DCB attributes" to "datasets own attributes"; prerequisite for SORT/IEBGENER (jackal-1o2.3); retires jackal-ifq.

See docs/design/2026-10-05-jcl-to-be-architecture.md.
notes:
Decisions 2026-10-11 (brainstorm with the user):
1. Variable records (RECFM=V/VB) are stored with inline 4-byte RDWs, as z/OS does; no BDWs (blocking not modelled, like BLKSIZE).
2. The record codec lives in jackal, behind its I/O provider (AllocatedFileIOProvider) and catalog.open_dataset: a variable-record sequential driver implementing red-dragon's driver interface, chosen from the dataset's RECFM. red-dragon owns RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON semantics (filed upstream); until then a COBOL WRITE to a V dataset frames records at the full record-area length.
3. No Forge runtime accepts an unlabelled dataset. Every dataset brought in carries RECFM/LRECL/DSORG (key extent for KSDS), built by some step (declaration or inference); never guessed from the first opener.
4. A dataset a job creates (NEW, no DCB=) gets its label at its first OPEN OUTPUT by the z/OS DCB merge (program FD, then DD DCB=). Opening it before then with nothing to merge from abends S013.
5. Labels are held by the catalog (the VTOC's role), not in sidecar files and not in a separate manifest. Bringing data in is an operation on the persistent system catalog (red-dragon-forge-93f), so 93f comes first; --data-dir and --dataset are retired in favour of it.
Upstream: red-dragon-1hc3 (RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON passes the record's true length to and from the I/O provider).
Decisions and IBM sources: docs/records/design/2026-10-11-jackal-dataset-decisions.md (D3-D7).
Step 2a done in the working tree (COBOL OPEN: format from the FD, pending label written on OUTPUT/EXTEND, conflicts fail with file status 39); decisions and IBM sources: docs/records/design/2026-10-11-jackal-cobol-open-record-format.md. Upstream: red-dragon-03sk (FD clauses in the ASG), red-dragon-p98c (status 39), to_ioresult public (0beec981). Left: 2b utilities read labels (REPRO; retires jackal-ifq), after researching IDCAMS's behaviour on an unlabelled input; 3 the RDW codec.
close_reason: Done: labels from FD at OPEN (status 39), REPRO at each side's label, RECFM=V/VB stored behind RDWs with REWRITE length rule (status 44). Records: 2026-10-11-jackal-cobol-open-record-format, 2026-10-12-jackal-idcams-repro-labels, 2026-10-12-jackal-variable-records. Open follow-ups: red-dragon-forge-14l, red-dragon-1hc3.

title: Split the catalog: persistent SystemCatalog + per-job dataset context (temps, PASS, referbacks, GDG bindings)
description:
One job-scoped DatasetCatalog stands in for three different z/OS levels: the persistent system catalog, the job's own dataset context (temps, passed datasets, referbacks, GDG bindings), and the step's allocations.

Today (jackal/catalog.py, runner.py):
- The catalog is created per JobRunner.run and dies with the job. run_job accepts a pre-built catalog, but nothing models what survives a job.
- Only DispNormal.DELETE acts. PASS, KEEP, CATLG and UNCATLG are the same no-op, so a (NEW,PASS) non-temp dataset that is never received persists, while z/OS deletes it at job end.
- DISP=NEW on an existing name silently truncates it (path.write_bytes(b"")). z/OS fails the allocation (duplicate name / NOT CATLGD).
- Temps live in the same namespace as real DSNs: &&EXTR is stored as DSN "EXTR", and _record_dds turns a temp referback into DirectDSN("EXTR"). z/OS gives temps system-generated unique names.
- Referback resolution state (resolved_dds) lives in the runner, apart from the rest of the job's dataset state.

Breaks:
- GDG (jackal-1o2.4; >=25% of production-census jobs): relative generations are resolved per job against a catalog that persists across jobs, (+1) means the same generation in every step of one job, and new generations are cataloged at step end and rolled against the base's LIMIT. That needs both a system level and a job level.
- Multi-job pipelines (job A catalogs, job B reads) and cross-job lineage in execution.
- IDCAMS DEFINE/DELETE/LISTCAT act on the system catalog, not on a job.

Target (to settle at brainstorm): a SystemCatalog (DSN -> dataset entry; GDG bases with generation lists; VSAM clusters), injected and shared across jobs in one run; a JobDatasetContext per job (unique temp names, the passed-dataset queue, referback table, GDG relative-to-absolute bindings fixed at first use in the job); step allocations built on both. Dispositions are applied by the step lifecycle against the right level: CATLG/UNCATLG on the system catalog, PASS on the job context, DELETE on both.

Depends on the dataset-attributes issue (catalog entries hold attributes) and the lifecycle issue (disposition is applied by the runner). Blocks jackal-1o2.4.

See docs/design/2026-10-05-jcl-to-be-architecture.md.
notes:
Decided 2026-10-11 (from the 8in brainstorm): 93f now comes before 8in. The system catalog is persistent on disk, the one place a dataset's location and (once 8in lands) its label live, playing z/OS's catalog + VTOC. Bringing data in is an operation on it (e.g. a 'jackal catalog add DSN --file PATH ...' command), run once, replacing --data-dir and --dataset; installing CardDemo becomes a one-time script of such adds. Datasets jobs catalog (NEW,CATLG) persist there for later jobs. A DSN not in the catalog is not found, as on z/OS.
Design approved 2026-10-11:
- System directory (--system DIR), persistent across runs: catalog.json (each cataloged dataset: location + label; parsed to typed models on read) and datasets/ (bytes owned by the system). Runs change it in place, as on a mainframe.
- Bringing data in: `jackal catalog add DSN --file PATH --recfm --lrecl --dsorg [--key-length --key-offset]` copies the bytes in. --data-dir and --dataset are removed; a DSN not in the catalog is not found (or a lenient stand-in).
- Labels (RECFM, LRECL, DSORG, key extent) on every catalog entry from day one; catalog add and IDCAMS DEFINE set them; a job-created dataset (lenient stand-ins included) is cataloged with its label pending, completed at its first OPEN OUTPUT in 8in. I/O does not read labels until 8in.
- SMS dispositions: CATLG and KEEP leave the dataset cataloged; UNCATLG is a no-op; DELETE removes entry and bytes; PASS hands the dataset to later steps, and one created in the job and never received is deleted at job end.
- A lenient stand-in for a missing dataset is cataloged like any created dataset and follows its DISP (user's choice over job-scoped).
- Per-job context (blueprint section 11): temps get unique names TempName(job, alias, seq); in-stream cards and sinks in a per-job scratch directory; all deleted at job end.
- Out of scope: GDG (deferred), volumes.
Commits: (1) catalog/store split + job context: unique temps, PASS, SMS dispositions, in memory; (2) labels on catalog entries; (3) persistence + CLI (system directory, catalog add, run --system, old flags removed); (4) CardDemo install script from its README table, checked against copybook record sizes and file sizes, end-to-end tests on an installed system.
Decisions and IBM sources: docs/records/design/2026-10-11-jackal-dataset-decisions.md (D7-D11). Correction 2026-10-11: PASS stays as built in 1c791a3; the current z/OS 3.1 text replaces PASS with KEEP only for existing VSAM (the OS/390 wording covering all permanent data sets is superseded).
close_reason: Done in four commits: temps' own namespace + PASS (1c791a3); persistent labelled system catalog, catalog add, run --system (e9cb457); omitted-DISP defaults (117f571, via 9po); CardDemo install (make jackal-install). GDG bindings are out of scope here (GDG deferred; jackal-1o2.4). Decisions: docs/records/design/2026-10-11-jackal-dataset-decisions.md.

title: Runner owns the step lifecycle: allocate all DDs -> dispatch -> dispose (in-stream and DUMMY fail today)
description:
Each program kind runs its own step lifecycle. In z/OS the initiator owns it: allocate every DD before the program starts, run the program against those allocations, then apply each DD's normal or abnormal disposition after it ends. Programs never allocate or dispose.

Today:
- run_cobol_step allocates every non-SYSOUT DD (cobol_step._overrides) and disposes after the run.
- utilities.iefbr14 allocates and disposes itself.
- utilities.idcams allocates nothing up front; REPRO allocates its input and `resolve`s its output (idcams/executor._handle_repro); no IDCAMS step ever applies a DISP.
- catalog.allocate matches TempRef and DirectDSN only and raises TypeError for InStreamDSN, DummyDSN and NoDSN. So a COBOL step with `SYSIN DD *` (very common control cards) or `DD DUMMY` should fail with TypeError (from reading the code; not reproduced, so the first task is a failing test).
- STEPLIB/JOBLIB are skipped by a name list in cobol_step (OPTIONAL_DDS), not by what the DD is.

Consequence: every new utility (SORT, IEBGENER, IEBCOPY) re-implements allocation and disposition, and gets DUMMY, in-stream, concatenation and DISP=MOD semantics slightly differently or not at all.

Target (to settle at brainstorm): the runner owns allocate -> dispatch -> dispose. Allocation turns each DD into a typed Allocation (dataset, concatenation, in-stream (materialised as a dataset), dummy (EOF on read, discard on write), sysout). Programs receive a DD environment (ddname -> Allocation) plus PARM and return a StepOutcome. Disposition reads the outcome (normal vs abnormal). The COBOL adapter maps the DD environment onto RealFileIOProvider.path_overrides, which stays as the binding seam.

Depends on the StepOutcome issue (abnormal disposition needs to know the step abended). Unblocks the dispatch issue (red-dragon-forge-xkk), DUMMY (jackal-1o2.14), concatenation (jackal-1o2.5) and every new utility.

See docs/design/2026-10-05-jcl-to-be-architecture.md.
notes: Also in scope for the allocator: DISP=MOD must position at end of file even when the program OPENs OUTPUT (z/OS appends). Today red-dragon's SequentialDriver opens OUTPUT with w+b, so a MOD dataset opened for OUTPUT is truncated. The allocation carries the MOD positioning and the COBOL adapter maps OUTPUT to EXTEND for it.
close_reason: The runner owns allocate -> run -> dispose (jackal.allocation); programs receive a DdEnvironment; DD * and DUMMY work for COBOL; IDCAMS applies DISP; DISP=MOD appends through jackal's COBOL file handler (jackal.cobol_files). Concatenation stays refused (1o2.5); allocation failures as outcomes are 552; abnormal disposition waits for abends (1o2.19).

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: Unit 1 of 2 committed: the runner allocates every DD (jackal.allocation: dataset, DD * as 80-byte EBCDIC cards, DUMMY/SYSOUT sinks; STEPLIB/JOBLIB skipped), programs receive a DdEnvironment, the runner applies normal DISP and releases sinks. IDCAMS now applies DISP. Unit 2: jackal's own CobolIOProvider over the allocations (MOD append, DUMMY discard).

title: Step outcome as a sum type: RC, abend, bypassed, flushed, unsupported (replace int RC + ran flag)
description:
A step's outcome is an int. z/OS step completion is a sum type, and the JCL features still on the roadmap all read the parts jackal cannot represent.

Today (jackal/results.py, runner.py):
- StepResult(name, return_code: int, ran: bool, disposition: EXECUTED|BYPASSED). `ran` and `disposition` overlap, and a bypassed step reports return_code=0, which COND evaluation could mistake for a real RC if a caller ever forgets to filter.
- A program failure inside the VM (or any utility) is a Python exception. It escapes JobRunner.run_job; the `finally` cleans temps and the caller gets no JobResult at all, so nothing records which steps ran.
- JobResult has no job-level outcome (max RC, abended step, flushed steps).

What z/OS distinguishes: completed with RC n; system abend Sxxx; user abend Uxxx (COBOL ILBOABN0/CEE3ABD, LE abends); not run, because bypassed by COND/IF, flushed after an earlier abend, or never started because of a JCL error.

Why it matters now:
- COND= semantics after an abend: every later step is flushed unless it says COND=EVEN/ONLY (jackal-1o2.8).
- IF (S.ABEND), IF (S.RUN), ABENDCC= tests (jackal-1o2.8).
- Abnormal disposition: the third DISP subparameter, e.g. (NEW,PASS,DELETE), seen in a production census, applies only on abend (jackal-1o2.19, and the lifecycle issue).
- The dispatch issue (red-dragon-forge-xkk) needs an "unsupported program" outcome that is neither an RC nor an exception.
- results.py is 24 lines and few callers read return_code. Cheap now; every new utility and test that reads `.return_code` raises the cost.

Shape (to settle at brainstorm): a StepOutcome sum type (Completed(rc) | Abended(code) | Bypassed(reason) | Flushed | Unsupported(program)) on StepResult, replacing ran/disposition/return_code. A VM failure is mapped to Abended at the program adapter boundary, not caught generically in the runner. JobResult gains the job outcome derived from step outcomes. cond.should_bypass reads only Completed outcomes.

See docs/design/2026-10-05-jcl-to-be-architecture.md.
close_reason: StepResult carries a StepOutcome; JobResult.outcome derives JobCompleted; cond.gate returns Run | Bypassed | Flushed.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: Scope added 2026-10-11: steps after a JOB COND test is met are Flushed(AfterJobCond(step)), not Bypassed. The runner already produces this case (end_job_tests in should_bypass) and labels it bypassed. Blueprint §6 table, gate rule 3.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: Done with option A: only the outcomes produced now (Completed, Bypassed, Flushed(AfterJobCond), SkippedUnresolved, JobCompleted). Interim Bypassed(REFERENCED_STEP_NOT_RUN) until 552. Abended/Halted/AllocationFailed arrive with 1o2.19, xkk/w0e, 552/8u3.

title: IDCAMS: wire the comprehensive parser; execute VERIFY/VFY and IF/THEN/DO/END (>=24% of jobs gate on VFY)
description:
Make the IDCAMS step execute the verbs a production corpus actually uses, starting with VERIFY.

Reach (census): IDCAMS is the most common utility, on >=64% of jobs. `VFY FILE(dd)` appears on >=24% of jobs, almost always as the first step, with every later step gated on it by COND=(0,NE). A job whose first step fails therefore runs nothing. The AMS retry idiom `VFY FILE(x) / IF LASTCC=12 THEN DO / SET MAXCC=0 / VFY FILE(x) / END` also occurs. REPRO INFILE/OUTFILE [REPLACE] with a DUMMY input is the "empty a dataset" idiom. DEFINE CLUSTER / DELETE ... CLUSTER PURGE pairs are common.

Today:
- `VFY` (the documented abbreviation) is in neither grammar. `VERIFY` exists only in the comprehensive grammar (idcams/grammar/ams.lark:1081).
- jackal/utilities.py still calls the narrow `parse_idcams`. The comprehensive parser (parser_comprehensive.py) is not wired in (open item (a) of jackal-1o2.6), and it has 342 pyright errors (red-dragon-forge-rqw).
- `IF ... THEN DO ... END` blocks: check whether the comprehensive modal grammar (ast_modal.py) accepts DO/END; the narrow one handles only IF LASTCC/MAXCC with a single SET.

Work:
1. Wire the comprehensive parser into the IDCAMS utility. This needs red-dragon-forge-rqw cleared first, or at least for the paths the executor touches.
2. Accept VFY as an alias of VERIFY in the grammar.
3. Execute VERIFY as a successful no-op (RC 0) against a dataset that exists in the catalog, and RC 12 when it does not. That RC is what drives the LASTCC=12 retry idiom.
4. Execute IF/THEN/DO/END blocks.
5. REPRO from a DUMMY input truncates the output. Needs jackal-1o2.14.

1o2.6's earlier note "do not implement VERIFY speculatively" was based on CardDemo usage. The census reverses it for production corpora.
notes:
2026-10-12 user decision (B): VERIFY/VFY and IF-THEN-DO-END go into the typed narrow grammar (jackal/idcams/grammar.lark) the executor already uses. Work item 1 (wire parser_comprehensive) moved to red-dragon-forge-tsw; rqw no longer blocks this issue. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-gdg.md G1.
2026-10-12: items 2-4 done (VERIFY/VFY, IF-THEN-ELSE/DO-END/null/nested, SET LASTCC, CANCEL; record 2026-10-12-jackal-idcams-modal.md). Item 5 (REPRO from DUMMY) next.
close_reason: VERIFY/VFY, IF-THEN-ELSE/DO-END (null, nested, nearest-THEN ELSE), SET MAXCC|LASTCC, CANCEL, and REPRO with DUMMY input or output, all in the typed IDCAMS grammar (user decision B). Wiring the comprehensive parser moved to red-dragon-forge-tsw. Record: 2026-10-12-jackal-idcams-modal.md.

title: Step dispatch: explicit 'unsupported program' result + stub mechanism for out-of-scope procs
description:
JobRunner._run_step (jackal/jackal/runner.py:129) knows only IEFBR14 and IDCAMS. Every other PGM= is assumed to be COBOL and read as `<source-dir>/<pgm>.cbl`. A SORT, IEBGENER, IKJEFT01, IRXJCL step, or a cataloged proc absent from the corpus (EXEC SAS, EXEC FTP, ...), therefore fails with a FileNotFoundError from deep in the step. That error says nothing about the real cause, and it ends the job.

Reach: in the census corpus a job is runnable only if every step is. Step programs and procs jackal cannot run cover most jobs: SORT >=40%, IEBGENER >=37%, IKJEFT01/DB2 26%, SAS-style macro procs >=27%, FTP >=13%, a message-queue trigger proc >=9%, an operator-broadcast proc 3%, IRXJCL/REXX 4%.

Work:
1. A typed StepResult for "program not supported", naming the program and the step, as a disposition beside BYPASSED. It is not an exception and not a fake RC.
2. Dispatch order: utilities registry -> COBOL source present in the source dir -> unsupported. The source-dir check uses the injected filesystem, not a bare Path.read_text.
3. A stub mechanism for programs that are outside the batch simulator by nature (file transfer, operator messaging, stats packages, message-queue triggers), so a job can run past them.

DECISION NEEDED (the user's, guardrails: no unilateral defaults): what a stubbed step does to the job, i.e. RC 0 and continue, a configurable RC, or stop with "unsupported". It also needs deciding whether the stub list is code or per-corpus config. Do not pick one to unblock this.

Static analysis is unaffected; cobble already reads these as program nodes.
close_reason: Missing program: MissingProgramStrategy. AbendMissingProgram gives Abended(S806) with abnormal disposition (EVEN/ONLY steps still run); StubMissingProgram gives Completed(0) and warns; the CLI stubs. COBOL source found through ProgramSources. D2 decided: no Halted, no stub list.

title: cobble JCL graph: COND= conditions as typed attrs on JOB->STEP edges
description:
`COND=` is parsed into Step.conds (simple and compound forms, with and without a step name) but never reaches cobble's graph. A reader therefore cannot see which steps are gated on earlier return codes, or on what.

Reach: the census found COND= on the large majority of EXEC statements, in effectively every job (the search output saturated before a file count was reached). The typical pattern is `COND=(0,NE)` on every step after a first IDCAMS `VFY` step, so the whole job is gated on that verify. Compound `COND=((4,LT),(8,LT))` also occurs.

Work: put the step's conditions on the JOB -> STEP edge as typed attrs (code, operator, optional step name), following the "opaque discriminant on the edge" precedent the `proc` attr already set. Job-card COND= goes on the job node. No evaluation; this is static display only.

Cheap: the data is already parsed. P2 because it adds understanding without fixing a broken fact, unlike S1-S4.

title: squall: two Db2 sample programs write 2-4 bytes past their WORKING-STORAGE region
description: Measured with temporary instrumentation on red-dragon's region writes (2026-10-04): tests/integration/test_db2_cursor_e2e.py::test_cursor_sqb_runs_against_db2 writes 80 bytes at offset 182 of a 258-byte region (4 past the end); test_db2_static_e2e.py::test_static_sqb_runs_standalone writes 80 bytes at offset 179 of a 257-byte region (2 past). Today the bytearray silently grows; under red-dragon's flat memory the bytes spill into the next segment. Find whether the host-variable binding writes a wider value than the field it targets.

title: cobble-fields-trace: step into a CALL, binding every USING argument
description: aliases.jsonl now binds each CALL USING argument to the callee parameter at its position (7vc), and the fixpoint query crosses those rows. cobble-fields-trace still does not: CALL is not in trace.CROSSING_VERBS, so the site is listed as transfer-not-crossable: CALL and its BY REFERENCE arguments are credited to %CALL:<program>. Two things stand in the way. A trace frame binds one window per site, and a CALL has one per argument. And Frame.returns means control comes back, which the alias row's returns (bytes come back) no longer implies: a BY CONTENT argument's row has returns false, but the CALL still returns.
close_reason: cobble-fields-trace steps into a CALL with one window per argument; only BY REFERENCE windows write back

title: cobble srccfg: lower EXIT PERFORM
description: Once EXIT PERFORM is distinguishable from EXIT (red-dragon-yd1j), desugar must lower it as an exit from the innermost inline PERFORM loop (CYCLE: to its next iteration). Today it is a no-op and the loop's back edge is the only way on.
close_reason: EXIT PERFORM jumps to a landing after its inline PERFORM; CYCLE to one after the body, before the loop's step and test

title: cobble srccfg: paragraph-name dedupe recurses once per paragraph
description: paragraphs._scan_names renames duplicate paragraph names by recursing once per paragraph, so a program with about a thousand paragraphs raises RecursionError while building its CFG -- the same failure fixed for conditions in 8d83896 and for the closure walk in 643e175. Make it iterative (accumulate over the order).
close_reason: Fixed in c50b2f1.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: Correction: the close reason cited c50b2f1 by mistake; the fix is a67a443.

title: cobble fields: numeric VALUE clauses are imaged as alphanumeric
description: PIC 9(4) VALUE 0 enters the initial image as '0   ' (left-justified, space-padded), not '0000'. Numeric display fields are right-justified and zero-filled, so the value set reports bytes the field never holds.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b9d7f5: numeric VALUEs imaged as zoned digits where text is faithful, else not imaged.

title: cobble srccfg: every out-of-line PERFORM keeps a FLOW edge past the performed code
description: _perform_edges reads the PERFORM node's FLOW successor to place the RETURN edge, and the FLOW edge stays in the CFG, so a walk can skip the performed paragraphs entirely though COBOL always runs them. Effects: PERFORM SET-PGM (always MOVE 'PROGB' TO WS-PGM) then CALL WS-PGM reports candidates [PROGA, PROGB] (PROGA being the VALUE), not the proven PROGB; code after a performed paragraph that always STOP RUNs appears reachable. Fix: drop the FLOW edge once the RETURN edges are placed, for every PERFORM whose range resolves.
close_reason: Fixed in e09dabc: PERFORMs that can return have no FLOW past their range; Node.resume carries the continuation.

title: cobble: a member declaring no storage is indistinguishable from one absent from extents.jsonl
description:
The fixpoint target reads layout from extents.jsonl and reports a recorded reason for any selected member the table does not cover. A member that declares no storage at all emits no rows either, so the two cases are indistinguishable: the stage reports 'no rows in extents.jsonl' and exits 3 where the honest answer is 'this member has nothing to lay out'.

Cannot be expressed in the table as it stands -- every row is one declared name, so a member with none has no row to carry the fact. Fixing it needs a new artefact shape: a covered-members manifest, or a row kind the two published consumers (fixpoint/query.py, fields/trace_query.py) would have to learn to skip.

Impact is bounded: such a member contributes no rows either way, so only the exit code and the reason text differ, never the analysis. No CardDemo member is affected. Surfaced by the change that made extents.jsonl the fixpoint's input (7e75874).

title: Unit 2: interprocedural propagation of a program name through the COMMAREA
description:
Unit 1 resolves a dynamic call target inside one member. A program name arriving through a COMMAREA resolves to no value with reason inbound-linkage: state.py:_missing answers that for any read in the LINKAGE region, and on the CardDemo artifact 23 of 29 sites carry it. Those are the sites Unit 1 cannot reach.

Design sketch is in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-cobble-dynamic-call-resolution-design.md section 11. Per-member independence survives: build_corpus._run is a reduce over member paths, and aliases.jsonl already states, per call site and caller window, which bytes a caller and its callee share -- so a callee's entry state can be seeded from the caller's settled state at the site through that table, without a member holding another member's walk.

Keep the artifact indirection: the whole-corpus fixpoint stays a separate stage from cobble-build, so a 448/832 reproducibility claim never depends on an analysis running inside a commit hook.

title: Extend the value analysis to TRANSID/MAP/MAPSET/FILE and retire _resolve_operand
description:
cobble/cics/verb_source_asg.py:_resolve_operand still serves TRANSID, MAP, MAPSET and FILE/DATASET: it looks up the named field's declared VALUE in asg.data_fields (WORKING-STORAGE only, first name match, blind to every later MOVE) and falls back to the operand's own text. Unit 1 replaced it for PROGRAM only, so the same defect ships for the rest -- the fabricated BMS_MAP node CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET.CCARD-NEXT-MAP is still in cobble/reference/nodes.jsonl.

Do it the way PROGRAM was done: carry the operand unresolved on the CicsVerb, resolve it from the settled byte state in the fixpoint's second pass, and emit a candidate or an explicitly-unresolved node rather than a node named after a variable. Then delete _resolve_operand.

The reference graph moves when the fabricated node goes, so regenerate it with the same row-by-row review.

title: Refine a dynamic candidate set by the guards reaching the site
description:
WHEN CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION) = 'COPAUS0C' pins the value exactly at the transfer, but cobble/dataflow/fields/state.py carries no guards by design (Source.node is the CFG node id, which is how a reader recovers them), so the site resolves to every value the table can hold -- 11 candidates on COMEN01C where the guarded path admits one.

The ingredients exist: the srccfg CFG holds the guard on each branch and cobble-srccfg-query already answers guard questions, and each Source names the node that wrote it. A refinement pass over ResolvedTarget could intersect the candidate set with the guards dominating the site, without the lattice itself becoming path-sensitive.

Decide first whether this belongs in the lattice or in a pass over the artifact: the second keeps the fixpoint's cost and termination argument intact.

title: exact_values misses a value read through a name other than the one that declared it
description:
cobble/dataflow/fields/state.py:exact_values is one dict lookup keyed on the whole FieldExtent, so a MOVE whose source is read through a different name than the one carrying the value does not carry it forward: a redefined table read as CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME where the VALUE was declared on the FILLER beneath it misses, and the transfer reports uninitialised rather than the literal.

Deliberate, and documented in the function: values_at's containment scan is O(|state.values|) per call and the MOVE path asks once per source extent on every statement, which made the walk quadratic on a large member. values_at keeps the scan, so the aliasing is resolved at a call site -- where it matters -- and not in a MOVE chain.

To close it, the per-statement path needs an index from byte range to valued extent (bucketed by region and start, as alias_key does for provenance) rather than a linear scan. Measure against the 90s COACTUPC budget in config/carddemo-fields-tests.toml before and after.

title: cobble-expand-corpus: write a corpus's expanded source, one file per member
description:
Cobble can produce an ASG per member and nothing else. There is no way to read
the expanded source -- copybooks inlined, continuations folded, comments
stripped -- which is what the COBOL grammar is actually handed.

That is the artifact you want when a member will NOT parse, which is precisely
the case where no ASG exists to read instead. On one corpus 328 of 3779 members
are in that state.

Add `cobble-expand-corpus`, a stage beside `cobble-parse-corpus`:

    uv run cobble-expand-corpus --config config/<corpus>.toml --out-dir <dir>

Same corpus TOML, same ProcessPoolExecutor with one JVM per member, same
.partial-then-rename write, same <stem>.fail record for a member that will not
expand. It drives the bridge's -expand-only mode (red-dragon-fhj7).

A separate stage rather than a flag on `cobble-parse-corpus`. A flag would be
skipped for every member the ASG cache already holds, so asking a warm corpus
for expanded source would produce an empty directory and exit 0. Keying the
stage's own skip on its own output removes that: a member is done when its
expanded file or its .fail exists.

Decisions taken:

- `--out-dir` on the CLI, not a TOML key. `asg_dir` is in the TOML because the
  parse and the build must agree on it; nothing consumes expanded source, so
  there is nothing to agree with, and `cobble-srccfg-build` already takes
  `--output` for the same reason.
- `<stem>.cbl`, so an expanded member can be fed straight back to the bridge or
  to `diagnose-cobol` with no copybook directories, to isolate a failure.
- latin-1 on write, matching RealSubprocessRunner and the bridge's SOURCE_CHARSET.
  Anything else mangles high bytes in a VALUE literal.
- parse_corpus.py is imported from, never modified: it carries ten standing
  python-fp-lint violations and touching it adopts them.
close_reason: Closed

title: fp-lint: no-list-dict-param-annotation (335) — 305 of them in the same idcams file as red-dragon-forge-rqw
description:
**335 violations** of `no-list-dict-param-annotation` as of 2026-09-26 — **29% of the workspace's 1,171 fp-lint violations, and the largest unowned rule bucket.** No live bead named this rule.

## It is concentrated in one file, and it is the same file as red-dragon-forge-rqw

| File | Violations |
|---|---|
| `jackal/jackal/idcams/parser_comprehensive.py` | **305** |
| `jackal/jackal/idcams/parser.py` | 10 |
| `jackal/jackal/jcl/bridge_parser.py` | 7 |
| `jackal/jackal/runner.py` | 3 |
| `tools/mainframe_inventory.py` | 3 |
| `squall/squall/statements.py` | 2 |
| `squall/squall/parser/parse.py` | 2 |
| `jackal/jackal/idcams/executor.py`, `squall/squall/dclgen.py`, `jackal/jackal/cobol_step.py` | 1 each |

By package: jackal 327, squall 5, tools 3.

`parser_comprehensive.py` also carries the 342 pyright errors in red-dragon-forge-rqw. Together that is **647 findings in one file**, a third of everything the two gates report across the workspace.

## Do this with red-dragon-forge-rqw, not separately

Both findings have the same cause: the file passes untyped `dict`/`list` bags of parsed IDCAMS options around and splats them into typed records. The mechanical fix here (`dict` → `Mapping`, `list` → `Sequence` in **parameter** annotations only, from `collections.abc`) and the fix there (narrow at the parse boundary so constructors receive `Literal`/`bool`) are the same refactor seen from two angles. Doing them as separate passes means rewriting the same signatures twice.

Sequence matters: widening a parameter to `Mapping` makes pyright reject any body that mutates it, which surfaces the genuinely-mutating sites. Those want to return a new value rather than a `dict` annotation restored.

## The 30 outside that file

`parser.py`, `bridge_parser.py`, `runner.py`, `mainframe_inventory.py`, the squall few — plain mechanical widening, independent of the jackal work, and a reasonable warm-up.

## Verification

`uv run --no-sync python -m python_fp_lint check --config fp.json cicada squall jackal red_dragon_forge cobble tools tests` total drops; `uv run --no-sync pyright` does not regress; each touched package's suite stays green. Note fp-lint is path-scoped via `fp.json` — lint the real repo-relative path, never a copy elsewhere, or it reports "No violations found" regardless of content (see red-dragon-forge-mp5's notes).

title: ruff parses jackal as Python 3.11, so PEP 695 type aliases read as invalid-syntax and the rest of the file goes unlinted
description:
fp-lint reports **3 `invalid-syntax` violations** that are not syntax errors:

```
jackal/jackal/dsn.py:54         Cannot use `type` alias statement on Python 3.11 (added in Python 3.12)
jackal/jackal/value_parts.py:23 Cannot use `type` alias statement on Python 3.11 (added in Python 3.12)
jackal/jackal/value_parts.py:24 Cannot use `type` alias statement on Python 3.11 (added in Python 3.12)
```

The code is valid. Ruff is parsing it as Python 3.11.

## Cause

- root `pyproject.toml`: `requires-python = ">=3.11,<4.0"`
- `jackal/pyproject.toml`: `requires-python = ">=3.13"` — and jackal uses PEP 695 `type X = ...`
- the venv is Python 3.14.7
- no `[tool.ruff] target-version` is set anywhere (the `target-version = ["py311"]` at root `pyproject.toml:52` and `["py310"]` at `cicada/pyproject.toml:52` are `[tool.black]`, which takes a list; ruff's is a string)

With no explicit setting, ruff infers its target from the nearest `requires-python` it resolves, and fp-lint invokes it from the repo root — so jackal's own `>=3.13` never applies and valid 3.13 syntax is reported as invalid.

## Why this is worth more than 3 violations

`invalid-syntax` means ruff **stopped parsing that file**. Every other rule in `ruff_select` is silently not being applied to `dsn.py` and `value_parts.py` from the failure point on. The count understates it: this is a hole in the gate, not three nits.

## Fix, and the blast radius to check first

Setting `[tool.ruff] target-version = "py313"` in the root `pyproject.toml` is the one-line fix, but it is not free: `target-version` also drives the `UP` (pyupgrade) rules, which are in `fp.json`'s `ruff_select`. Raising it from py311 to py313 will make `UP` suggest newer idioms repo-wide and may add violations in cicada and squall.

Measure before and after:
```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m python_fp_lint check --config fp.json cicada squall jackal red_dragon_forge cobble tools tests
```
Baseline 2026-09-26: 1,171 violations total, of which UP037 5, UP007 2, UP035 2.

Also settle the inconsistency itself — root says `>=3.11`, jackal says `>=3.13`, the venv is 3.14. If 3.13 is the real floor, the root `requires-python` is the thing that is wrong, and fixing that fixes ruff's inference without pinning `target-version` at all.

title: pyright: cobble test_statement_index — one unnarrowed access on a 33-member statement union, reported 363 times
description:
**363 pyright errors** in `cobble/tests/dataflow/srccfg/test_statement_index.py` as of 2026-09-26 — and they are **roughly 11 real accesses, not 363 defects**.

`red-dragon-forge-kvs` tracks cobble's pyright backlog as a number (436, now measured at 423). This file alone is 363 of it, from one pattern, so the backlog is far smaller than the count suggests. Worth doing first: it moves the whole-package total by 86% for a single narrowing fix.

## Shape

The test reads `.targets` (352 hits) and `.name` (11) off a statement value whose declared type is a union of **33 statement classes** — `ArithmeticStatement`, `IfStatement`, `EvaluateStatement`, `DisplayStatement`, `GotoStatement`, `StopRunStatement`, `GobackStatement`, `ExitProgramStatement`, `PerformStatement`, `WhenStatement`, `WhenOtherStatement`, `ContinueStatement`, and 21 more. Pyright reports one error per union member that lacks the attribute, which is why 11 source lines produce 363 errors.

Affected lines: 44, 45, 56, 82, 83, 98, 99, 115, 116, 142, 143.

## Approach

The union is the right model — most COBOL statements genuinely have no `targets`. The test is asserting about the ones that do, so it should say which:

1. Narrow before access (`match`/`isinstance`, or a helper that returns only statements carrying targets), or
2. If the index under test is *supposed* to expose `targets` uniformly, that belongs on the index's own return type rather than being recovered per test line — check `cobble/cobble/dataflow/srccfg/` for whether the production type should carry it.

Option 2 is the one to check first: if the production code has the same unnarrowed access, this test is reporting a real design gap rather than a test-only annotation problem.

Not `cast`, and not `# type: ignore` — both would hide the same question at 11 sites.

## Verification

`uv run --no-sync pyright` drops by roughly 363; cobble's suite stays green. Re-measure `red-dragon-forge-kvs`'s package total afterwards — it will be near 60, at which point "burn it down or scope a green target" becomes a genuinely small decision.

title: pyright: jackal idcams parser_comprehensive — 342 errors, all object/str into typed record constructors
description:
**342 pyright errors** in `jackal/jackal/idcams/parser_comprehensive.py` as of 2026-09-26, measured after `**/cics_grammar/**` was excluded from `pyrightconfig.json` (before that the real count was buried under 13,712 generated-ANTLR errors).

This is **44% of the whole workspace's 771 real errors, and jackal had no pyright bead at all** — `red-dragon-forge-kvs` covers cobble only.

## Shape: one boundary, not 342 defects

Every one of the 342 lands in a dataclass constructor (`in function "__init__"`), and **338 of them pass `object`** (3 pass `str`, 1 `Unknown | str`). The parser builds an untyped bag of parsed IDCAMS options and splats it into typed records, so each constructor rejects every field it receives.

Construction sites — 26 lines: 120, 499, 644, 653, 666, 675, 694, 731, 735, 749, 752, 755, 764, 771, 935, 986, 1071, 1162, 1219, 1280, 1308, 1337, 1358, 1435, 1496, 1497.

Most-rejected parameters: `file` 12, `owner` 11, `catalog` 10, `name` 9, `exception_exit` 8, `volumes` 8, `erase` 8, `reuse` 8, `model` 7, `share_options` 7, `write_check` 7, `retention` 6.

Two examples:
- `:120` — `str` into `unit: Literal['CYLINDERS', 'KILOBYTES', 'MEGABYTES', 'RECORDS', ...]`
- `:499` — `object` into `authorization: Literal['MODULE', 'STRING'] | None`, and `object` into `bwo: bool`

## Approach

Fix the boundary, not the 26 call sites. The parser knows which option it just parsed; that is where the `str` becomes a `Literal` or a `bool`. Options in rough order:

1. A typed extraction helper per value kind — `_literal(key, allowed)`, `_flag(key)`, `_int(key)` — that validates and narrows once, so constructors receive already-correct types. This also turns "IDCAMS gave us a keyword we don't model" into a real diagnostic instead of a silently-wrong record, which is the same class of bug as red-dragon-forge-5qt (over-length symbolic VOLUMES silently splitting).
2. `TypedDict` for the parsed-options bag, so the splat itself type-checks.

Do **not** reach for `cast` per site: 342 casts would preserve exactly the runtime looseness that the `Literal` annotations exist to rule out.

## Verification

`uv run --no-sync pyright` total strictly decreases; jackal's suite stays green (`. ./bridge-env.sh` then `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest` from `jackal/`). Because the pre-commit pyright hook is blocking and `files:`-scoped to staged files, fixing this also unblocks any future commit that touches this file.
close_reason: parser_comprehensive.py and the ast_*.py modules are replaced by the lean typed transformer in jackal.idcams.parser (record 2026-10-12-jackal-idcams-one-grammar O5, O7); jackal is at zero Pyright errors.

title: CicsOperand annotates its slice bounds ExprNode; the visitor builds RefModExpr
description:
cics/cics_visitor.py's CicsOperand declares:

    ref_mod_start: ExprNode | None
    ref_mod_length: ExprNode | None

but _build_refmod_side returns RefModLiteral/RefModReference -- RefModExpr, a
disjoint union -- and cics/strategy.py (_ref_mod_length, _copy_in_window) matches
on RefModExpr types. The values are RefModExpr; only the annotation says otherwise.

Nothing noticed until ExecCicsStatement.to_dict started serializing them
(forge-zgn): expr_to_dict raised 'Unknown expression node type: RefModLiteral'.
statements.py now carries the bounds across that seam with dataclasses.replace,
which typechecks because replace takes Any -- see _with_bounds there.

The one-line fix is to annotate them RefModExpr. It is held back because editing
cics_visitor.py stages it, and the file carries five unrelated pre-existing pyright
errors that the pre-commit hook would then block on: TerminalNode.getText at :392
and four dynamic lexer-mode attribute assignments at :490-493 (CICSzLexer does not
declare pliCode/classicCOBOLCode/freeFormCOBOLCode/cCode; the @lexer::members block
generates them as locals). Those five have to be answered in the same change.
close_reason: CicsOperand's slice bounds now annotate RefModExpr, matching what cics_visitor._build_refmod_side actually builds and what cics/strategy.py matches on. Two of the file's seven pyright errors WERE this bug (:433, the RefModExpr-to-ExprNode mismatch) and cleared with the annotation. The five pre-existing ones are answered rather than suppressed blindly: TerminalNode.getText exists at runtime and antlr4's stub omits it; the four lexer-mode flags are generated by the grammar's @lexer::members block, so they exist on the instance but not the class pyright sees. Each carries a comment saying so. cics_visitor.py 7 errors -> 0. statements.py's _with_bounds workaround is deleted -- it existed only to cross the annotation seam with dataclasses.replace, and both shapes now agree, so operand_reference and operand_from_dict construct the bounds directly. cicada 582 passed, cobble 1342 passed.

title: cobble: seed constants from VALUE clauses to resolve dynamic transfer targets
description:
Resolves 59 of 88 (67%) of every dynamic transfer site measurable across CardDemo and
bank-of-z, needs neither the fixpoint nor the CFG walk, and is days of work.

The rule, whole-program: a field with a VALUE clause that no statement in the program
ever writes always holds that literal.

Why the reaching-definitions lattice cannot do this. ReachingDef.definers is "which
STATEMENTS could have written extent". A VALUE clause is a declaration, not a statement,
so for `01 WS-ABEND-PGM PIC X(8) VALUE 'ABNDPROC'` with no MOVE anywhere, definers is
legitimately empty and the read looks uninitialised. The data is present in the ASG --
CobolField carries `value` and `value_is_figurative` -- the analysis simply does not
consider it.

Evidence (constprop spike, 2026-09-22, branch spike/const-prop-call-targets, commit
3259723b):
  - all 58 bank-of-z sites are EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM(WS-ABEND-PGM) against
    WS-ABEND-PGM PIC X(8) VALUE 'ABNDPROC'
  - zero writers in all 18 members that declare it, verified by sweeping every handled
    statement's write_operands for a may_alias against its extent
  - plus CardDemo's LIT-MENUPGM site = 59 of 88
  - all 11 distinct literals recovered name real members; zero phantom resolutions

Deliberately NOT a seeded fixpoint, though that is the textbook move. "Never written
anywhere in the program" is a whole-program fact, so a flat sweep is sound at the 14
sites the CFG walk never reached -- which a seeded fixpoint would still miss.

State the padding rule explicitly rather than discovering it: MOVE 'PGMA' to PIC X(8)
stores 'PGMA    '. The spike used rstrip and found 0 of 88 sites where a literal was
shorter than its field, so it changes nothing today, but it is one line and should be
written down.

Depends on nothing. Pairs with the subscript bead: independent causes, same symptom
table.

title: depgraph: a literal CALL's program node keeps its quotes, a CICS LINK's does not
description: flows._callee_node builds PROGRAM:'PROGB' for CALL 'PROGB' (operand_name, no strip), while flows._identity builds PROGRAM:PROGB for EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('PROGB'). The same callee therefore gets two dependency-graph nodes depending on which verb reached it, so CALL and LINK edges to one member never merge. Found while porting cobble to red-dragon's CallTarget (red-dragon-jgra); left alone there because fixing it changes existing node ids. srccfg's own call sites are unaffected: desugar._callee_name strips quotes on both arms.

title: Build a real-corpus regression fixture: every Db2-tier defect existed because fixtures never met a real IBM artefact
description:
Every squall/bridge defect this plan (2026-09-19-carddemo-db2-tier) found and fixed -- forge-kgd (trailing 8-digit sequence field), forge-yuo (VARCHAR field_meta from sidecars only), forge-qhi (bridge dropping WORKING-STORAGE EXEC_SQL entries), forge-pkw (+100 DML fidelity), forge-2xy (process-global plan pool) -- existed because squall's and the bridge's own test fixtures were generated by our OWN tooling (squall's dclgen generator, hand-built COBOL snippets) and had never met a real IBM-authored artefact until CardDemo's vendored app-transaction-type-db2 tree was thrown at them.

Without a fixture built from vendored, unmodified source (not squall-generated, not hand-simplified), the next real COBOL/DCLGEN program to reach this stack will surface the same class of gap again, one bug at a time, the way this plan did.

Proposal: add a regression fixture (unit or integration level, squall's or the bridge's own suite) built directly from a real vendored corpus file -- e.g. one of CardDemo's own .dcl/.cbl files already in vendor/carddemo/app/app-transaction-type-db2/ -- asserting the specific shapes that bit this plan: trailing sequence-number columns, DCLGEN level-49 VARCHAR groups with no sidecar, WORKING-STORAGE DECLARE CURSOR. Keeps the corpus-realism gap closed going forward rather than only in this one plan's tests.

title: RedDragon: no DSNTIAC stub, and CALL by data-name is unsupported -- COTRTLIC's error-reporting path is silently empty
description:
cpy/CSDB2RPY.cpy's 9999-FORMAT-DB2-MESSAGE (COTRTLIC/COTRTUPC's common Db2 error-message builder) does 'CALL LIT-DSNTIAC USING DFHEIBLK, DFHCOMMAREA, SQLCA, WS-DSNTIAC-FORMATTED, WS-DSNTIAC-LRECL' -- a CALL BY DATA-NAME (LIT-DSNTIAC is a literal holding the program name 'DSNTIAC', not a literal CALL 'DSNTIAC') to the real Db2 message-formatting utility DSNTIAC, then reads the COBOL special register RETURN-CODE.

Neither piece exists: (1) no DSNTIAC stub is provided anywhere in cicada/squall/red-dragon, and (2) CALL by data-name (CALL identifier USING ...) is unsupported by the interpreter -- only CALL 'literal' is. This is CardDemo's ONLY error-reporting path for every Db2 statement failure across both COTRTUPC and COTRTLIC (9998-PRIMING-QUERY and every *-EXIT paragraph's WHEN OTHER/negative-SQLCODE branch funnels through 9999-FORMAT-DB2-MESSAGE).

Silent today: this session's own characterisation tests (task 12,
test_admin_five_backward_fetch_exhaustion_reports_a_db2_error and
test_admin_six_insert_failure_reports_the_update_s_stale_sqlcode) observed real Db2 error messages ('Error on fetch Cursor C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD SQLCODE:  100', 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:  100:?Statem...') rendering with '?Statem' / truncated garbage where DSNTIAC's formatted text should be -- confirming the CALL is either a no-op or erroring silently rather than populating WS-DSNTIAC-FMTD-TEXT.

Not on the happy path (every currently-passing test avoids triggering an actual Db2 error message body), but needed before ANY of COTRTUPC/COTRTLIC's error handling can be trusted to show a real DSNTIAC-formatted message rather than whatever text happens to be in memory.
close_reason: Closed

title: DISPLAY drops intrinsic FUNCTION, printing the function name as a literal
description:
Surfaced while isolating forge-d79, and unrelated to it.

  DISPLAY 'x' FUNCTION TRIM(fld)

printed the literal text 'TRIM' rather than the trimmed value of fld. So the
DISPLAY lowering path does not treat an intrinsic FUNCTION as a function call at
all -- it appears to fall through to emitting the function's NAME as a string
operand.

Distinct from forge-d79, which is about subscripts being dropped on a FUNCTION's
operand. This one loses the function invocation itself, on the DISPLAY path only.

Not yet investigated: whether other statement paths that take a list of operands
(e.g. STRING, UNSTRING) share the defect, and whether it affects all intrinsics or
only some. Observed in red-dragon at 10d2e1f8.

title: SharedSqlStores.cursors is a spec-wide flat namespace keyed by bare cursor name
description:
squall/squall/strategy_stores.py:48 (SharedSqlStores.cursors) is shared region-wide across every SQL program a build_sql_spec serves, keyed by bare COBOL cursor name -- and unlike field_meta/plans, it is written at RUNTIME, not just compile time: squall/squall/builtins/exec_sql.py's _h_declare_cursor writes ctx.cursors[name] = parsed on every EXEC SQL DECLARE CURSOR execution, into the now-shared dict.

Failure scenario: program A declares cursor C-ROWS over 'SELECT ... FROM ACCOUNTS'; program B (composed in the same region/spec) also declares C-ROWS, over 'SELECT ... FROM CARDS'.
