Whichever program's DECLARE executes last at runtime owns the entry region-wide -- so if A DECLAREs at task N and B OPENs C-ROWS at task N+1 (having never DECLAREd its own, or having its own overwritten), B's OPEN silently runs A's query and fetches into B's host variables. _close_all_cursors also now iterates every program's declared cursors at every task end (for name in ctx.cursors: backend.close(name)), so per-task close cost grows with the region's total cursor count, not the current program's.

Not exercised by CardDemo today: COTRTLIC is the only cursor-using program in the Db2 tier, so there is no live collision -- this is latent, not active.

This needs a per-compilation-unit scoping decision, not a patch here: it belongs with forge-c2z (make copybook/name resolution per-compilation-unit rather than per-region) and its sibling forge-6o7 (same 'region-wide flat namespace' class of bug, for BMS map/copybook names instead of cursor names). plans is safe as a flat shared list because indices are allocated globally-unique by strategy_stores.append -- no name collision is possible there. cursors and field_meta are NOT safe: both are keyed by bare COBOL name with no per-program qualifier, so two programs using the same name silently collide. field_meta's specific precedence-inversion symptom (an earlier program's leftover metadata outranking a later program's own derived entry) was fixed directly in this same round (merge_field_meta now tracks sidecar_field_names so an inference from one program cannot silently displace another's) -- but that fix does not add per-program qualification, so the underlying namespace-collision hazard for field_meta (and, more visibly, for cursors, which is written at runtime) remains and is exactly what this bead is about.

Fix direction: qualify cursors (and field_meta) keys by owning program/compilation-unit, or give each program its own cursors dict while still sharing the plan pool -- a scoping decision that should be made alongside forge-c2z's compilation-unit work, not patched in isolation.

title: RedDragon bridge: a parenthesised group containing a FUNCTION collapses to just the FUNCTION
description:
COMPUTE WS-STRING-MID = (FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-INFO-MSG) - WS-STRING-LEN) / 2 + 1 evaluates as FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-INFO-MSG) / 2 + 1: the subtraction inside the parentheses is dropped.

Reproduced in isolation with WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) holding a 34-character message: WS-STRING-LEN computes correctly as 34, but WS-STRING-MID comes out 21 (= 40/2+1) instead of 4 (= (40-34)/2+1).

Consequence in CardDemo's Db2 tier: both COTRTUPC and COTRTLIC centre their INFOMSG prompt this way (COTRTUPC.cbl:1420-1429, COTRTLIC.cbl:1560-1571), so the prompt lands at offset 21 of a PIC X(40) item and only its first 20 characters survive -- 'Changes validated.Press F5 to save' renders as 'Changes validated.Pr'. Display only; no SQL or control-flow effect observed.

tests/integration/test_carddemo_db2_headless.py works around it in _shows_info_prompt (prefix match), which keeps passing unchanged once this is fixed.

Owned by RedDragon (interpreter/cobol/**) -- filed here only because ~/code/red-dragon is not checked out on this machine.
notes:
2026-09-20: re-diagnosed empirically at red-dragon d76d0380. STILL BROKEN -- the
forge-d79 FUNCTION-subscript fix did not address it.

**The original title understated the bug.** It is not "drops the subtraction when the
LEFT operand is a parenthesised FUNCTION". Position is irrelevant: any parenthesised
group containing a FUNCTION anywhere discards everything except the FUNCTION.

Repro matrix (WS-MSG PIC X(40), WS-LEN = 34), run through the full pipeline:

  A  COMPUTE WS-OUT = (40 - WS-LEN) / 2 + 1                      -> 4   CORRECT
  B  COMPUTE WS-OUT = FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-MSG) - WS-LEN           -> 6   CORRECT
  C  COMPUTE WS-OUT = (FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-MSG) - WS-LEN)         -> 40  WRONG (want 6)
  D  COMPUTE WS-OUT = (FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-MSG) - WS-LEN) / 2 + 1 -> 21  WRONG (want 4)
  E  COMPUTE WS-OUT = (WS-LEN - FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-MSG))         -> 40  WRONG (want -6)

A proves plain parens are fine. B proves the FUNCTION-minus-field IR is fine. E proves
the FUNCTION need not be the left operand -- it is the parenthesisation that is fatal.

**Owning layer: the Java bridge, NOT the Python lowering.** Raw bridge JSON for case C:

  "statements": [{"type": "COMPUTE",
                  "expression": {"kind": "function", "name": "LENGTH",
                                 "args": [{"kind": "ref", "name": "WS-MSG"}]},
                  "targets": [{"name": "WS-OUT", "rounded": false}]}]

The `- WS-LEN` never leaves StatementSerializer. Python executes faithfully what it is
given, so no IR or lowering change is needed; the defect is confined to the serializer's
handling of a parenthesised arithmetic group. Case B shows the correct target shape
already exists, so this is producing a node the IR can already represent.

Same family and same file as forge-d79 (red-dragon 39f9b2ac/10d2e1f8/d76d0380), where
ProLeap's grammar makes a parenthesised group ambiguous with other constructs and the
serializer takes the wrong alternative.

**Guard-rail required.** forge-d79's first attempt mis-joined FUNCTION MAX(A, (B)) into
a subscripted read A(B); only a purpose-built test caught it. Any fix here must keep
genuine multi-argument calls -- MAX(A B), MAX(A, (B)), MAX((A) (B)) -- intact.

Consequence unchanged: both COTRTUPC and COTRTLIC centre their INFOMSG prompt with this
expression, so prompts render truncated. tests/integration/test_carddemo_db2_headless.py
matches on the rendered prefix and keeps passing once this is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in red-dragon 8f432872 (bead red-dragon-nwm5). Root cause: StatementSerializer.serializeBasis probed the whole basis subtree for a functionCall, and for the parenthesised alternative of 'basis : LPARENCHAR arithmeticExpression RPARENCHAR | identifier | literal' that probe reached INSIDE the parens and returned the nested call as the entire basis. Fix excludes the parenthesised alternative so it falls through to the existing ArithmeticValueStmt branch -- no IR or lowering change. Affected COMPUTE, IF and PERFORM UNTIL relation operands, nested groups, and groups used as operands of larger expressions. Verified: the isolated repro now gives MID=4 (was 21), and tests/integration/test_carddemo_db2_headless.py's _shows_info_prompt now asserts the FULL prompt ('Update HIGHLIGHTED row. Press F10 to save', 41 chars, previously truncated to 23) instead of a surviving prefix. vendor/red-dragon bumped to 8f432872.

title: Make copybook resolution per-compilation-unit, not per-region
description:
Copybook resolution is currently a property of the REGION, but on a mainframe it is a property of the COMPILATION UNIT. Each compile step has its own SYSLIB concatenation; two programs can legitimately resolve the same copybook name to different members.

Today cicada/cics/tn3270/region.py builds ONE ProLeapCobolParser with one flat copybook_dirs list and compiles every program in the region with it. RegionConfig holds source_dirs, bms_dirs and copybook_dirs as three independent flat lists, so the association between a source tree and ITS copybooks is lost.

PROPOSED SHAPE: group paths by tree, and give each program the concatenation of the tree it was found in.

  [[trees]]
  source_dir    = "${CARDDEMO_HOME}/cbl"
  copybook_dirs = ["${CARDDEMO_HOME}/cpy", "${CARDDEMO_HOME}/cpy-bms"]
  bms_dir       = "${CARDDEMO_HOME}/bms"

  [[trees]]
  source_dir    = "${CARDDEMO_HOME}/app-transaction-type-db2/cbl"
  copybook_dirs = [".../db2/cpy", ".../db2/cpy-bms", ".../db2/dcl"]
  bms_dir       = ".../db2/bms"

A program in tree N compiles with: tree N's own generated sym_dir, then tree N's copybook_dirs, then the region-wide shared dirs. Each tree generates its symbolic copybooks into its OWN sym_dir, which makes forge-6o7's last-wins overwrite impossible by construction rather than by a first-wins rule.

WHY CARDDEMO ACTUALLY NEEDS THE ORDERING: COTRTUPC lives in the Db2 tree but does COPY COCOM01Y, which is in the MAIN tree's cpy/. Its correct concatenation is "my tree first, then the shared tree" — exactly a JCL concatenation. The current flat list gives the same answer only because no names collide; it is right by luck, not by construction.

COST: negligible. ProLeapCobolParser is a command-line builder and a JVM is spawned per parse anyway, so a parser per program adds nothing measurable.

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION, do not "fix" this one: the MAP CATALOG being region-wide is CORRECT and must stay that way. CICS mapsets are region resources defined in the CSD, so a map name genuinely is unique across a region on a real mainframe. Only the COPYBOOK path is per-compile. The two walk the same bms_dirs today, which invites conflating them, but they model different things.

Related: forge-6o7 (the precedence contradiction this would dissolve). Discovered while reviewing Task 9 of the Db2 tier plan, which made source_dir/bms_dir plural and thereby created the first region spanning two trees.

title: BMS map precedence contradicts itself across bms_dirs: catalog is first-wins, symbolic copybooks are last-wins
description:
cicada/cics/tn3270/region.py resolves a map name two different ways when a region spans more than one BMS directory.

_catalog builds the runtime MapCatalog with ChainMap over the per-directory catalogs, so an EARLIER bms_dirs entry wins.

_generate_symbolic_copybooks loops the same bms_dirs writing every generated <STEM>.cpy into one shared sym_dir, so a LATER directory's file OVERWRITES an earlier one — last wins.

So if two trees define the same map name, the program is COMPILED against the later tree's symbolic copybook while the runtime paints from the earlier tree's catalog entry. Silent, and it would surface as inexplicable field offsets or a field that reads as garbage — a long way from its cause.

Not reachable with CardDemo today: the main tree has 17 maps and app-transaction-type-db2 has 2 (COTRTLI, COTRTUP), verified disjoint. Introduced when Task 9 made bms_dir plural; every config before that had exactly one directory, so neither path had a precedence to express.

Fix: make the generation side first-wins to match the catalog (skip a stem already written, rather than overwrite), and pin it with a test using two directories that both define the same map name.

Related design note worth recording somewhere more durable: a region builds ONE parser for all its programs, so there is a single global copybook namespace. Real mainframe builds give each compile unit its own SYSLIB concatenation, so two programs can legitimately resolve the same copybook name to different members. Our model cannot express that. Fine for CardDemo; a constraint to know about.
notes: See forge-c2z: making copybook resolution per-compilation-unit would dissolve this contradiction by construction — each tree generates into its own sym_dir, so there is no shared directory for a later write to overwrite. If forge-c2z is done first, the first-wins fix here becomes unnecessary. If not, fix this independently; it is one line plus a test.

title: Move the fixed-format COBOL column model upstream into red-dragon's interpreter
description:
squall/squall/fixed_format.py models fixed-format COBOL's four positional zones (sequence cols 1-6, indicator col 7, code cols 8-72, identification cols 73-80) and is the only sanctioned way to rewrite such source without dragging the identification area into the code area.

But cicada needs the same knowledge, and the import-linter contract forbids cics from importing squall — so cicada/cics/preprocessor.py carries its own private code-area helper. The same COBOL-language fact is now encoded in two packages, and the reason is a forge architectural constraint rather than anything about the language.

Fixed-format column layout is a COBOL concern, so the honest home is red-dragon's interpreter/, where both packages may import it. The ProLeap bridge is hard-wired to FIXED format (Main.java:86 passes no -format), which is what makes the positional model correct for this stack.

Raised under the standing 'fix upstream, do not patch downstream' instruction (memory: fix-upstream-not-downstream). Task 3 of the Db2 tier plan explicitly flagged the question and deferred it; that deferral predates the instruction.

Work: move the module to ~/code/red-dragon's interpreter, commit and push there, bump the submodule here, and have both squall and cicada import it. Delete cicada's private helper and squall's copy.

title: Run CardDemo's Db2 tier — admin options 5 and 6 over CICS
description: Replace the STATUS and SUGGESTED ORDER blocks. STATUS: the feasibility gate is passed and the tier runs. Composition landed in 6e63bc5a (admin 5 COTRTLIC/CTLI and admin 6 COTRTUPC/CTTU over a composed CICS+SQL spec) with a live-3270 CLI in 1988b543 (`make db2-up`, `make db2-seed`, `carddemo-db2-cli`); coverage in tests/integration/test_carddemo_db2_headless.py (admin 6 update/insert/delete, admin 5 list/paging/type-filter/row update, plus two characterisation tests pinning CardDemo's own defects), test_carddemo_db2_region.py, test_carddemo_db2_compile.py and test_carddemo_db2_abend_rollback.py. All seven originally-parented children -- forge-9kx, forge-kgd, forge-yuo, forge-qhi, forge-pkw, forge-2xy, forge-brx -- are closed. REMAINING before this epic closes: forge-ss6 (the real-corpus regression fixture named in ACCEPTANCE) and the P3 follow-ups forge-602 and forge-a09. The 'both design/plan docs say the work is unbuilt' line no longer holds -- re-read them before relying on their status blocks.
notes:
INVESTIGATION FINDINGS 2026-09-19 (surveys live in gitignored .superpowers/sdd/db2-epic/; these are the durable conclusions).

SCOPE REDUCTIONS — things we do NOT need to build:
- No cross-task cursor state. COTRTLIC opens/fetches/closes its cursor entirely
  within one task and repositions using a 2-byte key held in the COMMAREA
  (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE / WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE, COTRTLIC.cbl:397-410, 768-783).
  Neither DECLARE has WITH HOLD. A look-ahead fetch after row 7 (1661-1673)
  makes "WHERE TR_TYPE >= :WS-START-KEY" land exactly on the next page. The
  runtime needs only DECLARE/OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE inside one task.
- No SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK anywhere in either program, so forge-1zu.15 is not on
  this critical path.

UNIT OF WORK — corrected, narrower than first reported:
- 7 SYNCPOINT sites: COTRTUPC 453 (PF3, before XCTL, no RETURN), 1557, 1606,
  1637; COTRTLIC 616 (PF3, before XCTL), 1856, 1909.
- Every DML site is followed by a RETURN TRANSID in the SAME task, and RETURN
  does fire the commit hook, so happy-path final state survives even with a
  no-op SYNCPOINT. What actually breaks: commit-before-repaint ordering; the
  PF3 paths leave the UOW open across the XCTL into COADM01C; error branches
  never roll back.
- Verified separately: EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT is a pure no-op (cics/strategy.py:131,
  :999); XCTL does not fire the task-end hook (cics/strategy.py:1373); an abend
  fires no hook at all. make_link_builtin restores result_holder across a LINK
  but NOT the hook, so a LINKed program's RETURN commits its caller's UOW and
  closes its cursors mid-task.

TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE CONSTRAINT (mandatory, or the suite agrees with the bugs):
- Committed-state assertions MUST read through a THIRD connection. Asserting
  through the program's own Db2Backend cannot distinguish committed from
  uncommitted, so without this the suite passes on every unit-of-work defect.
- Vendored index DDL XTRNTYPE.ddl / XTRNTYCAT.ddl FAIL on Db2 LUW (SQL0104N):
  ERASE NO / CLOSE NO are z/OS-only. The PKs already create equivalent unique
  indexes. Verified by execution.
- db2_env.sh defaults DB2_PORT=50000 and silently targets the unrelated
  db2server container; should fail loud (see forge-zka).

ASSERTION CONTRACT:
- Both programs set DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN = FUNCTION LENGTH(PIC X(50) field),
  i.e. always 50 (COTRTUPC.cbl:1541-1542, COTRTLIC.cbl:1843-1844). Assert
  RTRIM(TR_DESCRIPTION)='<text>' AND LENGTH(TR_DESCRIPTION)=50. Seed rows are
  unpadded, so the length change is itself a usable assertion.

RUNTIME REQUIREMENT FOUND IN THE MAPS:
- Both programs mark fields DFHBMPRF (protected + FSET) and re-read the
  protected key field on the next turn (COTRTUPC.cbl:656-684). A runtime that
  drops protected or unmodified fields on RECEIVE MAP loses the key and inserts
  a low-values row.
- Every task runs a priming query SELECT 1 FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1 FETCH FIRST 1
  ROW ONLY (cpy/CSDB2RPY.cpy:23-28, called COTRTLIC.cbl:684).

CARDDEMO SOURCE DEFECTS to reproduce, NOT fix (8 listed in the survey), incl.
the backward-fetch path having no +100 branch (COTRTLIC.cbl:1761-1790) and
9300's WHEN OTHER reporting a failed delete as success.

title: Builtins.TABLE is process-global while squall's plan pool is per-strategy: two SQL programs in one region collide
description:
squall registers its builtins into the process-global Builtins.TABLE, but the SQL plan pool those builtins index into is per-strategy (per compiled program). Compiling a second EXEC SQL program into the same region overwrites the registration, so call sites in the FIRST program index into the SECOND program's plan list.

A CICS region serving more than one Db2 program — which is exactly what CardDemo's admin options 5 and 6 together require — would therefore execute the wrong statements. Not reachable today only because no region serves two SQL programs yet.

Related: the 'Builtins.TABLE already contains ... — overwriting' warnings printed on every composed compile are the visible symptom of the same global.
notes:
2026-09-19, Task 7: _cursors_store is now a FOURTH per-program object published through the process-global Builtins.TABLE, alongside _plans, statement addresses and _field_meta_store.

Concrete reachable failure: compile COTRTLIC then COTRTUPC into one region and the second registration wins, so COTRTLIC's OPEN C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD resolves against COTRTUPC's cursor store and returns SQLCODE -1 — i.e. admin option 5 silently fails to open its cursor in exactly the region configuration Task 11 builds.

Positive finding worth keeping when this is fixed: _close_all_cursors (builtins/exec_sql.py:274-279) iterates names but does NOT clear ctx.cursors, so cursors recovered from WORKING-STORAGE survive CICS task end. That failure mode is already avoided and a fix must not reintroduce it.
2026-09-20, Task 11: FIXED. squall.strategy_stores.SharedSqlStores now holds the plan pool, the field_meta store and the cursor store; build_sql_spec creates ONE and hands it to every SqlLoweringStrategy it makes, mirroring build_cics_spec's spec-level context_holder/result_holder/program_cache. Verified by execution both ways: with the fix all 9 executing tests in tests/integration/test_carddemo_db2_headless.py pass against live Db2; reverting just 'stores=stores' in build_sql_spec makes all 9 fail with IndexError on the plan pool. Two unit tests pin it (squall/tests/unit/test_strategy.py), both confirmed to fail without the fix. _close_all_cursors still does not clear ctx.cursors, so that positive finding is preserved.
close_reason: Closed

title: squall: DML affecting 0 rows returns SQLCODE 0 instead of +100
description:
squall/squall/backends/db2.py: an UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT that affects no rows returns SQLCODE 0 rather than +100 (NOT FOUND), which is what Db2 returns and what COBOL programs branch on.

Consequence in CardDemo: COTRTUPC's add path checks for the not-found condition to decide whether a row already exists, so with SQLCODE 0 it silently never inserts. Programs that guard an UPDATE on +100 will likewise take the wrong branch.

Silent and data-affecting.
close_reason: Verified fixed: squall/squall/backends/db2.py:100 returns sqlcode=0 if rows else 100 for SELECT, and lines 126/130 return sqlcode=100 for zero-row DML explicitly, matching real Db2 fidelity. Landed in commit 38c2ad2a 'fix(squall): SQLCODE fidelity -- +100 zero-row DML, SQLERRM, VARCHAR trailing space'. Directly proven end-to-end by test_admin_six_inserts_a_new_transaction_type, which documents (and Task 8's report confirms) that forcing resolve_dml_sqlcode to return 0 instead breaks the test at 7 rows.

title: Delete squall/squall/dclgen_copybooks.py — superseded workaround
description:
Added on the CardDemo Db2 branch to strip the IBM DCLGEN 'EXEC SQL DECLARE <table> TABLE ... END-EXEC' preamble when staging copybooks, because ProLeap's grammar appeared to reject it inside a DATA DIVISION. Correct and tested (squall/squall/dclgen_copybooks.py + squall/tests/unit/test_dclgen_copybooks.py), but nothing in production calls it.

SUPERSEDED, not merely uncalled. The diagnosis it was built on was wrong -- see the 2026-09-19 note for the real cause (our own INCLUDE->COPY rewrite sliding cols 73-80 into Area B) and for task 4's proof that raw .dcl files parse with no staging at all. The task that would once have wired it in, forge-9kx, is now CLOSED and was completed WITHOUT it: build_db2_region composes squall's SQL CoprocessorSpec with CICS and serves both COTRTUPC and COTRTLIC against a live Db2 with the copybooks unstaged. So there is no longer any 'wire it in when forge-9kx resumes' option, and no caller is coming.

The module stays in place for now; this bead is the record that it is a superseded workaround whose pending action is deletion, kept open on the owner's call (which predates the standing 'fix upstream, do not patch downstream' instruction). Tested dead code invites someone to wire it back in and reintroduce a compensating layer.

Also noted by review, and moot if it is deleted: _source_files silently skips subdirectories, so a nested copybook tree would be dropped; and the regex does not match a DECLARE TABLE whose name is split across a line break before the TABLE keyword (DCLGEN never emits that form, so the real risk is ~0).
notes:
2026-09-19: re-scoped under the standing 'fix upstream, do not patch downstream' instruction (memory: fix-upstream-not-downstream).

This module staged sanitised copies of CardDemo's DCLGEN copybooks with the EXEC SQL DECLARE ... TABLE preamble stripped, because ProLeap appeared to reject that statement inside a DATA DIVISION. That diagnosis was wrong. The real defect was our own prepass: rewriting 'EXEC SQL INCLUDE DCLTRTYP END-EXEC' to 'COPY DCLTRTYP.' is 20 characters shorter, so the cols-73-80 identification field slid into Area B, and ANTLR's error recovery silently ate it plus the following 01 group. Stripping DECLARE TABLE only removed the token the already-derailed parser happened to choke on.

Task 4 of the Db2 tier plan now PROVES raw .dcl files parse correctly with no staging (commit 7f28fb38 compiles both COTRTUPC and COTRTLIC and asserts CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, SQLCA, DCLTRANSACTION-TYPE and DCLTRANSACTION-TYPE-CATEGORY are all present).

So this is not merely an uncalled utility — it is a workaround for a bug that has been fixed at its actual cause. It should be DELETED rather than kept, because tested dead code invites someone to wire it back in and reintroduce a compensating layer. Was previously kept unwired on the owner's call, which predates the standing instruction.

title: TN3270 region can't serve the Db2 CardDemo programs: no SQL coprocessor is composed in
description: cics/tn3270/region.py's build_region calls build_cics_spec alone, so the region it builds has only the CICS lowering strategy. Compiling COTRTUPC (CardDemo admin option 6, vendor/carddemo/app/app-transaction-type-db2/cbl) therefore dies with ValueError: Unknown COBOL statement type: 'EXEC_SQL' -- it parses fine, but nothing lowers its EXEC SQL. Serving admin 5/6 over the wire needs red_dragon_forge's composition layer (CICS + squall's SQL CoprocessorSpec) behind the TN3270 server, plus a live Db2 and the DDL in app-transaction-type-db2/ddl. Note these programs live in a SEPARATE source tree from app/cbl, so the config would need per-program source dirs too.
notes:
2026-09-19: attempted. The composition design is written up in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-carddemo-db2-tn3270-design.md with an implementation plan alongside it. Work stopped at the plan's Task 1 feasibility gate (compile COTRTUPC with CICS+SQL specs composed), which never passed.

Three real squall bugs were found and fixed on the way (all merged): EXEC SQL undetectable in sequence-numbered fixed-format source; the IBM DCLGEN DECLARE TABLE preamble breaking ProLeap; and a strip regex that could delete a real DECLARE CURSOR.

NOW BLOCKED on a ProLeap copybook-substitution bug, filed in red-dragon's own tracker: after resolving a staged DCLGEN copybook via COPY, the NEXT COPY in the same DATA DIVISION section silently loses its content, so CARDDEMO-COMMAREA never reaches the AST. Verified it is not the harness (COACTVWC compiles fine through the identical configuration) and not the interpreter's lowering.

Also note forge-kgd (trailing 8-digit sequence field) is a real squall gap on the same path, though not the blocker.
close_reason: Verified fixed: cicada/cics/tn3270/region.py's build_region now accepts extra_specs (Sequence[CoprocessorSpec]) composed alongside the CICS spec (line 26 imports CoprocessorSpec, lines 103-148 thread cics_spec + extra_specs through). red_dragon_forge.carddemo_db2_region.build_db2_region composes squall's SQL CoprocessorSpec with CICS to serve both COTRTUPC and COTRTLIC from one region against a live Db2. Landed across task 9 (a0db3854, plural source_dirs/bms_dirs/extra_specs seam) and task 10 (122d4f8b, CardDemo Db2 schema + composed region), proven end-to-end by tests/integration/test_carddemo_db2_headless.py (12 passing tests as of task 12, all against live Db2).

title: COACTVWC/COACTUPC/COCRDSLC/COCRDUPC abend handlers use bare EXEC CICS SEND FROM(...), which is unsupported
description: These four programs' abend/error-diagnostic paths issue a bare EXEC CICS SEND FROM(data-name) rather than SEND MAP or SEND TEXT FROM(...). cicada's SEND builtin does not support the bare FROM(...) form, so whenever one of these abend handlers actually runs, its diagnostic message can never reach the screen -- the operator sees nothing where real CICS would show the error text. Not on the happy path exercised by the existing wire tests, but it means any of these four abend handlers is currently silent.

title: COACTUPC's 'account updated but customer rewrite failed' path issues SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK, which abends instead of reporting the failure
description: COACTUPC's error-recovery path for 'account REWRITE succeeded but the paired customer REWRITE failed' issues EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK to undo the partial update. cicada deliberately leaves SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK on the unsupported/loud path (only the plain no-op SYNCPOINT is supported), so this failure mode abends instead of showing the intended error message on screen. Reachable only when the customer REWRITE genuinely fails after the account REWRITE succeeds, so it doesn't affect the happy-path wire tests, but it means this recovery path can never be observed end-to-end today.
close_reason: SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK now has its own lowering (rollback hook), so COACTUPC's partial-update recovery path no longer abends on the verb.

title: region.py builds the CICS spec without program_cache, so INQUIRE PROGRAM always answers PGMIDERR
description: cics/tn3270/region.py's build_region calls build_cics_spec(...) without passing program_cache, even though build_cics_spec accepts it and forwards it to the spec (cicada/cics/coprocessor.py). EXEC CICS INQUIRE PROGRAM therefore always returns PGMIDERR regardless of whether the named program is actually compiled into the region. Only COMEN01C's main-menu option 11 (COPAUS0C) currently consults INQUIRE PROGRAM, which is why it degrades gracefully today ('This option ... is not installed') -- but the answer it gets is wrong for any caller, compiled or not. Fix: pass a program_cache (e.g. derived from config.programs / the compiled LinkedProgram map) into build_cics_spec so INQUIRE PROGRAM reflects reality.

title: Document why _run_dispatcher_with_runner keeps the pre-fix input-retention behaviour
description: cics/dispatcher.py's _run_dispatcher_with_runner (the blocking-loop driver, used by _resume) deliberately does NOT drain unreceived terminal input at task end -- only CicsRegion._advance does (forge-1zu.6's fix). Its model is a pre-filled input queue fed by an external driver/transport, where _peek_input_event's get-then-put-back already assumes at most one pending item and the next blocking get() naturally waits for a fresh one; draining here has no equivalent CardDemo-observed defect because this driver is not what runs the TN3270 CardDemo path today. Record in a comment on _run_dispatcher_with_runner (or _resume) why it diverges from CicsRegion here, and what would have to change (its queue-fill contract, or unifying the two drivers) before it would need the same drain.

title: Simplify wire CRUD tests' PF3-then-reselect 'search again' workaround now that forge-1zu.6 is fixed
description: test_tn3270_crud_e2e.py currently re-displays a committed record via each program's own 'search again' ENTER cycle instead of PF3 back to the menu and reselecting, because PF3-then-reselect used to land on the sign-on screen (forge-1zu.6). That defect is fixed (23556fea: CicsRegion now discards terminal input the ending task never RECEIVEd at task end, not on XCTL). Simplify the workaround: drive PF3-then-reselect directly where it reads more naturally, dropping the 'search again' detour.

title: CardDemo COCRDUPC zeroes CARD-CVV-CD and blanks the record FILLER on every card update
description:
Found by the TN3270 wire CRUD suite (forge-1zu.3) while asserting that fields the operator did not edit survive a REWRITE. This is a CardDemo application bug, not a cicada defect — recorded here because our tests are what surfaced it and future assertions will trip over it.

Trace (vendor/carddemo/app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl): CCUP-NEW-CVV-CD (COMMAREA, X(3), part of CCUP-NEW-DETAILS) is declared and only ever INITIALIZEd (line 586); no MOVE ever populates it from the record that was read, unlike CCUP-NEW-ACCTID/CARDID/CRDNAME. 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING then does INITIALIZE CARD-UPDATE-RECORD (line 1461) followed by MOVE CCUP-NEW-CVV-CD TO CARD-CVV-CD-X / MOVE CARD-CVV-CD-N TO CARD-UPDATE-CVV-CD (lines 1464-1465), so the CVV is rewritten as zeros on every card update, and the record's trailing FILLER X(59) at [91:150] (CVACT02Y.cpy) is blanked for the same reason.

Observed over the wire: CARD-CVV-CD at [27:30] went 747 -> 000 after an unrelated embossed-name change. CARD-ACCT-ID at [16:27] IS carried forward, which is why the card-update test asserts on that instead.

Not actionable in cicada — the fix belongs in the vendored CardDemo source, which this repo does not modify. Keep as documentation so a future 'untouched fields survive' assertion is not mistaken for a runtime regression.

title: Cursor-traversal coverage missing: DFHBMPRO autoskip->bare PROTECTED change, no Tab()-driven test
description:
Whole-branch review finding M4: DFHBMPRO moved from autoskip to bare PROTECTED (see the
DFHBMSCA attribute-constant normalisation work on this branch), which changes whether the
cursor stops in a protected field during Tab()-driven traversal versus skipping over it.

No test in cicada/tests/integration/cics/test_tn3270_crud_e2e.py or test_tn3270_e2e.py
exercises this: every wire test navigates with explicit MoveCursor(row,col) calls, never
Tab(). A regression in cursor-stop/skip behaviour for autoskip vs. bare PROTECTED fields
would pass the whole suite today.

Needed: a wire test that drives at least one screen via repeated Tab() from the first
unprotected field and asserts the cursor lands where BMS's autoskip/PROTECTED semantics
say it should (skipping DFHBMPRO-attributed fields, stopping in plain PROTECTED ones without
autoskip, per BMS ATTRB semantics) -- not just typing into fields whose position is already
known via MoveCursor.

title: A/F-byte overlap drops MDT on COUSR02C's re-entry SEND: faithful BMS behaviour, not our defect
description:
RE-SCOPED after review (fix round 1): this is faithful BMS/A-F-byte-overlap behaviour
triggered by CardDemo's own COUSR02C re-entry path, not a defect in cicada's runtime.
Keeping the full original trace below because it is still the right diagnostic record;
the "Fix" section that follows supersedes the original bead's proposed remedies.

## Original trace (mechanism confirmed correct)

cics/builtins/screen.py: _overrides() reads <base>A (per CardDemo's own MOVE DFHBM* TO xxxA
OF xxxI idiom, used by COACTUPC/COCRDUPC) to detect a SEND-time attribute override. But
<base>A REDEFINES <base>F (COUSR02.CPY etc.), and _received_writes()'s _FLAG_CLEARED=0x80
marker (written to <base>F when a field arrives empty on RECEIVE MAP) lands in that same
byte. On the NEXT SEND MAP, _overrides() reads that leftover 0x80 as if it were a real
override (0x80 & ATTRIBUTE_BITS(0x3F) == 0), zeroing the field's MDT bit even though the BMS
map declares static ATTRB=FSET.

Reproduced live: COUSR02C (Update User) sends FNAME/LNAME/PASSWD/USRTYPE with ATTRB=FSET but
no runtime attribute override (unlike COACTUPC/COCRDUPC, which always re-assert an override
before every SEND). After one RECEIVE MAP turn where those fields arrive without being
retyped (real 3270 behaviour: FSET forces the terminal to report them anyway, empty), the
following turn's SEND MAP drops their MDT, so a PF5 that doesn't retype every field fails the
program's own 'field can NOT be empty' validation. Confirmed via s3270 ReadBuffer(Ascii):
attribute renders as SF(c0=c0,...) (no MDT) instead of the expected SF(c0=c1,...). Confirmed
via s3270 ReadBuffer(Ascii) and by instrumenting _overrides() directly: A=128 (exactly
_FLAG_CLEARED) on the fields that lost MDT.

## Why this is faithful behaviour, not our defect (review finding)

Every link in the chain matches real BMS/CICS semantics, checked individually:
- COUSR02.CPY:21-22 really declares `02 FILLER REDEFINES <f>F. 03 <f>A PIC X.` -- the SAME
  byte, in the genuine AWS-shipped symbolic map, not something cicada invented.
- screen.py:235 writes 0x80 into <f>F when a field arrives empty on RECEIVE -- real BMS sets
  the flag byte to X'80' for a field that was modified-but-then-erased; same condition, same
  value.
- screen.py:153 reads <f>A on the next SEND, and payload.py:39-41's "zero means the program
  left the map's own value in place" is IBM's own documented null-attribute rule (a
  non-zero byte in the attribute position IS the override, by definition).
- The trigger is CardDemo's OWN COUSR02C, not our test or our runtime: `MOVE LOW-VALUES TO
  COUSR2AO` (COUSR02C.cbl:97) sits only in the `IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER` branch (the very
  first SEND). The re-entry path (COUSR02C.cbl:106-111) RECEIVEs, then SENDs again, with NO
  re-initialisation of the map area in between. So the stale X'80' from the prior RECEIVE
  is genuinely still sitting in the attribute position when the next SEND reads it.

On real z/OS CICS, this same sequence -- COUSR02C RECEIVEing a field that returns empty
(FSET forces it to report even when the operator didn't retype), then SENDing again without
re-initialising COUSR2AO -- would ALSO find X'80' in the attribute byte and use it, dropping
MDT there too. This is the textbook A/F-byte overlap hazard from IBM's own BMS documentation;
COUSR02C not re-initialising its map area before the re-entry SEND is CardDemo's own latent
quirk, not a place where cicada diverges from real hardware.

## Fix: rejected

The original bead proposed two remedies. Both are now REJECTED as they would each make
cicada LESS faithful to real CICS, not more:
- "shadow byte" (track the override separately from <f>F) -- real hardware does not have a
  shadow byte; this would make a program that fails on z/OS pass here.
- "reset <f>A to LOW-VALUES after RECEIVE, before the next SEND" -- real BMS does not do
  this reset either; same objection.

Neither remedy is being pursued. cicada correctly reproduces the hazard as-is.

## Residual uncertainty (reviewer-named, unresolved)

Whether any real BMS implementation validates the attribute byte on SEND and falls back to
the map's own default attribute for a non-attribute value like X'80' (i.e., whether real CICS
treats X'80' as "not a recognised DFHBMxxx-style attribute code, ignore it" rather than
literally using it as the field's new attribute). If real CICS DOES validate and fall back,
cicada's SEND MAP path would need to do the same, and this WOULD then be a genuine
faithfulness bug. Not resolved here; would need IBM documentation or a real 3270/CICS system
to confirm either way.

## Disposition

Closing as "not a defect" (faithful behaviour) rather than leaving as an open runtime bug.
If the residual uncertainty above is later resolved against IBM documentation in cicada's
favour (i.e., real CICS does validate/fall back), reopen with that citation.

Workaround status: cicada/tests/integration/cics/test_tn3270_crud_e2e.py's
test_admin_update_user_rewrites_usrsec retypes every editable field on the PF5 turn. This is
not a workaround for a bug in our runtime -- it is what a real 3270 operator would be forced
to do against this exact COUSR02C re-entry path on genuine CICS too.
close_reason: Confirmed faithful BMS A/F-byte overlap triggered by CardDemo's own COUSR02C re-entry path (no re-init of COUSR2AO before the second SEND); not a cicada defect. Proposed remedies (shadow byte, reset <f>A post-RECEIVE) rejected as less faithful to real hardware. Residual uncertainty (whether real CICS validates the attribute byte and falls back for a non-attribute value like X'80') documented in the issue; reopen with an IBM-documentation citation if resolved in cicada's favour.

comments.author: avishek-sen-gupta
comments.text:
Whole-branch review counterpoint (not a settled resolution): the deciding line is
cics/screen/terminal_screen.py:120 -- `attribute=attrs.attr & ATTRIBUTE_BITS if attrs.attr
else field.attribute` tests presence on the RAW attrs.attr byte but then uses the MASKED
value (attrs.attr & ATTRIBUTE_BITS) as the override. Gating presence on the MASKED value
instead (i.e. `if attrs.attr & ATTRIBUTE_BITS`) would be self-consistent with payload.py:31-32's
own stated rule ("zero means the program left the map's own value in place") and would
dissolve this bead's symptom for X'80', since a masked X'80' & 0x3F == 0 would then read as
"no override" rather than as a real one.

This means the current behaviour is one of two internally-defensible readings of "zero means
no override" -- raw-byte presence vs. masked-value presence -- not something IBM's own BMS
semantics force either way absent documentation. The residual uncertainty section already
on this bead (whether real CICS validates/falls back on a non-attribute byte like X'80')
is the same question from a different angle. Not reopening outright; leaving this note so
the closure doesn't read as more settled than it is. Reopen at low priority (or full P3) if
someone finds documentation, or an IBM-authoritative test, resolving which reading is correct.

title: Investigate: account-update field content appeared to vanish with a bare-PROTECTED runtime attribute override (repro not reproducible; screen-model path exonerated)
description:
Discovered while normalising cicada/cics/copybooks/DFHBMSCA.cpy for
forge-1zu.3's wire CRUD tests: driving COACTUPC's account-update flow with
DFHBMPRF set to a byte masking to bare PROTECTED|MDT (0x21, no NUMERIC bit)
appeared to render ACCTSID/ACSTNUM/ACSCTRY blank on the "found" screen, while
re-adding the NUMERIC bit (0x31, ASKIP+MDT) rendered them correctly.

RESOLVED by tracing the actual render path and diffing the outbound 3270
record byte-for-byte between the two configurations:

- cics/bms/attributes.py: NUMERIC (0x10) is read ONLY by attribute_byte() at
  BMS-map-layout (compile) time; nothing in the runtime SEND MAP path
  consumes it.
- cics/screen/terminal_screen.py: _with_attributes (117-123) copies
  `attrs.attr & ATTRIBUTE_BITS` verbatim and never inspects it; _with_data
  (130-138) sets `carries_data = sent or bool(field.content)` -- both
  operands content-derived, not attribute-derived; _over/_placed branch only
  on carries_data and address. ScreenField.dark (attribute & 0x0C == 0x0C)
  is the only attribute-sensitive render check, and both 0x21 and 0x31 clear
  it.
- cics/tn3270/encoder.py emits field content unconditionally; only the
  attribute's GRAPHIC_CODES translation differs (0x61 vs 0xF1), and both are
  valid.
- Captured the TerminalScreen immediately before encode_screen() and the raw
  encode_screen() output itself for the SAME COACTUPC "found" screen under
  both DFHBMPRF=X'E1' (masks 0x21) and X'F1' (masks 0x31): in both cases
  ACCTSID/ACSTNUM/ACSCTRY held their correct content (`00000000020`,
  `000000020`, `USA`) pre-encode, and the two encoded 2244-byte records
  differed in exactly 3 bytes (the three fields' attribute bytes: 0x61 vs
  0xF1) plus 2 unrelated bytes from the wall-clock TIME field between the
  two separate test runs. Zero content bytes differed.
- Re-ran the full test_tn3270_crud_e2e.py three times with DFHBMPRO=X'60',
  DFHBMPRF=X'61' (the real IBM values) and cicada's existing
  MoveCursor-explicit typing: both tests passed deterministically every
  time. Could not reproduce the original blanking under controlled retest.

Conclusion: the screen-model/encoder path is exonerated -- it never omits
field content based on the NUMERIC bit either way. The original observation
was very likely a confound in an ad hoc manual exploration during that
investigation (a botched `sed` edit at one point left a stale attribute
value in place without my having verified it before re-running), not a real
defect. DFHBMPRO/DFHBMPRF now carry their real IBM values (X'60'/X'61'),
verified safe by this record diff and by three deterministic full-suite
passes; see forge-1zu.3 task-C-report.md fix round 2 for the diff summary
and tests/unit/cics/test_dfhbmsca.py for the pinned expectations.

No code fix was needed beyond restoring the faithful DFHBMPRO/DFHBMPRF
values; closing as resolved-by-investigation.
close_reason: Resolved by investigation: record diff proves the screen-model/encoder path never drops content for either attribute value; original observation not reproducible under controlled retest. DFHBMPRO/DFHBMPRF now carry their real IBM values (X'60'/X'61').

title: Ending task's unreceived terminal input survives to steal the next task's RECEIVE MAP (PF3-then-reselect false sign-on)
description:
Discovered while writing forge-1zu.3's wire CRUD tests (test_tn3270_crud_e2e.py).

Repro (two-step, over a real s3270 wire session against carddemo-tn3270.toml):
  1. Sign on, select menu option 02 (or 05), complete an account/card update through PF5 commit.
  2. Press PF3 -> lands correctly on "Main Menu" (COMEN01C's blank menu render).
  3. Type another option (e.g. "02") + ENTER -> instead of the target program,
     lands back on COSGN00C's sign-on screen ("Please enter User ID ...").

Observed via test transcript: step 2's "Main Menu" render is genuine (asserted
in test_account_update_rewrites_custdat and test_card_update_rewrites_carddat),
so PF3 itself reaches the menu correctly. The break is specifically in
re-selecting a NEW option afterward.

Suspicion (untraced -- do not assume without re-deriving): COMEN01C.cbl's
MAIN-PARA treats "IF EIBCALEN = 0" as "no commarea, fresh entry" and XCTLs to
COSGN00C. Landing on sign-on after step 3 suggests EIBCALEN/commarea state is
lost specifically on this XCTL round trip (COACTUPC/COCRDUPC's PF3 handler
does EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM(COMEN01C) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) directly, no
intervening RETURN/new-task boundary) -- possibly interacting with SYNCPOINT
now being a no-op (forge-1zu Task A), or with how the TN3270 driver threads
commarea across an XCTL-into-COMEN01C-then-RETURN-TRANSID sequence.

Workaround in place: the wire CRUD tests re-display the committed record via
each program's own "search again" cycle (a plain ENTER re-prompts within the
same program) rather than PF3 back to the menu and reselecting, so this does
not block forge-1zu.3.

Root cause not chased this round -- next investigator should trace commarea
threading through PseudoConversationalDriver/CicsRegion across exactly this
XCTL-then-RETURN sequence.
close_reason: Root cause: CicsRegion never discarded terminal input the ending task had not RECEIVEd, so an unconsumed InputEvent survived task end on the shared FIFO input channel and was read by the NEXT task's RECEIVE MAP. COACTUPC's WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK03 branch (COACTUPC.cbl:927-959) decides on EIBAID alone and XCTLs to COMEN01C without ever reaching 1100-RECEIVE-MAP, and COMEN01C's send-menu path does not receive either, so the PF3 keystroke was still queued when the task ended. COMEN01C's next turn then RECEIVEd that stale PF3 instead of the operator's ENTER and took its WHEN DFHPF3 -> RETURN-TO-SIGNON-SCREEN branch. The bead's commarea suspicion was wrong: EIBCALEN was 2000 on every turn (min_commarea_len padding) and the commarea threaded across the XCTL round trip intact; SYNCPOINT's no-op is irrelevant. Fix: _discard_pending_input() in cicada/cics/dispatcher.py, called from CicsRegion._advance on every outcome except XCTL (a transfer within the same task, whose successor may still legitimately RECEIVE). Regression test: test_carddemo_terminal_screen.py::test_menu_reselects_a_second_option_after_pf3.

title: Account-update flow overwrites ACCT-ADDR-ZIP with the group id
description: cicada tests/integration/cics/test_vsam_persistence.py::test_account_update_dump_before_after fails: after the COACTUPC update flow, ACCTDAT ACCT-ADDR-ZIP (@102 X(10), not screen-editable, should be carried from the seeded record '12345') reads 'GRP9' -- the value typed into AADDGRP (ACCT-GROUP-ID @112). Pre-existing: fails identically with vendor/red-dragon at a5422b3a and at 68c3d4f3. Suspect an offset/rewrite-assembly bug in how the updated account record is built or written back.
notes: Root cause: not a cicada bug. COACTUPC's own ACCT-UPDATE-RECORD (cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:418-433) omits ACCT-ADDR-ZIP and pads FILLER X(188); CVACT01Y has ACCT-ADDR-ZIP @102, ACCT-GROUP-ID @112, FILLER X(178). Fields before the gap sum to 102, so ACCT-UPDATE-GROUP-ID sits at 102 and the REWRITE overwrites ACCT-ADDR-ZIP with the group id, leaving @112 blank. Real CardDemo does the same on a mainframe; cicada reproduces it faithfully. Fix belongs in the test expectation, not the runtime.
close_reason: Not a runtime bug: COACTUPC's ACCT-UPDATE-RECORD omits ACCT-ADDR-ZIP (FILLER X(188) vs CVACT01Y's X(178)), so ACCT-UPDATE-GROUP-ID sits at offset 102 and the REWRITE overwrites the ZIP, leaving @112 blank. CardDemo's own defect, faithfully reproduced. Test expectation corrected to assert the misalignment.

title: fields trace: coverage per path is still ~2 branch edges on a large online member
description:
Superseded in its mechanics by the plan-enumeration rewrite (vh2), but its question survives and is now the whole remaining problem: branch coverage per path.

Post-rewrite measurement on a 9181-node / 6980-branch-edge member: 207 edges at 100 paths, still 207 at 500, 355 at 2000, still 355 at 10000, 521 at 40000 (340s). 1866 of 2000 paths add zero new branch edges. Cost per path is no longer the issue -- the per-path frontier sweep is gone, so 100 paths take 0.3s instead of 128s, and the answer to this bead's original cost-attribution question is 'the sweep, and it has been deleted'.

What is left is structural and will not yield to a scheduling tweak. Every alternative plan is the base route with exactly one decision flipped, so consecutive paths share almost every edge and the ceiling is about two new branch edges per path. 6684 branch edges in one member therefore needs >3300 productive paths, and one path in eight to fifteen is productive. Drain order measured at 2000 paths: FIFO 355, LIFO 153 (depth-first starves -- queue falls to 65), productive-ancestor-first split 578. The split is a 63% win for one extra field and is the cheap thing to take if throughput is wanted without a shape change.

The shape change that would actually work is directed: for a named untaken branch edge, construct a plan that reaches it, instead of enumerating routes outward from the entry and hoping. That needs a reachability query from the entry to a given node under the re-entry rule -- which is what the deleted backward frontier was a crude, useless-because-total version of. A cheaper variant, resuming a path from the untaken edge's node rather than from the entry, trades soundness the trace currently has: a path starting mid-program has no provenance for its reads.

Still a throughput question, not a soundness one -- the report prints the fraction reached alongside the answer.
acceptance_criteria: A measurement that attributes the per-path cost, and either a change that raises branch edges per path on the same member or a recorded decision that the entry-restart shape is the one we keep.
close_reason: Both causes located and fixed in e5ebcec (plus 75c02af's arm ordering). Coverage now climbs monotonically, 5% to 76% at 3000 paths on the same member. See the superseding comment.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text:
Superseded: the 'structural, about two new branch edges per path, will not yield to a scheduling tweak' verdict above was wrong. The step-shaped curve was two defects.

1. _ended unwound only to a CROSSING frame, so a path inside a PERFORM frame whose one exit the re-entry rule refuses was thrown away -- 487 of 500 path deaths on the same member. The performer's resume point was on the stack the whole time.

2. The pending queue is enormously redundant against coverage, not against routes. Every plan is a distinct route, but 93083 pending plans flipped only 475 distinct branch edges, 202 of them already taken -- the same node recurs at dozens of positions across plans, and coverage counts (program, node, arm). Insertion order therefore spent thousands of paths re-covering arms.

Fixed in e5ebcec: a plan carries the branch edge its own flip will take, and the queue has two lanes -- plans reaching an edge nothing has taken or promised, then the rest. Nothing is dropped, so an empty queue still means every route was walked exactly once. This is not the 'productive-ancestor-first' heuristic recorded above; it is directed at the metric and each fresh-lane plan raises coverage by construction.

Curve on the same member after both fixes, branch edges by path: 790/250, 1364/500, 2036/750, 2443/1000, 2822/1250, 3473/1500, 3834/1750, 4279/2000, 4750/2250, 5253/2500, 5679/2750, 6099/3000 of 8028. Monotone. Cost is about 120ms/path because paths now reach much further; the denominator rises from 7018 to 8028 as new members are entered.

Remaining: the fresh lane was down to 27 at path 3000, so the next question is what the stale lane is worth, not whether the enumeration climbs.

title: Progress logging for the path-sampling trace CLI
description:
cobble-fields-trace is silent from start to finish: the only output is two stderr error lines and the report file, written once at the end. On a real CICS member with a large callee fan-out a run takes minutes with nothing to watch, and there is no way to tell path 3 of 20 from path 19, nor to see the coverage curve flattening -- which is the number that says whether --paths was set too low.

The seam is _round in trace.py, called once per sampled path by traced's reduce. It already holds everything a progress line wants: the path index, the nodes the walk ran, the coverage so far, the programs entered and the dead ends hit.

Follow build_corpus.py's convention rather than inventing one: logging.getLogger(__name__), a 'trace: [i/n] ...' message, and configure_cli_logging() called from cli(). While there, move the CLI's two sys.stderr.write error lines onto logger.error so the run has one output channel instead of two.
design: Log per completed path, not per skipped one: once the coverage target is met, _round returns early on every remaining iteration and logging there would spam the tail of the run. A final line after the reduce reports where it stopped, which is how a reader distinguishes 'met the target' from 'ran out of paths'.
acceptance_criteria: A run logs one line per sampled path carrying index, nodes walked, cumulative branch coverage and programs entered, plus a closing line naming why it stopped. Tests assert through caplog. No change to Trace or to any artefact.
close_reason: Per-path and closing progress lines added to trace.py via _reported/_closed; the CLI's two stderr writes moved onto logger.error behind configure_cli_logging, so the run has one output channel.

title: Path-sampling byte trace: interpret concrete paths, cross a CALL as an edge
description: A second walk beside the fixpoint, path-sensitive rather than path-insensitive. Interprets one concrete path at a time with a single store and no join anywhere, sampling paths until a branch-coverage target or a path budget is met. Because a path has a stack, two costs the fixpoint pays disappear rather than being worked around: a PERFORMed paragraph returns to the caller actually on the stack instead of to all of them (srccfg/build.py's 'deliberate imprecision'), and a LINK becomes a step into the callee -- bind DFHCOMMAREA onto the caller's window and keep interpreting, with write-back needing no mechanism because the two sides are the same storage. Under-approximate by construction: every reported dependency is witnessed by an actual path, absence means 'not sampled'. Branch coverage is the disclosure. Targeted CLI, no artefact, nothing existing changes.
design: Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-path-sampling-trace-design.md. Store keyed by program OUTSIDE the FieldExtent, because RegionId is an enum of six DATA DIVISION sections and carries no program -- two programs' WORKING_STORAGE@100 are the same extent and may_alias would conflate them. Slicing by program keeps every may_alias/must_cover inside one program's storage and needs no change to vendored cobol_memory. Re-entry rule is one rule for three cases: never traverse an edge back to a node already on the current path's stack -- that is unroll-once for loops, allows a paragraph PERFORMed twice sequentially, and handles recursive PERFORM and LINK cycles. Branch choice is a per-node cursor, global across paths, so the sampling is deterministic and reproducible. Reuses build_program, statement_index, transfer.py, state.py's write/reaching (join never called), cell_index, commarea_aliases, extent_text.byte_range, and query.py's rebase arithmetic.
acceptance_criteria: cobble-fields-trace PROGRAM --field NAME --asg-dir DIR reports witnessed flows per path with the crossing route, plus a branch-coverage line. Crosses a LINK into a callee with no artefact present. LINK resumes at the call site, XCTL does not. A loop body runs once. A paragraph PERFORMed twice in one path is entered twice. fixpoint.py, transfer.py, state.py, aliases.py, build_corpus.py and query.py unchanged. fp-lint zero on the new module, ruff clean, black clean, 11/11 import contracts.
notes:
Shape: a targeted CLI, `cobble-fields-trace PROGRAM --asg-dir DIR --out FILE [--paths N] [--coverage F] [--max-depth N]`. No artefact, no table, no contract -- it reads the ASG cache directly, which is what lets it enter a callee `aliases.jsonl` has no rows for.

No `--field` flag, and there could not be one. The walk emulates all of memory and reports all of it: `transfer` writes whatever a statement writes, and tracking one field means tracking everything reaching it, which is everything. Filtering the report is grep's job on a file already grouped by extent.

Two modules, not one: `trace.py` for the walk (knows nothing about text) and `trace_report.py` for rendering plus argparse. `query.py` in the same directory is the counter-example -- it reached ~1000 lines by fusing a walk with its output format.

The payload is `defined at`, and no existing artefact can say it: the node whose write last put those bytes there on this path, in whichever program that was. It comes from `state.reaching` against the slice as it stood BEFORE the statement, which is the store's whole reason to exist -- `transfer.writes_of` never reads the in-state, so without that read the walk would merely restate each statement.

A `Frame` is one open invocation (program, site, resume, crossing, returns, window, visited), popped whole on return. That is what makes the one re-entry rule -- never traverse an edge to a node an open frame already visited -- come out right in all three cases: a loop back edge is refused (unroll-once); a paragraph PERFORMed twice sequentially is allowed, because the first frame took its visited set with it; recursion and LINK cycles are refused with no extra machinery. The path root is a frame like any other, so the stack is never empty while running.
close_reason: Path-sampling byte trace shipped: cobble/cobble/dataflow/fields/trace.py (walk) + trace_report.py (render + CLI), entry point cobble-fields-trace. Commits b765acf 1429be9 88c075e adf7c52 9768933.

title: A crossing answer cannot tell an external origin from an absence
description: A range whose only writer is a READ INTO from a file and a range nothing writes at all produce the identical crossing answer: the same landings, and nothing saying where the walk ran out. A reader cannot tell 'the data comes from outside the program' from 'nothing writes this'. The synthetic sources are already in the graph (FILE:, .LITERAL, %CICS-STATE, %CALL:), so a terminal frontier entry whose only inbound flows come from one of them is nameable -- but naming it needs a channel, and the query-time stop layer that would have carried one was deleted on 2026-09-07 for being unreadable. Whatever replaces it has to be legible to a human first: one short phrase per landing at most, not a ten-reason verdict tuple. Named in the README's limits list.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: Deviation accepted by the user on 2026-09-07: shipping without the spec's third termination category (a named external origin) is a known gap, not an oversight. Named in the cobble README limits list. Build it here when picked up.

title: cd cobble && make lint is red with 433 pre-existing pyright errors, so the gate cannot be used
description: The premise moved: `cd cobble && make lint` no longer exists (cobble has no Makefile, and its vestigial standalone .pre-commit-config.yaml -- whose pyright hook was `uv run pyright || true` and could never fail -- was deleted in commit 258996a9). cobble is now inside the root blocking pyright gate: cobble/cobble and cobble/tests are in pyrightconfig.json's include and in the pre-commit pyright hook's files pattern, scoped to staged files, so touching a file obliges fixing that file's errors while the rest of the backlog does not block unrelated commits. What remains of this bead is the backlog itself: 436 pre-existing pyright errors across cobble as of 258996a9, which makes any whole-package pyright run red and unusable as a gate. Either burn it down or scope a green whole-package target. Same shape as red-dragon-forge-mp5 for fp-lint.
notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-26 (main @ 06076ac), and the headline number was mostly an artefact.

`uv run --no-sync pyright` reported **14,483 errors**. 13,712 of them (94%) were in `cicada/cics/cics_grammar/` -- ANTLR-generated code (every .py there is 'Generated from ... by ANTLR 4.13.1'; 13,698 in CICSzParser.py alone, plus a dead `typing.io` import that Python 3.13 removed). `fp.json` excludes that directory; `pyrightconfig.json` did not. Because the pre-commit pyright hook is blocking and files:-scoped, staging anything in cics_grammar/ made a commit impossible.

Fixed by adding `**/cics_grammar/**` to pyrightconfig.json's exclude. Real total: **771 errors**, and the run went from 33.1s to 8.2s.

Cobble's own share is **423**, close to the 436 this bead recorded -- so the number here was right; what was wrong was the impression that a whole-package pyright run is hopeless.

**363 of cobble's 423 are one pattern in one file**: `cobble/tests/dataflow/srccfg/test_statement_index.py` reads `.targets`/`.name` off a 33-member statement union across 11 lines, and pyright reports once per union member that lacks the attribute. Filed as red-dragon-forge-76s. Fix it and cobble's total falls to roughly 60, which turns this bead's 'burn it down or scope a green whole-package target' into a small decision rather than a campaign. Re-measure before choosing.

The 66-error tail outside the big clusters is red-dragon-forge-jip.

title: overlaps sits where covers is the honest rule in frontier pruning and landing supersession
description:
Two reporting decisions in cobble/cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/query.py prune on overlap where coverage is the sound test, and both lose bytes from the published answer. (1) _fresh (query.py:632) drops a frontier candidate that a seen entry merely OVERLAPS, so bytes nothing has reached are never explored. This is the rule that makes a callee repacking its whole commarea (MOVE CALLEE-REC TO DFHCOMMAREA) lose its write-back: the repack lands on bytes the inbound hop already stood on, so the return direction is pruned even though it carries different content. The two-program synthetic writes back through a narrower reference-modified target to sidestep exactly this. (2) _add_if_not_superseded (query.py:670) drops a landing that a kept entry merely overlaps, so uncovered bytes vanish from the answer. The supersession rule is the minimum-hops cost model, so changing either rule changes frontier growth and the landing set. _within (query.py:388), over ByteRange.covers, already shows the honest shape. Needs its own measured piece of work, not a word swap.

(Corrected: _fresh's rule is no longer shared with reaches()' _unseen — _unseen at query.py:497 is now a separate predicate over (id, range) pairs while _fresh takes (id, range, hops) and re-admits a cheaper arrival, so a change to _fresh does not move reaches().)
notes: The _fresh drop is now REPORTED rather than silent: _pruned emits 'pruned by overlap at PROGRAM:node' for any arrival overlap pruning dropped whose bytes no cheaper-or-equal entry covers (_uncovered), so the repack shape names the statement it lost instead of returning stops: (). That is a disclosure, not the fix -- the answer is still short a landing, and this bead still owns the arithmetic. test_a_whole_record_write_back_names_the_statement_it_was_pruned_at pins the reported-not-silent behaviour and is what must change when the predicate does.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: The 'now REPORTED rather than silent' note is obsolete as of 2026-09-07: the query-time stop layer was deleted at the user's direction, so _pruned and its 'pruned by overlap at PROGRAM:node' line are gone. The _fresh drop is silent again, and the repack shape is pinned only by a landings-absence assertion in test_a_whole_record_write_back_does_not_reach_the_callers_sink. The pruning arithmetic this bead is about is unchanged.

title: FieldStore.aliases is unindexed, so a crossing walk rescans every alias row per hop
description: aliases is the one FieldStore member that is not indexed. across() scans every alias row per call, and the crossing walk calls it once per frontier entry per level. Measured 18 s for a 2-hop walk on a 931-program synthetic; tolerable for an analysis CLI, which is why it shipped. An index by caller fixes it. dead_ends(), the second unindexed scan this bead originally counted, was deleted with the query-time stop layer on 2026-09-07, so an index by callee is no longer needed for it. Note a later measurement attributed a ~1 s regression at --depth 4 hops=1 on 2400 aliases to a different change and was corrected: the cost is this scan.

title: extent.py's _placements collapses a record name declared in two sections
description: _placements keys placements by record name alone, so a program declaring the same 01 name in WORKING-STORAGE and in the LINKAGE SECTION collapses the two. A WORKING-STORAGE cell can then be published with a linkage extent (or the reverse), which silently misplaces every byte offset downstream -- extents, flows, and the commarea rebase all read those extents as region coordinates. The key needs the section origin as well as the name.

title: Add a WebGL render target for the source CFG
description:
cobble-srccfg-dot is the only way to look at a source CFG, and graphviz dot does not finish on a closure-sized graph: 6638 nodes / 9468 edges ran past 12 minutes and was killed, while sfdp lays the same graph out in ~5 seconds. depgraph/render.py already reuses knowledge_graph's sfdp layout plus the sigma.js page for the variable dependency graph; the source CFG needs the same target so a closure can be looked at at all.

Node labels and the cross-program CALL edge are already computed in dot.py (LABELS, _qualified, _entries, _call_nodes) and must be shared rather than duplicated, so the two renderers cannot disagree about what a node is called. Colours stay per-renderer: dot.py's fills are pale graphviz pastels that vanish on the WebGL page's white background.
design: New cobble/dataflow/srccfg/webgl.py plus a cobble-srccfg-webgl entry point mirroring cobble-srccfg-dot's --cfg/--output surface, with a --program filter for one member out of a closure. Shared node naming/labelling extracted out of dot.py into its own module that both renderers import. Own saturated node/edge palette; cross-program CALL edges get their own kind so the legend names them.
acceptance_criteria: cobble-srccfg-webgl --cfg <closure.json> --output <page.html> writes a self-contained page for the largest member's closure in seconds; dot.py and webgl.py agree on every node label because both read one module; cobble suite, pyright, lint-imports and Black all green.
close_reason: Delivered: srccfg/webgl.py renders the source CFG as a self-contained sfdp+sigma.js page, alongside the existing dot.py target.

title: ASG bridge: emit the PROCEDURE DIVISION USING list
description:
AsgSerializer.java emits linkage_fields for a program but never the PROCEDURE DIVISION USING phrase, so nothing downstream can bind a CALL's argument position i to the callee parameter it lands on. srccfg/synthetic.py papers over this with a positional placeholder (%USING[i]), which names a position, not a field.

Without the USING list, the only way to resolve position i is to assume the LINKAGE SECTION's level-01 declaration order IS the USING order. That is wrong wherever LINKAGE declares items USING omits, or orders them differently, and a guess is indistinguishable from a fact in an artefact consumers trust.

Blocks extending cross-program byte dataflow (see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-cross-program-commarea-dataflow-design.md, which scopes static CALL out for exactly this reason) to static CALL ... USING. The commarea path needs nothing from this: a commarea has one implicit parameter, so there is no position to bind. Not urgent for the corpus in hand, which has zero CallStatement.
acceptance_criteria: The serialised ASG carries, per program, the ordered USING parameter names with their BY REFERENCE / BY CONTENT / BY VALUE mode and any OMITTED slots, distinguishable from the LINKAGE declaration order. A consumer can resolve argument position i to a named callee field without consulting LINKAGE order.
notes: Work lands in the bridge under vendor/red-dragon, which is never modified from this repo -- file upstream and consume the result here.
close_reason: Already done. The bridge emits procedure_using (red-dragon 415d7c64: 'a called program binds its parameters in USING order'); cobol_asg CobolASG.procedure_using carries it through the parse cache; cobble fields/aliases.py binds CALL ... USING arguments to callee parameters by position (cobble 14e323d). Verified 2026-10-05 on CardDemo: aliases.jsonl has 15 bound CALL rows (COACTUPC, CORPT00C, COTRN02C -> CSUTLDTC, one per argument).

title: srccfg reaching_conditions does not finish in 10 minutes on the largest corpus members
description:
reaching_conditions on the largest cached member (~3900 nodes) ran past 600s without returning and was abandoned. Measured cost scaling on smaller members, with max_paths held at the default 64 unless stated:

  237 nodes: 0.06s at cap 64, 42s at cap 4096
  830 nodes: 0.65s at cap 64, 129s at cap 4096
  1692 nodes: 1.1s at cap 64, 99s at cap 4096

So cost grows roughly 10x per 4x cap, and superlinearly in node count. The pass is usable at the default cap up to ~2000 nodes and not above it.

Not a correctness bug: the answers it does produce are sound, and the cap is reported. Filed so the ceiling is written down rather than rediscovered. Deliberately not fixed alongside the frame model and resume work.

Fix directions, unevaluated: memoise per (node, stack, seen) rather than re-walking; collapse walks whose guard and frame are equal before expanding them; or make the cap a per-program budget rather than a per-node one.
acceptance_criteria: A named ceiling: either the largest member completes in a stated time, or the pass declines the member up front with a reason rather than hanging.

title: srccfg models no STOP RUN / GOBACK, so every paragraph falls through to the next
description:
build.py:_fallthru() pairs every consecutive paragraph via pairwise(order) unconditionally. Nothing in asg_types.py, desugar.py, cfg.py or statements.py handles STOP RUN, GOBACK or EXIT PROGRAM (verified by grep: zero occurrences).

Consequence: control runs off the entry paragraph's #end through EVERY subsequent paragraph in declaration order, forever. On any whole program this top-level cascade reaches every node, so:

1. Genuine dead code is currently inexpressible. A paragraph nothing performs and nothing runs into still gets guards from the cascade, so reaching_conditions cannot report it and query.py's 'unreachable from <program> entry' line can essentially never fire on a real member.
2. Reaching.abandoned is empty on every whole-program fixture, because a node cannot have zero guards when the cascade reaches it. The set still works on hand-built graphs, which is where its remaining test coverage lives.
3. A performed paragraph legitimately gets a second activation (once performed, once cascaded into), which inflates arrivals against the path cap.

Fix direction: a terminator statement ends its paragraph's flow -- no FALLTHRU out of the #end that follows it, and for STOP RUN no RETURN either. That is a builder change, not a walk change.

Reported effects are consequences, not separate bugs: red-dragon-forge-a3d's measured over-report of 'abandoned' stopped reproducing once the frame model plus this cascade gave the following paragraph guards, and will reappear the moment terminators are modelled.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A program whose entry paragraph ends in STOP RUN does not reach the paragraphs after it. 2. A paragraph nothing performs and nothing falls into reports zero guards and is NOT named abandoned. 3. reaching_conditions on a synthetic program with a terminator produces a non-empty 'unreachable' set.
notes:
Fixed in desugar.py, not build.py. A terminator lowers to the same node as any other statement MINUS its exit: _terminator() = replace(_plain(...), exits=()), registered for StopRunStatement/GobackStatement/ExitProgramStatement. Exits are what seq() and build.py already sequence on, so one subtraction settles everything -- seq gives each exit the next statement's entry (so the rest of the paragraph goes unreachable) and _paragraph_cfg gives a paragraph's exits its #end (so #end is unreachable, severing BOTH the FALLTHRU to the next paragraph and the RETURN hanging off that end). _fallthru() is unchanged and still pairs every consecutive paragraph; deciding it there would mean asking whether the LAST statement terminates, which is the wrong question when it sits in one arm of an IF.

Two corrections to the fix direction recorded above. (1) All three verbs are treated alike -- the note said STOP RUN loses its RETURN but GOBACK might keep it. GOBACK/EXIT PROGRAM in a subprogram return to whatever CALLed the program, never to the PERFORM that reached the paragraph, so no PERFORM of such a paragraph comes back in any of the three cases. (2) No new NodeKind: the node stays a NOP carrying transfer GOBACK/STOPRUN/EXITPROGRAM, which _plain already produced.

Plain EXIT is deliberately NOT a terminator: it is the no-op sentinel at the end of a PERFORM THRU range and outnumbers the real terminators 77256 to 2380 in the reference corpus. Treating it as one would cut most of a program in half. Tests pin this.

One imprecision kept on purpose: a PERFORM of a paragraph ending in a terminator keeps its FLOW edge, so the statement after the PERFORM still gets a guard although it is genuinely dead. The walk refuses a call's FLOW only when it predicts a RETURN instead, and here it cannot, since nothing reaches the paragraph's #end. Refusing it would zero the rest of the program; keeping it over-approximates in the direction link.py chose for XCTL.

Measured on 12 real members (2 larger ones exceed the 45s two-arm budget): zero-guard nodes 41->74, of which the REPORTABLE finding (zero guards and not abandoned) goes 26->63, while abandoned falls 15->11. Runtime unchanged or slightly better. The rise in zero-guard nodes is the point -- the cascade was giving dead paragraphs guards.

Tests: tests/dataflow/srccfg/test_desugar_terminator.py, 16 cases, all three verbs parametrised. Full cobble suite 1094 passed / 12 skipped, pyright 0, Black clean.
close_reason: Terminator model landed in desugar.py; 16 tests; measured on real members

title: no source position on any dataflow answer: statements and declarations carry no line
description: Positions now exist; what is missing is that the dataflow answers do not carry them. The bridge serialises line_start/col_start/line_end/col_end on every statement (StatementSerializer.java:157-163) and line_start on declarations (DataFieldSerializer), cobol_asg carries a SourceSpan, and srccfg's cfg.Node carries one with source_file. The fields dataflow artefacts did not follow: cobble/cobble/dataflow/fields/emit.py:79,161 writes a flow row whose only locator is still the node id (PARAGRAPH/ordinal), and extents.jsonl carries no 'declared at'. The copybook hazard the bead named is also unresolved: Main.java still parses the preprocessed (COPY-expanded) stream and no line map back to the original exists, so every serialised line is an expanded-stream line, silently wrong in any member with a copybook. Either label them honestly as listing lines alongside a kept listing artefact, or build the line map (cobol_imports already scans COPY lexically with line numbers). Bridge and cobol_asg are upstream (vendor/red-dragon, never modified here), and any change invalidates the whole ASG cache.
acceptance_criteria: A writer or reader reported by the fields query names a position a human can open, and the position is either a line in the original source file or explicitly labelled as a line in a listing artefact that ships with it.

title: python-fp-lint pre-commit hook tracks a mutable ref and rejects committed code
description: The blocking hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml pins 'rev: main'. Its ruleset has moved past the tree: linting HEAD's own committed cobble/cobble/dataflow/ yields 163 violations, and knowledge_graph/export.py fails on an unrelated import-sort rule. pre-commit only lints staged files, so the drift is invisible until you touch a file, then blocks a commit over code you did not write. Most of the volume is no-object-type on 'object' annotations at JSON boundaries -- the same situation that already earned asg_walk.py an explicit exclude, since 'object' is what pyright needs there.
acceptance_criteria: Either the hook pins an immutable rev, or the package's existing violations are resolved, so that committing an unrelated change to cobble/cobble/ does not fail on pre-existing code.
notes:
Narrowed and partly deferred, 2026-09-06.

Correction to the correction, 2026-09-06: no-object-type DOES fire. My earlier
