title: naming tie-break picks a REDEFINES alias over the record the statement named
description: naming.smallest_covering ranks candidates by (length, -level, -len(path), name) -- smallest, then deepest. A record and a REDEFINES child of the same size tie on length, so the deeper alias wins and becomes the edge's endpoint id, even when the statement itself named the outer record. Verified on synthetic COBOL: a group move whose source_extent reads 'SRC-REC@...' gets the endpoint id of the level-05 field inside its redefinition. Bounded: source_extent still spells the right name and every query predicate joins on ranges, so no flow answer changes -- only the human-readable endpoint column, which is the traceability surface. Fix: when a covering cell's name equals extent.field_name, that name wins the tie.
acceptance_criteria: A flow whose extent names a record reports that record as its endpoint id, even when a same-sized REDEFINES child covers the identical bytes. test_fields_synthetic's backward-walk assertion names the record rather than the alias.
notes:
Fixed, plus the recovery surface the fix implies.

naming._rank now takes the extent's own field_name and ranks a name match second,
below the length and above the level. Below the length on purpose: a whole-field
reference already lands in the minimum-length group, and a reference modification
(SRC-REC(2:3) naming eight bytes for three) must still lose to the smaller field
the bytes actually are.

The fix only decides which of several names over one range the artefact keys on,
so it needed a way to recover the others. Added FieldStore.overlapping(ranges) +
the 'overlapping' CLI query: every declared name sharing any of the given bytes,
whole or in part. It is the only predicate with no level gate and no total
containment, which is what lets it answer the two cases containment cannot -- an
equal-level REDEFINES alias, reported by neither contains nor within, and a range
straddling two records, contained by neither. An endpoint id is therefore a label,
not a claim: 30% of ranges are owned by more than one declared name.

Also converted the fields query dispatch from string literals to a Query enum, so
a question added without an arm to answer it is a pyright error rather than a
silent fall through the wildcard case; the wildcard is gone.

Verified: cobble suite 1072 passed / 12 skipped, pyright 0 errors, 11/11 import
contracts, Black clean. Synthetic-COBOL tests assert overlapping against the
bridge's own levels and offsets, not a fixture's.
close_reason: Tie-break fixed and the label-not-a-claim surface (overlapping) shipped with it; see notes.

title: fields artefacts do not record whether a member settled
description: The sweep budget can run out while the fixpoint state is still growing. When it does, the run says so on stderr and counts it in the stdout summary's 'unsettled', but no artefact row carries it. A consumer reading defs.jsonl on its own cannot tell a definer set is partial, so it reports a confident provenance answer over a subset of the paths. Measured: definer totals 806 / 2764 / 3383 at 1 / 2 / 3 sweeps on a real member, while edges.jsonl was byte-identical across all three -- flows converge in one forward pass, reaching definitions need a pass per back edge.
acceptance_criteria: A defs.jsonl (or a sibling manifest) consumer can determine, without reading the run's log, whether the definer sets for a given program are exhaustive.

title: fp-lint backlog blocks commits that touch fields/srccfg
description: Scoped down: three of this bead's four findings have moved or been resolved. (1) dataflow/fields/fixpoint.py is now cobble/cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/fixpoint.py (commit b9af2b6a) and is excluded in fp.json:41 -- that deferral is tracked by forge-uar, not here. (2) The srccfg fp-lint backlog was cleared in commit 912e405d; fp.json's explicit-stack exclusion covers cobble/cobble/dataflow/srccfg/worklist.py (:39), while dataflow/srccfg/order.py's depth_first_order is neither excluded nor confirmed still failing -- re-measure before acting. (3) knowledge_graph/graph_writer.py's no-object-type on `*exc: object` in __exit__ (cobble/cobble/knowledge_graph/graph_writer.py:144) is unchanged and unexcluded: it has no fix that also satisfies no-optional-none. What is left: decide whether order.py still trips the iterative-traversal rules and, if so, exclude it with the rationale worklist.py/asg_walk.py already set a precedent for, and settle graph_writer.py's __exit__. Also still open: five low-severity Talisman false positives on commit 52027d0 (function signatures and docstrings) that .talismanrc deliberately does not carry.
notes:
Beware a false-negative check: fp-lint's rule set is path-scoped via fp.json, so linting a copy of a file from outside the configured trees reports 'No violations found' regardless of content. Verified by control: the working graph_writer.py, which the hook rejects, lints clean when copied elsewhere. Always lint the real repo-relative path.
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-26 (main @ 06076ac): whole-workspace fp-lint is **1,171 violations across 35 distinct rules** (`--config fp.json` over cicada squall jackal red_dragon_forge cobble tools tests).

This bead's remaining two questions are unchanged and still need answering: whether `cobble/cobble/dataflow/srccfg/order.py`'s depth_first_order still trips the iterative-traversal rules, and how `knowledge_graph/graph_writer.py:144`'s `*exc: object` in __exit__ settles.

Coverage context this bead now sits in: the rules no live bead named are filed as red-dragon-forge-2lt (no-list-dict-param-annotation, 335 -- the single biggest bucket, 305 of them in jackal's idcams parser) and red-dragon-forge-nzj (the remaining 26 rules, 209 violations). `invalid-syntax` x3 turned out not to be debt at all -- ruff is parsing jackal as Python 3.11, so PEP 695 type aliases read as syntax errors and the rest of those files go unlinted: red-dragon-forge-3h4.

Your notes' warning about path-scoped false negatives was carried into all three.

title: A file-verb write can carry an empty FILE: origin
description:
Some file-verb writes reach the artefact with the origin string 'FILE:' -- the prefix with no file name after it. Observed on a single member: 4 of 19 file-origin writes.

Two producers build that string. _read_writes (dataflow/fields/transfer.py:325) uses statement.file_name from a native ReadStatement; _cics_origin (line 369) uses _option(statement, 'FILE') from the dialect-parsed EXEC CICS form, and _option returns the empty string whenever the key is absent or not a CicsOperand.

An origin that says only 'a file wrote this' cannot be joined to the file node, so the interprocedural view loses the edge from the record to the program that read it. Establish which of the two producers is responsible (the affected statements should say), then either recover the name from whatever option actually carries it, or make the unresolved case say so explicitly rather than emitting a truncated name that reads as valid.
acceptance_criteria: No emitted origin is a bare kind prefix. An origin whose name could not be resolved states that, and is distinguishable from a resolved one.

title: Cut srccfg query to guards+coassign, rename entry point, add provenance
description: cobble-srccfg exposed four verbs (writers, guards, derivation, coassign). The bare entry-point name reads as the stage main when it is one of three (cobble-srccfg-build, cobble-srccfg-dot), so rename to cobble-srccfg-query. Drop writers and derivation: both are single-direction, name-keyed provenance, superseded by one provenance verb that closes backward and forward over def_use/reaching_definitions and carries guards. writers_of and base_field stay -- coassign uses them.
design: Provenance is name-keyed, not extent-keyed, so an implicit group write (INITIALIZE GROUP, EXEC CICS READ INTO GROUP) is filed under the group name and will not surface under a child field name. Accepted for the first cut: srccfg carries guards and control dependencies, which the fields graph does not, and that is the reason to build it here. The extent-aware counterpart over fields edges.jsonl is a separate follow-up.
close_reason: Landed in 52027d0 (fields source_node + sweep budget + determinism) and the srccfg cut/rename in the same commit; pushed to origin/main.

title: cobble-fields requires an explicit member selection: --member or --all
description:
The stage currently always globs the whole ASG cache. The intended use is per-program and on demand -- investigating individual fields in one program and its related programs -- so a whole-corpus pass must be asked for, not defaulted into.

Exactly one of --member (one or more member names) and --all is required. Both together is a usage error; neither is a usage error. A named member the cache does not hold exits 2 before any analysis, because a coverage figure over the remaining members answers a question nobody asked.
acceptance_criteria: Neither flag and both flags are argparse usage errors; --member analyses only the named members; a named member absent from the cache exits 2; --all keeps the whole-cache behaviour; README and the exit-status table say so.
close_reason: Closed

title: One-pass mode for field dataflow, fixpoint as the opt-in correct mode
description:
A single reverse-postorder pass over the CFG -- each node processed once, never re-enqueued -- gives the provenance the intended use actually wants, at a fraction of the fixpoint's cost. The fixpoint stays the default; one-pass is a flag.

What one pass loses is narrow and nameable: loop-carried flow only. Straight-line and branching provenance is complete after one pass. An accumulator inside a PERFORM (ADD X TO WS-SUM) would show its initialising write and not the value arriving on the back edge. Everything else is unaffected.

Raised by the user 2026-09-06: 'even 1-pass is usually enough to get provenance of the sort i am looking for, but sure fixpoint is the correct-er version.'
design:
Sound as an under-approximation, which is what makes it worth having. Dropping back edges gives every node a smaller entry state; the transfer is monotone, so reaching() returns a subset of the true source set and write()'s kills only remove what is present. One pass therefore MISSES edges and never invents one -- every emitted def-use pair is real. Both directions come from the same output: filter on target for what fed a field, on source for where it went.

Exactly what is lost: a read preceding its feeding write inside a loop body, and accumulator recurrence (ADD X TO Y in a loop loses the Y-from-Y edge). Flow out of a loop survives, because the exit edge is forward. For online programs whose provenance is straight-line MOVE chains through a shared communication area, the loss is small.

Not implementable as 'cap at one dequeue per node'. It needs REVERSE POSTORDER visiting so every predecessor settles before the node -- the current queue is FIFO (fixpoint.py:199), and a single FIFO sweep would leave arbitrary predecessors unprocessed and drop forward flow as well. So the change is an ordering plus an identified back-edge set.

Report the count of ignored back edges per member. Zero means the pass was exact for that program; a large count is the signal to re-run under the fixpoint. Without that count the mode repeats the red-dragon-forge-9fa failure -- a partial answer that looks complete.

Cost, measured against a 3919-node member: about 3919 transfers versus roughly 400k dequeues to converge. Seconds against tens of minutes. Cheaper than the widening in red-dragon-forge-1f5 and answers the common question; widening remains the way to get the loop-carried answer under a bound.
acceptance_criteria: A flag selects one-pass; a program whose only unresolved flow is loop-carried shows the difference between the two modes in a test; the mode used appears in the JSON summary.
notes: Redacted 2026-09-07: corpus program, file, field and paragraph names replaced with stable pseudonyms (PROG-*, FILE-*, MST-*, SCR-*, BUF-*, LAY-*, MSG-*). Measured numbers and source line references are unchanged. The mapping and the pre-redaction text are in .knowledge_graph_scratch/ (untracked, per-machine).
close_reason: Landed in 52027d0 (fields source_node + sweep budget + determinism) and the srccfg cut/rename in the same commit; pushed to origin/main.

title: Field dataflow per-program latency is superlinear in write count
description: Same defect, corrected path: the intra-program byte-extent fixpoint now lives at cobble/cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/fixpoint.py (moved out of cobble/dataflow/fields/ in commit b9af2b6a). It costs 1.5-24s per member against ~1s for the ASG cache load, and scales superlinearly with the number of writes: 84 writes cost 1.6s, 281 writes cost 23s. One member ran over four minutes. The metric that matters is per-program latency, not corpus throughput: the intended use is dataflow for one named program and its related programs, on demand, not a whole-corpus pass. 24s is tolerable interactively; four minutes is not, and the shape of the curve says there are worse members. Measured 2026-09-06 during Task 7 of the intra-program plan, by timing CobolASG.from_dict and analysed() separately over a 20-member sample (first 12 in sorted order plus the 8 largest ASGs). Coverage is not the problem: sampled members resolve 97-100% of their writes.
design: Suspect the per-node state is copied rather than shared, so a member with N writes and M nodes pays O(N*M) copying on top of the iteration count. Profile before choosing between a persistent map for the state, narrowing the join to changed extents, or a coarser first pass. Do NOT relax the coverage floor to compensate; the floor measures reach and this is a cost problem.
acceptance_criteria: A member with ~280 writes analyses in under 3s, and the worst member in a sample of 50 stays under 30s.

title: cobble: no shared walk over nested ASG statements
description: A shared walk now exists -- cobble/cobble/asg_walk.py's `descend` -- but only one consumer reads it. cobble/cobble/dataflow/fields/transfer.py:33 imports it; cobble/cobble/dataflow/srccfg/desugar.py (nesting keys hard-coded at :70-71, :442, :616) and cobble/cobble/dataflow/depgraph/graph.py:143 (only "children", "else_children") still reimplement descent, each enumerating the keys it happens to know, so a statement form the bridge learns later is silently skipped by whichever was not updated. Measured cost of getting it wrong: a one-level walk sees 36% of MOVE statements on the current corpus. The third consumer this bead named, diagnosis/asg_operands.py, was deleted in commit b9d5db79. Remaining work: repoint desugar.py and depgraph/graph.py onto asg_walk.descend.
design: Prefer a whole-document stack walk over a key enumeration. Enumerating keys is what produced the defect; 'whens' and 'not_invalid_key' are not names anyone guesses. No dict outside a statement list carries a statement 'type', so a whole-document walk cannot over-count.
notes: Raised from P3 on the final whole-branch review's judgment. A fifth independent ASG descent was written during the re-measurement, which is the evidence that four was already past the point where the next author writes their own rather than finding one. Best fixed as the FIRST task of the plan that builds cobble/dataflow/fields/, since that plan needs a descent anyway and would otherwise add a sixth. cobble/cobble/diagnosis/asg_operands.py:_move_operands is the reference shape: depth-agnostic over every mapping value and non-string sequence element, no enumeration of nesting keys.

title: Unit of work over recoverable VSAM: SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK and abend backout do not undo file changes
description:
SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK lowers to __cics_rollback_hook (strategy.py:1230, :974) and no longer abends UNSP; a composed SQL runtime (squall) can undo its pending unit of work through that hook.

What is NOT done, and is all that remains of this bead: VSAM has no unit-of-work bookkeeping, so a rollback cannot discard uncommitted VSAM writes. strategy.py:127-134 records the current stance — the VSAM engine writes through at the point of WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE, so ROLLBACK has nothing to undo there. Decide whether that stance stands or whether VSAM writes must become deferrable (same bookkeeping forge-urh's commit side would need); if the stance stands, close this bead.
acceptance_criteria: A task that writes a VSAM record then issues SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK leaves the file as it was before the write, asserted by reading the record back.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): Rescoped 2026-10-05. The verb is no longer unimplemented: strategy._lower_syncpoint_rollback emits __cics_rollback_hook, which is a no-op by default (strategy.py register_default) and does real work only when squall is composed in. VsamEngine writes through on WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE, so neither SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK nor an abending task can back out VSAM changes, which CICS does for recoverable files. Census: SYNCPOINT 24 statements in 23 programs, 16 programs with ROLLBACK, used to compensate partially applied multi-file updates. Also affects every task that abends after updating a recoverable file. Structural: needs a unit-of-work log over the VSAM engine (before-images per task, committed at SYNCPOINT or normal task end, applied in reverse on ROLLBACK or abend), composed with squall's unit of work so both commit or both back out.

title: MOVE CORRESPONDING cannot express operands in two different sections
description:
lower_move_corresponding (interpreter/cobol/lower_arithmetic.py:610) takes ONE DataLayout and ONE Register and uses them for both source and destination. statement_dispatch.py:100 always passes the WORKING-STORAGE pair, with the comment 'uses first WS section'.

So MOVE CORRESPONDING LK-REC TO WS-REC — the common shape, copying a LINKAGE record into working storage — fails. Verified by probe:

  KeyError: "Group not found in layout: 'LK-REC'"

Loud, not silent: it raises rather than corrupting, which is why this is P2 and not P1 like the CALL bug (forge-how) it was found alongside.

FIX SHAPE: resolve each operand's group and region independently. _find_group_and_reg (lower_arithmetic.py:634) already does exactly this — it walks local_storage, working_storage, linkage, file and returns the matching (layout, reg) pair — so the change is to give lower_move_corresponding a per-operand (layout, region) and drop the single-pair signature. ArithmeticCorrespondingStatement already routes through the multi-section path, so the two CORRESPONDING forms would then agree.
acceptance_criteria: MOVE CORRESPONDING from a LINKAGE group to a WORKING-STORAGE group copies matching leaves correctly, asserted on an executed program; the reverse direction works too.

title: Conditions outside the raisable nine are registered but never raised
description:
cics/conditions.py CONDITION_CODES carries 21 names; RAISABLE carries ten — the nine the production corpus codes (NOTOPEN, NOTFND, INVREQ, ERROR, LENGERR, MAPFAIL, NOSPACE, DUPKEY, DUPREC) plus DISABLED, which VsamEngine returns for a file with no FCT entry. HANDLE CONDITION for any of the other eleven — ITEMERR, PGMIDERR, TRANSIDERR, ENDDATA, ILLOGIC, ENDFILE, IOERR, EOF, TERMIDERR, FILENOTFOUND and so on — writes the handler slot but leaves DFH-RAISABLE 'N', so the handler never fires and the program is not told.

Decide per condition: raise it, or reject the registration at compile time. Silently accepting a registration that cannot fire is the failure mode this work exists to remove.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the eleven non-raisable conditions is either raised by the runtime or rejected at compile time with a message naming it.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): Raised P3 -> P2. HANDLE CONDITION ENDFILE in 60 programs and QIDERR in 25 never fire (not raisable), and IGNORE CONDITION ENDFILE/ENDDATA/QIDERR appears in 401/210/41 programs. A browse loop that leaves via HANDLE CONDITION ENDFILE does not terminate. Note the code comment in conditions.py calls RAISABLE 'the ones the production corpus codes HANDLE CONDITION for'; this census has ENDFILE, ITEMERR, QIDERR, ENDDATA, RTEFAIL, SYSIDERR in HANDLE CONDITION too.

title: Recover strip precision for mutually-exclusive REDEFINES views
description:
layout.py denies a strip to any table whose ancestry is aliased, because two strips over one piece of storage would let a write through either view go unseen by a read through the other. Sound, but it costs 36% of tables their row strip.

Most of that loss is benign: the dominant shape is a constant table whose parent redefines a run of FILLER VALUE literals, and collapsing it to 'one of these entries' is arguably the correct provenance. 38 cases in a 300-program sample are not benign. They are one buffer carrying several alternative layouts, one per transaction:

    10 BUF-OUT REDEFINES BUF-IN.
       15 BUF-VIEW-A.
          20 BUF-ENTRY-A OCCURS 400 TIMES.
       15 BUF-VIEW-B REDEFINES BUF-VIEW-A.
          20 BUF-ENTRY-B OCCURS 100 TIMES.
       15 BUF-VIEW-C REDEFINES BUF-VIEW-A.
          20 BUF-ENTRY-C OCCURS 300 TIMES.

These views are mutually exclusive in time -- a given invocation uses exactly one -- so a 400-row contract table collapsing to a single weak span loses real precision for nothing gained. Same shape in MEMBER-V3, MEMBER-V2, MEMBER-V1.

layout.py cannot fix this, because which view is live is a flow fact and layout sees only declarations. The fix is to keep the strips and carry explicit alias edges between them, letting the dataflow pass kill the views a function code rules out. Depends on the worklist fixpoint (ujr) existing first.

Do not attempt this before measuring whether it matters: if the analysis never reaches these commarea tables with a precise-enough subscript, the strips buy nothing.
notes: Redacted 2026-09-07: corpus program, file, field and paragraph names replaced with stable pseudonyms (PROG-*, FILE-*, MST-*, SCR-*, BUF-*, LAY-*, MSG-*). Measured numbers and source line references are unchanged. The mapping and the pre-redaction text are in .knowledge_graph_scratch/ (untracked, per-machine).
close_reason: Moot: layout.py no longer has strips. Materialising every OCCURS occurrence puts all of a record's fields in one flat coordinate space, so the BUF alternative-layout tables keep every row -- BUF-ENTRY-A(7) is its own cell at offset 4+6*9, and its overlap with BUF-IN is plain interval overlap needing no alias edge. The 36% precision loss this bead was filed to recover never happens.

title: INTO buffers truncate silently instead of raising LENGERR
description:
Every builtin that fills a program's INTO area does 'data[:length]' and reports NORMAL, so a record or start-payload longer than the receiving field is silently cut and the program cannot tell. Real CICS raises LENGERR (DFHRESP 22) for exactly this, and sets EIBRESP accordingly.

Affects the whole Option-A buffer-fill family:
  cicada/cics/builtins/interval.py  _write_into_ws  (RETRIEVE)
  cicada/cics/builtins/vsam.py      _write_into_ws  (READ, READNEXT, READPREV)

This is the defect shape docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md
is about: the component cannot do what was asked, does not say so, and produces a
plausible result instead. A truncated record looks like a short record.

Found during the forge-9zb interval-control review; RETRIEVE inherited the pattern
from the VSAM builtins rather than introducing it, so fixing one should fix both.
acceptance_criteria: A payload longer than its INTO field sets EIBRESP to LENGERR (22) and fills the field to its length; a test asserts the decoded truncated content AND the resp code, for both a VSAM READ and a RETRIEVE.
notes: The LENGTH operand matters here too: in CICS, LENGTH is a data area that on input carries the maximum and on output receives the actual length. Neither builtin writes it back today, which is the other half of how a program would detect the truncation.

title: Onboarding a corpus with no CSD: synthesise the transid to program map
description:
run_carddemo_region (cics/bootstrap.py:61) requires exactly one of transid_to_program= or csd_path=. A corpus arriving without a CSD has no mapping and cannot be composed into a region.

Only matters at COMPOSITION time — a single-program region can pass the dict directly, which is how the first execution ran. It becomes blocking the moment a multi-program flow is brought up from a corpus that shipped no CSD.

Sources for a synthesised mapping, roughly in order of reliability: an EXEC CICS START/XCTL/LINK target inventory across the corpus (tools/mainframe_inventory.py already extracts these), the programs' own RETURN TRANSID operands, and naming convention as the last resort.
acceptance_criteria: A region can be built from a corpus with no CSD, with the synthesised mapping reported explicitly (including which entries came from convention rather than evidence) rather than silently guessed.
notes: Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md 'Also known, not re-verified here'.

title: AlternateKeyDriver is read-only — every write verb raises
description:
vendor/red-dragon/interpreter/cobol/file_drivers.py raises NotImplementedError('alternate-key datasets are read-only point lookups') on every write verb. Unlike the rest of the analysis this one is LOUD, so it is a blocker rather than a wrong answer.

Not re-verified and not measured: whether it bites depends on which programs write through an alternate-index path. Measure that before designing — the fix shape differs a lot between 'a handful of programs REWRITE through an AIX' and 'the corpus treats alternate indexes as fully updatable'.
acceptance_criteria: Either write verbs work through an alternate-key path with the base cluster and every index kept consistent, or the measurement shows the corpus never writes through one and this is closed as not-needed with the count recorded.
notes: Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md 'Also known, not re-verified here'. First step is measurement, not code.

title: EXEC CICS temporary storage: READQ/WRITEQ/DELETEQ TS unimplemented
description:
WRITEQ TD is implemented; the TS queue family is not. Occurrences in the production online corpus: DELETEQ TS 144, READQ TS 98, WRITEQ TS 88 (330 total).

All three fall through to _lower_unsupported and abend UNSP when reached (since 1511575a) rather than being silently dropped, so this is a coverage gap rather than a stale-data correctness bug — a program using TS now fails loudly instead of running on with an unfilled INTO area.

The three verbs share one store and must be designed together: a per-region queue map keyed by QUEUE name, ITEM-numbered records, with MAIN/AUXILIARY treated identically and REWRITE honoured. Queue lifetime is the open question — TS queues outlive a task and are typically how a pseudo-conversational flow carries state across turns, so the store belongs on the region, not the task.
acceptance_criteria: Write-then-read round-trips across two pseudo-conversational turns; ITEM numbering, REWRITE, NUMITEMS and QIDERR on a missing queue all covered.
notes:
Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect E verb table.
Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): Lowered P1 -> P2 by reach: WRITEQ/READQ/DELETEQ TS 321 statements in ~66 programs (3%). ITEM+NUMITEMS on most reads (indexed access, not FIFO only); MAIN on 64% of writes. QIDERR/ITEMERR handling comes with it. No TD queue usage at all in the census. title: EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT (explicit) is unimplemented
description:
20 occurrences in the production online corpus. Emits no IR today (see the unimplemented-verb policy bead), so an explicit commit point is silently skipped and a later failure rolls back work the program had already committed.

Related but distinct from cicada-6hv (implicit SYNCPOINT + cursor close at pseudo-conversational RETURN) — that one is the automatic commit at task end; this is the programmer-issued verb, including SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK.
acceptance_criteria: SYNCPOINT commits and SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK backs out, over both VSAM file control and the SQL coprocessor path; test asserts data state either side of the verb.
notes: Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect E verb table. Coordinate with cicada-6hv so both go through one commit seam.

title: Root make test must source squall's DSN env
description: The root Makefile's `test` target runs pytest without sourcing squall/db2/dsn-env.sh, so tests/integration/test_inqcust_e2e.py fails with KeyError: 'SQUALL_DB2_DSN' under `make test`/`make test-all`. squall/Makefile's test target already sources it; the root one should too. dsn-env.sh resolves .env relative to the cwd, so it needs a seam for being sourced from the workspace root.
acceptance_criteria: `make test-all` runs the root suite green (including test_inqcust_e2e) with squall/.env present; `cd squall && make test` still works unchanged.
close_reason: Root make test and the squall pre-commit hook now both source squall/db2/dsn-env.sh, which gained a SQUALL_DIR seam for locating .env from the workspace root.

title: [bug] External floating-point PICTURE now aborts a corpus sweep at field ingestion
description:
pic_parser refuses an external floating-point PICTURE (e.g. +999.99E+99) with UnsupportedEditPictureError, and asg_types re-raises it named with the field. That is right for a program being compiled to run: there is no storage category for it.

It is wrong for cobble's diagnosis commands, whose whole job is to parse everything in a corpus and report what failed. A single external floating-point field now aborts the member's ingestion, and CobolASG.from_dict raising costs the whole program -- the same failure shape the _BUILDERS table exists to prevent, one layer down.

Surfaced when cobble stopped carrying its own pic_parser (forge 868955fe); cobble's own test had asserted the old EXTERNAL_FLOAT category and was rewritten to assert the refusal.

Options: give the sweep a mode that degrades an unrepresentable field to an opaque-but-preserved descriptor, or let diagnosis catch and report per-field rather than per-member. Decide against the parse-everything consumer, not the compile-to-run one.

title: interpreter/__init__.py eagerly imports the VM and LLM stack
description:
Any 'import interpreter.x' executes interpreter/__init__.py, which imports interpreter.api and interpreter.run -- loading 115 interpreter modules plus litellm, pydantic and tree_sitter, ~1.7s, for a consumer that only wanted a leaf like interpreter.cobol.condition_name.

Found while repointing cobble (VM-free by design, and the reason it kept its own copies) onto red-dragon's canonical modules. Cobble now pays this on every CLI invocation.

Fix is to stop re-exporting from the package __init__ and let consumers import the submodules they use; submodule imports ('from interpreter import constants') are unaffected. Check consumers of the re-exported names first: build_cfg_from_source, dump_cfg, dump_ir, dump_mermaid, extract_function_source, ir_stats, lower_and_infer, lower_source, ExecutionStats, VMConfig, execute_cfg, run.

title: [epic] Bridge-to-lowering coverage: keep what the bridge emits, what parses, and what lowers in step
description:
Three layers must agree and nothing checks that they do: the Java bridge emits statement types and expression kinds, cobol_statements/cobol_expression decide what parses, and statement_dispatch/condition_lowering decide what lowers.

STATUS UPDATE (re-audit 2026-09-24):
  - Expression kinds: CLOSED. cobol_expression.py's kind table now handles all 8
    emitted kinds — figurative, length_of and dfhresp were added (lines 163-177,
    223-225), so the forge-ptc gap no longer exists.
  - Statement types: an audit script and its unit tests exist
    (red-dragon scripts/audit_cobol_frontend.py, tests/unit/test_audit_cobol_frontend.py)
    and compare BRIDGE_SERIALIZED_TYPES against _DISPATCH_TABLE and _LOWERED_TYPES.
    But BRIDGE_SERIALIZED_TYPES is a hand-maintained constant, not derived from
    StatementSerializer.java, so a type the bridge grows still goes unnoticed.

The remaining deliverable is exactly that: derive the emitted type/kind sets from
the Java source (grep -o 'newStatement("[A-Z_0-9]*")' and '"kind", *"[a-z_]*"' over
StatementSerializer.java) so the test fails when the bridge and the Python frontend
drift, rather than encoding today's snapshot by hand.

Both fallbacks remain silent: forge-r5r (unhandled statement emits no IR) and
forge-ozw (unknown ExprNode lowers to constant 0).

title: Unhandled statement type in statement_dispatch is a warning, not a failure
description:
statement_dispatch.py's dispatch ends:

    else:
        for strat in ctx.extension_strategies:
            if strat.handles(stmt):
                strat.lower(ctx, stmt, materialised)
                return
        logger.warning('Unhandled COBOL statement type: %s', type(stmt).__name__)

A statement type that parses but has no lowering emits no IR and the program runs as though it were absent. Nothing fails; the only trace is a log line nobody reads during a batch run. The result is a program that executes to completion with silently missing behaviour.

Sibling of forge-ozw (unknown ExprNode lowers to constant 0). Same shape: the lowering degrades quietly where it should refuse.

The tension is real and should be decided deliberately rather than by default. Graph extraction wants a permissive parse — an unmodelled type is fatal to the whole ASG, which is why XML_GENERATE was modelled at all (forge-73x). Execution wants a strict lowering. Those are different consumers of the same pipeline, so the answer is probably a mode or an explicit allowlist of known-unlowered types, not a blanket raise: a blanket raise would break the graph paths that legitimately never lower.

Red-dragon change: fix in ~/code/red-dragon, then bump the submodule pointer.

title: XML GENERATE parses but has no lowering — the statement silently does nothing at runtime
description:
XML_GENERATE was added to the bridge serializer and the Python dispatch table (red-dragon 4c9ef5f0) because an unmodelled statement type is fatal to the whole program's ASG. Modelling it was the right call, but it only reaches the parse: statement_dispatch.py has no XmlGenerateStatement branch, so lowering falls through to

    logger.warning('Unhandled COBOL statement type: %s', type(stmt).__name__)

and emits no IR. A program containing XML GENERATE now compiles and runs as though the statement were not there — the receiving XML document is never written, COUNT IN is never set, and neither ON EXCEPTION nor NOT ON EXCEPTION runs.

This is strictly better than the previous behaviour (the whole ASG was lost), and it is fine for graph extraction, which is what motivated modelling it. It is not fine for execution.

Scope: decide whether to lower it or to refuse it loudly. Lowering needs a runtime that serialises a record to XML per the COUNT IN / ON EXCEPTION contract the serializer already emits. Refusing loudly is cheap and honest in the meantime, and is what forge-<statement-dispatch-fallback> would give for free.

Found by auditing bridge-emitted types against the lowering dispatch; see the tracking issue for the method.

title: Unknown ExprNode in condition_lowering silently lowers to constant 0
description:
condition_lowering.py ends its ExprNode dispatch (condition_lowering.py:1321) with

    logger.warning('Unknown expression node type: %s', type(node).__name__)
    return _float_operand(ctx, ctx.const_to_reg(0, span=span), floating, span=span)

An unhandled expression shape therefore becomes the literal 0 — a plausible-looking wrong answer rather than a failure. A warning in a log is not a gate: nothing fails, and the emitted IR is wrong. (The sibling fallback this issue originally also named, _expr_node_to_arg_dict returning {'kind': 'ref', 'name': ''} for a nameless node, no longer exists; that function is gone. Note the DFHRESP arm immediately above now raises rather than guessing — the loud shape this issue is asking for, already precedented in the same function.)

This is the reason forge-ptc is dangerous to fix naively: adding new ExprNode types makes the parse succeed and routes them straight into this fallback. Making the fallback loud is arguably a prerequisite for that work rather than a follow-up.

Red-dragon change: fix in ~/code/red-dragon, then bump the submodule pointer.

title: CICS grammar: FORMATTIME TIMESEP must parse without a value
description:
cicada/cics/cics_grammar/CICSzParser.g4 has 'timesepOption : TIMESEP arg' — the argument is mandatory. Written bare, TIMESEP is valid CICS and defaults the separator to ':', so EXEC CICS FORMATTIME ... TIMESEP fails to parse and takes the containing program's ASG down with it.

Fix is 'TIMESEP arg?', matching what cobble carries (cobble d25b9a4), plus regeneration of the parser.

Distinct from forge-4of, which is about FORMATTIME's lowering and ABSTIME plumbing — this one never gets that far, failing at parse time. Same shape as the APPLID/RETCODE-on-LINK fix already landed in e101d01c: the option exists in the grammar but the rule is stricter than the real syntax.
close_reason: Fixed: the grammar rule is now 'TIMESEP arg?', so a bare TIMESEP parses.

title: KG FILE-CONTROL stage builds ASGs without registering dialect parsers
description:
knowledge_graph/build_carddemo_graph.py's _build_cobol_file_graph builds ASGs through AstStore.get without registering coprocessor dialect parsers. parse_statement resolves coprocessor statement types through the _dialect_parsers ContextVar, whose default is empty, and an unregistered type raises rather than yielding an opaque statement — which is fatal to the whole program's ASG, not just the one statement. The program then contributes nothing to the graph, not even its PROGRAM node.

Masked today by two things: the stage filters CICS programs out by name using the CSD-derived set, and each program is wrapped in 'except Exception' that downgrades the failure to a logged warning plus a failures entry. So it degrades silently rather than crashing.

Still fires for any coprocessor statement reaching the stage — notably a batch program with embedded EXEC SQL and no CICS anywhere, which the CICS skip list does not exclude. Found in cobble, where the equivalent defect accounted for 2,129 of 3,779 corpus members.

Fix: register the dialect parsers around ASG construction (cobble's cics/asg_dialect_scope.py is the shape). The stage only wants FILE-CONTROL, but it cannot reach FILE-CONTROL without building the ASG, so it must register them like any other consumer. Independent of the cobble consolidation (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-cobble-consolidation-design.md), though that design moves asg_dialect_scope into cicada.
close_reason: Obsolete: knowledge_graph/build_carddemo_graph.py and its whole stage were deleted in fb83182d when forge's graph pipeline was retired in favour of cobble. File a fresh bead against cobble if the dialect-registration gap survives there.

title: Black pre-commit hook's 'git add -u' sweeps the vendor/red-dragon pointer into unrelated commits
description:
The black hook runs: bash -c '... python -m black ... && git add -u'. pre-commit stashes unstaged changes before running hooks, but its patch-based stash does not cover submodule pointer changes, so a modified vendor/red-dragon survives the stash and 'git add -u' stages it. Any commit made while the submodule checkout differs from the recorded pointer silently acquires that pointer bump, whatever the commit was actually about.

Observed twice while landing the cobble import: a commit staged with an explicit pathspec (.pre-commit-config.yaml only) came out as '2 files changed' with vendor/red-dragon in it. Worked around by checking the submodule back to the recorded commit, making the unrelated commits, then restoring it - which should not be necessary.

Fix options: narrow 'git add -u' to the paths black actually formats, or drop the auto-add and let black --check fail the commit instead.
close_reason: Fixed: the black hook re-stages only the files pre-commit hands it (git add -- "$@"), so an unrelated submodule pointer is no longer swept in.

title: Accept APPLID and RETCODE on EXEC CICS LINK in cicada's grammar
description: cobble adds applidOption and retcodeOption to the LINK option set in CICSzParser.g4 (two lines). cicada/cics/cics_grammar/CICSzParser.g4 needs the same, plus regeneration of the checked-in ANTLR Python parser (CICSzParser.py, .interp, Listener, Visitor) with antlr-4.13.1.
close_reason: Imported from cobble. -copybook-ext landed in red-dragon 2896da3f (with the Python copybook_exts seam); CICS LINK APPLID/RETCODE landed in forge e101d01c with a regenerated parser and a regression test.

title: Add -copybook-ext flag to red-dragon's ProLeap bridge Main
description: Import from cobble: a repeatable -copybook-ext flag replacing the hardcoded copybook extension list. ProLeap resolves a COPY by name + extension, so the list is corpus shape rather than a constant: a corpus whose members all carry one unconventional extension resolves nothing under the default. Falls back to DEFAULT_COPYBOOK_EXTENSIONS ('', cpy, CPY, cob, cbl, copy, COPY) when the flag is absent - never empty, since an empty list makes ProLeap search nothing. Comes with MainTest.
close_reason: Imported from cobble. -copybook-ext landed in red-dragon 2896da3f (with the Python copybook_exts seam); CICS LINK APPLID/RETCODE landed in forge e101d01c with a regenerated parser and a regression test.

title: CICS RECEIVE MAP ignores MAPSET (SEND MAP options are already forwarded)
description:
The SEND MAP branch of CicsLoweringStrategy._emit_map_call now forwards MAPSET, a flags list (ERASE, MAPONLY, DATAONLY, ALARM, FRSET, FREEKB, CURSOR) and the CURSOR operand to __cics_send_map, and cics/builtins/screen.py consumes erase/freekb/cursor. The remaining gap is RECEIVE MAP: its arm (strategy.py:1494-1496, and the conversational SUSPEND arm above it) calls with only MAP and the symbolic field names, so MAPSET is still parsed into stmt.options and never looked at.

Usage-surface inventory over a real CICS corpus: RECEIVE MAP 3 occ / 3 files each carrying MAPSET.

MAPSET is a correctness risk: the map name is resolved on its own, so two mapsets defining the same map name are indistinguishable. Harmless in a single-mapset corpus, wrong in general.
acceptance_criteria:
- MAPSET participates in map resolution rather than being ignored
- ERASE and CURSOR are conveyed to ScreenChannel, or explicitly documented as unmodelled
- FREEKB is an explicit, documented nop rather than a silent drop
- Test asserting a SEND MAP with ERASE/CURSOR reaches the screen channel with those attributes
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): RECEIVE MAP: 1,042 statements in 1,026 programs, 100% with MAP+MAPSET. SEND MAP flags are already forwarded (this issue's remaining scope is RECEIVE MAP's MAPSET). Census SEND MAP vocabulary: MAP/MAPSET 100%, FREEKB 98%, CURSOR 98%, ERASE 97%, DATAONLY 3%; never ALARM/FRSET/ERASEAUP/PRINT. Lowered P1 -> P2: the defect only bites when two mapsets define the same map name.

title: mainframe_inventory: recursive CICS/JCL/tool usage surface inventory script
description: Standalone stdlib-only script (tools/mainframe_inventory.py) that recursively inventories mainframe feature usage across an arbitrary codebase: JCL statements/params, DSN shapes, CICS verbs+options by functional area, and -- the centerpiece -- a tool registry (PGM= -> control-DD -> deck dialect) extracting tool/verb/operand-keyword triples plus verbatim PARM. Unknown tools are profiled (DD fingerprint + deck leading tokens + PARM) rather than dropped. Purpose: replace guesswork with a measured coverage surface for prioritising jackal/cicada work. No supported-set join yet -- inventory only.
close_reason: tools/mainframe_inventory.py implemented TDD with unit + CardDemo integration coverage; black clean, import contracts kept

title: IDCAMS DEFINE CLUSTER: comma-separated RECORDSIZE()/KEYS() args not parsed
description:
jackal/jackal/idcams/grammar.lark's recordsize_param ("RECORDSIZE" "(" INT INT ")")
and keys_param ("KEYS" "(" INT INT ")") both require space-separated integers.
Real CardDemo IDCAMS jobs frequently use comma-separated args instead:
RECORDSIZE(80,80), KEYS(8,0). Confirmed via grep against
vendor/carddemo/app/{jcl,proc}: RECORDSIZE(n,n) appears in 6 files,
KEYS(n,n) in 2 files (e.g. DUSRSECJ.jcl, ESDSRRDS.jcl, TCATBALF.jcl).

Discovered while fixing jackal-1o2.6's bare-DELETE/standalone-SET gap: a
test parsing ESDSRRDS.jcl's exact DEFINE CLUSTER text failed on
RECORDSIZE(80,80) specifically, unrelated to that fix, so it was trimmed
out of scope rather than bundled in. See jackal-1o2.6 for the sibling
IDCAMS grammar work this was found alongside.

Fix: comma should be an allowed separator between INT tokens in both
params (either accept an optional comma in the grammar rule, or add
"," to the ignore pattern between digits -- the latter is broader and
should be checked against ambiguity with other comma-bearing param
values first).
close_reason: Subsumed by the comprehensive IDCAMS grammar (jackal/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-08-idcams-comprehensive-grammar.md) -- RECORDSIZE()/KEYS() now accept comma-separated args as part of full parameter fidelity, verified against real DUSRSECJ.jcl/ESDSRRDS.jcl text.

title: jcl_graph.py: _step_proc_provenance mislabels proc attribute when a job has duplicate step names
description:
Discovered while verifying PlanB Task 8 (build_carddemo_graph.py real proclib wiring).

In jackal/jackal/jcl_graph.py, _step_proc_provenance() builds:
    original_by_name = {s.name.upper(): s for s in job.steps}
keyed by step name. Real CardDemo JCL (jackal/third-party/carddemo/app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl)
has two steps both literally named STEP05R:
  - line 23: //STEP05R EXEC PROC=REPROC,...
  - line 37: //STEP05R  EXEC PGM=SORT

The dict comprehension keeps only the LAST occurrence (the SORT step), so when resolving
provenance for the expanded inner step TRANREPT.STEP05R.PRC001, outer_step =
original_by_name['STEP05R'] incorrectly resolves to the SORT step instead of the REPROC
step. Result: the JOB->STEP edge to TRANREPT.STEP05R.PRC001 carries attrs={'proc': 'SORT'}
instead of the correct attrs={'proc': 'REPROC'}.

The step itself IS still correctly expanded (TRANREPT.STEP05R.PRC001 -> IDCAMS, right DDs,
right dataset), so this is a provenance-attribute-only bug, not a structural one — REPROC
no longer appears as a spurious PROGRAM node (Task 8's primary goal), but the 'proc' edge
attribute for this expansion is wrong.

Fix should key original_by_name by (name, position) or otherwise disambiguate steps that
share a name within one job, since JCL does permit step name reuse across what are
effectively unrelated step groups in some real-world jobs.

Out of scope for PlanB Task 8 (which only touches knowledge_graph/build_carddemo_graph.py) —
filed as a follow-up against jcl_graph.py / Task 6.
close_reason: Fixed: _step_proc_provenance now uses a positional walk instead of a name-keyed dict, correctly attributing each expanded PROC step to its true originating outer step even when step names repeat within a job. Commit f0a2b50d, TDD (regression test added first, verified red, then fixed). 181/181 tests pass.

title: Repo-wide black formatting drift surfaced by consolidated pre-commit black hook
description: Discovered during the monorepo migration (Task 9, pre-commit consolidation). Running the new consolidated global 'black' hook across all package paths in one pass (black cicada/cics cicada/tests squall/squall squall/tests jackal/jackal jackal/tests red_dragon_forge tests) reformats pre-existing formatting drift in red_dragon_forge/run.py, tests/integration/test_inqcust_e2e.py, tests/integration/test_run_program.py, tests/integration/test_sql_adapter.py. These are not black-clean at HEAD; the old per-package hooks apparently never caught them (possibly a black version difference, or these files simply predate a black bump). Not fixed as part of Task 9 (out of scope - no package internal code changes). Needs a dedicated black pass to land the formatting fix cleanly as its own commit.
notes: Escalated: Task 11 added a root CI 'lint' job (black --check + import-linter) that will fail red until this drift is fixed, since black --check is not scoped to skip these 4 files. Fix this before/alongside wiring CI for real.
close_reason: Already fixed - discovered the drift was silently resolved as an unlogged side effect of commit 61f968d4's black auto-fix hook (git add -u), which I failed to catch/revert that one time unlike every other run this session. Verified black --diff is now clean across all 228 files and 'make test' still passes (7 passed) - pure formatting, no behavior change.

title: Reconcile core.hooksPath (Beads) with the consolidated .pre-commit-config.yaml so git commit actually enforces it
description: Discovered during the monorepo migration (Task 9, pre-commit consolidation). cicada/squall/jackal each use the standard .git/hooks/pre-commit installed by the python pre-commit framework, which chains Talisman in as pre-commit.legacy. red-dragon-forge instead has core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks (set by 'bd init', run earlier in this migration), whose pre-commit script invokes Talisman directly plus 'bd hooks run pre-commit' - it never invokes the python pre-commit framework or reads .pre-commit-config.yaml at all. Task 9's consolidated root .pre-commit-config.yaml is verified correct and runnable via 'pre-commit run --all-files'/'pre-commit run --files', but is NOT currently triggered by a real 'git commit' in this repo. Needs a decision: either unset core.hooksPath and let 'pre-commit install' chain in normally (matching cicada/squall/jackal's pattern, verify this doesn't silently drop needed Beads hook behavior), or teach .beads/hooks/pre-commit to also invoke 'pre-commit run' (durability risk: that file has 'DO NOT REMOVE' markers and may be regenerated by future bd commands).
close_reason: Resolved: unset core.hooksPath (was .beads/hooks) and ran 'pre-commit install', matching cicada/squall/jackal's pattern exactly. Talisman auto-chained in as pre-commit.legacy. Verified bd hooks run pre-commit was a no-op (no output, exit 0) before removing it, and that cicada/squall/jackal already operate with zero Beads git-hook integration, so dropping it here is safe and consistent.

title: squall/db2/dsn-env.sh does not export PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR sourced from .env
description: Discovered during the monorepo migration (Task 7, root test-all target). squall/db2/dsn-env.sh sources .env (via '[ -f .env ] && . ./.env') without 'set -a' or an explicit 'export PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR', so PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR set in .env stays a local shell variable in the Make recipe's shell and never reaches the pytest subprocess it launches. 'cd squall && make test' fails in a truly clean shell (env -i) with KeyError: 'PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR' on every test needing the JAR. It only 'worked' in every prior agent verification this migration by accident - their persistent shell sessions happened to already have PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR exported from an earlier cicada/jackal command in the same session. CI is unaffected (its ci.yml sets PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR at the job env level). Fix: add 'set -a' before sourcing .env in db2/dsn-env.sh, or explicitly 'export PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR' there.
close_reason: Fixed in commit e4d3dab5 - squall/db2/dsn-env.sh now wraps 'source .env' in set -a/set +a so PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR (and DB2_*) actually reach the pytest subprocess. Verified 'cd squall && make test' passes standalone in a genuinely clean shell (env -i): 271 passed, 1 skipped.

title: EXEC CICS LINK: set EIBRESP=0 on success
description: After EXEC CICS LINK completes successfully, EIBRESP must be set to DFHRESP(NORMAL) (0) in the caller's EIB. UID002.cbl checks EIBRESP = DFHRESP(NORMAL) immediately after the LINK call. Currently the __cics_link builtin returns BuiltinResult(value=0) but does not write EIBRESP, so the check may fail depending on prior EIBRESP state.
close_reason: Closed

title: EXEC CICS LINK: support LENGTH option
description: UID002.cbl (walmartlabs/zUID) uses LENGTH(LENGTH OF Zuid-COMM-AREA) on EXEC CICS LINK. The current LINK lowering in cics/strategy.py ignores the LENGTH option and always passes the full natural byte length of the COMMAREA field. Need to emit a LENGTH-capped copy of the COMMAREA bytes when LENGTH is present, so the inner program sees exactly the caller-specified number of bytes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Adopt mapa ANTLR grammar for EXEC CICS parsing
description: Replace the verb-agnostic Lark grammar in cics_parser.py with the mapa ANTLR grammar (CICSzParser.g4 + CICSzLexer.g4), grafting our COBOL-aware value rule (CicsOperand: literal/data-name/subscripts/ref-mod) onto it. Goal: unknown CICS verbs and invalid options are caught at parse time rather than falling through to CatchAllLoweringStrategy. Changes go in ~/code/red-dragon; submodule bumped in cicada after. CardDemo integration tests are the primary regression gate.
close_reason: The mapa ANTLR grammar is adopted: cics_parser.py re-exports cics_visitor.parse_exec_cics_text, the grammar is vendored under cicada/cics/cics_grammar/, and CicsOperand is the COBOL-aware value rule.

title: DUMMY / DSN=NULLFILE DDs (empty input / discard output)
description: 4 CardDemo jobs use DUMMY/NULLFILE DDs — a read returns EOF immediately, a write is discarded. Execution: catalog/provider resolves a DUMMY DD to an empty-source / sink dataset. Parsing from 1o2.9.
notes:
Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): DD DUMMY is on >=47% of jobs, both as a placeholder and as the empty input to IDCAMS REPRO that truncates a dataset (the idiom red-dragon-forge-vqa needs). Raised P3 -> P2: after unsupported-program dispatch (red-dragon-forge-xkk) it is the most widespread missing execution feature. Parsing already works (bridge emits dummy=true).
Status 2026-10-11: parsing (DUMMY and DSN=NULLFILE, the bridge maps NULLFILE to dummy) and allocation are done (lrk). A COBOL read from DUMMY gets EOF, tested in test_step_lifecycle. Writes go to a sink deleted after the step, untested. Left: one test that a COBOL step writing to DUMMY and to NULLFILE keeps nothing, then close. The IDCAMS REPRO-from-DUMMY truncation idiom belongs to red-dragon-forge-vqa.
close_reason: COBOL writes to DUMMY and DSN=NULLFILE keep nothing (test_step_lifecycle); reads get EOF; REPRO truncation idiom stays with red-dragon-forge-vqa.

title: PARM= — pass parameters into the executed program
description: 4 CardDemo jobs pass PARM= on EXEC. A program receives PARM via its entry linkage (COBOL: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING / the JCL parm area). Execution: thread the parsed PARM string into the red-dragon run() so the COBOL program sees its startup argument. Parsing from 1o2.9.
close_reason: Closed

title: Honor DCB attributes (LRECL/RECFM/BLKSIZE) in allocation + record I/O
description: 13 CardDemo jobs specify DCB=/RECFM/LRECL. Record length + format drive file I/O (fixed vs variable records, blocking). Execution: thread DCB attrs from the parsed DD into dataset allocation and into the record codec red-dragon uses, so reads/writes use the declared LRECL/RECFM instead of assumptions. Subsumes/【generalizes the v2 debt item jackal-ifq (REPRO LRECL assumption). Parsing comes from the adopted grammar (1o2.9).

title: Broaden IDCAMS verb coverage (bare DELETE, standalone SET, GDG define, alternate-index toolchain)
description: Rescope to execution only, and repair the truncated tail. Done since filing: (1) bare `DELETE dsname` without CLUSTER, (2) standalone `SET MAXCC = n`, (5) `DELETE ... CLUSTER PURGE`, (6) `IF LASTCC=12 THEN SET MAXCC=0` including bare '=' -- all in jackal/idcams/grammar.lark + executor.py. Remaining: (3) DEFINE GENERATIONDATAGROUP and (4) the alternate-index toolchain (DELETE ALTERNATEINDEX, DEFINE ALTERNATEINDEX, DEFINE PATH, BLDINDEX) now have a full comprehensive grammar and typed AST (jackal/idcams/parser_comprehensive.py, grammar/ams.lark) but NO executor support, and the comprehensive parser is not yet wired into jackal/utilities.py (which still uses the narrow parse_idcams). The remaining work is therefore (a) switch the utility to the comprehensive parser and (b) implement GDG-base and AIX/PATH/BLDINDEX execution. Confirmed ZERO real CardDemo usage of LISTCAT, PRINT, REPRO FROMKEY/TOKEY/COUNT/SKIP, EXPORT/IMPORT/VERIFY and standalone ALTER -- do not implement those speculatively (they are parse-only today, which is enough).
design:
Suggested slicing, smallest/highest-leverage first:
  a. Bare DELETE + standalone SET (items 1+2) -- pure grammar fixes, unblocks 3 files outright, no executor changes needed (Delete/IfMaxcc handlers already exist, just need the grammar to recognize the bare forms).
  b. DEFINE GENERATIONDATAGROUP (item 3) -- ties directly into jackal-1o2.4 GDG work; do alongside or right after that epic child.
  c. IF LASTCC=n / bare `=` operator (item 6) -- small grammar extension, single file but repeated.
  d. DELETE ... CLUSTER PURGE (item 5) -- trivial trailer addition.
  e. Alternate-index toolchain (item 4) -- biggest lift, real VSAM AIX execution semantics, should be its own follow-up/sub-issue, not bundled with (a)-(d).
Audited directly against vendor/carddemo/app/jcl/*.jcl + proc/*.prc SYSIN blocks (grep + manual read), not inferred from the bead's original text.

PROGRESS (2026-07-09): Items a/c/d now DONE end-to-end in the executable IDCAMS path (jackal/jackal/idcams/{commands,grammar.lark,parser,executor}.py), TDD:
- (a) bare DELETE + standalone SET MAXCC -- landed earlier (commit f2dbda36).
- (c) IF LASTCC=n with bare "=" operator -- landed 75a2b639; LASTCC now tracked as a genuinely distinct counter from MAXCC in run_idcams (only functional commands update LASTCC; SET MAXCC doesn't, per the manual).
- (d) DELETE...CLUSTER PURGE trailer -- landed 75a2b639; PURGE parses, currently a documented no-op (no retention/expiration tracking in the simulated catalog to override).
Real-file proof: CBEXPORT.jcl's whole STEP01 SYSIN block executes end-to-end; DEFGDGB.jcl's verbatim IF LASTCC=12 idiom parses+executes in isolation. 742/742 jackal tests.

REMAINING: item b (DEFINE GENERATIONDATAGROUP -- needs new catalog-level GDG-base execution semantics, ties into jackal-1o2.4) and item e (alternate-index toolchain: DELETE...ALTERNATEINDEX / DEFINE ALTERNATEINDEX / DEFINE PATH / BLDINDEX -- biggest lift, real VSAM AIX execution machinery). Both are execution-semantics work; the comprehensive parsing-only grammar (jackal/jackal/idcams/parser_comprehensive.py) already parses all of these, but nothing is wired from that AST into executor.py yet.

Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): The census shows no alternate-index usage and no DEFINE GDG in JCL; GDG bases may be defined outside the job stream. title: Generation Data Groups (GDG): relative + absolute generation refs
description: GDGs (DSN=A.B.C(+1), (0), (-1)) are pervasive for dated/cyclic batch datasets. Add a GDG base + generation model to the catalog: define a GDG base (IDCAMS DEFINE GDG or pre-seeded), resolve (+1)=new generation, (0)=current, (-n)=nth prior; roll generations on job completion per DISP. Without this, jobs referencing generation datasets fail to resolve DSNs.
design: Catalog gains a GDG registry mapping base -> ordered generation list; DSN resolution interprets the (gen) suffix at allocate time; (+1) allocations are cataloged on step/job success per normal disposition. Parse the (gen) suffix in the DSN grammar token, not regex.
notes:
Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): Relative generations (+1)/(0) on >=25% of jobs, usually (+1) with DISP=(NEW,CATLG) and DCB=(<gdg-base>,...). Often pre-created by an IEFBR14 step with UNIT=(,,DEFER); separately, (MOD,DELETE)+SPACE=(TRK,0) empties a dataset before re-creation. Both idioms belong here. Lowered P1 -> P2 because the static track goes first; still the highest-reach data-plane item after DUMMY.
The bare-base reference (all generations) is filed as red-dragon-forge-zbb.

title: SORT and IEBGENER utilities
description: Every batch chain sorts and copies. Add two utilities to the registry: SORT (DFSORT/SyncSort — SORT FIELDS=, INCLUDE/OMIT, SUM, OUTREC/INREC reformatting via SYSIN control statements; SORTIN->SORTOUT) and IEBGENER (sequential copy SYSUT1->SYSUT2, optional record reformatting). Both read control statements from SYSIN in-stream (already supported). Start with the common subset (SORT FIELDS + basic INCLUDE/OMIT; IEBGENER straight copy).
design: New jackal/sort/ + jackal/iebgener/ (or a shared utility module) with Lark grammars for the control languages, mirroring jackal/idcams/. SORT FIELDS=(start,len,format,order) operate on byte-faithful EBCDIC records via red-dragon drivers. MAXCC/RC mapping like IDCAMS. Scope the SORT control-statement subset explicitly.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): SORT on >=40% of jobs (both EXEC PGM=SORT and EXEC SORT, the cataloged-proc form), IEBGENER on >=37%. Minimum SORT subset for 80/20: SORT FIELDS, INCLUDE/OMIT COND with nested AND/OR groups (>=62% of jobs), OUTREC FIELDS with reorder, C'..' literals and nX padding (>=22%, moved here from 1o2.24's scope), SUM FIELDS=NONE, OPTION COPY. Match-merge via SORTJNFn and ICETOOL IFTHEN/SEQNUM stay in 1o2.24. IEBGENER: straight SYSUT1->SYSUT2 copy; >=31% of jobs feed it in-stream data carrying $DJDE$ print-descriptor lines, which are payload to copy verbatim, never JCL. IEBGENER can land before SORT. Both need record lengths, so depend on 1o2.12.

Refactor to a single ParsedSql whose every field is a non-optional value of a small sum type with an explicit null object (no None anywhere): Kind/WheneverCondition as proper enum.Enum (NOT StrEnum — no implicit str comparability); WheneverAction/CursorRef/IncludeRef/ConnectSpec/DbName as frozen-dataclass unions with empty-dataclass null objects. Types are PURE DATA (no interpreter imports); emit/resolve behavior stays in strategy/binding via match. Parameterize loose collections: _plans: list[ParsedSql], cursors: dict[str, ParsedSql], field_meta: Mapping[str, FieldMeta] (TypedDict). Pure type refactor, zero behaviour change; 267 existing tests are the net. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-15-sql-model-rich-types-design.md

Pure-data model in squall/parser/sql_model.py; emit/resolve behaviour stays in strategy/binding via match. Zero behaviour change; 271 tests green. pyright noise from tuple[str|None,...]/unparameterized collections removed; remaining pyright items are pre-existing lark Token/Tree narrowing + the build_query scanner.

title: Implicit SYNCPOINT + cursor-close at pseudo-conversational RETURN
description: At a pseudo-conversational RETURN (TRANSID), model CICS task-end: commit the unit of work (rollback on abend) and close all DB2 cursors, resetting the SQL session per turn. WHY: squall's session (cursors/connection) lives in the module-global Builtins.TABLE __exec_sql closure, NOT in VM state. cicada re-invokes run_cics with a fresh VMState per turn but the SAME Builtins.TABLE, so the session persists across turns — leaking turn-1 cursors into turn-2, the opposite of CICS (each pseudo-conversational turn closes cursors and releases the DB2 thread). True conversational (one continuous run, no RETURN boundary) correctly preserves the session, so the fix keys on the RETURN. The RedDragon suspend/resume continuation (ExecutionState) holds only VM state, never Builtins.TABLE, so the session is never part of resumable state regardless of in-process vs serialized resume. MECHANISM: cicada's RETURN lowering emits a call to a named squall session-end builtin (no cics<->squall import; same name-convention composition as Builtins.TABLE / the strategy registry); no-op if DB2/squall not wired. DEPENDS ON the squall __sql_session_end builtin.
close_reason: Implemented: cicada's RETURN lowering emits the name-convention __cics_task_end_hook (cicada/cics/strategy.py:1374, default no-op at :972), squall binds its commit+close-all-cursors reset to it (squall/strategy.py:172); tested in cicada/tests/unit/cics/test_task_end_hook.py and squall/tests/unit/test_strategy.py:157.

title: __sql_session_end builtin: close all cursors + SYNCPOINT (reset SQL session)
description: Expose a named builtin (e.g. __sql_session_end) that closes all open cursors and SYNCPOINTs the unit of work (commit on normal end, rollback on abend). This is the squall-side hook cicada calls at a pseudo-conversational RETURN to reset the SQL session per turn — modelling real CICS task-end (implicit SYNCPOINT + cursor close at thread dealloc, incl. WITH HOLD). Standalone squall never calls it; it exists for the cicada+DB2 compose. Small: reuse the cursor-registry close + the COMMIT/ROLLBACK already built (618ddf5). Composition is name-convention only (no cics<->squall import).
close_reason: Implemented as reset_session, registered under the generic name __cics_task_end_hook rather than __sql_session_end (squall/strategy.py:172; commit+close-all-cursors in builtins/exec_sql.py _end_of_uow/_reset_session), with __cics_syncpoint_hook and __cics_rollback_hook alongside; tested in squall/tests/unit/test_strategy.py.

title: Typed validation: data_layout category must agree with dclgen sql_type (fail loud)
description: Split out of squall-6kp (codec + JSON consumption shipped in a076508). When binding a host var that carries dclgen field_meta, validate that ProLeap's data_layout category agrees with the recorded dclgen category/sql_type, and fail LOUD on mismatch — catching copybook/schema drift (e.g. dclgen generated BINARY but the inlined copybook parsed as something else, or a VARCHAR group is missing its -LEN/-TEXT children). For VARCHAR: assert the len_var child is BINARY and the text_var child is ALPHANUMERIC. For scalar kinds: assert data_layout[host_var].category == dclgen category. Runs where data_layout is available (bind time / first builtin run). TDD: a deliberately-mismatched sidecar must raise. No existing fields mismatch, so it is additive.
close_reason: validate_field_meta fails loud (FieldMetaMismatch) on dclgen/data_layout category drift: scalars by category equality, VARCHAR by its 49-group children (len_var BINARY, text_var ALPHANUMERIC); a host var missing from data_layout raises via _require_field. Run once on the first __exec_sql call (nonlocal guard; earliest data_layout is populated). Additive — the COMP-3/VARCHAR e2e exercise it on real ProLeap data_layout and pass (vocabularies agree); empty field_meta is a no-op. 278 tests green.

title: WHENEVER SQLERROR / SQLWARN: program-controlled error branching
description: Surfaced reviewing Db2Backend error handling. Today a SQL failure sets a (now real) negative SQLCODE and execution continues — faithful to the DEFAULT 'WHENEVER SQLERROR CONTINUE'. But real embedded SQL lets a program declare 'EXEC SQL WHENEVER SQLERROR GOTO handler' / 'PERFORM' / 'STOP', and the precompiler then auto-inserts a SQLCODE check+branch after every EXEC SQL statement. Implement WHENEVER (SQLERROR/SQLWARN/NOT FOUND -> CONTINUE/GOTO/PERFORM) so a program can opt into automatic error branching/halting instead of hand-checking SQLCODE. This is the 'should it halt on errors' mechanism: the backend stays faithful (SQLCODE + continue); WHENEVER is where halting/branching is expressed, program-controlled. Faithful numeric SQLCODE (get_sqlcode) already landed (bbfd4f7).
close_reason: Slice 1 shipped: WHENEVER SQLERROR (<0) / NOT FOUND (=100) with CONTINUE / GO TO. Implemented as a real precompiler directive — strategy keeps lexically-scoped per-condition state and lowers a synthetic IF SQLCODE <cmp> <val> GO TO target via ctx.lower_statement after each non-whenever statement (reuses RedDragon IF+GOTO lowering; no raw-IR branch, no label-naming coupling). Removed the latent bug where WHENEVER lowered to a __exec_sql query. 267 tests green incl. DB2 e2e (WHENEVER SQLERROR GO TO branches to handler). SQLWARNING deferred (needs SQLWARN population / squall-ud0); PERFORM/STOP are not DB2 WHENEVER actions. Found+filed a ProLeap EXEC SQL preprocessor bug in red-dragon (underscore/literal patterns -> 'missing END_EXEC').

title: Endianness-aware binary codec (COMP big-endian vs COMP-5 native)
description: squall's SQLCA is standardized on COMP (big-endian) and squall's _binary codec is big-endian — self-consistent in the closed squall+RedDragon system (no real Db2 wire to match), which is why the static.sqb SQLCA (SQLCODE=0) round-trips fine. But db2-samples DATA host vars are often COMP-5 (native/little-endian). If RedDragon decodes COMP-5 as little-endian while squall's codec is big-endian, a COMP-5 numeric host var would mismatch. Verify RedDragon's COMP-5 handling and, if it differs from COMP, make _binary_decode/_binary_encode honor the field's endianness (COMP vs COMP-5) per data_layout. Trigger: the first testbed program that binds a non-zero COMP-5 numeric host var.
close_reason: Investigated for criticality: COMP-5 endianness is a NON-issue. squall's binary codec round-trips COMP-5 self-consistently (big-endian), and RedDragon maps COMP-5 -> BINARY -> big-endian too, so values are correct. The observed cursor.sqb symptom (dept not displaying) was NOT COMP-5: it was a RedDragon multi-operand DISPLAY bug (only the first operand emitted) — filed + fixed as red-dragon-8g6r (e6fe21c7), bumped here in ddd30c8. cursor.sqb now displays 'SANDERS  in dept. 20 is a manager' etc. No squall-side change needed for COMP-5.

title: Faithful CONNECT: backend registry + connection lifecycle (not a no-op)
description:
CONNECT/DISCONNECT/SET CONNECTION/CONNECT RESET are currently no-ops (SQLCODE 0) because squall is handed a single pre-established SqlBackend. This discards real semantics:
- Database-name routing: CONNECT TO <name> selects WHICH database; multiple CONNECT targets collapse onto one backend today.
- Connection lifecycle: after CONNECT RESET, the next SQL should fail with SQLCODE -1024 (no connection); squall keeps working.
- Auth: USER/USING credentials are ignored.

Faithful model: squall holds a {database-name -> SqlBackend} registry. CONNECT TO <name> looks up + sets the ACTIVE backend; SET CONNECTION switches; CONNECT RESET clears; SQL before any connect / after reset returns -1024. The single-backend case becomes a one-entry registry with an implicit connect. Fine to defer while the testbed is single-database (CONNECT TO sample), but needed for multi-DB / lifecycle fidelity.
close_reason: Faithful CONNECT shipped: name->backend registry, per-run connection lifecycle (always-disconnected start; -1024 no-connection / -1013 unknown-db / -1338 not-established), idempotent re-connect with ignored USER/USING creds (testbed double-CONNECT idiom), CONNECT TO / SET CONNECTION / DISCONNECT / CONNECT RESET. Structured CONNECT grammar (no catch-all value-matching). 261 tests green incl. two-real-DB2-database routing e2e (MOJO+MOJO2). Out of scope (not regressions): credential validation, two-phase commit, cicada pseudo-conversational reset (cicada-6hv/squall-ipq).

title: Tolerant host-var/column type coercion (convert + SQLWARN + indicator)
description:
The coercion layer currently fails strict: any host-var (PIC-derived) type vs column (metadata) type mismatch aborts the statement with a genuine-failure SQLCODE (-301), writing nothing. This issue tracks making it tolerant, matching production DB2 SQL assignment rules:

- Bucket 1 (convertible, lossless): silently convert across compatible types (numeric<->numeric, DATE<->CHAR, narrowing into wider fields). SQLCODE 0.
- Bucket 2 (convertible, lossy): convert WITH a diagnostic. String truncation -> keep SQLCODE 0, set SQLWARN1='W', and if an indicator variable is supplied set it to the ORIGINAL (pre-truncation) length. Numeric fractional truncation behaves analogously.
- Bucket 3 (won't fit / incompatible): the genuine failures the strict layer already returns, refined to the right codes — -304 (value out of range for host var on fetch), -302 (input host var out of range for column), -301 (incompatible data type).

Depends on: the NULL-indicator host-var plumbing (:VAR:IND) being threaded through binding, since bucket-2 truncation reporting uses the indicator. The strict coercion seam built now is the branch point this fills in.

title: EXEC CICS LINK + logical-level stacking (suspend across LINK)

DispatchKind was NOT extended -- cicada/cics/types.py:31 is still {RETURN, RETURN_TRANSID, XCTL, ABEND}. What REMAINS is Layer 2 only: suspend/resume across a LINK boundary -- the task's continuation as a STACK of ExecutionStates owned by a first-class Task, freezing a LINKed callee at RECEIVE and popping back to the caller on its RETURN. No test suspends inside a LINKed program today. Retitle/rescope to Layer 2.

title: Conversational CICS support (suspend/resume + zBANK benchmark)
description:
Support CONVERSATIONAL CICS flows (one task looping SEND/RECEIVE, working-storage persists across the wait, single terminal RETURN) — as opposed to the pseudo-conversational CardDemo flows. Benchmark: Nantero1/zBANK (140-line conversational COBOL). Design deck: docs/design/conversational-suspend-resume.html.

Status: delivered, but NOT by the planned route. The Phase-0 greenlet spike was superseded: red-dragon shipped the cooperative suspend/resume primitive (ExecutionState/Suspend/resume), conversational RECEIVE MAP lowers to SUSPEND, and cics/conversational.py drives the task with run_linked_resumable/resume_linked. The zBANK benchmark runs green (login, deposit, withdraw, re-login proving VSAM persistence, 16-turn extended session). Confirm whether the 'EXEC CICS LINK logical-level stack' part of Phase 3 is still wanted before closing.

title: EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD is never dispatched (verb-key mismatch)
description:
CORPT00C submits a JCL deck via EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD QUEUE('JOBS') FROM(JCL-RECORD), but cicada never dispatches it.

Root cause: the Lark EXEC CICS grammar surfaces the statement as stmt.verb == 'WRITEQ' (with 'TD' as an option keyword), while cics/strategy.py:_SYS_VERBS only registers the composite key 'WRITEQ TD'. _SYS_VERBS.get('WRITEQ') -> None, so the verb falls through to 'unimplemented verb, no IR emitted' (strategy.py:789). The submission loop runs but enqueues nothing; td_queue stays empty.

Two parts to a fix:
1. Dispatch: match verb=='WRITEQ' with a 'TD' option (like READ/WRITE handle their option keywords) -> __cics_writeq_td. (Symmetrically, a future READQ TD would need the same.)
2. Operands: the generic _SYS_VERBS path calls the builtin with args=() , so even once dispatched the QUEUE/FROM operands are dropped. make_writeq_td_builtin already accepts (data, queue_name) (see tests/unit/cics/test_system_builtins.py::test_writeq_td_appends_to_queue); the strategy must LoadRegion the FROM operand and pass the QUEUE name so real JCL/queue content is captured.

Current behaviour is pinned by tests/integration/cics/test_carddemo_reports.py (asserts the screen-first success message + td_queue == []). When fixed, that test should assert the JCL deck (~17 lines) was enqueued to 'JOBS'.

Scope: cics/ runtime only (strategy + builtin); no RedDragon/VM change. The grammar already parses the statement fine.
close_reason: Fixed: WRITEQ TD's dispatch-mismatch half was already resolved by the ANTLR4 grammar migration (WriteqTd rule -> composite verb string 'WRITEQ TD', matches _SYS_VERBS cleanly). The remaining operand-dropping bug is fixed: WRITEQ TD is now lowered in its own explicit block in cics/strategy.py (pulled out of the generic no-operand _SYS_VERBS dispatch), resolving QUEUE and FROM via emit_operand_value and passing them as real CallFunction args. TDD: unit test (tests/unit/cics/test_strategy_screen.py::test_writeq_td_lowers_with_real_args) + strengthened real-COBOL integration test (tests/integration/cics/test_carddemo_reports.py::test_real_carddemo_custom_report_submitted), both verified to fail without the fix. RESP/RESP2 writeback (a separate bug found at the same call site) is intentionally out of scope, tracked as cicada-y6l.

title: Field-to-field numeric MOVE loses fractional digits (decode→string coercion)
description:
MOVE of a numeric-DISPLAY field into another numeric field drops the fractional part. E.g. WS-SRC PIC S9(9)V99 VALUE 12345.67; MOVE WS-SRC TO WS-DST (also S9(9)V99) stores 12345.00, losing .67.

Root cause: in lower_move, the source is decoded (emit_decode_field yields the correct float 12345.67 — verified by running build_decode_zoned_ir in isolation) then converted via emit_to_string. But in the full pipeline the decoded register value is coerced from float to int before str() is called (no int() builtin call occurs; the runtime division 1234567/100 correctly yields 12345.67, yet str receives int 12345). The coercion appears to come from the VM type environment (_coerce_value / coerce_local_update in interpreter/vm/vm.py) inferring the decode-result register as Int.

Reproduces on clean code (independent of the numeric-editing / edit_picture work). A LITERAL source (MOVE 12345.67 TO WS-DST) is NOT affected — it preserves the fraction — because it skips the field decode path.

Impact: any field-to-field MOVE of fractional values; also blocks full fractional fidelity when MOVEing a numeric field into a numeric-edited item.

Fix likely in interpreter/vm/** (off-limits for cicada) — file against red-dragon. Note: this is the engine, so coordinate with red-dragon core constraints.

Covered-around in tests/integration/test_cobol_numeric_edited.py (field-source test uses a whole number to avoid this bug).
close_reason: Moved to RedDragon's Beads DB as red-dragon-d3ww (RedDragon VM bug; linked depends-on red-dragon-4q25.1). RedDragon issues belong in ~/code/red-dragon per CLAUDE.md.
