title: Fix condition_lowering: DFHAID values unusable as comparison operands in compound IF
description:
In COTRN00C (and likely other CICS programs), DFHAID constants appear as comparison values in compound IF conditions:

  IF EIBAID NOT = DFHENTER AND DFHPF7 AND DFHPF3
  IF EIBAID NOT = DFHENTER AND DFHPF8

condition_lowering.py cannot resolve DFHPF3/DFHPF7/DFHPF8 as comparison values in this context and logs 'unparseable condition — never matching', causing the sub-clauses to evaluate as always-false. The full condition collapses to FALSE for all EIBAID values.

Observed impact: in COTRN00C's PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD, the skip-one-READNEXT guard never fires. Page-forward (PF8) therefore starts the browse AT CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST instead of past it, producing a one-record overlap between pages. Pinned as a regression baseline in test_real_carddemo_transaction_list_page_forward.

Fix should make condition_lowering resolve DFHAID PIC X VALUE literals (defined in DFHAID.cpy) correctly when they appear as the right-hand operand in a compound relational condition.
notes: Fixed in condition_lowering.py: added _extract_implied_relation helper and abbreviated-condition repair in _lower_condition_node. ProLeap mis-serialises abbreviated operands as {condition_name: X} when X is not level-88; fix detects this and reconstructs the full relation using the inherited subject/op from the left subtree. test_real_carddemo_transaction_list_page_forward updated to assert correct pagination.

title: inject_dfheiblk must not use regex text-search to locate WORKING-STORAGE SECTION
description: preprocessor.py inject_dfheiblk uses _WS_SECTION_RE = re.compile(r'^(\s*)WORKING-STORAGE\s+SECTION\s*\.', re.IGNORECASE) to find the injection point in raw COBOL source text. title: Cross-program COBOL CALL not linked: CALL 'CSUTLDTC' goes symbolic, blocking COTRN02C transaction-add date validation

The result stays SPACES (MOVE SPACES TO CSUTLDTC-RESULT precedes the CALL), so CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD != '0000' AND CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM != '2513' both hold -> 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...' error -> SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN -> RETURN, so ADD-TRANSACTION (STARTBR/READPREV id-gen + EXEC CICS WRITE) never runs. title: VsamEngine STARTBR+READPREV does not return last record (CardDemo COTRN02C transaction-add)
description: COTRN02C ADD-TRANSACTION does MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO TRAN-ID; STARTBR; READPREV; ENDBR to find the highest existing TRAN-ID and generate the next. Two bugs in interpreter/cics/vsam/engine.py: (1) startbr() leaves idx=0 when no key>=prefix (HIGH-VALUES) instead of positioning past end (len(keys)); (2) readprev() uses a fixed -2 offset assuming a prior READNEXT, so a STARTBR-then-READPREV (no intervening READNEXT) returns ENDFILE instead of the last record. Fix: position startbr past end on no-match; track browse direction so READPREV returns keys[pos-1] on a fresh/continuing reverse and skips the just-read record only on a READNEXT->READPREV reversal (preserving existing test_browse_reverse).

The old interpreter/cics/vsam/engine.py bugs described (startbr leaving idx=0 on no-match HIGH-VALUES, readprev's fixed -2 offset) were superseded when this logic moved into RedDragon's shared IndexedDriver (vendor/red-dragon/interpreter/cobol/file_drivers.py): start() now explicitly positions the cursor at EOF on a past-end GTEQ seek, and read_prev() is cursor-based rather than offset-based. Verified live: vendor/red-dragon/tests/unit/cobol/test_read_prev.py::test_indexed_startbr_past_end_then_read_prev_walks_back (the exact HIGH-VALUES seek-last scenario) passes, and tests/integration/cics/test_carddemo_add_transaction.py (the real COTRN02C flow) passes as part of the full CICS integration suite.

title: CICS dispatcher: peek (don't consume) input queue for EIBAID so RECEIVE MAP still gets the event
description: When the full autonomous _run_dispatcher_with_runner is written, reconcile terminal-input consumption: the loop must read the incoming InputEvent's eibaid BEFORE running the program (CardDemo programs test EIBAID / CCARD-AID-PFKxx early, before any RECEIVE MAP), but must NOT consume the event, because the program's RECEIVE MAP builtin then input_queue.get()s the same event for its field values (+ eibaid). Today _run_dispatcher_with_runner does its own input_queue.get() for the next context's eibaid, which competes with RECEIVE MAP for the same queue (latent double-consume if a program RECEIVEs). Fix: peek the next event non-destructively (queue.Queue has no peek -> add a small peekable queue wrapper, or use q.queue[0] under the lock / a deque) to set context.eibaid, leaving the event for RECEIVE MAP to consume. The per-turn CicsRegion API (interpreter/cics/dispatcher.py, added 67b3a0e2) already has the single-consume property the manual way: the caller passes the InputEvent once, the region sets context.eibaid from it AND puts it on the queue for RECEIVE; CicsRegion deliberately does NOT replicate the loop's separate get(). peek() is the autonomous-loop analog. Tie this into the deferred full-dispatcher work. Note for design: an InputEvent currently carries BOTH eibaid and fields and is consumed once by RECEIVE — the loop should treat that single event as the terminal input, not pull a second one.
close_reason: Fixed: get-then-put-back soft-peek helper (_peek_input_event) so RECEIVE MAP still gets the event after the dispatcher loop reads EIBAID. TDD: unit test (tests/unit/cics/test_dispatcher.py::test_dispatcher_resume_leaves_event_on_queue_for_receive_map) + real-COBOL integration test (tests/integration/cics/test_region_e2e.py::test_return_transid_then_receive_map_both_see_the_same_event), both verified to fail without the fix.

title: CICS VSAM: REWRITE without RIDFLD must extract key from FROM record
description: EXEC CICS REWRITE has no RIDFLD; the strategy lowering passes an empty key. VsamEngine.rewrite then matched key[:klen]=b'' against records and returned NOTFND, so CardDemo COACTUPC 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING REWRITE would never persist. FIXED: VsamEngine.rewrite derives the match key from the FROM record's own key field when the passed key is empty (mirrors write()). File: interpreter/cics/vsam/engine.py. Test: tests/unit/cics/test_vsam_engine.py::test_rewrite_without_key_extracts_key_from_record.
close_reason: Stale — already fixed. cics/vsam/engine.py:169-187 VsamEngine.rewrite already derives the match key from the FROM record when the passed key is empty (matches the fix described in the issue body itself, which was never marked closed). Verified by reading the current implementation.

title: VSAM engine: support reads keyed at a non-zero record offset (alternate index)
description:
interpreter/cics/vsam/engine.py VsamEngine.read matches the search key at record OFFSET 0 only (engine.py:78-79, with a code comment that offset-based keys are a future refinement). Real CardDemo COACTVWC reads the card cross-reference via an alternate-index PATH (LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH) keyed on ACCT-ID, which lives at offset 25 in the 50-byte CARD-XREF-RECORD (CVACT03Y: CARD-NUM X(16)@0, CUST-ID 9(9)@16, ACCT-ID 9(11)@25). So the xref read by acct-id cannot match against the natural record layout.

NEEDED: VsamEngine should support a key at a configured record offset/length (FctConfig/DatasetConfig key_offset) or an alternate-index abstraction, so READ DATASET(path) RIDFLD(acct-id) finds the record whose ACCT-ID@25 matches. ACCTDAT (key@0) and CUSTDAT (key@0) are fine. Surfaced driving COACTVWC turn 5; gated behind red-dragon reenter-flag bug (separate issue). CICS-LAYER (interpreter/cics/vsam/), editable.
close_reason: VsamEngine read/write/rewrite/delete/startbr now match the search key against record[key_offset:key_offset+key_length]; DatasetConfig gained key_offset/key_length (default 0 preserves offset-0 prefix match). Commit fb450944. Enables COACTVWC CXACAIX alt-index read (acct-id @ offset 25).

title: COBOL: PERFORM VARYING with FROM LENGTH OF + reference-modified loop-variable subscript in UNTIL loops incorrectly
description:
PERFORM VARYING WS-IDX FROM LENGTH OF WS-S BY -1 UNTIL WS-S(WS-IDX:1) NOT = SPACES OR WS-IDX = 1 terminates with the wrong index. Verified: WS-S PIC X(4) VALUE 'AB  ' -> final WS-IDX = 0 (expected 2, the position of the last non-space char). 

NOTE: base PERFORM VARYING works, INCLUDING descending (PERFORM VARYING I FROM 5 BY -1 UNTIL I < 1 correctly iterates 5 times). The gap is this combination: (a) FROM LENGTH OF <field> as the initial value, and/or (b) a reference-modified subscript that uses the loop variable — WS-S(WS-IDX:1) — re-evaluated against the changing WS-IDX in the UNTIL condition. The construct lowers without error but loops wrong. Implementer should isolate which of (a)/(b) is at fault (likely the ref-mod-subscript-in-condition re-evaluation, possibly the LENGTH OF FROM init).

Surfaced in COMEN01C PROCESS-ENTER-KEY: it scans the entered OPTION field right-to-left to find its significant length before parsing the option number.
acceptance_criteria: PERFORM VARYING WS-IDX FROM LENGTH OF WS-S BY -1 UNTIL WS-S(WS-IDX:1) NOT = SPACES OR WS-IDX = 1 leaves WS-IDX at the last non-space position (2 for 'AB  '); FROM LENGTH OF and ref-mod-subscript-in-UNTIL both evaluate correctly each iteration.
notes: Re-spike after 0cci: the real COMEN01C menu-action happy path works (option 01 parsed correctly -> WS-OPTION=1 -> XCTL COACTVWC), so the option-length scan yields the right result for clean input in the real flow. The isolation failure (final idx 0 for 'AB  ') may not replicate the exact real construct or is masked for well-formed input. Keep open (real isolation gap) but NOT a happy-path blocker -> P2; revisit if a malformed/odd option exposes it.
close_reason: PERFORM VARYING FROM <expr> (LENGTH OF) now evaluated as an expression instead of stored as a literal string; ref-mod operands (WS-S(WS-IDX:1)) in a condition relation decode+slice per iteration. Structured (bridge emits {kind:length_of}/ref_mod fields), no regex, no core. Full suite 14050 green.

title: COBOL: class conditions (IS [NOT] NUMERIC / ALPHABETIC / ...) not lowered
description:
Class conditions are not lowered: IF WS-X IS NUMERIC always takes the ELSE branch. Verified: WS-X PIC X(2) VALUE '01'; IF WS-X IS NUMERIC MOVE 1 ELSE MOVE 2 -> result is 2 (ELSE), should be 1. condition_lowering.py has no class-condition handling (grep for NUMERIC/ALPHABETIC/class -> none); it falls through to the text/never-match path. (z31u deferred CLASS/SIGN conditions.)

Scope (language feature): lower the COBOL class conditions IS [NOT] NUMERIC, ALPHABETIC, ALPHABETIC-LOWER, ALPHABETIC-UPPER (and user-defined class names if present). The bridge already serializes a structured class node (z31u contract: {t:class, not, operand, class:NUMERIC|...}); the frontend condition lowering must emit the actual test:
  - NUMERIC: every byte of the field is a digit (per its category/PIC; for DISPLAY numeric, all 0-9, sign handling for signed).
  - ALPHABETIC: every byte A-Z/a-z/space; ALPHABETIC-LOWER/UPPER accordingly.
Surfaced in COMEN01C menu: 'IF WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC OR WS-OPTION > CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT ...' validates the entered option; without NUMERIC the validation is wrong. The '> count' relation already works.
acceptance_criteria: IF X IS NUMERIC true for all-digit X, false otherwise; IS NOT NUMERIC inverts; ALPHABETIC variants work; integrated into the structured condition lowering (no silent never-match).
notes: Re-spike after 0cci: the real COMEN01C menu-action HAPPY PATH works (valid option 01 -> XCTL COACTVWC) WITHOUT this fix. Reason: COMEN01C's check is 'IF WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC OR > count OR = 0'; for a VALID numeric option all disjuncts are false whether or not NUMERIC is correctly lowered, so the broken class condition produces the same (false) result. This bug only manifests on INVALID input (non-numeric option should be rejected but isn't). Real but edge-path, not a flow blocker -> P2.
close_reason: Class conditions IS [NOT] NUMERIC/ALPHABETIC now lower from a structured {not,class,operand} node (bridge) to a CallFunction against COBOL-layer builtins (__is_numeric/__is_alphabetic). No text re-parse, no core. Full suite 14047 green.

title: COBOL: figurative VALUE (VALUE SPACES/ZEROS/LOW-VALUES) stored as literal text, not the figurative fill
description:
A data item declared with a figurative VALUE clause stores the literal NAME instead of the figurative fill. E.g. '01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE SPACES.' initializes WS-X to the text 'SPAC' (the word 'SPACES' encoded + truncated) rather than 4 actual spaces; likewise VALUE ZEROS / LOW-VALUES / HIGH-VALUES / QUOTES. Surfaced while fixing condition lowering (red-dragon-z31u): integration tests had to use 'MOVE SPACES TO WS-X' to initialize fields because 'VALUE SPACES' produced wrong bytes, isolating it as a separate data-division-init defect.

Root area: the VALUE-clause encoding path in the COBOL frontend (interpreter/cobol/lower_data_division.py -> ctx.emit_field_encode(region_reg, fl, fl.value) -> emit_encode_value in interpreter/cobol/emit_context.py -> encode_alphanumeric). This is the SAME init path that red-dragon-3mx4 fixed for hex literals (X'nn'): emit_encode_value got a special case for hex literals (parse_hex_literal) but NOT for figurative constants. A figurative VALUE arrives as fl.value == 'SPACES' (a bare name) and is encoded as character data.

Fix: detect figurative constants in the VALUE-encoding path and fill the field accordingly, sized to the field's byte length and respecting category:
  SPACE/SPACES   -> all spaces (EBCDIC 0x40 across the field)
  ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES -> all zeros (numeric 0 / EBCDIC '0' 0xF0 per field category)
  LOW-VALUE/LOW-VALUES   -> 0x00 bytes
  HIGH-VALUE/HIGH-VALUES -> 0xFF bytes
  QUOTE/QUOTES   -> quote char
Confirm whether ProLeap/the bridge surfaces a figurative VALUE distinctly (a figurative marker) or as the bare name 'SPACES' in fl.value; prefer detecting it structurally if the bridge exposes it, else recognize the canonical figurative names. Note: a real field literally named the same as a figurative is not valid COBOL, so name-matching is safe, but structural detection is cleaner.

Not on the sign-on critical path (programs MOVE figuratives at runtime), but real CardDemo data layouts use figurative VALUE init widely.
acceptance_criteria: 01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE SPACES initializes WS-X to 4 spaces (0x40); VALUE ZEROS/LOW-VALUES/HIGH-VALUES fill correctly per field category; normal literal VALUEs and hex-literal VALUEs (red-dragon-3mx4) still encode correctly.
close_reason: VALUE HIGH-VALUES now emits raw 0xFF bytes via COBOL_RAW_FIGURATIVE_BYTES path in emit_encode_value; ZEROS and LOW-VALUES were already correct. 4 new integration tests added.

title: COBOL: SEND TEXT FROM(field) with a continued VALUE literal resolves to 'None'
description: MOVE CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU TO WS-MESSAGE then EXEC CICS SEND TEXT FROM(WS-MESSAGE) yields 'None' — likely a continued/multi-line VALUE-literal load or a WS-MESSAGE decode issue (CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU has a continued VALUE clause). Observed on the PF3 exit path. Investigate continued VALUE literal handling and field decode for SEND TEXT FROM.
acceptance_criteria: A field initialized from a continued VALUE literal SEND TEXTs its actual text, not 'None'.

title: CICS: dispatcher input_queue.get() on RETURN TRANSID blocks forever with no timeout
description: dispatcher.py:105 input_queue.get() (RETURN TRANSID turn transition) has no timeout. An error-path re-entry (SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN + RETURN TRANSID with an empty input queue) hangs the region forever instead of abending/timing out. Emulation robustness gap (caused spike runs to hit the wall-clock limit). Consider a configurable timeout that abends/returns rather than blocking unboundedly in non-interactive/test contexts.
acceptance_criteria: A RETURN TRANSID with no forthcoming input does not hang indefinitely in test/non-interactive mode (configurable timeout -> clean termination/abend).
close_reason: Fixed: _peek_input_event (cics/dispatcher.py) now takes a timeout parameter (hardcoded default 30.0s, not threaded/configurable per explicit scope decision) and _run_dispatcher_with_runner catches the resulting queue.Empty, returning DispatchResult(kind=DispatchKind.ABEND, abcode='AZCT') instead of hanging forever. AZCT verified against real IBM CICS documentation as the actual transaction abend code for a terminal read-time-out condition. Mirrors the existing TRNI/PGMI early-return style in the same function. TDD: tests/unit/cics/test_dispatcher.py::test_peek_input_event_raises_empty_on_timeout (direct, real queue.Queue, short override) + test_dispatcher_return_transid_timeout_abends_azct (monkeypatched, proves the ABEND/AZCT translation), both verified to fail without the fix. No existing test reaches the new timeout path (all pre-populate their input queue before calling), confirmed via full unit + integration suite regression run.

title: CICS: BMS symbolic map modeling (field <-> COBOL group suffixes I/O/L/A/F)
description: The BMS loader built in pz9g.5 models maps as flat offset+length fields only. Real BMS symbolic maps expose per-field COBOL subfields with name suffixes — input (I), output (O), length (L), attribute (A/F) — and CardDemo MOVEs to/from the suffixed names (e.g. an output field's ...O subfield). SEND/RECEIVE MAP must map each BMS field to the correct symbolic-map COBOL subfield so names line up with what the program references. The current flat byte-offset model cannot express this, so even after field-ref wiring (pz9g.7) the field names will not match.
design: Extend the BMS map model to carry the symbolic-map subfield structure per field. Loader should derive the symbolic group layout (or parse it from the generated copybook). SEND MAP reads each field's output subfield; RECEIVE MAP writes each field's input subfield. Decide whether to add the real external map-generation tool as a submodule or keep an enriched in-house model.
acceptance_criteria: SEND/RECEIVE MAP exchange data via the symbolic-map subfield names a CardDemo program actually references; covered by tests using a representative map.
notes: Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-cics-bms-symbolic-map-design.md
close_reason: BMS symbolic-map data flow: SEND reads <base>O, RECEIVE writes <base>I via vm.data_layout + WS region (mirrors EIB init); flat region model kept as fallback. Loader derives I/O/L subfield names. 129 CICS tests pass.

title: CICS audit: DFHRESP table completeness + verb coverage (LINK, TS queues, etc.)
description: Two audits to de-risk later work. (1) The pre-pass substitutes only 3 DFHRESP codes (NORMAL=0, NOTFND=13, ENDFILE=20). Spec says the full ~120-entry table is bundled. Any other DFHRESP(name) the program references (e.g. DUPREC, NOTOPEN, LENGERR, INVREQ, DUPKEY) currently substitutes wrong/not at all -> parse error or wrong literal. Audit actual usage and bundle the full table. (2) Verb coverage: plans cover RETURN/XCTL/ABEND/ASSIGN/ASKTIME/FORMATTIME/INQUIRE/WRITEQ TD/HANDLE*/READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE/STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV/ENDBR/SEND MAP/RECEIVE MAP/SEND TEXT. Likely-needed but unplanned: LINK (call program + return, distinct from XCTL), READQ/WRITEQ/DELETEQ TS (temp storage, distinct from TD), RECEIVE (no map), SEND CONTROL, SYNCPOINT, GETMAIN/FREEMAIN, START/RETRIEVE. Audit which the target programs use and file follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: DFHRESP table covers every code referenced; a documented list of EXEC CICS verbs used vs covered, with follow-up stories for any gap (LINK and TS queues most likely).
notes:
Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-cics-audit-dfhresp-verbs-design.md
AUDIT DONE (18 online programs). DFHRESP codes used: NORMAL, NOTFND, ENDFILE (have) + DUPREC, DUPKEY (missing) -> add these + full table + no-silent-miss guard. Verb coverage: NO gaps. No LINK, no TS queues (READQ/WRITEQ TS/DELETEQ), no interval-control START (all 21 START hits are STARTBR), no SYNCPOINT/GETMAIN. Everything used is covered by A-E + planned D. Minor verify: confirm a few bare RECEIVE are multi-line RECEIVE MAP, not keyboard RECEIVE.
close_reason: DFHRESP table completed: added DUPKEY=15 + full canonical 0-44 set + preserved higher codes; values verified unique. Unknown-condition fallback now substitutes a 9999 sentinel (never equals a real EIBRESP) instead of 0/NORMAL, so a typo'd condition can't masquerade as the normal path. Verb-coverage audit confirmed no gaps (no LINK/TS/START). 138 CICS tests pass.

title: CICS: BMS map runtime model (headless SEND/RECEIVE MAP)
description:
Backs SEND MAP / RECEIVE MAP — the screen layer of the online tier. Two halves:

(1) Map definitions (partly external): CardDemo ships 10 .bms screen sources (HLASM DFHMSD/DFHMDI/DFHMDF macros) plus generated symbolic copybooks (e.g. COSGN00.CPY with ...I input and ...O output field groups). The ~/code/bms-tools project (HLASM -> JSON -> COBOL symbolic copybook) is taking shape to generate these. Once generated, our existing DATA DIVISION machinery already handles the map records.

(2) Runtime model (this child): a headless representation of a map — fields, attributes, lengths — and SEND/RECEIVE semantics:
- RECEIVE MAP populates the symbolic ...I fields (and length/flag subfields) from supplied input.
- SEND MAP reads the symbolic ...O fields (+ ERASE/CURSOR/FREEKB options) into an output screen record.
- No real 3270 terminal required — represent the screen as a structured record the dispatch driver can feed/inspect.

Depends on bms-tools (or equivalent) for symbolic copybooks; coordinate so generated copybooks resolve via COPY. No decision here on terminal rendering — headless is sufficient for the fitness function.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A generated BMS symbolic copybook resolves via COPY and exposes ...I / ...O field groups. 2. RECEIVE MAP populates input fields from a supplied screen-input record. 3. SEND MAP reads output fields (with ERASE/CURSOR/FREEKB recognized) into an output record. 4. The sign-on map (COSGN00) round-trips: SEND then RECEIVE preserves field values headlessly.
close_reason: BMS screen engine complete: BmsLoader, SEND MAP/RECEIVE MAP/SEND TEXT builtins + lowering, symbolic-map data flow (pz9g.10), EIBAID write-back (pz9g.8). Exercised by real end-to-end flow in pz9g.9.

title: CICS: VSAM/KSDS file model behind CICS file control
description:
Backs the CICS file-control verbs (READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE + browse STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV/ENDBR). CardDemo online reads VSAM KSDS files (USRSEC user-security, accounts, cards, transactions) by key.

Semantics required (access-method level, independent of storage choice):
- KSDS = records keyed by primary key (RIDFLD). READ by exact key; RESP NORMAL/NOTFND.
- Browse cursor: STARTBR positions at/after a key; READNEXT/READPREV iterate in key order; ENDBR closes.
- WRITE (new key, DUPKEY if exists), REWRITE (update in place), DELETE (by key).
- File status / RESP mapping from each operation.
- Records load from CardDemo seed data (app/data EBCDIC/ASCII datasets).

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH IS NOT DECIDED. Options to evaluate (do not pick here):
- Custom: back KSDS with an embedded ordered key->record store (sorted map / SQLite / B-tree); browse = range iteration over sorted keys. In-memory, deterministic, no external dep — likely fits a VM best.
- Open-source precedent: GnuCOBOL's indexed-file layer uses VBISAM (libvbisam, LGPL, C-ISAM compatible) or Berkeley DB (--with-db). KICKS (open CICS-alike) emulates VSAM by opening files per-transaction.
The choice (custom KV vs adapting an OSS ISAM lib) is a deliberate decision for when this child is scheduled; capture trade-offs (determinism, dependency weight, EBCDIC record handling) before committing.
acceptance_criteria: 1. KSDS READ by RIDFLD returns the keyed record into INTO; RESP NORMAL/NOTFND correct. 2. Browse STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV iterate records in key order; ENDBR closes cleanly. 3. WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE mutate the dataset with correct RESP (incl. DUPKEY). 4. CardDemo seed data loads into the file model. 5. Implementation approach documented with trade-offs before coding.
close_reason: VSAM engine (SortedDict KSDS + FCT YAML), point ops (READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE) and browse (STARTBR/READNEXT/READPREV/ENDBR) builtins + lowering. READ/READNEXT/READPREV fill the INTO buffer (Option A); all verbs write EIBRESP/RESP via F's copy-back. Real WRITE->READ and browse round-trips through run_cics. 122 CICS tests pass.

title: env.toml: name the Db2 connection for programs that CONNECT TO a location
description:
forge-run registers the one Db2 DSN (SQUALL_DB2_DSN) under its `DATABASE=` value and makes it current from the start. A program that issues `EXEC SQL CONNECT TO <location>` with a location other than that name finds no connection.

Example: `CONNECT TO DSNDB0G` against a DSN with `DATABASE=testdb` looks up `DSNDB0G`; only `TESTDB` is registered.

Look at: an env.toml `[sql] location` key (default the DSN's DATABASE=), or several named connections. No CardDemo program issues CONNECT TO today. User, 2026-10-16.

title: CardDemo CBSTM03A never finishes: it reopens TRNX-FILE through CBSTM03B until the step budget runs out
description: A one-step CREASTMT run of CBSTM03A (CBSTM03B linked beside it, TRXFL/XREF/ACCT/CUST KSDS seeded) opens STMT-FILE and HTML-FILE, then calls CBSTM03B to open TRNX-FILE again and again (about 470 opens per 2M steps) and abends S322. Behaviour is identical before and after jr5 (checked against 717430f0 + red-dragon 101e4947). Suspect: CBSTM03A's ALTER/GO TO dispatch at 0000-START / 8100-FILE-OPEN. Pinned by jackal/tests/integration/test_carddemo_statement_e2e.py.

title: CICS COMMAREA: pad to the caller's real storage instead of a 32763-byte default
description: assemble_region pads every follow-on COMMAREA to MAX_COMMAREA (32763, CICS's maximum COMMAREA length) because the region does not know the length the receiving program's DFHCOMMAREA declares. Replace the padding with the caller's real storage: hand the next program the COMMAREA the previous one passed, at its own length, and let the receiver's LINKAGE map onto it. Source: spec 2026-10-15-forge-runner-design D9.

title: Named tolerance flags at build and run time, in place of one boolean each
description:
Tolerance is one boolean today, at two points:
- **Compile time:** `build.toml [build] tolerant`, passed to red-dragon's `compile_program`, which skips programs that fail to lower.
- **Run time:** `env.toml` top-level `tolerant`, passed to every runtime that has one. Today that is only squall's `install_sql_runtime`: skip host variables missing from the layout.

Other tolerances are hard-wired defaults rather than config: jackal's `LenientAllocation` (an empty dataset for an unallocatable DD) and `StubMissingProgram` (RC 0 for an absent program).

Replace or extend these with a set of named flags, so a user chooses which tolerant behaviours are on, at build time and at run time separately. User, 2026-10-15.

title: cicada: parse each program's field layout once per run, not per CICS builtin call
description:
cicada's CICS builtins parse the program's field layout from `vm.declarations` once per builtin call: `screen.py` SEND MAP and RECEIVE MAP, and `system.py`. That costs about 9 ms per call on a 1,284-field program. Before 96h this was a dict lookup.

squall now parses a program's layout once per run, in its per-run state, keyed by the identity of the program's `Data` (forge 193bfcb3). Give cicada the same treatment, held in its per-run state; a LINKed program gets its own layout. Measure on a SEND MAP loop before and after.

title: jackal: a SELECT name a main and its callee share resolves to one file table entry
description: program_files_of lists the main's files first, then callees in link order; RealFileIOProvider and AllocatedFileIOProvider key by file_name, last wins, so both programs' OPENs go to the callee's DD and meet its FD. This is pre-96h parity (pinned by test_a_select_name_the_main_and_its_callee_share_takes_the_callees_dd_and_fd). Whether each program should get its own file table is a user decision.

title: carddemo_3270_video.sh never installs the CardDemo system before starting the region
description: `docs/presentation/capture/carddemo_3270_video.sh` starts `cicada-tn3270` without first installing CardDemo's data into the system directory the region TOML names (`/tmp/carddemo-system`), so the region stops at startup with "not cataloged". It was already broken after Task 5 (which required --system). Fix: run `make catnip-install-carddemo SYSTEM=/tmp/carddemo-system` before starting the region.

title: jackal: compare ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clauses with the cataloged AIXs (status 39 + log)
description:
jackal compares an indexed FD's record length and RECORD KEY with the cataloged label (status 39 on conflict, N10 log line), but not its ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clauses. IBM Enterprise COBOL requires those to match the file's alternate indexes too (quoted in the catnip final-fix report, igy6lr40 ~6329/6369). The label carries no AIX list; the catalog does (`SystemCatalog` aixs over a base cluster).

Done when: OPEN of an indexed FD whose ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clauses do not match the base cluster's cataloged AIXs (offset, length, DUPLICATES vs unique) gets status 39 and logs the DSN, field, declared and FD values; test asserts status and exact log lines.

title: Region and job sharing a system directory: CICS file open/close state and locking
description: After catnip (red-dragon-forge-zave), a CICS region and a batch job can share one system directory, but neither locks anything: running both at once can interleave writes to the same cluster. z/OS coordinates this with CICS file state (CEMT / EXEC CICS SET FILE CLOSED|OPEN|DISABLED, used by CardDemo's CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL jobs) and VSAM share options. Model file open/closed state in the region and decide what a job sees while a region has the file open. Out of scope for zave.

title: jackal: run IDCAMS DEFINE AIX / DEFINE PATH / BLDINDEX against catnip
description: jackal parses IDCAMS DEFINE ALTERNATEINDEX, DEFINE PATH and BLDINDEX to NotExecuted. Once catnip (red-dragon-forge-zave) catalogs AIXs and paths, these can create the same entries `catnip install` does: DEFINE AIX (RELATE, KEYS, UNIQUEKEY/NONUNIQUEKEY, UPGRADE), DEFINE PATH (PATHENTRY), BLDINDEX (reject a UNIQUEKEY AIX over repeated keys). Parked by the user 2026-10-14: setup is declarative via `catnip install`; running a codebase's own setup JCL is not required. Acceptance: CardDemo's XREFFILE/CARDFILE/TRANFILE JCL builds the same catalog as config/carddemo/data.toml.

title: catnip: alternate-index duplicates come back in primary-key order, not arrival order
description:
catnip (red-dragon-forge-zave) computes an alternate index's order when a path is opened: records sorted by alternate key, duplicates in primary-key order. z/OS returns duplicates "in the order in which they were placed in the file", and a random read returns "the first record written" in a run of duplicates (IBM Enterprise COBOL, ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause, https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cobol-zos/6.4.0?topic=section-alternate-record-key-clause). The two agree for data loaded at install and differ for records written, or whose alternate key is rewritten, afterwards — e.g. a card added to an existing CardDemo account with a lower card number shows first through CXACAIX.

Fix: store each AIX as an index (alternate key -> primary keys in arrival order), maintained on every base write/rewrite/delete (UPGRADE; a rewrite that changes the alternate key moves the pointer to the end of the new key's run), built in load order by `catnip install`. Confined to red-dragon's alternate-key driver and catnip install; existing system directories are reinstalled. Deferred by the user 2026-10-14; zave lands an xfail test pinning the z/OS order, referencing this issue.

title: jackal reads FD formats from AST files via LinkedProgram.ast_paths; a linked program is not self-contained for jackal
description:
jackal's `ProgramCompiler` (jackal/jackal/program_compiler.py) gets a program's file definitions (FD record formats, used for DD datasets) by re-reading each `.ast.json` named in `LinkedProgram.ast_paths` right after the compile. So a linked program is not enough for jackal on its own: it also needs the AST files in the compile's work directory, and `ast_paths` is the one field of a linked object that points outside it.

Fix: produce the file definitions at lowering and carry them in the compiled output, so jackal reads nothing but the linked program. Then `ast_paths` can be dropped from `LinkedProgram` (a red-dragon change, filed upstream once this lands).

Found while designing the forge's prebuilt-program runner (2026-10-14); that runner covers no-coprocessor, sql and cics programs and does not read ASTs, so it is not blocked by this.
close_reason: file definitions and data layout are IR Data; jackal, squall and cicada read them from the linked program

title: squall tests: rename compile_cobol helper; enter by linked entry label
description: squall/tests/integration/squall_cobol_helpers.py defines compile_cobol(source, bridge_jar_path, connections, copybook_dirs), a wrapper that builds a parser with squall's copybooks plus one SQL CoprocessorSpec and calls red-dragon's compile_program. Its name shadows red-dragon's compile_cobol (different signature, does more); used by ~9 squall test files. Rename it (e.g. compile_sql_program). Its run_cobol picks the procedure entry by scanning linked.func_symbol_table for a label not starting func_init_params_ — the pre-linker two-phase selection; use EntryPoint.function(lambda r: r.label == linked.entry_func_label) instead. No behaviour change intended.

title: jackal: derive a step's link list from cobble's dynamic call targets (targets.jsonl)
description:
Derive jackal's link list from cobble's dynamic-call analysis instead of naming it by hand.

cobble-dataflow-fixpoint (and cobble-dataflow-combine across programs) writes targets.jsonl: per dynamic CALL site its caller and the candidate program names. For a step, start from its program and literal callees, add the candidates of every site whose caller is in that set, and repeat until nothing is added; compile only those. jackal must not import cobble, so it reads the file through its own Pydantic model of the fields it needs. A site with reasons (from-file, uninitialised, ...) may have candidates missing.

User suggestion, 2026-10-12; the explicit list (red-dragon-forge-ua7) was built first as the simpler start. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-dynamic-call-link-list.md.

title: jackal: LIKE=dsname / REFDD=ddname as label models for a new dataset
description:
`LIKE=dsname` (JCL Ref 3.1, "LIKE parameter", p. 208) copies a cataloged model's attributes to a new dataset, including RECFM and LRECL. The SMS counterpart is `REFDD=ddname`. jackal-1o2.12 labels a new dataset from `DCB=dsname` and `DCB=*.dd` (record 2026-10-12-jackal-dcb-attributes.md, A3). The bridge parses `LIKE=` and `REFDD=` but drops them, so such a dataset's label stays pending.

Work: carry LIKE and REFDD as models through the bridge, wire and model, the way the DCB source is carried. Count them in the census first.
close_reason: LIKE=dsname and REFDD=*.dd label a new dataset (LIKE copies a cataloged model, a KSDS's included; REFDD copies the referenced DD's coded RECFM/LRECL); REFDD and DCB referbacks are checked for resolution. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-like-refdd.md.

title: jackal: a DD naming a GDG base reads all its generations (FIFO/LIFO, GDGORDER)
description:
A DD that names a GDG base with no generation number (DSN=A.B.HIST) gets every active generation, concatenated. AMS p. 178 (FIFO|LIFO): "Specifies the order in which the GDS list is returned for data set allocation when the GDG name is supplied on the DD statement". LIFO (newest first) is the default; the JCL keyword GDGORDER overrides it.

Today such a DD resolves as a plain dataset name and fails allocation with DATASET_NOT_FOUND.

Work:
- Keep FIFO|LIFO on the GdgBase. The DEFINE GDG grammar already accepts both.
- At allocation, expand the base into a ConcatenatedAllocation of its active generations, reusing the concatenation path (jackal-1o2.5).
- GDGORDER on the DD, if the bridge carries it.

Split from jackal-1o2.4 (2026-10-12). Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-gdg.md.
close_reason: A DD naming a GDG base reads every active generation as a concatenation, in the GDG's FIFO/LIFO order or the DD's GDGORDER; deleting a generation drops it from the GDG. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-gdg-all.md.

title: IDCAMS: run the executor on the comprehensive parser; retire the narrow grammar
description:
Move the IDCAMS executor from the narrow typed grammar (jackal/idcams/grammar.lark, parser.py) onto the comprehensive parser (grammar/ams.lark, parser_comprehensive.py, ast_*.py), so there is one IDCAMS parser.

Split out of red-dragon-forge-vqa by user decision, 2026-10-12. The census verbs (DEFINE GDG, VERIFY, IF-THEN-DO-END) grow the narrow grammar first so they are not held up by this cleanup. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-gdg.md G1.

Cost measured 2026-10-12. Touching parser_comprehensive.py adopts 342 pyright errors (red-dragon-forge-rqw) and about 440 fp-lint violations: 305 no-list-dict-param-annotation, 30 no-object-type, 24 no-subscript-mutation, 21 no-optional-none, 15 no-deep-nesting, plus smaller counts. The ast_*.py modules carry more.

Done when utilities.py calls the comprehensive parser, every command the narrow executor runs today maps from its AST, and the narrow grammar and parser are deleted.

title: IDCAMS REPRO from a concatenated INFILE DD
description:
IDCAMS REPRO INFILE(dd) where the DD is a concatenation raises TypeError ("DD IN is ConcatenatedAllocation"): REPRO reads one Dataset through DdEnvironment.dataset().

COBOL reads concatenations since jackal-1o2.5 (docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-concatenation.md). Before supporting REPRO, check IBM's AMS Commands (z/OS 3.1) for whether REPRO INFILE accepts a sequential concatenation and with which attributes, then read member after member with jackal.concatenated_records.
close_reason: REPRO reads a concatenated INFILE member after member, each at its own label; a pending member or an output that is also an input ends the command with 12. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-repro-concatenation.md.

title: IDCAMS REPRO: reject records whose length the output cannot hold (IDC3309I), ending after four
description:
REPRO writes every record whatever its length. z/OS rejects some (MSG6 IDC3309I, z/OS 3.1 MVS System Messages Vol 6, p. 790, "RECORD xxx NOT WRITTEN. LENGTH INVALID"):

- a record longer than the output's LRECL;
- a record shorter than the output's LRECL when the output is RECFM=F/FB or an RRDS.

REPRO "continues processing until four such errors occur", then ends the command (UDS z/OS 3.1 p. 121 also ends it on four errors).

Two related gaps to settle here, each from IBM sources:

- red-dragon's drivers pad a short record to the slot length; a KSDS keeps short records at their own length.
- REPRO into an output whose label is still pending: which attributes does the output get?

Decision record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-idcams-repro-labels.md (R3).

title: CARDDEMO_HOME means the checkout root to jackal's CLI but the app/ directory to carddemo-env.sh and cicada
description:
CARDDEMO_HOME means two different directories:
- jackal's CLI (jackal/jackal/cli.py _resolve_dir) and docs/how-to/run-jcl-job.md treat it as the CardDemo checkout root (vendor/carddemo) and append app/cbl, app/cpy.
- carddemo-env.sh, cicada and the root test fixtures (tests/integration/conftest.py carddemo_home) treat it as vendor/carddemo/app.

So sourcing carddemo-env.sh and then running `jackal run` without --source-dir resolves vendor/carddemo/app/app/cbl. Found while adding make jackal-install (which now takes an explicit --data-dir instead of reading the variable). Pick one meaning (the forge-wide one is app/) and make jackal's CLI and its how-to agree.

title: A runaway COBOL program halts with StepBudgetExhausted instead of running forever
description:
A program that never ends (a PERFORM loop with no exit) runs the step forever: nothing bounds a COBOL step's execution.

Blueprint §6 gives it the outcome `Halted(StepBudgetExhausted(n))`: jackal stops the program after a budget of n interpreter steps and records the step as halted, kept apart from the job's own behaviour (z/OS would give S322 for a CPU time-out; mapping it is decision D1). Its effect on the rest of the job is decision D2.

Needs: a step budget passed to the program run, the halt recorded as the step's outcome, and a test with a COBOL program that loops forever. Depends on the outcome type (red-dragon-forge-5fu) and on Halted, which the dispatch issue (red-dragon-forge-xkk) introduces.
close_reason: A COBOL step that exhausts its per-program step budget (JobRunner program_step_budget; CLI 500,000) abends S322, via red-dragon's BudgetExhausted run outcome (red-dragon-lc7c, vendored at 725df8b8). No Halted.

title: jackal: an override DD should merge with the PROC's DD per parameter
description: expand_procs replaces a PROC step's DD wholesale with an override DD of the same name. IBM merges per parameter: //P1.IN DD DISP=OLD changes only DISP and keeps the PROC's DSN; today the result has NoDSN. Likewise an override with only DSN= drops the PROC DD's concatenated members. Predates the object model (old proc_expand did the same); found by the units 2-4 review (2026-10-10).
close_reason: Override DDs merge per parameter: DD.disp is Disp | NotCoded, DSN= is NullifiedDSN in a parsed override, DD.overridden_by applies the JCL Reference pp.28-29 rules (keep / replace / nullify, DUMMY, SYSOUT-DISP exclusion, positional members).

title: Port the presentation capture script to the JCL object model
description: docs/presentation/capture/jcl_capture.py (the evidence capture for the 2026-09-14 capabilities deck) still imports the old jackal model: jackal.jcl.proc_expand, jackal.model.Step, jackal.dsn.dsn_key. Object-model units 3-4 replaced them with jackal.expansion (ExpandedJob, QualifiedStep), ProgramStep and DSN.dataset_name(). No suite or gate runs the script, so it was left for this issue; re-capturing the deck's evidence needs the port first.

title: jcl-bridge: the word NOT in an IF relational expression is a grammar error
description: IF NOT S1.ABEND THEN is a grammar error; the symbol form ¬S1.ABEND parses. The JCL Reference allows both NOT and ¬. Found by the object-model acceptance review (2026-10-10); pinned by jackal/tests/acceptance/test_if.py::test_if_terms_parse. Separate from 2cy.7 (IF structure flattened by the serializer).
close_reason: Fixed in the jcl-bridge lexer/grammar (object-model unit 2, task 1); pinned by ParseFixesTest.

title: cobble: render-webgl --out uses Path() to mean not given
description: `cobble-render-webgl --out` defaults to `Path()` and `_render` treats `Path()` as "not given". `Path()` is `.`, a real path, so `--out .` is silently read as the default, and the meaning rides on a value's representation. The choice between "beside the graph" and "this file" should be explicit. Check also that a missing parent directory of `--out` is created.
close_reason: --out is a function from the graph path to the page's path: the default puts it beside the graph, a given path is taken as given (so --out . is no longer read as the default), and the page's directory is created if missing.

title: cobble-bms-metadata and cobble-bms-render resolve a relative macros_dir against cobble/, not the working directory
description: bms_metadata.resolve_config prefixes a relative [bms] macros_dir with the cobble/ directory. Every other config path, including cobble-sym's use of the same key, resolves against the working directory. Reproduced from the forge root with macros_dir = "cobble/bms-macros": hlasm_export gets cobble/cobble/bms-macros, finds no macros, and cobble-bms-metadata writes a record with no maps for every source while reporting 0 failures; cobble-bms-render then reports no BMS map named COSGN0A. Fix: resolve like every other path, and treat an hlasm_export result with no DFHMSD as a failure.

title: JCL grammar: a null statement or JES2 control statement is allowed only once per job segment
description: JCLParser.g4 lists nullStatement and jes2CntlStatement only in the tail of the statement group that execJCL spells out twice. Two mid-job // null statements, or two mid-job /*ROUTE statements, close the job and fail with mismatched input 'EXEC' expecting JOB. delimiterStatement was fixed by adding it to the mid-job alternation; adding nullStatement there the same way measured slower (SS starts every statement) and recovered nothing on the corpus it was tried on. Latent until a corpus needs it.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: Deferred 2026-10-11: two mid-job null or JES2 statements are rare (a mid-job // ends the job on z/OS), a fix measured slower and recovered nothing, and neither CardDemo nor the census reported it. Revisit when a corpus needs it.

title: Field dataflow does not model EXEC SQL ... INTO / FETCH ... INTO host-variable writes
description: The fixpoint transfer (cobble/dataflow/fields/transfer.py) has no handler for EXEC SQL. The SQL text is opaque and nothing names its host variables as writes, so a SELECT INTO or FETCH INTO write is lost: readers of those host variables see no definer. squall.parser is on cobble's allowed import surface and could name the INTO targets; they would enter as unmodelled (weak) writes.

title: jackal proc_expand reads PROC members with a strict locale decode
description: jackal/jackal/jcl/proc_expand.py parses a PROC member with paths[0].read_text(), which raises UnicodeDecodeError on a byte >= 0x80. Every other corpus read goes through cobol_asg.source_text.decode_source (latin-1, byte-identity). CorpusIndex._expand catches the error, so the job stays indexed unexpanded and its PROC steps are lost from the graph. Fix: decode PROC members with decode_source.
close_reason: DirectoryProcLibrary decodes members with decode_source (latin-1, byte-identity); pinned by tests/integration/test_proc_library.py

title: jackal: replace the three regex uses with grammar productions
description:
jackal parses JCL and IDCAMS by grammar, never by regex (guidelines/project/workflow.md). Three modules use `re`:

- `jackal/jackal/tso.py:49` — `_RUN` pattern
- `jackal/jackal/idcams/preprocess.py:14` — `_PLUS_CONTINUATION` (IDCAMS `+` continuation)
- `jackal/jackal/idcams/ast_values.py:16-17` — `_PLAIN_NAME`, `_GENERIC_NAME` (dataset-name shapes)

Move each into the relevant grammar (TSO command / IDCAMS Lark grammar) and delete the `re` import.

title: Cobble: diagnose-jcl counts 101 CardDemo steps, the graph has 100 STEP nodes
description:
Two Cobble tools count CardDemo's JCL steps differently:
- `diagnose-jcl --config config/carddemo.toml` reports 101 steps (and 327 DDs) across the 38 members.
- The knowledge graph built by `cobble-build` from the same corpus has 100 STEP nodes.

The capabilities deck shows both figures, on different slides.

Find which step the graph drops or merges. Likely candidates are a duplicate step name within a job, an in-stream PROC step, or a step that runs no program. Either fix the graph or document why the two counts measure different things.

title: srccfg SourceSpan uses 0 for absent, but 0 is a valid column
description: NO_SPAN = SourceSpan() is all zeros, and col_start 0 is a real column, so a missing span and a span at column 0 look the same on line_start alone only by accident (line_start 0 is never real). Readers should test absence explicitly, e.g. a typed absent marker, rather than by value. Split out of forge-a7x when its empty-span cause was fixed (2026-10-05).

title: DFHRESP names missing from the table resolve to sentinel 9999 (ENQBUSY, NOSPOOL, NODEIDERR); audit codes
description:
`DFHRESP(name)` for a name missing from cicada's DFHRESP table resolves to the sentinel 9999 (cics/dfhresp_prepass.py, with a warning), so any `IF EIBRESP = DFHRESP(name)` is silently false.

Missing names seen in the census: ENQBUSY (DFHRESP comparisons in 3 programs), NOSPOOL (IGNORE CONDITION in 28 programs), NODEIDERR (IGNORE in 28 programs). The 18 names the census compares account for 55,786 DFHRESP comparisons; the other 15 resolve correctly.

Work: add the missing names with codes taken from the CICS Application Programming Reference (EIBRESP values), and audit the existing table against it at the same time: several entries above 50 (e.g. SYSBUSY 79, SESSIONERR 82) look doubtful from memory and were not checked here. Unknown names should fail the compile rather than become a sentinel, since a sentinel turns a typo into wrong control flow. Do this together with forge-rkh: cicada has two DFHRESP tables (preprocessor._DFHRESP_TABLE and conditions.CONDITION_CODES) that already disagree in coverage.

title: cobble CICS graph: link SPOOLOPEN/SPOOLWRITE programs to their JES spool output
description:
Online programs that write JES spool output (SPOOLOPEN OUTPUT / SPOOLWRITE / SPOOLCLOSE) produce batch-side output, but nothing in the graph connects the CICS program to it.

Reach: 116 statements in 28 programs, always OUTPUT+TOKEN+NODE+USERID+CLASS. Also IGNORE CONDITION NOSPOOL in 28 programs.

Work: a PROGRAM -WRITES-> spool output node (class + node as attrs). Low priority, but it is the only CICS->batch data link in the census, so it matters for end-to-end lineage between the online and batch tiers.

title: cobble CICS graph: carry START TERMID and FROM on START_TRANSID edges
description:
cobble records `START TRANSID(x)` as PROGRAM -START_TRANSID-> TRANSACTION but drops TERMID, so the graph cannot say that a transaction is started on another terminal, e.g. a printer or a session terminal.

Reach: START 3,024 statements in 1,017 programs; 99.8% carry TERMID; 72% carry FROM(+LENGTH). Never INTERVAL/AT/AFTER/REQID. In the census, START is an immediate hop to a named terminal, the pair of RETRIEVE (922 programs).

Work: carry TERMID (literal, or the data-name unresolved) and whether FROM is present as edge attrs on START_TRANSID. Static display only. P3: it refines an edge the graph already has.

title: Execute IKJEFT01 DSN RUN PROGRAM steps through squall (forge composition, 26% of jobs)
description:
Execute the program an IKJEFT01 (TSO) step runs under DB2: `DSN SYSTEM(x) / RUN PROGRAM(p) PLAN(q) / END` in SYSTSIN. Run COBOL program p with its EXEC SQL served by squall.

Reach: 26% of census jobs (exact count), the largest program class after the utilities. Statically this already works: jackal/tso.py extracts the RUN PROGRAM target, and cobble draws STEP -TSO_RUNS_PROGRAM-> PROGRAM. Execution does not; the step falls into the COBOL-source fallback under the name IKJEFT01 (see the dispatch issue).

This crosses runtimes. jackal must not import squall (.importlinter cicada-squall-jackal-independence), so the composition belongs in red_dragon_forge/, which already composes squall with the interpreter for the CardDemo Db2 region (carddemo_db2_region.py). jackal needs a seam: an injected step executor for TSO monitor steps that forge supplies.

Needs design first (Heavy, per workflow.md): the jackal-side seam, how the PLAN maps onto squall's connection/schema setup, Db2 availability in tests (make db2-up), and RC propagation from SQLCODE-driven programs. Depends on the dispatch issue for the "unsupported" result it replaces.
close_reason: IKJEFT01/1A/1B steps run each SYSTSIN RUN PROGRAM as the step's COBOL program, with the step's DDs and the runner's injected coprocessors (squall composed in red_dragon_forge; root test runs SQLRPT under IKJEFT01). Codes follow DSN (highest) and the TMP (abend: 12 under 01, S04C under 1A/1B). Record: 2026-10-12-jackal-tso-run-program.md.

title: JclSerializer flattens IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF: both branches look unconditional
description:
JCL-level `// IF (S1.RC = 0) THEN / ELSE / ENDIF` parses, but JclSerializer emits the steps in both branches as plain unconditional steps and drops the condition and the branch structure. The output asserts something false: that both branches run.

Reach: ~7 jobs in the census (~1%). Real but marginal, hence P3. jackal-1o2.8 (execution of IF/THEN and COND=EVEN/ONLY) needs this structure first.

Work: serializer emits the IF construct (condition expression, THEN steps, ELSE steps) or attaches the guard to each enclosed step. The model gains a typed condition (RC/ABEND/RUN tests on named steps, AND/OR/NOT), not a string. cobble shows the guard on the JOB -> STEP edge next to S5's COND attrs. jackal must reject a job containing IF until jackal-1o2.8 lands, rather than running both branches.
close_reason: Bridge half fixed by the unit 2 contract (ContractTest). The model half lands in units 3-4 (2cy.9, 2cy.10), pinned by the acceptance suite.

title: squall builds its Lark parser twice: _grammar.py duplicates parse.py's setup for two test files
description: squall/parser/_grammar.py builds a second Lark instance from grammar.lark, differing from parse.py's by propagate_positions. Only tests/unit/test_grammar_matrix.py and test_lexer.py use it, so they run a configuration production does not. Point them at parse.py's parser and delete _grammar.py.
close_reason: squall's EXEC SQL parser is built once, in parse.py; the grammar tests use it

title: cobble: value sets in the program's storage encoding (EBCDIC), not text
description: Cobble's value sets are ASCII/UTF-8 text: alphanumeric VALUEs are imaged as UTF-8, candidates decoded as text. Numeric fields are therefore imaged only where a text form is faithful -- unsigned or positive zoned decimal, as digits -- and every negative, COMP, COMP-3 and edited value is left out. Follow-up: keep values as the bytes the program's storage holds (EBCDIC zoned with sign overpunch, packed, binary), using RedDragon's storage encoders once they live in a package cobble may import, and convert literals, candidates and program-name comparisons at the boundary.

title: cobble duplicates the interpreter's numeric digit alignment
description: cobble/dataflow/fields/numeric_digits.py reimplements left_adjust and align_decimal from RedDragon's interpreter/cobol/data_filters.py to image numeric VALUE clauses: cobble may not import the interpreter (import contract cobble-no-interpreter). Follow-up: move those two helpers into RedDragon's cobol_numeric (which both may import), repoint the interpreter's importers (pic_scale, zoned_decimal, comp3, binary and their tests), and have cobble import them -- leaving one copy.

title: cobble fixpoint: a read after a non-literal write reports 'uninitialised'
description: state._missing answers a value-map miss in WORKING-STORAGE with UNINITIALISED, and a write whose content is not a literal (MOVE 1 TO X, any arithmetic) stores nothing, by design (_UNINFORMATIVE), so a later read of X reports 'uninitialised' though X was written. The reason should distinguish 'never written' from 'written with content the walk cannot name' (not-a-literal); today the two collapse into the first.
close_reason: a miss on bytes a write reached reports not-a-literal

title: cobble fixpoint: a VALUE clause's definer is reported as the reading statement
description: A read of a field whose only definition is its VALUE clause gets definers [<the reading node>] in defs.jsonl, rather than anything naming the initial image. A consumer reading definers cannot tell an initial value from a write by that statement.
close_reason: Fixed in 41be8db: a read no statement wrote has empty definers.

title: squall/parser/parse.py: 33 fp-lint violations, excluded rather than fixed
description:
`squall/squall/parser/parse.py` carries 33 python-fp-lint violations and was added
to `fp.json`'s exclude list so that a WHENEVER parser fix could land without a
large unrelated refactor blocking it.

Breakdown: 7 `C901` complexity ceilings, 2 `PLR0915` statement ceilings, the rest
`no-is-not-none` and one `I001`. The complexity ones are the awkward kind --
Lark tree-walking, where each `whenever_cond` / `whenever_action` / `_cursor_ref`
style extractor branches over child node shapes.

Per `fp.json`'s own convention a file leaves the exclusion list, with its
violations fixed, in the change that first touches it. This one did not, by
explicit decision: the change that touched it was fixing a live defect where a
corpus containing Pro*COBOL `WHENEVER ... PERFORM` lost members permanently to a
cached `.fail`, and 33 unrelated violations in squall's central parser should not
gate that.

`cicada/cics/cics_parser.py` is on the list for the same shape, so the precedent
is parsers rather than a new category.

To clear it: fix the violations, drop the `exclude` entry and its `exclude_why`
key together. The `no-is-not-none` and `I001` ones are mechanical; the complexity
ones want the per-node extractors split so each branches once.

title: fp-lint: 26 unowned rule buckets (209 violations) — make every rule in the run attributable
description:
**26 fp-lint rules, 209 violations** that no live bead named as of 2026-09-26. Filed so every rule in the current run is attributable; most are small enough to clear opportunistically rather than as a campaign.

(The 27th unowned rule, `invalid-syntax` ×3, is red-dragon-forge-3h4 — a ruff target-version problem, not real debt. The largest, `no-list-dict-param-annotation` ×335, is red-dragon-forge-2lt.)

## The buckets

**Complexity (31)** — `PLR0915` 31. Note `fp.json` sets `max_statements: 10` and `max_complexity: 3`; those ceilings have never been validated against this workspace, so decide the threshold before refactoring. `C901` 46 is already owned via `fp.json`'s `exclude_why` entries.

**Mutation family (75)** — `no-subscript-augmented-mutation` 28, `no-list-append` 25, `no-mutation-outside-init` 11, `no-set-add` 5, `no-list-pop` 2, `no-local-augmented-mutation` 2, `no-attribute-augmented-mutation` 2, `no-list-extend` 1, `no-dict-clear` 1, `no-set-discard` 1. Check each against the precedent `fp.json`'s `exclude_why` already sets: `asg_walk.py`'s explicit stack and `worklist.py`'s fixpoint earn their mutation on measured grounds (837s vs under a second), while `depgraph/` and `fixpoint.py` are recorded as deferred backlog, not exemption. New sites should be judged the same way — is the mutation the algorithm, or an accumulator a comprehension would say better?

**Nullability (34)** — `no-is-not-none` 20, `no-is-none` 14. Read `squall/squall/builtins/exec_sql.py`'s `exclude_why` entry first: it argues at length that `None` is the connector protocol's own return type for "no such backend", so some of these are structurally forced rather than fixable. Do not convert them to private sentinels that mean the same thing one term over.

**Import/format hygiene (21)** — `I001` 21. Ruff safe autofix: `uv run --no-sync ruff check --select I001 --fix <paths>` then black.

**Mechanical, needs a glance each (23)** — `RUF022` 6 (`__all__` not sorted), `SIM905` 6 (`.split()` on a literal), `UP037` 5 (quoted annotations no longer needed), `UP007`/`UP035` 2 each, `BLE001` 1 (`cobble/cobble/parsing/parse_corpus.py:106`, blind `except Exception`), `no-unfrozen-dataclass` 1 (`tools/mainframe_inventory.py:522`).

**Design rules (18)** — `no-static-method` 6, `no-none-default-param` 4, `no-any-type` 4 + `ANN401` 4 (same sites, double-counted), `T201` 4 (`print`; if the 4 are in `tools/`, a per-file-ignore is the right answer, not logging).

## Verification

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m python_fp_lint check --config fp.json cicada squall jackal red_dragon_forge cobble tools tests
```

title: cobble: lower-bound candidate sets for dynamic transfer targets
description:
Second tier after the VALUE seed, and only if the closure bundle wants it.

Not "resolved" -- a lower bound: "this XCTL reaches at least these N members, plus an
unknown cross-program arm". Reaches 87% of CardDemo sites, 17 of them naming exactly one
program (constprop spike, 2026-09-22).

MUST be labelled incomplete and never as resolved. The slots already exist: `resolved:
bool` on srccfg's CallSite, `target_resolved` on the CFG node, `unresolved_sites` for the
report. srccfg's own convention is "record it, mark it unresolved, let the consumer
decide" -- follow it rather than inventing a second vocabulary.

Why strict reaching-definitions propagation is NOT the thing to build: it resolves 0 of
88. Against CardDemo's dominant shape it is structurally incapable -- the target is a
COMMAREA field written by the PREVIOUS program, and no intra-program lattice can close
that. The relaxed candidate-set version is what pays, by allowing one VALUE-constant hop
through a MOVE.

Also note there is not one dynamic COBOL CALL in any ASG cobble can produce: 51 literal
CALLs, zero identifier ones across two corpora and 58 parsed members. The CALL LIT-DSNTIAC
case that motivated this work is unreachable twice over -- behind an EXEC SQL INCLUDE
ProLeap does not expand, in COTRTLIC.cbl which does not parse. So justify and measure any
work here against CICS LINK/XCTL, not against CALL.

title: COTRTUPC's insert-failure message shows uninitialised memory, not DSNTIAC text
description:
test_admin_six_insert_failure_reports_the_update_s_stale_sqlcode observes ERRMSG as 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:  100:?Statem' -- the ':?Statem' tail is uninitialised storage rendered in front of the operator.

It is NOT the DSNTIAC path: squall now links a DSNTIAC stub and every message built by CSDB2RPY.cpy's 9999-FORMAT-DB2-MESSAGE carries real formatted text (see the two COTRTLIC tests in the same file, which now assert 'DSNTIAC: SQLCODE=+100'). COTRTUPC's 9700-INSERT-RECORD builds its failure message itself rather than PERFORMing 9999, so it STRINGs a field nothing ever populated.

Determine whether this is CardDemo's own defect (a field the program never initialises, in which case it is characterisation-test material like the stale-SQLCODE bug the same test pins) or a gap in how this tier initialises COTRTUPC's working storage. Scope is COTRTUPC only; the DSNTIAC CALL path is done (forge-brx).

title: ProLeap cannot parse COTRTLIC (CardDemo admin option 5)
description: Compiling vendor/carddemo/app/app-transaction-type-db2/cbl/COTRTLIC.cbl through the ProLeap bridge fails: 'syntax error in line 2899:7 extraneous input YYYY-STORE-PFKEY expecting {ACCEPT, ADD, ...}'. Line 2899 is in the PREPROCESSED output, not the source -- the source's own columns are clean (no junk past col 72, no odd indicator column), and the identical 'PERFORM YYYY-STORE-PFKEY THRU YYYY-STORE-PFKEY-EXIT' split across two lines parses fine in COACTVWC. Suspect a copybook expansion: COTRTLIC uses EXEC SQL INCLUDE (CSDB2RWY, SQLCA, DCLTRTYP), which is a SQL INCLUDE rather than a COBOL COPY. Its sibling COTRTUPC parses fine and fails later, at lowering. Blocks admin option 5 independently of the Db2 wiring.
close_reason: Disproven. COTRTLIC parses cleanly now. The original 'syntax error in line 2899:7 extraneous input YYYY-STORE-PFKEY' was an artifact of how I probed it: that run composed only the CICS spec, so squall's prepass never expanded the program's EXEC SQL INCLUDE statements and ProLeap saw raw EXEC SQL blocks in the DATA DIVISION. With the SQL spec composed (and after the sequence-number fix in d0264d8a), ProLeap's parse phase succeeds completely. COTRTLIC now fails later, at lowering, on a missing DFHEIBLK, which looked like a scratch-harness artifact (no CICS EIB wiring) rather than a program defect. Any further work on admin option 5 is covered by the ProLeap copybook-substitution bug filed in red-dragon's tracker, which blocks both Db2 options.

title: CCXREF/CXACAIX config: two keyed views of one physical VSAM file, inert until something writes CARDXREF
description:
Whole-branch review finding L6: the TN3270 region config declares [datasets.CCXREF] and
[datasets.CXACAIX] as two separate keyed views (different key definitions) over what is
the SAME physical CARDXREF file, seeded into two independent VSAM stores rather than one
store with two access paths/AIX-style key views.

Currently inert: nothing in the CRUD flows writes CARDXREF (COTRN02C/COBIL00C only READ it
via CVACT03Y), so the two stores can never actually diverge today. But the moment any future
flow WRITEs through one keyed view (e.g. CCXREF), the other (CXACAIX) silently goes stale --
a correctness trap for whoever adds that write path, with no test able to catch it since
both views currently only ever see the same seed data.

Needed: either model CARDXREF as one physical VSAM store with two key definitions/alternate
indexes (matching real VSAM AIX semantics), or, if kept as two independent stores, document
the divergence risk directly in the config/loader and add a bead-tracked TODO gate before
any write path is added to either dataset name.

title: fp-lint: cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/fixpoint.py is a deferred backlog, not a design exemption
description:
After pinning python-fp-lint to 38058041 (was the mutable `rev: main`), 9 pre-existing violations in the byte-dataflow solver began blocking any commit that stages the file: no-loop-mutation and no-subscript-mutation over `_propagated`'s sweep loop (409-412), no-deep-nesting at 409, C901 on `_eta` (263) and `_propagated` (393) at 4 > 3, and the reassignment gate on `settled`/`sweep`/`states` in `_swept` (444-445). The file is excluded in fp.json so an unrelated rename could land; the exclusion is a deferral, not a claim that mutation is the design here.

Decide per site whether the loop is genuinely the algorithm (a worklist fixpoint has a real case, the way asg_walk.py's explicit stack does) or just an accumulator that a reduce would say better, then either rewrite it and drop the exclusion, or rewrite exclude_why to state the constraint instead of the backlog.
acceptance_criteria: Either fixpoint.py passes fp-lint and its fp.json exclusion is removed, or exclude_why records a design constraint rather than a deferral.
notes: Same shape as the depgraph/ exclusion already in fp.json. Surfaced by the rename of cobble.dataflow.fields -> cobble.dataflow.fixpoint; the file's content was unchanged by that commit.

title: Path trace: nested via and the two unenterable-callee dead ends are untested
description: Three paths through cobble/cobble/dataflow/fields/trace.py have no test. (1) _Walk.via reports the INNERMOST crossing site when calls nest, so a two-hop path A->B->C should credit C's writes to B's call site, not A's; only the one-hop case is covered. (2) The UNSIZEABLE dead end -- a callee whose WORKING-STORAGE cannot be laid out (UnsizeableFieldError) cannot be entered, and the spec is explicit that the callee's LINKAGE laying out is not evidence the rest of it does. (3) The NO_PROCEDURE dead end -- a callee with no PROCEDURE DIVISION entry node. Both dead-end reasons are produced by _callee_unenterable and rendered in the report's 'dead ends:' section, and neither is exercised.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails if via stops reporting the innermost crossing site, and a test fails if either unenterable-callee reason stops reaching the report.
notes: Found by the final whole-branch review of the path-sampling trace (finding M11) and deferred: each needs a fixture that costs more to build than the branch it pins. Nested via needs three real members parsed through the JVM, or a hand-built three-program loader. UNSIZEABLE needs a member whose WORKING-STORAGE genuinely fails to lay out, which is easier to fake through the Loaded seam than to write in COBOL -- traced() takes a loader precisely so a caller can hand it graphs it built itself, and Loaded carries a 'reason' field, so a stub loader returning Loaded(program=..., reason=UNSIZEABLE) is probably the cheap route for (2) and (3).

title: Path trace: --max-depth truncation is silent in the report
description: cobble/cobble/dataflow/fields/trace.py's sampler bounds one path's node count with --max-depth (default 5000). When a path is truncated the walk stops mid-flight: _ended never runs, so a LINK callee's commarea write-back is skipped and the caller's remaining path is dropped, and nothing in the report says a path was cut. The coverage denominator is recomputed over programs actually entered, so a truncation that stops the walk before it enters a callee shrinks numerator and denominator together -- the percentage under-reports rather than over-reports, which is why this is not a wrong answer, only an invisible one. Found by the final whole-branch review of the path-sampling trace (finding I3) and deferred deliberately: making truncation legible is a design question about what the report should say, not a bug fix, and the spec's four stated limits do not currently mention it.
acceptance_criteria: A reader of the report can tell how many sampled paths were cut short by --max-depth, without a verdict or confidence channel being introduced.
notes: Deferred from the path-sampling trace branch (bead nxy) rather than fixed there. Whatever it reports must not become a verdict or a confidence score: a query-time stop layer was deleted from the sibling query.py on 2026-09-07 for being unreadable, and this must not reintroduce it in another shape. A truncated-path count on the summary line, or a 'paths truncated at --max-depth: N' line beside 'dead ends:', is the shape to consider.

title: callee-not-in-cache can name a callee that was parsed, because the cache is keyed by filename
description: aliases.py's _callee_commarea reads asg_dir / f'{callee}.json', where callee is the PROGRAM literal off the call site. The ASG cache names its files after the member, so wherever a member's PROGRAM-ID differs from its member name -- routine in real corpora -- a callee that was parsed and is present under another filename is reported as callee-not-in-cache. The reason then sends a reader to check the parse when what is wrong is the lookup key. Distinct from 1e5, which is about members genuinely not parsed. Fix by resolving through the program-id index the corpus pass already builds and falling back to the filename; or, if filename keying is the contract, say so in the reason's documentation. Not constructed: it needs a cache directory whose filenames disagree with its program ids.

title: call_sites' empty-target filter drops a call site before it can become an alias row
description: srccfg/link.py's call_sites filters on 'node.transfer in CALL_TRANSFERS and node.target'. A call node whose target resolved to the empty string is therefore not yielded at all, so commarea_aliases never sees it and the site emits no aliases.jsonl row -- silence, against the constraint that every call site is a row naming what stopped it. Reachability is argued, not constructed: for CICS, desugar's _with_call leaves the node untransferred when PROGRAM is missing, so the one literal route is PROGRAM('') (is_literal is true and the quotes strip to empty); for COBOL, _cobol_call sets the transfer unconditionally and takes program via getattr with a '' default, so an ASG CallStatement without a program is a CALL with an empty target. Constructing that needs the JVM parser. The cheap fix is to drop 'and node.target' and let _target/_dead report it as dynamic-target or a new unnamed-target reason. Not fixed in the plan's last round: call_sites is shared srccfg surface with other consumers and the trigger is unconstructed.

title: _flow_step credits a flow to one frontier entry when its near end overlaps several
description: query.py's _flow_step emits one _At per flow rather than one per (flow, matching frontier entry) pair: 'for flow in store.touching(ranges, side)' with _from picking a single entry. A flow whose near end overlaps two frontier entries standing on different bytes is therefore attributed to one of them, and the arrival it produces carries that entry's cost and via. What masks it is _from's own min: the entry chosen is the cheapest of the matches, so the cost is right even when the attribution is arbitrary, while via can still name a route that did not carry those particular bytes. Emitting per pair is the correct shape and would grow the frontier, so it was left; the misattribution surfaces the day _from stops taking the minimum. Do not read _canonical as a second guard here: it dedupes a level, and since _from and _deduped both take the minimum a dearer twin changes no reported cost -- what it does is keep the twin off the next frontier, which is frontier size, not attribution.

title: A COMMAREA operand of nothing but qualifiers is reported as caller-field-unknown
description: aliases.py's _reference drops every qualifier keyword from the operand and takes the first word that is left, defaulting to the empty string: COMMAREA(OF) yields name=''. _windows then finds no cell of that name and the site's row reads caller-field-unknown, which is a limit reason meaning 'the operand named nothing this member's layout holds'. For a malformed operand the honest reason is that the operand itself did not parse, not that the caller's layout was searched and came up empty -- a reader triaging caller-field-unknown rows will go looking for a missing copybook. Either add a reason for an unparseable operand or say in the reason's documentation that it covers both. Unreachable from valid CICS syntax; found while reviewing the raise this replaced (see closed 3da).
close_reason: Resolved by documentation: _reference's docstring now names the all-qualifier operand case and why CALLER_FIELD_UNKNOWN is the truthful reason for it.

title: .talismanrc has ~150 entries, many inert, and an upsert re-whitelists a file wholesale
description: The file keeps growing and a large share of its entries do nothing. Talisman resolves duplicate filenames first-occurrence-wins (see forge-9yz for the convention doc that says otherwise), so a second entry for an already-listed filename is inert from the moment it is written; and every entry is checksum-pinned, so it goes inert again the next time its file changes. The convention is now upsert rather than append-only, which unblocks the immediate problem, but leaves a real hazard: an upsert re-whitelists the whole file, so a genuinely new finding is suppressed alongside the benign ones it was meant to cover. Worth a sweep to drop the inert entries and a note that talisman's output must be read before upserting.

title: aliases.jsonl coverage is bounded by the parse, not by the model
description: A third of measured LINK sites resolve to callee-not-in-cache: a literal target the parse never covered. The reason makes the gap visible, which is the point, but the table's usefulness scales with corpus coverage. Worth measuring the reason tally per corpus config after a full parse so the number is tracked rather than rediscovered.

title: _rebased hardcodes known=True instead of deriving it from the row it rebases
description: _rebased sets known=True as a literal. It is sound only by an invariant on rows that file does not write: that a live alias row always carries two parseable extents. If a live row ever carries an unparseable callee_extent, the crossing walk proceeds on a range it only believes it knows -- a reviewer got a phantom '@[0:12]' in program '' back from store.across by breaking that invariant. Nothing guards it any more: the one .known check that stood downstream lived on the query-time stop layer, deleted on 2026-09-07. Derive known from the parsed extents, or assert the invariant where the rows are read.

title: 'depth limit N' is emitted from hitting the cap, not from the cap costing the answer anything
description: The same hindsight flaw that was fixed for 'hop limit N' is still present for 'depth limit N'. It is emitted from the bare fact that the walk reached its depth budget, never from whether the level the cap refused would have added bytes nothing else reached -- so a walk that had already found everything still tells the reader its answer may be truncated. That is the reader-trust failure the hop-limit fix exists to kill. The same machinery serves it unchanged: record what the depth cap refused as candidate landings on _Cross and resolve them at assembly against the finished seen, exactly as _limits now does for blocked crossings. Deliberately not fixed when found -- pre-existing and plan-prescribed.
close_reason: Obsolete: the query-time stop layer was deleted on 2026-09-07 at the user's direction, so there is no 'depth limit N' line to make honest. Crossing() now publishes landings only. If a truncation warning is ever wanted again it has to be designed to be readable first -- that was the failure of the layer this bead described.

title: A crossing answer's hops is minimal only within the depth budget, and does not say so
description: Landing.hops is the minimum among the routes the walk found within its --depth budget, which is now delivered: _from prices a flow off the cheapest frontier entry over its bytes and each level's admitted set is deduped to one entry per (field, bytes) at minimum cost, so a landing's cost no longer depends on the order the step built its arrivals. What remains is the depth qualification. A route costing fewer commarea hops but more flow steps than --depth allows is never found, so the published hops is an upper bound on the global minimum. The walk knows when it hit the depth cap (it emits 'depth limit N') but nothing connects that to the hop figures. Either state the qualification per landing or record which landings a deeper budget could still re-cost. The crossing() docstring and the README already scope the claim to 'within the depth budget'.

title: Nothing reports that a call graph loops, now that the byte-level cycle stop is gone
description: A loop in the call graph is genuinely useful to a human reading a member, and nothing reports one. The byte-level 'cycle at X' stop the crossing walk once emitted was not it: at byte level a loop and a fan-in re-convergence are indistinguishable, so it fired on diamonds with no loop anywhere, and it was not a stop either -- the bytes had already been reached at equal or lower cost. It was deleted, and then the whole query-time stop layer around it was deleted too (2026-09-07), so there is no 'hop limit N' line standing in for it any more. The honest version needs its own channel and its own definition at CALL-GRAPH level, where a loop and a diamond can be told apart. Do not re-add the byte-level stop.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: Deviation accepted by the user on 2026-09-07: the spec required a cycle stop distinct from the hop limit, and it was deleted deliberately. Do not restore it in the byte-level walk -- it fired on fan-in diamonds with no loop anywhere, because at byte level a re-convergence and a loop are indistinguishable. This bead is the correct home for it, at call-graph level.

title: Alias rows do not say machine-readably whether no bytes are shared or whether it is unknown
description: The reason field on a dead-end row carries two different claims and nothing separates them. 'No bytes are shared' is a fact about the two programs (no-commarea-operand, callee-declares-no-commarea, empty-window). 'We cannot say which bytes are shared' means sharing likely happens at runtime and the analysis stopped (callee-not-in-cache, dynamic-target, caller-field-unknown, call-using-unsupported, unreadable, unsizeable, alias-phase-failed).
