The artefact says neither: a consumer joining aliases.jsonl gets a bare string and must hardcode a partition of ten constants it has no way to discover from the row, and when an eleventh reason is added every such consumer is silently wrong. The README now names all ten labelled fact or limit, so the partition is recoverable by a human reading prose -- that is the standing-in-for, not the fix. A shares: no | unknown field would make it a join. Deliberately deferred when the split was found: a new artefact field had no authority in the spec.

title: Two members with an empty program_id never register as a collision
description: build_corpus's _seen guards on 'if result.program', so a member whose program_id is empty is never entered in the collision map. Two such members therefore share a namespace with no report at all: the run gives aliased: 2 against one alias row, collisions: 0, and exit 0 -- where two members that DO share a non-empty program_id are exit 3. README's unconditional 'a program_id two members declare is exit 3' was qualified for this. Fix is to key collisions on the member path when the program name is absent, or to report an empty program_id as its own defect.

title: A dead-end alias row's blank callee cannot be told from a target the pass failed to resolve
description: A dead-end row derives callee from site.resolved, so the blank means 'the target could not be resolved'. That is honest but conflates two cases a consumer would separate: a dynamic-target site whose callee is genuinely unknowable without a runtime value, and a site whose target the pass simply did not manage to resolve. Both read as one blank. Needs either a distinguishing reason or a resolution-attempt field; not a rename, since the blank's current meaning is documented and relied on.

title: A COMMAREA operand that is only a qualifier keyword raises out of _reference
description: aliases.py's _reference splits an operand on the qualifier keyword and indexes the result, so an operand that is nothing but that keyword -- COMMAREA(OF) -- raises an uncaught ValueError. Unreachable from valid CICS syntax, but it is the one route that reaches the per-site alias-phase-failed wall, so it is how that wall was proven reachable at all. One-line hardening: refuse the operand as a named dead end instead of raising.
close_reason: Already fixed and on a stale premise. _reference ends 'return _Reference(name=next(iter(named), ""), qualifiers=named[1:])' -- next() has a default and cannot raise, and the docstring covers the all-qualifiers operand. The per-site alias-phase-failed wall this bead said the raise reached was deleted in f24e138, the same commit that fixed the raise. The residual it was reaching for is filed separately.

title: A subscripted COMMAREA operand dead-ends instead of resolving one occurrence
description: EXEC CICS LINK ... COMMAREA(WS-TABLE(1)) is written as a caller-field-unknown dead-end row, because the alias pass resolves the operand as a bare name and the subscript makes the lookup miss. Resolving it needs the occurrence arity read off the operand text and the element's per-occurrence extent selected from it, which is a real piece of work rather than a lookup fix. Until then the row correctly names the limit rather than inventing a window; this bead is to close the gap.

title: UNSIZEABLE alias reason and the NO_INDEX guard are both unreachable dead code
description: Two guards in the field dataflow build can never fire, for the same root cause. aliases.py's UNSIZEABLE reason is only reachable when _binary_bytes raises, which needs more than 31 digits, but parse_pic rejects anything over 18 first -- so PIC S9(38) COMP comes back as 'unreadable: ValueError(... must be 1 to 18)' and UNSIZEABLE is never written. side_tables/analysed's 'index is NO_INDEX' silence branch is unreachable for the same reason: no input the emitter can produce reaches it. Both docstrings now say so. Fix is to delete the constant and the branch, or to widen layout so the >18-digit case reaches them honestly. Merged from two carry-forwards the reviewers identified as one item.

title: Field walk needs one more sweep to prove settledness after the terminator model
description:
A member can now report settled=False at a sweep budget that previously reported True, with byte-identical results. Measured on a 76-node member in the CICS corpus: 28 edges and 15 reaching defs at every sweep count from 2 to 6, both before and after red-dragon-forge-6ry, but settled goes True at 3 sweeps before the change and only at 4 sweeps after it.

Cause: giving STOP RUN, GOBACK and EXIT PROGRAM no exit removes edges from the CFG, which changes the depth-first order the sweep walk propagates in. Stability is therefore observed one pass later. The fixpoint itself is unmoved -- nothing is missing at 3 sweeps, the walk just has a pending change queue when the budget ends.

Consequence: settled=False is documented to mean 'the edges are a subset', so a consumer reading the flag conservatively will now discard a complete answer on some members. That is the wrong direction for a flag whose only job is to distinguish partial from whole. Cost is bounded at one extra sweep in the case measured; whether it is one sweep in general is not established.
design: Two candidate fixes, neither investigated yet. (1) Detect stability by comparing the state after a sweep with the state before it, rather than by whether a change queue is empty when the budget runs out -- an equal state is settled regardless of pending work. (2) Leave detection alone and raise the default sweep floor, which costs every member time to fix a flag on a few. (1) is the honest one; (2) trades correctness of the flag for nothing.
acceptance_criteria: A member whose results are identical across sweep budgets reports settled at the lowest budget that reaches them. Regression test uses a synthetic program, not a corpus member.

title: srccfg: abandoned over-reports where a FALLTHRU was refused as never-executing
description:
reaching_conditions names a zero-guard node 'abandoned' (walk gave up) whenever some guarded node leads to it. That predicate cannot tell 'the walk lost a route' from 'the walk correctly refused an edge that never executes'.

Concretely: a paragraph performed from elsewhere has, at its end, a RETURN edge to its caller AND a FALLTHRU edge into the next paragraph in source order. Only the RETURN executes. _not_a_fallthrough_a_return_will_take refuses the FALLTHRU, correctly. But the paragraph end HAS guards, so the next paragraph -- which nothing performs and nothing runs into -- comes out zero-guard with a guarded predecessor, and is reported as abandoned rather than as dead code.

Measured on a synthetic program: MAIN performs DRIVER then stops; NEVER-RUN sits after DRIVER in source order; nothing performs NEVER-RUN. All three of its nodes land in abandoned. Guards are correct (empty); only the classification is wrong.

Direction of the error is the safe one -- 'do not trust this' instead of 'this is dead' -- which is why it is P3 and was not folded into the 3ao fix. The cost is the one Reaching's own docstring names: reading dead code as abandoned throws away a finding worth having, because a paragraph nothing performs and nothing falls into is a real thing to report.

Candidate fix: when deciding whether a guarded predecessor is evidence of abandonment, skip a FALLTHRU edge whose source carries a RETURN edge. That is the graph-level shape of 'this fallthrough is not the continuation'. It stays correct inside a PERFORM A THRU C range, where the interior paragraph ends carry no RETURN of their own and their fallthrough IS the executing edge -- only the range's last paragraph end has the return.

Exposed while reviewing the 3ao fix: became visible only once that fix gave the paragraph end guards it previously lacked.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic program with a performed paragraph followed in source order by a paragraph nothing performs reports that second paragraph as dead code (zero guards, not in abandoned). An interior paragraph of a PERFORM THRU range still reaches the next paragraph in the range by fallthrough. Full cobble suite green.
notes:
RE-VERIFIED reproducing as of 6ry landing (2026-09-07). 6ry was masking it: the fall-through cascade gave the supposedly-dead paragraph real guards, so the predicate was never reached. With terminators modelled, the bead's own synthetic example reproduces exactly as described.

MAIN: PERFORM DRIVER. GOBACK. / DRIVER: MOVE 'D' TO WS-D. / NEVER-RUN: MOVE 'N' TO WS-N.
NEVER-RUN#label, NEVER-RUN/0 and NEVER-RUN#end all have zero guards (correct) and all three are in abandoned (wrong -- they are dead code). DRIVER#end has one guard, and its FALLTHRU into NEVER-RUN is refused because a RETURN will take it, which is exactly the shape the description names. MAIN#end correctly has no guards now.

Note when writing the test: the simpler shape without a PERFORM does NOT reproduce -- a paragraph whose predecessor's #end is itself unguarded has no guarded predecessor, so it is already reported unreachable rather than abandoned. That case is covered by test_an_unreached_paragraph_is_reported_unreachable_and_not_abandoned in tests/dataflow/srccfg/test_desugar_terminator.py. The a3d shape needs the refused FALLTHRU out of a GUARDED paragraph end.

title: EXEC CICS SEND (terminal control, no MAP) is unimplemented
description:
Bare EXEC CICS SEND FROM(...) LENGTH(...) — terminal control, writing a data area straight to the terminal without a map — has no lowering branch. SEND MAP and SEND TEXT are implemented; this third form is not.

12 occurrences across the test corpus, all on abend paths, e.g. COACTVWC:

  EXEC CICS SEND
                   FROM (ABEND-DATA)
                   LENGTH(LENGTH OF ABEND-DATA)
                   NOHANDLE
  END-EXEC
  EXEC CICS HANDLE ABEND ...

Since 1511575a it abends UNSP when reached rather than being silently dropped, so a program relying on it now fails loudly instead of running on. That makes this a coverage gap rather than a correctness bug.
acceptance_criteria: A program executing EXEC CICS SEND FROM(x) LENGTH(n) writes x to the screen queue and continues, asserted on the rendered output.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): Bare SEND (no MAP): 22 statements in 22 programs, a 2-byte FROM payload. Lowered P2 -> P3 by reach. Duplicate of cicada-0du?

title: EXEC CICS HANDLE AID is a registered no-op, so AID-driven branching never happens
description:
HANDLE AID names a paragraph to branch to when a given AID key (PF3, PF12, CLEAR, ENTER, PA1...) ends the next RECEIVE MAP. cicada registers it via make_handle_noop_builtin, so the statement parses and lowers but the branch never occurs — the program falls through as though the key were ENTER. This is the same silent-fallthrough shape defect F fixed for HANDLE CONDITION, and the machinery now exists to fix it the same way: a table indexed by AID keyed off EIBAID, a raise tail after RECEIVE MAP, and a dispatcher branch.

Deliberately left out of the condition-handling work (forge-5by) to keep that change to one mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: A program coding HANDLE AID PF3(PARA-EXIT) branches to PARA-EXIT when RECEIVE MAP ends with PF3, asserted by what that paragraph wrote.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): HANDLE AID: 10 statements in 9 programs (PF3, ANYKEY, ENTER, PA1-3). AID dispatch is otherwise done by EVALUATE on EIBAID (3,772 references, 1,040 programs), which works today. Lowered P2 -> P3.

title: The unhandled-condition abend uses one AEIZ code instead of the per-condition AEIx mapping
description:
Real CICS abends an unhandled condition with a distinct AEIx code per condition (AEIL for NOTFND, AEIM for LENGERR, and so on). cics/conditions.py defines a single UNHANDLED_ABCODE = 'AEIZ' and __cics_abend_unhandled uses it for every condition, carrying the EIBRESP value in the log message instead. A program or operator keying off the abend code sees the wrong one.

Source the real mapping and replace the placeholder.
acceptance_criteria: An unhandled NOTFND abends AEIL and an unhandled LENGERR abends AEIM, asserted by abcode.

title: EXEC CICS PUSH HANDLE and POP HANDLE are unimplemented
description: PUSH HANDLE saves the current HANDLE CONDITION/HANDLE AID/IGNORE registrations and POP HANDLE restores them — the standard idiom around a LINK to a routine that installs its own handlers. Neither is implemented. With the handler table in WORKING-STORAGE, a stack would need a saved copy of DFH-HANDLER and DFH-RAISABLE per push.
acceptance_criteria: PUSH HANDLE followed by new registrations and POP HANDLE restores the prior registrations, asserted by which paragraph dispatches.

title: EXEC CICS LINK isolation of the condition handler table is untested
description:
The handler table lives in each program's WORKING-STORAGE, so a LINKed program having its own handler registrations is a consequence of COBOL scoping rather than something the runtime enforces. No test exercises it: the HNDLINKA/HNDLINKB fixtures in tests/integration/cics/test_condition_handling.py use a COBOL CALL, not EXEC CICS LINK, despite the names. The implementation plan's own self-review flagged this gap and it was not closed.

Add a test where a program registers a handler, LINKs to another program that registers a different handler for the same condition, and asserts the caller's registration survives the return.
acceptance_criteria: A test LINKs between two programs that both register handlers for the same condition and asserts each dispatches to its own paragraph.

title: NOTOPEN is raisable but no code path ever produces EIBRESP 19
description:
cics/conditions.py lists NOTOPEN in RAISABLE, so a program coding HANDLE CONDITION NOTOPEN registers a handler and gets DFH-RAISABLE set to 'Y'. Nothing in the runtime ever writes EIBRESP 19, so that handler can never fire. NOTOPEN is among the most-handled conditions in the corpus.

This is NOT simply the eibresp.py mapping being wrong. cics/vsam/eibresp.py maps a driver-level AccessCondition.NOT_OPEN to RESP_IOERR by a documented decision (its Decision A): in CICS a program never opens or closes files, so a driver reporting NOT_OPEN means an internal adapter inconsistency, and labelling that NOTOPEN would tell the program to handle an adapter bug. File state is an FCT/enable concern the adapter decides before calling a driver, where it returns RESP_DISABLED (84).

The real gap: no path produces the condition CICS would actually raise for a closed file. Either the FCT/enable path should raise NOTOPEN where CICS does, or NOTOPEN should be removed from RAISABLE so a handler for it fails loudly at compile rather than silently never running.
acceptance_criteria: Either a test shows EXEC CICS READ against a closed/unenabled file raising NOTOPEN and running a registered handler, or NOTOPEN is removed from RAISABLE and coding a handler for it is rejected with a clear message.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): DFHRESP(NOTOPEN) is compared 13,412 times in 1,804 programs, but only matters when a file is closed, which this runtime cannot model (no CEMT SET FILE CLOSED). The branches are defensive error paths. Lowered P2 -> P3; revisit if file open/close state is modelled.

title: cicada has two DFHRESP tables and conditions.py's docstring overclaims
description:
cicada carries two condition tables:

  cics/preprocessor.py _DFHRESP_TABLE   the live DFHRESP name-resolution table
                   imported by cics/dfhresp_prepass.py. Must resolve every name a
                   translator's DFHRESP(...) can mention, including the de-collided
                   LENOVF 522 and UNEXPIN 523.
  cics/conditions.py CONDITION_CODES    21 entries. Covers the conditions the
                   handler table is indexed by, and nothing else.

The original cost argument against merging no longer applies: preprocessor.py:80
already sizes the injected tables from _DFHRESP_TABLE (CONDITION_TABLE_SLOTS =
max(_DFHRESP_TABLE.values()) + 1 = 524), not from CONDITION_CODES, because
DISABLED (84) is a legal EIBRESP and the raise tail subscripts DFH-RAISABLE by
EIBRESP + 1. So the DFHHANDLE tables are ALREADY PIC X(524) / PIC X(1048).

What is left is the design decision about what conditions.py is FOR: either it owns
every DFHRESP name (with the handler table deriving its size from the raisable
subset), or the two stay separate with their different purposes named in both
docstrings. Either way conditions.py's docstring still overclaims — it opens 'The
single source of truth these codes are converging on', and it is the source of truth
for the handler table only, not for DFHRESP name resolution.
acceptance_criteria: Either one table serves both purposes without inflating the injected copybook, or the two are documented as separate with their scopes stated; conditions.py's docstring no longer claims to be the single source of truth for something it does not cover.
notes:
Raised by the Task 2 reviewer of the condition-handling plan and correctly declined by its implementer as not trivially resolvable — the 1.5KB-per-program consequence is the reason. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-cics-condition-handling-design.md, which records the scattered-codes finding this came from.
Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): Do together with red-dragon-forge-dbk.9 (missing DFHRESP names resolve to sentinel 9999; audit codes against the IBM reference).

title: Blocking dispatcher loop and CicsRegion disagree about which terminal a next-transid task gets
description:
The two CICS drivers implement the same routing rule twice — deliberate, so that _advance_routing stays a pure function of the DispatchResult — but they diverge on one detail.

  CicsRegion._adopt_next_transid -> _adopt(routing, self._region_termid)
  _run_dispatcher_with_runner    -> CicsContext(..., termid=initial_context.termid)

Meanwhile the loop FILTERS runnable start-requests on region_termid. So the loop
uses one value to decide which starts it may run and another to attach a
next-transid task, while the region uses region_termid for both. They are equal in
every current construction, which is why nothing fails today.

The interval-control work established that the two drivers are kept honest only by
their tests; a divergence nothing asserts is where drift begins. Either collapse the
two names in the loop, or state why they must differ.
acceptance_criteria: Both drivers derive a next-transid task's terminal from the same source, or the difference is documented where CicsRegion's contract is described, with a test pinning whichever behaviour is intended.
notes: Raised by the Task 11 review of the forge-9zb interval-control plan. The line originates in the Task 8 fix that stopped the loop dropping termid from follow-on contexts entirely, so it was an improvement on what preceded it.

title: A RETURN TRANSID self-loop is unbounded when a driver never supplies input
description:
The interval-control runaway guard (cicada/cics/dispatcher.py) bounds consecutive STARTED-task dispatches, because a started task needs no terminal input and so nothing else breaks that cycle. A transaction that ends with RETURN TRANSID naming ITSELF is a different shape: it normally waits for terminal input, which is what breaks the chain — but a driver that supplies an InputEvent on every step (or a test harness looping step()) would spin unbounded.

Not reachable from the blocking dispatcher loop, which blocks on a real input queue with a timeout and abends AZCT when nothing arrives. Reachable in principle from CicsRegion, whose caller decides when to hand over an event.

Raised by the Task 10 implementer while placing the guard's counter reset; recorded rather than fixed because no current driver exhibits it.
acceptance_criteria: Either a self-referential RETURN TRANSID chain is bounded by its own guard with a distinct abend code, or it is documented as caller-bounded by design with the reasoning stated where CicsRegion's contract is described.
notes: Related: the started-task guard deliberately resets only in _adopt_next_transid, not _adopt, so that a START-self / XCTL cycle cannot evade it. See the forge-9zb interval-control work.

title: Conversational RECEIVE MAP and SEND TEXT bypass the non-terminal INVREQ guard
description:
Terminal I/O from a non-terminal task returns INVREQ for SEND MAP and RECEIVE MAP, but two paths skip it:

  - Conversational RECEIVE MAP lowers to SUSPEND + __cics_apply_input
    (cicada/cics/strategy.py:1490-1495), so the INVREQ guard — which lives in
    __cics_receive_map (cics/builtins/screen.py:349-351) — is never reached.
    The resp writeback DOES happen (_lower_bms passes __cics_apply_input's value
    to _emit_resp_and_raise), but __cics_apply_input (screen.py:359-373) has no
    guard of its own, so it can never report INVREQ.
  - SEND TEXT has no guard and no resp writeback at all: _lower_bms returns at
    strategy.py:1470-1472 before _emit_resp_and_raise, and __cics_send_text
    (screen.py:375-381) returns value=None.

Unreachable today: a started task is dispatched only by CicsRegion's
pseudo-conversational path, so a non-terminal task never runs under
ConversationalRegion.

The asymmetry is the point: three of five terminal verbs are guarded. Someone
enabling conversational mode for started tasks later would get silent screen writes
from a task that has no screen.
acceptance_criteria: A non-terminal task's SEND TEXT sets EIBRESP to INVREQ (16) and writes nothing to the screen channel; the conversational RECEIVE MAP path does the same rather than suspending. Tests assert the decoded resp and an untouched channel.
notes: Raised by the Task 8 review of the forge-9zb interval-control plan; the implementer diagnosed and deferred both correctly, but neither was tracked. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-cics-interval-control-design.md for the non-terminal task design.

title: SEARCH ALL lowers to a linear scan, indistinguishably
description:
serializeSearch calls newStatement('SEARCH') with no flag for the ALL form, and SearchStatement (cobol_statements.py:957-963) has no field for it. So SEARCH ALL silently becomes a linear SEARCH. CobolFeature.SEARCH_BINARY exists in features.py:91 and is claimed by no test — correctly, since it is unimplemented.

Deliberately low: for an equality WHEN over a sorted table a linear scan returns the SAME ANSWER, just slower, and AT END semantics coincide. The production online corpus contains ZERO SEARCH ALL. Recorded for completeness — do NOT sequence work behind this.

The defensible minimum is to stop hiding it: carry the ALL flag through the bridge and the ASG so the downgrade is visible, then either honour it or reject it explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Either SEARCH ALL performs a binary search over the table's KEY IS clause, or it is rejected explicitly at lowering time. Silently downgrading is acceptable only while it stays documented.
notes: Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect C4. In vendor/red-dragon (bridge + lower_search), unlike the CICS beads.

title: EXEC CICS low-volume verb tail: SPOOL, ROUTE, DELAY, GETMAIN, ENQ/DEQ
description:
The remainder of the unimplemented-verb table, none individually large enough to sequence on its own. Occurrences in the production online corpus:

  SPOOLOPEN/WRITE/CLOSE  116  report spooling
  ROUTE                   25  BMS routing
  DELAY                   25
  GETMAIN                  7
  ENQ / DEQ              3/3

Since 1511575a each abends UNSP when reached (strategy.py:_lower_unsupported) rather than being a silent nop, so a flow that hits one fails loudly. Triage each when a flow actually reaches it rather than implementing the set speculatively.

Cheap stances worth considering ahead of real implementations: DELAY as a no-op is defensible in an emulator with no wall clock; ENQ/DEQ as no-ops are defensible single-threaded; GETMAIN is not (it hands back storage the program then writes through).
acceptance_criteria: Each verb either implemented or explicitly rejected by the strictness policy — none left on the silent-nop path.
notes:
Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect E verb table.
Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): Census volumes for the tail: SPOOLOPEN/WRITE/CLOSE 116 statements in 28 programs (always OUTPUT+TOKEN+NODE+USERID+CLASS); SEND PAGE 41 and ROUTE LIST NLEOM 25 (25-27 programs, printer/broadcast); DELAY INTERVAL 25 (23 programs, never with CANCEL); GETMAIN 7 (always SET ADDRESS OF + LENGTH + INITIMG, to build a ROUTE list); ENQ/DEQ 3 each with NOSUSPEND (2 programs); INQUIRE/SET TERMINAL UCTRANST 4/8; QUERY SECURITY 1; ALLOCATE/CONNECT PROCESS/FREE 1 each (one subroutine). Unchanged P3.

title: EXEC CICS RESETBR is unimplemented — completes the browse family
description:
8 occurrences in the production online corpus. STARTBR, READNEXT, READPREV and ENDBR are all implemented (strategy.py:143 _VSAM_BROWSE_VERBS); RESETBR is the one gap, so the browse family is complete except for repositioning. Smallest verb bead here and the highest ratio of value to work.

Since 1511575a it abends UNSP when reached rather than being silently dropped, so a browse does not quietly continue from the OLD position — the program fails loudly instead. That makes this a coverage gap rather than a silent-wrong-answer bug.
acceptance_criteria: RESETBR repositions an open browse to a new RIDFLD; test asserts the record returned by the next READNEXT, and NOTFND/ENDFILE behaviour on repositioning past the end.
notes:
Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect E verb table.
Census 2026-10-05 (external production CICS estate, 2,126 programs, 49,529 EXEC CICS statements; see red-dragon-forge-dbk): RESETBR: 8 statements in 5 programs, always GTEQ. Lowered P2 -> P3 by reach.

title: Wrap lark's UnexpectedInput as CsdParseError in cicada's csd_parse
description:
cobble adds a CsdParseError exception wrapping lark's UnexpectedInput in csd_parse, so a consumer can distinguish a corpus-shaped CSD failure from a bug without importing lark and without catching bare Exception. cicada's csd_parse still lets lark's own exception escape.

Small and self-contained (~10 lines plus the two try/except sites). Deliberately not imported with the rest of the cobble sweep: it changes an exception contract, and any consumer catching lark.UnexpectedInput today would need updating. Owner's call.

Last remaining structural difference between cobble and this workspace after the Aug 2026 import sweep.
close_reason: Done: cicada's csd_parse wraps lark's UnexpectedInput as CsdParseError at both sites, with tests and cobble consumers already reading it.

title: Port cobble's corpus parse diagnostics (diagnose-cobol/jcl/copybooks) into forge
description:
cobble.diagnosis (~1060 lines: cobol.py, copybooks.py, jcl.py, report.py) provides parse-only sweeps of a corpus with progress reporting and a copybook fix mode, exposed as console scripts diagnose-cobol, diagnose-jcl, diagnose-copybooks.

Complements tools/mainframe_inventory.py: that measures usage surface (what features a corpus uses), these measure parse success (what the parsers actually accept). Needs porting to forge's package layout - cobble collapses cicada/jackal/knowledge_graph into one cobble.* package, so the imports do not transfer as-is, and the root .importlinter contract constrains where it can live.
notes:
Scoping done: this is NOT a mechanical file copy. cobble.diagnosis imports four cobble-only modules forge has no equivalent for: cobble.corpus_config (load_corpus_config, 101 lines - a corpus-YAML abstraction naming directories and globs, which forge does not have as a concept at all), cobble.cli_logging (35), cobble.matching_files (26), and cobble.jackal.jcl.jcl_store (152, absent from forge's jackal). So the real cost is ~1060 lines of diagnostics plus ~314 lines of new infrastructure, and it introduces the corpus-config concept into forge.

Open question for the owner: whether corpus diagnostics belong in forge at all, given cobble exists precisely to run a corpus. Recommend deciding that before any porting.
close_reason: Obsolete: cobble was imported into the workspace wholesale, so cobble.diagnosis and its three console scripts are already available from forge; no separate port is needed.

title: Add tools/ to Black and fp-lint scope (pre-commit + CI)
description: tools/mainframe_inventory.py landed outside every lint scope: black's pre-commit hook and CI --check list packages explicitly, and python-fp-lint likewise. Nothing enforces formatting on tools/ going forward. Mirror commit 73b36116 (which did the same for knowledge_graph): add tools to the black entry in .pre-commit-config.yaml and .github/workflows/ci.yml, and tools/ to the fp-lint entry.
close_reason: tools/ added to black (pre-commit + CI) and fp-lint scope; black --check clean

title: CardDemo corpus has an IMS/Db2/MQ JCL subtree the executability analysis never covered
description: tools/mainframe_inventory.py over the whole vendor/carddemo tree finds TOOL.DFSRRC00 (IMS region controller) in 5 jobs and TOOL.IKJEFT01 (TSO batch shell, incl. nested DSN RUN PROGRAM) in 5 files, all under app/app-authorization-ims-db2-mq/jcl/. The 2026-07-09 whole-job executability analysis scoped itself to app/jcl (33 jobs) and so reports neither. Decide whether that subtree is in scope for jackal; if it is, the 33-job denominator and the 51%% capability-clean ceiling both need restating.

title: Populate GraphNode.file_path uniformly across all KG extractors
description:
Today GraphNode.file_path is sparsely and inconsistently populated: only the CALL/COPY extractor (interpreter.project.cobol_connections._add_node) sets it, and only for the top-level compiled program, whose value in the KG build is the placeholder '__main__.cbl' (the build feeds source bytes with a placeholder main path). The other three extractors (jackal.jcl_graph, jackal.cobol_file_graph, cics.flow_graph_core) construct GraphNode(id, kind) with file_path=None. Result: of 449 CardDemo nodes, only 29 carry a file_path, all the placeholder '__main__.cbl'.

Make file_path uniformly meaningful: every PROGRAM / COBOL_FILE node (and any node with a resolvable source) should carry its real on-disk source path, so the graph supports 'jump to source' navigation and file-scoped queries. This means (a) threading the real source path into cobol_connections instead of the __main__.cbl placeholder, and (b) having the JCL / FILE-CONTROL / CICS extractors tag the PROGRAM/COBOL_FILE nodes they create with the source file they parsed.

Follow-up split out of the AST-store + streaming-graph work (design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-kg-ast-store-and-streaming-graph-design.md), which deliberately PRESERVES the current placeholder behavior (buffer-merge in GraphWriter keeps the existing file_path-or semantics) rather than changing output as a side effect of a plumbing refactor.
close_reason: Superseded: GraphNode.file_path became GraphNode.location (a FileLocation carrying the resolution reason) and every extractor now populates it via CorpusIndex.resolve_file_path; the __main__.cbl placeholder and the file_path=None extractors are gone.

title: IDCAMS comprehensive grammar spec's abbreviation-exclusion rationale is factually wrong (CISZ is real in CardDemo)
description:
jackal/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-idcams-comprehensive-grammar-design.md (around line 22, Global Constraints section) states keyword abbreviations are excluded from grammar scope because "real CardDemo JCL never abbreviates." This is factually wrong: Task 12's real-corpus sweep found CISZ (IBM's documented keyword abbreviation for CONTROLINTERVALSIZE) used twice in the real corpus, in DUSRSECJ.jcl and ESDSRRDS.jcl (each defines a DEFINE CLUSTER block using CISZ(...)). Confirmed by jackal/tests/integration/test_idcams_comprehensive_carddemo_e2e.py, which explicitly asserts these two files' CISZ usage fails to parse (lark.exceptions.UnexpectedCharacters) as a pre-approved out-of-scope exclusion.

The underlying DECISION to exclude abbreviations from the grammar remains sound -- building a full abbreviation-resolution table for every parameter across every command for a real-corpus benefit of exactly 2 occurrences is genuinely low-value. Only the STATED REASON in the spec doc is wrong; it should not claim abbreviations never occur in real CardDemo JCL.

Recommended fix: rewrite the spec's rationale in the Global Constraints section to something like "abbreviation-resolution tables are high-cost for a real-corpus benefit of exactly 2 occurrences (CISZ in DUSRSECJ.jcl and ESDSRRDS.jcl)" instead of claiming abbreviations never appear. The scoping decision itself does not change -- only the justification text.

Filed per the established pattern from forge-9yz (a similar doc-accuracy gap found earlier in this same plan): filed as a tracking issue rather than immediately editing the spec doc.

title: .talismanrc append-only convention doc is wrong -- Talisman resolves duplicate filenames first-occurrence-wins, not last
description:
jackal/CLAUDE.md documents .talismanrc as "for stable files append a
by-checksum entry before the version: line -- append-only -- never
modify existing entries". Empirically verified false for the case of
a file's content changing again after an entry already exists: the
real talisman_darwin_arm64 binary resolves duplicate filename entries
first-occurrence-wins, not last. Appending a new correct checksum
after a stale one for the same filename still fails the hook -- only
removing/replacing the stale first entry works.

Discovered during Task 3 of the comprehensive IDCAMS grammar plan
(jackal/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-08-idcams-comprehensive-grammar.md)
when ams.lark/parser_comprehensive.py needed a second checksum update
after Task 2's entries went stale. Verified independently by the task
reviewer using an isolated scratch repo + the real hook binary.

Fix: update jackal/CLAUDE.md's .talismanrc guidance to say "for a file
whose content changes again, replace its existing entry rather than
appending a second one -- Talisman resolves duplicate filenames
first-occurrence-wins" instead of the current append-only-always text.

title: tests/integration/db2_env.sh references stale vendor/squall/.env path
description: Discovered during the monorepo migration (Task 6, uv workspace consolidation). tests/integration/db2_env.sh derives SQUALL_DB2_DSN from vendor/squall/.env, but Task 5 removed the old vendor/squall submodule - squall now lives at squall/ (its own .env at squall/.env). The helper silently exports nothing when the stale path doesn't exist, causing test_inqcust_e2e.py to fail with KeyError: 'SQUALL_DB2_DSN' unless the var is exported by hand. Fix: update db2_env.sh to point at squall/.env.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 1584836b - db2_env.sh now points at squall/.env

title: Root-level submodule init needed before per-package build.sh/make setup on a fresh monorepo clone
description: Discovered during the monorepo migration (Task 2, Cicada subtree merge): cicada/build.sh's 'git -C "$ROOT" submodule update --init --recursive' is now scoped only to cicada/, and no longer reaches the external root vendor/red-dragon submodule the way it did when RedDragon lived inside Cicada. A fresh monorepo clone relying solely on a package's own build.sh/make setup to bootstrap everything would fail to initialize the shared root vendor/red-dragon submodule first. Needs a documented (or automated) 'git submodule update --init --recursive' at the repo root before any per-package make setup, once all three packages (cicada/squall/jackal) are merged in.
close_reason: Obsolete - verified via a fresh disposable clone that 'git submodule update --init --recursive' run from inside any package subdirectory (e.g. cicada/) initializes ALL submodules repo-wide, including the shared root vendor/red-dragon, since git submodule commands operate on the whole repo's .gitmodules regardless of cwd, not scoped to a subtree. The original finding assumed path-scoping that doesn't exist.

title: Nest each package's tests/ directory inside its own package dir for import-linter test coverage
description: Currently squall/tests, cicada/tests, jackal/tests are siblings of their respective source package dirs, not nested inside them, so they cannot appear in one shared import-linter independence contract as squall.tests.*, cicada.tests.*, jackal.tests.* (dotted paths require true nesting, not sibling directories). Decided (2026-07-05, monorepo migration design) to ship the migration with a source-only shared contract (cics, squall, jackal) and defer test-directory coverage. This issue tracks the follow-up: physically move each package's tests/ directory one level deeper inside its own package dir (e.g. squall/tests -> squall/squall/tests), then extend the shared .importlinter contract to include the resulting *.tests modules.

title: EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD never writes back RESP/RESP2
description: CORPT00C's WRITEQ TD call includes RESP(WS-RESP-CD)/RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), which it EVALUATEs immediately after the call (third-party/carddemo/app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl:517-529). But 'WRITEQ TD' is not in cics/strategy.py's _RESP_PRODUCING_VERBS set, so emit_resp_writeback is never called for it — WS-RESP-CD stays at its VALUE ZEROS initial value, which happens to equal DFHRESP(NORMAL)=0, so CORPT00C's error-handling branch is silently unreachable today (masked by luck, not correctness). Found while designing the fix for cicada-vcq (operand-dropping bug on the same verb/call site); deliberately scoped out of that fix per user decision to keep it narrow. Fix: add 'WRITEQ TD' to _RESP_PRODUCING_VERBS (cics/strategy.py) and have make_writeq_td_builtin (cics/builtins/system.py) return a real eibresp int (RESP_NORMAL/0 today, since nothing in this emulation can fail a TD-queue append) instead of BuiltinResult(value=None), then route it through emit_resp_writeback like the VSAM verbs.
close_reason: Fixed: make_writeq_td_builtin now returns a real resp code (_RESP_NORMAL = 0, a named constant, since nothing in this emulation can fail a TD-queue append) instead of BuiltinResult(value=None), and WRITEQ TD's lowering in cics/strategy.py now calls emit_resp_writeback — the same shared helper the other 10 RESP-producing verbs already use. Also cleaned up make_inquire_builtin's pre-existing magic numbers (0/27) in the same file, using the same two new named constants (_RESP_NORMAL, _RESP_PGMIDERR). Scope: RESP/EIBRESP only, WRITEQ TD only — RESP2 support remains out of scope for all verbs, unchanged. TDD: unit test (tests/unit/cics/test_strategy_screen.py::test_writeq_td_lowers_with_resp_writeback) + a synthetic-COBOL integration test with a poisoned sentinel value (tests/integration/cics/test_region_e2e.py::test_writeq_td_writes_back_resp, since real CardDemo's WS-RESP-CD already starts at 0 and can't distinguish fixed-from-broken), both verified to fail without the fix. Confirmed CORPT00C's real observable behavior (test_carddemo_reports.py) is unchanged, as expected — nothing in this emulation can currently fail a WRITEQ TD, so this closes a correctness landmine for future failure-path modeling rather than fixing a currently-visible bug.

title: Backward references: *.STEP.PROCSTEP.DD (PROC-nested form)
description: Keep the defect, drop the stale blocker. DSN=*.STEP.PROCSTEP.DD three-segment backward references are still unsupported: jackal/jcl/bridge_parser.py raises ValueError('Three-segment backward reference ... is not yet supported'). The deferral premise no longer holds -- cataloged PROC expansion landed in jackal/jcl/proc_expand.py and JobRunner.run_job, and expansion names inner steps 'OUTERSTEP.PROCSTEP', so the PROCSTEP segment now has a referent and this can be implemented (resolve the three-segment form against the expanded qualified step name in JobRunner._resolve_step, and drop the ValueError in bridge_parser._dd_from_json).
notes: Status 2026-10-11: *.STEP.PROCSTEP.DD parses and resolves through PROC-call coordinates (acceptance fixture dsn/kinds.jcl, //PCOPY DD DSN=*.S1.P1.IN), and the runner copies the referenced DSN for any resolved referback (8u3/552). Left: a runner test of a PROC-nested referback, then close.
close_reason: *.STEP.PROCSTEP.DD parses, resolves through PROC-call coordinates, and the runner copies the referenced DSN; test_proc_referback.py proves a PROC step's passed dataset is received and cataloged by a later job step. The in-stream PROC dependency was stale: the referback works for cataloged PROCs.

title: Guard against &&NAME / DirectDSN backing-file collision in catalog
description: TempRef('&&FOO') and DirectDSN('FOO') both resolve to workdir/'FOO'. If a job allocates both, the second write truncates the first silently. Add a test and a guard (e.g. check for path collision on allocation, or prefix temp backing files with a sentinel).

title: Eliminate double-parse when PARM is set in cobol_step (merge _file_control into compile_cobol)
description: When step.parm is non-empty, cobol_step.py calls both _file_control() (ProLeap Java bridge subprocess) and compile_cobol() separately — parsing the COBOL source twice and paying two JVM startup costs. _file_control only needs the file_control list from the ProLeap parse result, which compile_cobol already produces internally. Merge the two calls into one.

title: Expose stable cobol_entry_point() helper in red-dragon to avoid func_init_params_ prefix coupling
description: cobol_step.py scans func_symbol_table for non-func_init_params_ labels to find the COBOL program entry point (mirroring run() internals). This couples jackal to red-dragon's internal naming convention. red-dragon should expose a stable API like cobol_entry_point(linked: LinkedProgram) -> EntryPoint that encapsulates this logic.

title: PARM e2e via real CBACT04C/INTCALC (deferred — needs batch AIX PATH)
description: Once batch alternate-index PATH access (jackal-1o2.22) lands, add a real INTCALC.jcl / CBACT04C e2e that asserts PARM='2022071800' (passed via PARM=, jackal-1o2.13) reaches PARM-DATE and appears in the written TRANFILE transaction record (CBACT04C 1300-B-WRITE-TX: STRING PARM-DATE ... WRITE FD-TRANFILE-REC). Currently blocked: CBACT04C needs 5 VSAM files incl. XREFFIL1=CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH (an alternate-index PATH), which batch jackal does not support yet. PARM faithfulness itself is validated now by a minimal purpose-built EXTERNAL-PARMS program (jackal-1o2.13); this is the fuller real-job witness. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-26-parm-linkage-design.md.

title: make jar does not rebuild when only Java sources change (stale-JAR footgun)
description: Rewrite for the current single root Makefile. The JCL-bridge half is FIXED: root Makefile's `_jcl_bridge` is .PHONY and always shells to `mvn -DskipTests package` (mvn is incremental), so editing a .java/.g4 in jackal/jcl-bridge can no longer leave a stale JAR. The remaining defect is the ProLeap bridge: `$(PROLEAP_BRIDGE_JAR): ; cd vendor/red-dragon/proleap-bridge && ./build.sh` still gates purely on the JAR file existing with no source prerequisites, so editing ProLeap bridge Java silently tests against a stale JAR unless `make jar-force` is run. There are no longer per-package Makefiles in cicada/squall/jackal (commit 7aec5579), so the fix is the one root target.

title: COBOL stub for ZUIDOO1 service program to enable UID002 integration test
description: ZUIDOO1 (the program LINKed to by UID002.cbl) is written in assembler and cannot be compiled by cicada. Need a COBOL stub that accepts the same COMMAREA structure (FILLER 'LINK', CA-STATUS-CODE, CA-FORMAT, CA-UID PIC X(36)), writes a deterministic fake UID into CA-UID, sets CA-STATUS-CODE='200', and does EXEC CICS RETURN. This stub plus UID002.cbl would form a realistic end-to-end LINK integration test.

title: EXEC CICS SEND (raw terminal write, no BMS map)
description: UID002.cbl ends with EXEC CICS SEND FROM(TERM-RESPONSE) LENGTH(...) ERASE NOHANDLE. This is a raw terminal write distinct from SEND MAP. Not currently in strategy.py. Needed to compile UID002 end-to-end.

title: EXEC CICS LINK: NOHANDLE option is silently ignored
description: UID002.cbl uses NOHANDLE on EXEC CICS LINK. NOHANDLE suppresses CICS condition handling for that specific command. Currently it is a no-op which is probably harmless, but should be tracked.
close_reason: NOHANDLE is honoured: emit_raise_tail suppresses the condition-raise tail for any command coding NOHANDLE (or RESP).

title: Abend model: program abends (Sxxx/Uxxx) distinct from return codes
description: Failures are RC-shaped today; real programs ABEND (S0C7 data exception, U-user abends) which is distinct from a clean nonzero RC and flushes the rest of the job unless COND=EVEN/ONLY. Needed for realistic failure semantics + EVEN/ONLY (jackal-1o2.8) + dump DDs. Model an abend outcome on StepResult (alongside the StepDisposition enum from 1o2.1) and have run_job stop subsequent steps on abend.
notes:
Status 2026-10-11: system abends are done: Abended(SystemAbend), Flushed(AfterAbend), the gate rule (EVEN/ONLY go on to their own tests), abnormal DISP and JobAbended; produced for a missing program (S806, xkk) and an exhausted step budget (S322, w0e). Left: (1) user abends from COBOL, CALL CEE3ABD / ILBOABN0 giving Abended(UserAbend(n)), blocked on blueprint D4 (LE stubs, see red-dragon-forge-355); (2) program faults such as S0C7, which red-dragon raises as Python exceptions (D1's open half). No longer blocks jackal-1o2.8.
2026-10-12: D4 settled by user direction: CEE3ABD is a jackal COBOL stub that leaves its abend code in its own WORKING-STORAGE and STOP RUNs; jackal reads it from the finished VM -> Abended(UserAbend(code)). Record: 2026-10-12-jackal-user-abend.md. Still open: D1 (faults such as S0C7 still surface as Python exceptions).
close_reason: D4 done: CEE3ABD abends the step with its user code (record 2026-10-12-jackal-user-abend.md). D1's fault half is won't fix for now: invalid packed data is decoded unchecked in the lowered IR (record 2026-10-12-jackal-invalid-packed-decimal.md); the future check is red-dragon-forge-13p (deferred).

title: IEBCOPY utility — copy/compress PDS members
description: Common library utility: copy members between PDSes, compress, selective COPY/EXCLUDE via SYSIN. Depends on PDS member support (jackal-1o2.16). New jackal/iebcopy/ grammar+executor in the IDCAMS shape; register in UTILITIES.

title: JCL-level IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF + COND=EVEN/ONLY (abend-conditional execution)
description: Split from jackal-1o2.1. The modern JCL conditional construct (// IF (cond) THEN ... // ELSE ... // ENDIF) and the abend-conditional COND=EVEN/ONLY forms. NOT used by CardDemo (its IF/THEN are all IDCAMS SYSIN, already handled; no EVEN/ONLY present), so deferred. IF/THEN/ENDIF reintroduces nesting into the flat Job.steps model + runner (needs a job-item tree or block construct) and abend modeling (jackal has no abend concept yet — failures are currently RC-shaped). Design when a real job needs it.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): Structured IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF in only ~7 jobs (~1%); COND= dominates. Support it, don't over-invest. Needs the serializer to keep the IF structure first (red-dragon-forge-2cy.7). Unchanged P3.
close_reason: IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF guards are evaluated (jackal.if_guard) per z/OS 3.1 JCL Reference ch. 18; COND=EVEN/ONLY was already done. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-if-then-else.md.

title: REPRO assumes PS LRECL == KSDS record_size
description: jackal/idcams/executor.py REPRO uses the OUTFILE KSDS record_size for BOTH the SequentialDriver (INFILE/PS) and IndexedDriver (OUTFILE/KSDS). Correct when PS LRECL == KSDS RECORDSIZE (the v2 case, 300), but a PS with a different LRECL would be mis-blocked. Source the input record length from the PS dataset/its DD, not the output KSDS.
close_reason: REPRO opens each side at its own label (8in 2b); see docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-idcams-repro-labels.md R1

title: Capture and surface SYSOUT output
description: SYSOUT=* DDs are parsed but their output is discarded. Programs/utilities write messages, reports, and control-statement echoes to SYSOUT; for real-job fidelity and debugging, capture per-step SYSOUT and surface it (in JobResult/StepResult, optionally to files in the workdir). IDCAMS especially echoes its control statements + condition codes to SYSPRINT.
design: Route SYSOUT/SYSPRINT writes to an in-memory buffer per step, expose on StepResult (e.g. sysout: tuple[str,...]); optionally persist to workdir. Utilities (IDCAMS/SORT) should emit their standard message lines + final condition code. Keep StepResult frozen.

title: DD concatenation (multiple datasets under one DDname)
description: Concatenated DDs (a //DD with DSN, followed by // DD cards with no ddname) present multiple datasets to a program as one logical sequential stream — common for STEPLIB/JOBLIB and multi-file input. Add: grammar for the unnamed-continuation DD form; model a DD as carrying an ordered list of datasets; sequential reads span the concatenation in order.
design: Grammar: a dd_card with an empty NAME position concatenates onto the preceding DD. Model: DD.datasets: tuple[...] (or a Concatenation wrapper) — preserve frozen/FP. red-dragon SequentialDriver reads must chain across members (or jackal concatenates at provide time). Interacts with STEPLIB once PROC/load-lib semantics land.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): Concatenation is common in the census (multi-source merges). The grammar already has ddStatementConcatenation; the serializer drops continuations (red-dragon-forge-2cy.3), so the 'add grammar' step in this issue is not needed. Execution only, after 2cy.3; jackal rejects concatenated DDs explicitly until then. Lowered P2 -> P3.
close_reason: Concatenated DDs allocate/dispose per member and read member after member in COBOL; output opens fail status 37. Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-concatenation.md. REPRO follow-up: red-dragon-forge-2dz.

title: RECEIVE MAP does not right-justify/zero-fill NUM (numeric) BMS fields
description: A 3270 NUM field transmits its data right-justified and zero-filled. cicada's __cics_receive_map writes every InputEvent field value LEFT-justified, space-padded (_write_ws_field ljust). So a short value in a NUM field is mis-placed: e.g. AMOUNT(10) entered as '100' lands as '100' + padding and a MOVE to PIC 9(10) reads 1_000_000_000 instead of 100. Surfaced in zBANK deposit (cicada-lkx). Workaround in tests: send the right-justified wire form ('0000000100'). Proper fix: the RECEIVE builtin should right-justify+zero-fill fields whose BMS attribute is NUM. Needs the NUM-ness of each field, which the symbolic copybook may not currently carry — may require threading BMS field attributes (ATTRB NUM) into the receive path.
close_reason: Resolved faithfully. Root cause clarified: z/OS BMS right-justifies/zero-fills an input field only for a numeric PICIN (PIC 9(n)); a default X(n) field — including ATTRB=NUM without PICIN — maps left-justified and the program de-edits (NUMVAL). So cicada's existing left-justify was ALREADY faithful; the only gap was the PICIN path. Implemented: RECEIVE de-edits numeric-category (ZONED_DECIMAL) input fields (right-justify+zero-fill), keyed off data_layout.category, which bms_copybook_gen already populates from PICIN. No sidecar/no ATTRB special-casing. zBANK left unmodified (no PICIN -> X(10) -> test sends full-width wire form). CardDemo unaffected. New unit test test_receive_map_numeric_field_is_de_edited; 313 tests pass.

title: CardDemo batch tier (CB* posting/statement/utility programs)
description: Exercise the CardDemo BATCH programs (CBACT01-04C account/card/xref/interest, CBTRN01-03C transaction posting, CBCUS01C customer, CBEXPORT/CBIMPORT). These are NOT CICS online transactions — they run as batch jobs straight through the VM (no dispatcher / BMS / pseudo-conversational state), so they need a different harness than the CO* e2e tests (read input files, run main, assert output files / posted records). Separate category from the online tier; scope per-program beads under this epic when picked up.

title: Numeric edit-picture formatter mis-formats unsupported symbols ($ * CR DB floating sign)
description:
edit_picture.format_edited implements only the AWS CardDemo subset: fixed leading/trailing sign (+/-), Z zero-suppression, comma and decimal insertion. Pictures containing other edit symbols are SIZED correctly but FORMATTED wrong.

Mechanism:
- is_numeric_edited() returns True for these pictures because they contain '.' and/or ',' (e.g. $$$,$$9.99, ****9.99, ZZ9.99CR), so parse_pic produces a NUMERIC_EDITED descriptor with the correct character width (countEditedWidth / parse_edit_picture.width count every position).
- But format_edited()'s walk has no case for floating/fixed currency ($), check-protection (*), or CR/DB. They hit the 'else: out.append(sym)' fallback and are emitted VERBATIM. Worse, $ and * are not counted as digit positions (only 9/Z are), so the numeric value is also mis-placed.

Example: PIC $$$,$$9.99 with value 1.23 -> '$$$,$$1.23' instead of the correct floating '    $1.23'.

Scope/impact: LATENT. Grep of AWS CardDemo (cpy/cbl/cpy-bms) shows NO numeric-edited PIC uses $, *, CR, or DB — they appear only in VALUE literals (VALUE '$', VALUE ALL '*') and X(n) fields. So no current CardDemo flow is affected; this is a correctness gap for general COBOL only.

Fix: extend format_edited to handle floating sign/currency ($$$, ++++, ----), * check-protection, and CR/DB trailing sign; count $/*/floating-sign positions as digit positions in parse_edit_picture. See edit_picture.py 'NOT supported' docstring list.

Related: [[cicada-sn9]] (implemented the supported subset).
close_reason: Mis-filed in cicada DB; refiling in red-dragon beads DB (RedDragon-level bug)

title: Eliminate remaining CICS pre-pass regexes (DFHEIBLK injection, EXEC inline-comment strip)
description: Two more regexes in the CICS text path, to drive toward zero-regex: (1) interpreter/cics/preprocessor.py _WS_SECTION_RE locates WORKING-STORAGE SECTION via regex to inject COPY DFHEIBLK -- replace with a non-regex structural locate (or inject the EIB structurally). (2) interpreter/cics/cics_parser.py _END_EXEC_RE + _strip_inline_comments strip '*>' inline comments from EXEC text before the Lark grammar -- handle inline comments IN the Lark grammar (%ignore) instead of regex pre-stripping. Note: the Lark grammar's own terminal regexes (STRING/CHARS/NAME/EXEC_CICS) are legitimate lexer definitions and are NOT in scope. Companion to red-dragon-kieo (DFHRESP) -- together they retire all CICS pre-pass regexes.
close_reason: Closed: _END_EXEC_RE and _strip_inline_comments eliminated; inline comments now handled structurally via Lark %ignore in cics_parser.py. _WS_SECTION_RE / inject_dfheiblk broken out to red-dragon-z6ad.1.

title: CSD parsing uses a regex; replace with a small Lark grammar
description: interpreter/cics/dispatcher.py parse_csd uses _CSD_PATTERN = regex DEFINE\s+TRANSACTION\((\w+)\)\s+PROGRAM\((\w+)\) to extract transid->program from a CICS CSD file. Replace the regex with a small Lark grammar for the CSD DEFINE subset we consume (DEFINE TRANSACTION(x) PROGRAM(y), and any other DEFINE forms we rely on), so CSD parsing is structural and extensible rather than a single regex that silently ignores anything it doesn't match.
close_reason: Closed

title: catnip plan: deferred minor findings (triage)
description:
Minor findings from the catnip plan's task and final reviews (2026-10-14) that were deferred, not fixed. Each is small; triage individually.

AlternateIndexDriver (red-dragon):
- write/rewrite leave _cursor/_last unadjusted; keyless delete uses _last (as IndexedDriver).
- `_entry(old.data or b"")` defensive fallback in rewrite; _swap re-sorts the whole view per update.
- view snapshot at open: writes from another opener unseen until reopen; a browse after a point delete can yield OK with no data.
- start() maps <, <= to >= (as IndexedDriver).
- COBOL DELETE through a path returns 02 (IBM defines 02 for READ/WRITE/REWRITE); a WRITE creating an allowed duplicate alt key returns 00 (COBOL says 02).
- per-function docstring on open_alternate_index_driver; test helpers unannotated; tests lack @covers; unique-key test doesn't assert base/view unchanged after rejection.
- real_file_provider: _accept annotated with a private type; _open_mode keeps str(filename).

catnip:
- DSN namespaces (entries/aixs/paths) can collide; define_aix/define_path don't reject a used DSN; define_aix doesn't check the key fits base lrecl.
- a hand-edited catalog with a dangling AIX/path raises KeyError, not CatalogError.
- untested: remove of a path/AIX by name, _stored_wire/_ksds raises, AlternateIndex validation, second install into a new dir being identical.
- side-effecting tuple comprehensions in _drop_cluster/_drop_aix.
- size check applies lrecl to V/VB sequentials (a valid VB seed is rejected) — needs a ruling before any VB seed.
- duplicate message says `dsn:` even when the repeat is an AIX `path`; semantic errors lack the `[[section]]` prefix shape errors carry.
- a failed install leaves an empty datasets/ dir; a typo'd system dir is created empty and the region reports "not cataloged" with no install hint.
- DecodedRecord.__getitem__ rebuilds a dict per lookup (cicada).

cicada / tests / docs:
- engine._sized (record-length N10 warning) untested; engine._shape's fallback branch unreachable.
- cobol_harness VsamFixture aliases its mutable files dict into VsamEngine; seed has an isinstance assert.
- carddemo_system fixtures pin data to the vendored corpus while sources/CSD follow CARDDEMO_HOME; declaration-loading test code repeated in three places; the integration XREF-sort assertion can't fail.
- cicada CLI docstring's install instructions miss the FORGE_ROOT export.
- cicada pyproject requires-python ≥3.10 while depending on catnip (≥3.13); guidelines/project-context.md and guidelines/project/workflow.md omit catnip and understate the widened hook triggers (user-owned files).
- docs/presentation/capture/cics_flow.py: never executed after migration; 9 pyright errors (outside the include list).
- IDCAMS VERIFY of a path returns RC 12 (unresearched).

title: Invalid packed-decimal data should fault (S0C7) via a validity check in the lowered IR
description:
Possible future work; won't fix for now (user decision, 2026-10-12). Record: docs/records/design/2026-10-12-jackal-invalid-packed-decimal.md.

Invalid packed-decimal (COMP-3) data is decoded as a number, not faulted. Arithmetic on a field holding 'ABC' (C1 C2 C3) gives 22232 under jackal and completes RC 0. On z/OS it abends S0C7.

Where the fix goes: the COBOL lowering emits a validity test in the IR before each packed-decimal decode. The test checks that every digit nibble is 0-9 and the sign nibble is a valid sign. When it fails, the run ends with a fault outcome, and jackal maps that to Abended(SystemAbend(0x0C7)). The VM needs no knowledge of packed decimal.

GnuCOBOL 3.2 does the same only when EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE is compiled in (-debug, -fec=ALL or -fec=DATA-INCOMPATIBLE). By default it reads the nibbles unchecked. Whether ours is always on or opt-in is decided when this is built.

title: Decide whether a PROC call's COND= reaches the steps of PROCs nested inside it
description: expand_procs applies a call's unqualified COND= (cond_for_every_step) to the program steps of the PROC it calls, not to steps of PROCs that PROC calls in turn. The JCL Reference says it overrides COND on every EXEC statement in the procedure; whether that reaches into a nested procedure is not stated. Decide, then pin with a test. Raised by the units 2-4 review (2026-10-10).
close_reason: Decided: an unqualified COND reaches every level of nesting, derived from JCL Reference p.326 (a calling EXEC's COND replaces the COND on every EXEC statement in the procedure; a nested call is one). Pinned by test_a_calls_cond_reaches_every_level_of_nesting.

title: IDCAMS IF LASTCC: a false test sets MAXCC to LASTCC
description: jackal/idcams/executor.py _if_maxcc: when IF LASTCC <op> n is false, MAXCC becomes LASTCC, which can lower MAXCC. Kept as-is through the object-model refactor; check against the IDCAMS reference and fix with a test. Found by the units 2-4 review (2026-10-10).

title: IDCAMS REPRO command names its DDs as str
description: jackal.idcams.commands.Repro holds infile_dd/outfile_dd as str, so the executor wraps them in DdName on arrival. The IDCAMS parser that builds Repro (jackal/idcams/parser.py, a Lark transformer) should produce DdName itself. Not done in object-model units 3-4 because that module carries 11 lint violations of its own that touching it would adopt.

title: cobble srccfg: CICS RETURN / ABEND / XCTL do not end the path
description: Already documented (cobble README, srccfg/link.py): control flows to the next statement after EXEC CICS RETURN, ABEND and XCTL, though none returns. Sound but imprecise; filed so the follow-up the docs mention is tracked.
close_reason: XCTL/RETURN keep only their failure paths; ABEND ends the path

title: cobble srccfg: SEARCH is lowered as one test, not a loop over the table
description: SEARCH ... WHEN ... AT END lowers to the WHEN test with AT END on its FALSE arm; the index advancing through the table is not modelled, and neither is the write to the index. An approximation: the arms are right, the iteration and the index's definers are not.
close_reason: Won't do: SEARCH does not need to be modelled as a loop (user decision, 2026-10-02).

title: cobble srccfg: EVALUATE ... ALSO ANY lowers ANY as a test that can fail
description: WHEN 'C' THRU 'F' ALSO ANY lowers the ANY subject to a TEST node with a FALSE edge to the next WHEN, a path that cannot occur. Sound but imprecise: ANY should be no test at all.
close_reason: Fixed in 9c4f390: ANY parts dropped from ALSO conjunctions when a real comparison remains.

title: XCTL's COMMAREA is modelled as a callee write-back, though the only path past an XCTL is one where the callee never ran
description:
cobble/dataflow/srccfg/desugar.py's terminator map holds only STOP RUN / GOBACK / EXIT PROGRAM, so an EXEC CICS XCTL/RETURN falls through to the next statement in the CFG. cobble/dataflow/fields/transfer.py then models an XCTL's COMMAREA exactly as it models LINK's -- a callee write-back onto the caller's bytes -- although cobble/dataflow/srccfg/link.py documents that XCTL never returns control to the site that issued it.

Consequence, measured on the CardDemo corpus artifact: 23 of 29 dynamic call sites carry the from-callee reason (and, since the commarea read reaches no local write, inbound-linkage with it), so build_graph's three-way rule emits *_CANDIDATE edges -- 45 XCTL_CANDIDATE against 5 proven XCTL -- for sites whose candidate set is a single correct program. Only 3 of the 17 singletons have empty reasons.

Fix: make a verb that does not return a CFG terminator, and stop deriving a write-back from it. Both halves have to move together: dropping the write-back alone leaves the fall-through edge carrying the callee's state.

Expect the reference graph to move -- candidate edges promote to proven -- so regenerate cobble/reference/ with the row-by-row review that unit 1's reference regeneration used.

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text:
MEASURED, premise falsified -- do not implement as specified.

Probe: removed the XCTL COMMAREA write-back in transfer.py (_cics_targets returns () for XCTL), re-ran the fixpoint over COMEN01C/COUSR00C/COADM01C/COACTVWC, reverted.

Result: from-callee clears, but inbound-linkage REMAINS on every CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM site, so no site becomes complete and no *_CANDIDATE edge is promoted to proven. The stated benefit does not materialise. inbound-linkage is correct -- a path reaches each site with the commarea field never written locally -- and only Unit 2 (red-dragon-forge-sjp) can clear it.

Worse, precision DROPS: COACTVWC 1 -> 2 candidates, COUSR00C 2 -> 4. The FROM_CALLEE write was an EXACT write that KILLED stale values at the commarea; removing it lets older literals survive the join.

Why the issue read as valuable when filed: at that point from-callee was the only reason on those sites. INBOUND_LINKAGE was wired up later the same session (state.py:_missing, commit range 8cae274..7e75874 era), which made it the binding constraint.

The write-back is still a false claim -- a failed XCTL means the callee never ran, a successful one never returns -- so it is worth fixing eventually, but only paired with something that preserves the kill, and with no expectation of promoting edges. Deprioritised to P4.

Separately: the CFG-terminator half should NOT be done. All 31 XCTL fall-throughs lead to the verb's own #raise condition arm (PGMIDERR), which is real control flow; severing it would also cut each paragraph's #end and the RETURN edge, which is the mechanism that lets a dead paragraph be found at all (see _terminator's docstring).

comments.author: Avishek Sen Gupta
comments.text: CORRECTION to the 2026-10-01 verdict on the CFG-terminator half. The edge INTO an XCTL's #raise test is real, but its FALSE arm (nothing raised = the XCTL succeeded) went on to the next statement, and a successful XCTL never comes back. Fixed under red-dragon-forge-qut: without RESP/NOHANDLE, XCTL and RETURN keep only the raised arm to the handler; with RESP/NOHANDLE their single FLOW edge is the failure path and stays; ABEND ends the path. A paragraph ending in one has an unreachable #end, and a PERFORM of it keeps its FLOW past it through the never-returns safety net. The CardDemo cobble-build output is byte-identical. This issue now covers only the write-back half: the XCTL COMMAREA write-back rides the failure path, where the callee never ran.

title: IDCAMS comprehensive grammar: over-length symbolic VOLUMES(&sym) silently splits into two tokens instead of erroring
description:
jackal/jackal/idcams/grammar/ams.lark's INDIRECT_VOLUME_SYMBOLIC terminal
(/&[A-Z0-9#@$]{1,5}/, from Task 4 of the comprehensive IDCAMS grammar
plan) combined with nonvsam_volume_item+'s adjacency allows a malformed
over-length symbolic volume reference like &TOOLONG1 (no space) to
silently parse as two separate volumes ('&TOOLO', 'NG1') instead of
being rejected as invalid.

Not spec-mandated behavior (real IBM symbolic volumes are &SYSR2-style,
<=5 chars after the &), and no real CardDemo corpus usage exercises
this at all -- low priority, garbage-in/garbage-out for malformed
input, not a functional defect against any documented real syntax.

Flagged by Task 4's reviewer as a minor follow-up, not blocking.

title: SET statement support in JCL PROC expansion
description:
The JCL PROC-expansion feature (jackal/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-jcl-proc-expansion-design.md,
implementation plan jackal/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-08-jcl-proc-expansion.md)
implements PROC-statement symbol defaults and caller EXEC PROC=...,SYM=value
overrides, but deliberately does NOT implement SET statements inside a PROC
body (// SET SYM=value, which updates a symbol for subsequent steps only,
requiring the model to preserve step/SET interleaving order rather than a
flat step list + one symbol table per invocation).

Verified during planning: neither REPROC.prc nor TRANREPT.prc (the only two
real PROCs in the CardDemo corpus) use SET statements. The grammar already
supports them (JCLParser.g4: setStatement/setOperation, SET_PARM_NAME
token) but JclSerializer.java does not serialize them, and the deferred
scope means jackal's Job/Step model has no ordered step+SET sequence type.
design: Would need: (1) JclSerializer.java to serialize setStatement/setOperation nodes with their source-order position relative to jclStep siblings within procJCL; (2) a richer Job/ProcDef body representation than a flat steps tuple, e.g. a sequence of tagged Step|SetOp entries; (3) proc_expand.py's expand_procs to walk that sequence maintaining a running, mutated symbol table instead of building one static table per invocation.
acceptance_criteria: A PROC body containing // SET SYM=value between two steps correctly applies the new binding only to steps after the SET, verified against a synthetic .prc fixture (no real corpus PROC uses this, so no CardDemo e2e coverage is required).
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): 0 SET statements in the census. Lowered P3 -> P4.
close_reason: Stale: the bridge serializes SET inside a PROC, ProcDef keeps statements in source order, and expansion ranks a PROC's SET below its EXEC and PROC values and above the outer value (JCL Ref p. 48, Table 13). Proven by test_real_jar_applies_a_set_inside_a_proc_below_its_exec_and_proc_values.

title: JCL symbolic substring notation (&SYM(1:5)) not resolved by PROC symbol substitution
description:
The jcl-bridge grammar's KEYWORD_VALUE rule has a dedicated alternative for
JCL symbolic substring notation, e.g. &SYM(1:5) — substringing positions 1-5
of a symbolic parameter's bound value. See JCLLexer.g4:4981:
  (AMPERSAND AMPERSAND? ALNUMNAT LPAREN_DFLT NUM_LIT_DFLT? ':' NUM_LIT_DFLT? RPAREN_DFLT)+
This construct tokenizes as KEYWORD_VALUE, not SYMBOLIC — the same token
type as ordinary literal text — so the structured Literal/Symbol value-part
classification used by the JCL PROC-expansion feature (see
jackal/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-jcl-proc-expansion-design.md) will
treat it as an opaque literal, not a symbol reference needing substitution.

CardDemo's actual PROC corpus (REPROC.prc, TRANREPT.prc) does not use
substring symbolic notation — only plain &SYMBOL references. This gap was
identified but explicitly deferred while verifying the Literal/Symbol
classification rule during PROC-expansion planning; it is real and
verified, not speculative, but out of scope for that feature.
design: Would require the Java serializer's structured-value-part builder to recognize this KEYWORD_VALUE alternative specifically and decompose it into a Symbol part plus substring-offset metadata, rather than treating the whole token as one opaque Literal.
acceptance_criteria: A DSN or PARM value containing &SYM(1:5)-style substring notation is decomposed into structured parts that preserve the symbol reference and substring bounds, so PROC symbol substitution can resolve it correctly.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): 0 symbolic substitution of any kind in the census. Lowered P3 -> P4.

title: jcl-bridge: condFromWords silently catches NumberFormatException -> code=0
description: Code-quality follow-up from the COND= (jackal-1o2.1) final review. JclSerializer.condFromWords wraps Integer.parseInt of the COND code slot in try{}catch(NumberFormatException){/* 0 */}, silently defaulting a non-numeric code to 0. Unreachable for valid JCL (the mapa number token guarantees numeric), and the Python op-validation still fails loud for EVEN/ONLY — so it cannot mask a bypass decision — but it violates the letter of the no-silent-guard constraint. Fix: remove the catch (let it parse) or assert it cannot happen. Trivial.
close_reason: Fixed (merged to main, 7d640ed): condFromWords parses the COND code slot directly; removed the swallowed NumberFormatException->0. Fails loud on a malformed code; EVEN/ONLY unaffected (handled separately). 4 COND bridge tests + full suite green against the rebuilt JAR.

title: OUTPUT JCL statement — JES spool output descriptors
description: JCL-language construct: the //name OUTPUT statement defines a spool/print output descriptor (CLASS, DEST, FORMS, etc.) that SYSOUT DDs reference via OUTPUT=. 3 CardDemo jobs use it. Almost entirely operational (print routing) with no batch-execution effect in an emulator. Execution: parse-and-ignore (record the descriptor, don't act on it) is sufficient; surface it only if/when SYSOUT capture (1o2.7) wants the CLASS/DEST. Low priority; mainly here so it is parsed-and-modeled, not a gap that breaks a job.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): OUTPUT FORMS=/GROUPID= with OUTPUT=(*.ddname.x) references on >=32% of jobs. They parse today and are ignored, which is correct for analysis. Execution value only once SYSOUT capture (1o2.7) exists. Unchanged P4.

title: TYPRUN= (SCAN / HOLD) — parse-only and hold execution modes
description: JCL-language execution semantics. TYPRUN=SCAN means 'syntax-check the JCL only, do not execute any step' (a dry-run mode); TYPRUN=HOLD means 'queue but do not run until released'. 0 CardDemo jobs use it, but it is a real JCL-language execution mode. Execution: SCAN -> parse + validate, return a JobResult with all steps disposition=NOT-RUN and RC 0, run nothing; HOLD -> in a non-interactive runner, treat as a no-op/immediate-release (or a clear 'held' status). Parsing from 1o2.9. JOB-card param.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): TYPRUN=HOLD on 54 jobs (~6%); parses today and is ignored. Unchanged P4.

title: RESTART= — resume a job at a named step/procstep
description: JCL-language execution semantics. RESTART=stepname (or stepname.procstep) on the JOB card makes execution begin at that step rather than the first, skipping all prior steps (used for rerunning a failed job from the point of failure). 1 CardDemo job uses it. Execution: the runner skips steps until the named one, then runs normally; skipped steps -> StepResult(disposition=BYPASSED/SKIPPED, like COND). Parsing comes from the adopted ANTLR grammar (1o2.9). Pure JCL-language feature (no OS/utility dependency).
design: Pairs with the StepDisposition enum from 1o2.1. Interacts with referbacks (1o2.10) — a RESTART that skips the step a later DSN=*.step.dd refers back to must error clearly. Job-card param.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): 0 job-level RESTART= in the census (the only hit was a DFSORT SEQNUM RESTART option). Lowered P3 -> P4.

title: Deeper DFSORT (INREC/OUTREC/JOINKEYS) + ICETOOL
description: Beyond the SORT subset in jackal-1o2.3 (FIELDS/INCLUDE/OMIT/SUM): record reformatting (INREC/OUTREC), multi-file joins (JOINKEYS), and the ICETOOL report/stats toolkit. Large surface — scope incrementally as real jobs demand. Extends jackal-1o2.3.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): Match-merge via multiple SORTJNFn DDs is a repeated idiom; ICETOOL INREC IFTHEN=(WHEN=INIT,OVERLAY=(..SEQNUM..RESTART=..)) appears in only 2 jobs but is the most complex construct there; give it one dedicated test. OUTREC FIELDS moves to 1o2.3. Unchanged P4.

title: JCL system symbols (&SYSUID, &SYSDATE, &SYSTIME, JES symbols)
description: System-defined symbolic substitutions (distinct from PROC symbolics) used in DSNs/dates/generated names. Resolve during/after parse; shares the substitution machinery with PROC symbolics (jackal-1o2.2).

title: VSAM alternate indexes (DEFINE AIX + BLDINDEX, PATH access)
description: Secondary-key access over a base KSDS: IDCAMS DEFINE AIX + BLDINDEX builds the index; programs open the PATH. Extends IDCAMS depth (jackal-1o2.6) + the VSAM model.

title: VSAM ESDS / RRDS access methods
description: Entry-sequenced (ESDS) and relative-record (RRDS) VSAM datasets, beyond the KSDS already supported. Catalog DatasetOrg + red-dragon driver wiring; IDCAMS DEFINE for the new org types. Narrower than KSDS but blocks specific real jobs.

title: Diagnostic DDs: SYSUDUMP / CEEDUMP / SYSABEND capture
description: Abend dump DDs programs declare for diagnostics. Start as capture-and-route-to-sysout (or workdir file); meaningful content depends on the abend model. Pairs with SYSOUT capture (1o2.7) and the abend model.

title: Load-library resolution: find programs via STEPLIB/JOBLIB PDS members
description: Today jackal resolves a program by name from source_dir (<pgm>.cbl). Real jobs locate the load module as a member of a STEPLIB/JOBLIB library (often concatenated). Once PDS members exist (depends on jackal-1o2.16), resolve EXEC PGM=X by searching the STEPLIB/JOBLIB member chain before falling back to source_dir. Removes the OPTIONAL_DDS STEPLIB-skip workaround in cobol_step.py.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): Same as 1o2.16: JOBLIB is near-universal but name-based program lookup suffices. Lowered P3 -> P4.

title: PDS/PDSE partitioned datasets + member access (DSN=LIB(MEMBER))
description: BIGGEST structural gap surfaced by the roadmap map. A jackal dataset is a single file with no member concept; real jobs reference DSN=SOME.LIB(MEMBER) pervasively. Add a partitioned-dataset model (a directory of members) + member resolution in the catalog/DD layer. Underpins: STEPLIB/JOBLIB load-library member resolution (programs loaded from a lib, not just source_dir), library-based PROC/INCLUDE/copybook/SORT-control lookup, and IEBCOPY. Prerequisite for shop-standard (Class D) jobs. Likely a small sub-epic.
design: Model: a PDS Dataset whose backing path is a directory; members are files inside; DSN(MEMBER) resolves to <dir>/<MEMBER>. DD without member = whole PDS (concatenation/IEBCOPY); with member = that file. Threads into allocate/resolve and the COBOL/utility provider. Interacts with DD concatenation (1o2.5) for STEPLIB chains and PROC libs (1o2.2/1o2.15).
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): JOBLIB is on almost every census job, but analysis and execution resolve programs by name from the source dir. Member-level PDS access is not on the 80/20 path. Lowered P2 -> P4.

title: INCLUDE / JCLLIB expansion (execution)
description: 3 CardDemo jobs use INCLUDE/JCLLIB (splice a shared JCL fragment from a library). Execution: resolve the INCLUDE member from a configured library dir and splice its statements before sequencing. mapa's grammar parses INCLUDE; its JCLPP preprocessor may do expansion (see 1o2.9 raw-vs-preprocess fork). Parsing from 1o2.9.
notes: Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): JCLLIB ORDER= on 2 jobs, INCLUDE not observed. Lowered P3 -> P4.

title: e2e step-name list assertion is brittle
description: tests/integration/test_carddemo_acctfile_e2e.py asserts the exact step-name list ['STEP05','STEP10','STEP15']. Non-vacuous but tied to the shipped JCL; would give a confusing failure if the JCL is restructured. Consider asserting per-step RC keyed by name, or relaxing to count+presence.

title: PROC support + symbolic parameters (&VAR, cataloged + instream PROCs)
description: Narrow to what is left. Cataloged PROC resolution from a proclib search path, symbolic parameter substitution (PROC defaults + EXEC-level override), qualified //STEP.DD overrides/additions, and recursive PROC nesting all LANDED in jackal/jcl/proc_expand.py, wired into JobRunner.run_job, and proven against real CardDemo TRANREPT.jcl/REPROC.prc. Remaining gaps: (a) instream PROC (//name PROC ... // PEND inside a job) -- the bridge's JclSerializer only builds a ProcDef from a bare procJCL document (.prc file), and the execJCL step walk ignores instream PROC bodies; (b) SET statements inside a PROC (forge-6qr), deliberately unsupported and verified absent from the CardDemo corpus. Note the parent epic's claim that 0 CardDemo jobs use cataloged PROCs is wrong -- TRANREPT.jcl does.
design: Symbolic substitution must NOT be a regex pass over text (violates the no-regex constraint) — model symbolics as grammar tokens and resolve during/after parse into the Step/DD model. PROC expansion = splice resolved PROC steps into the job step list with symbolic bindings applied. Needs a proclib dir CLI flag (mirror --source-dir/--copybook-dir). This is the largest single task; may warrant its own sub-epic.
notes:
SCOPE (2026-06-24): include the JCL SET statement (// SET VAR=val) here — it is the symbolic-assignment half of the substitution layer (defines/overrides symbols for subsequent &VAR references). 1 CardDemo job uses SET. Belongs with PROC/symbolic-parameter handling, not a separate issue.
Census 2026-10-05 (external production batch corpus, ~860 jobs, counts are lower bounds; see red-dragon-forge-2cy): 0 uses of SET or &var symbolics and ~0 in-deck PROC/PEND definitions in the census; procs are only called by name. Cataloged-proc expansion already works for corpora that ship their proclib. Lowered P3 -> P4.
Status 2026-10-11: job-level SET is done (red-dragon-forge-626). Left: (a) in-stream PROC (//name PROC ... // PEND inside a job), which the bridge does not build; (b) the CLI passes no proclib directories, so a --proclib flag. SET inside a PROC body stays forge-6qr.
close_reason: In-stream PROC ... PEND is gathered by the bridge into a procedure definition, found before the library by calls after it (JCL Ref pp. 25-26), with IBM's nested in-stream example expanding as documented. SET inside a PROC already ranked per Table 13 (6qr closed). Along the way: null EXEC symbolic overrides (A=) parse (0f39e3f), and nested procedures inherit the enclosing level's symbols (f49d7bb). Record: 2026-10-12-jackal-in-stream-procs.md.

title: State change: status → in_progress
description: Set status to in_progress
